Lena was having a nightmare.

Muffled footsteps sounded in her ears before a brief pressure seized her chest. Then she was catapulted into a catalogue of her worst memories. She saw the day her mother had died, the night she’d been adopted by the Luthors, Lex’s trial, Kara’s ouster as Supergirl…

And then she woke, suddenly feeling peaceful. Her memories of the dream slipped away rapidly, so that in a few seconds she felt nothing but a lingering sense of uncertainty.

Lena yawned as she slipped out of bed. Four days since the announcement of the takeover and things still hadn’t begun to quiet down. She stepped into her living room, thinking about calling Kara for a quick early breakfast, when she realized her girlfriend had beaten her to it.

The hero was sitting at the dining room table, a mountain of junk food sitting before her and a healthy meal prepared for Lena. She looked happier than she’d been in weeks. Maybe longer.

Smiling, Lena took her seat. “This looks amazing. What’s the occasion?”

Kara grinned. “Do I need a reason to make breakfast for my wife?”

Lena froze. “What…what did you just say?”

The hero rolled her eyes. “Someone’s still a little tired. Don’t forget you have that press conference in a few hours. People aren’t going to be thrilled by seeing the mighty Protector of Earth and its Colonies yawning through her speech.”

“Right…the press conference.” It was coming back to her now. An announcement to the people of the world that order had been entirely restored to their sector of space, partially thanks to the addition of three new human Green Lanterns.

Still slightly confused, Lena stood up and made her way to the window to look upon the world.

Her world. Lena Luthor ruled it all with a firm and gentle hand. Violence was at an all-time low, prosperity had been spread to every corner of the globe, and most of the people of Earth adored her. The only individual with greater popularity was her wife, Supergirl, who’d stood at her side every step of the way.

“Reminiscing?” Kara asked.

“Yes,” Lena replied honestly. “Sometimes I can’t believe we made it to this point.” She thought back to her campaign of world domination, the memories rapidly falling into place. It hadn’t always been easy, but it had all been worth it. She’d mobilized enough of the Earth’s resources into a defense grid just in time to thwart the planet’s first alien invasion. After repulsing the armada with next to zero casualties, most of the human population was ready to stand behind L-Corp.

Those who disagreed with her rule were more than welcome to speak out against her. No leader was universally beloved, even one who had saved the planet.

“Don’t you have a meeting?” the Protector of Earth asked her wife.

Kara nodded. “In a bit. But with Clark not around, no one else is such a huge stickler for time. No one’s going to kill me for being five minutes late.”

Clark? Wasn’t he…? Oh yes, Lena had briefly forgotten. Clark and Lois were currently offworld at the moment, taking a brief break from heroism following the birth of their first child. She’d grown so used to having them around it was hard to believe they’d be gone for a year.

“Are you sure you’re okay?” Kara must not have missed the brief look of uncertainty in Lena’s eyes. But as the hero walked over and wrapped her arms over Lena’s shoulders, any sense of unease immediately faded away.

“Positive,” the CEO grinned, kissing her wife on the cheek. “Everything is perfect.”

Fantasy

Thirty miles out of National City, Reign was furiously hacking her way into L-Corp’s systems. Samantha Arias’s CFO clearance gave her a lot of access, but there were many secrets hidden deep within the network meant for Lena Luthor’s eyes alone. Normally, the CEO would instantly have been alerted to a potential breach and responded swiftly. Even with the alien technology at Reign’s disposal, this would take some time.

Fortunately, time was something she had plenty of. For all of Lena Luthor’s caution, the CEO had been incapacitated by an attack she could never have seen coming. Once Pestilence had prepared the plant, all Reign had had to was place a microscopic lure on Lena’s chest during the next morning’s business meeting.

The Black Mercy, small and stretchy until it reached a host, had easily made its way through the apartment’s plumbing.

Luthor’s death was all but guaranteed. Reign had made certain that she had released the plant during a time when the executive had no appointments on her schedule. Supergirl was in Midvale speaking with Eliza Danvers over dinner, a painful conversation that would likely take all of the hero’s attention. She would not be contacting her girlfriend for a few hours.

The Black Mercy would drain every ounce of life from Luthor’s body.

Even if Luthor was found before she died, there was little chance she could be saved. Supergirl could possibly know about the plant’s weakness, but even that would not be enough. Breaking the fantasy required convincing the host that their dream world was an illusion. The Black Mercy deployed the intelligence of its host against it, using the powers of their mind to fight back against the words of an intruder. With Luthor’s intellect at its disposal, overpowering the plant was all but impossible.

Lena Luthor would die. Samantha Arias would seize control of L-Corp, and the next stage of Earth’s history could finally begin.

Of course, there was a remote chance the CEO could survive. Reign had been instructed not to enter Luthor’s penthouse and finish the job herself; they didn’t know what automated defenses had been prepared for such an attack.

But even if Luthor survived, Reign’s work here would accomplish all what was needed.

Am I really doing this?

Alex didn’t have access to Lena’s apartment. She did, however, have access to Kara’s apartment. And since the hero had left her keycard lying on her bedroom table…Alex now had access to Lena’s apartment.

Ding!

Alex stepped into the penthouse. Even at this late stage, it was hard to imagine that this was actually happening. She called for the CEO, steeling herself for one of the most painful conversations of her entire life.

What she found was far worse.

\

“I’m sorry.”

Eliza frowned at her impatiently. “For what? There’s nothing else you could have done, and we both know it. You love being Supergirl, and I am so proud of you. Jeremiah would have been too. I was prepared to deal with the consequences; they’re a small price to pay for all the lives you’ve saved.”

It would have been easier if Eliza had shouted. Her adoptive mother had refused to try to bond with the Harun-el, though the aging of her cells probably made that a moot point. Vulnerable, she had been forced to quit her job and accept an L-Corp security detail. Eliza was clearly unhappy about the situation, but she had refused to direct any of the blame to her second daughter.

That didn’t help with any of the guilt Kara was feeling. Yes, she had been morally obligated to act as Supergirl. But if she had been more careful, maybe this nightmare wouldn’t have come true.

Buzz! Kara reached for her phone and automatically answered once she saw her sister’s picture.

“Hi Alex. What’s going-”

“You need to get to Lena’s penthouse now.” Alex’s voice was so full of steel that Kara knew she was repressing panic. “Lena’s unconscious. There’s some plant thing wrapped around her and I can’t wake her up.”

Supergirl’s heart froze. It can’t be. The Black Mercy was native only to Krypton; there couldn’t be any left. Clinging to that hope, Kara responded to her sister. “Are there black tentacles wrapped around her? What about thorns?”

A pause. “Yes. Kara, what is this thing?” Alex’s voice insisted. “I can’t get it off!”

“Don’t try!” Kara warned. “It would kill her! I’ll be there in a minute.” Her limbs shaking with anxiety, she turned to Eliza. “Lena’s in trouble. I have to go!”

Kara busted through the windows of Lena’s penthouse. Either the CEO didn’t have any defenses set up, or they’d been specifically calibrated not to target Supergirl’s DNA. Hopefully it was the latter.

Her eyes lit on Alex, standing on Lena’s bedside.

Rao. It was a Black Mercy. Lena was prone in bed, the rise and fall of her chest the only sign of life still in her body. Four black tentacles were wrapped possessively around her lithe form, large thorns sticking out of each one. The flower-like center of the organism was resting in the middle of Lena’s chest.

“What is this thing?”

Kara turned to Alex, her heartbeat going a million miles a minute. “A Black Mercy, a plant native to Krypton. It seeks out a host and sucks the life out of them in a single day. How long has she been like this?”

Lena can’t die. Lena can’t die.  

“I don’t know! I found her five minutes ago, but there’s no telling when this thing got her. You have to get it off!”

“I can’t! Rip it off and the victim dies. They taught us about these things in school. There’s only one way to get a Black Mercy off, and it almost never works.” Kara was moving towards her girlfriend now, trying to steady her breathing. She knew what she had to do.

Her only advantage was time. Lena couldn’t have been here for more than five hours, and the plant had never been known to kill in less than twenty.

I won’t let this happen. Not to her. “The plant works by putting its victim inside a fantasy of their own creation…their perfect world. The only way to get it to release its hold is to enter the trance yourself and get the victim to reject the illusion.”

Alex’s head was shaking with confusion. “Enter the trance? How?”

The hero placed her hand over the central thorn. “These things can pierce anything. If it enters my bloodstream, I’ll go unconscious and enter the illusion. It can only entrance one person at a time, so I’ll be aware it’s not reality. Then I find Lena and fix this.”

There were actual tears in Alex’s eyes. “And if you fail?”

“Then we die together.”

The ex-officer jumped forward, seizing Kara’s arm. “No! Lena wouldn’t want this! The world needs you! I need you!”

“You’re right; Lena would tell me to let her die. But this isn’t up to her. You can’t stop me, so don’t even try.” The pain in her sister’s eyes tormented Kara more than Alex would ever know, but there was no other choice. “Don’t take my hand off the thorn; the plant would kill me. If I don’t make it back, tell everyone…”

Alex’s arm darted out, going for the central thorn.

WHOOSH!

A blast of super-breath caught Alex mid-motion, throwing the ex-officer across the room. She collided with the bedroom wall and collapsed to the floor, groaning in pain.

“I love you, Alex.”

“KARA, NO-!”

Supergirl’s hand pierced the thorn.

\

“Alright, so we’re ready to adjourn. Unless there was anything else. Supergirl?”

Kara’s eyes blinked open. She knew that, if a person was present in a Black Mercy victim’s fantasy, entering the illusion would involve her taking over the body of her fantasy-self. The hero had been well prepared for that.

What she wasn’t prepared for was to find herself sitting at the head of a table in a massive conference room. Surrounded by other people in costumes. In a space station.

The floor-to-ceiling windows revealed a magnificent view of the stars, with the Earth itself rotating above them. Kara was no stranger to space travel, but still. Wow.

“Supergirl?” Another voice prompted.

Kara forced herself to look at the people around her. If she was going to break Lena out of her fantasy, she needed to know what she was getting into. The only way to save the victim was to convince them that the illusion wasn’t real. To accomplish that, she needed to understand the world she’d been placed in.

One of them was a man dressed in a red full-body suit adorned by a lightning bolt. There were another two, a man and woman, dressed in dark green apparel and also glowing green. The figure at the other end of the table seemed to be almost entirely robotic.

There was an empty chair to her right adorned with a logo that looked like a pair of wings.

“No, I have nothing else,” Supergirl stated.

Lightning Bolt Man turned to her. “Then are we good to go? I’m supposed to be meeting my wife soon for our wedding rehearsal.”

It took a moment to realize that she was being asked permission. “Y-yes, we’re adjourned.”

There were smiles and casual goodbyes as the assembled heroes- for that’s what they had to be- left. One figure, however, remained behind before approaching Kara. He was green-skinned and dressed in a dark suit. With a start, she recognized him as the Martian they had failed to save.

“Kara, are you alright?”

Play it cool, play it cool. “I’m fine. I just can’t help but feel like I’ve forgotten something. I need to think for a few minutes.”

The Martian gave her a look that was almost fatherly. “Well, there is your wife’s press conference in a few hours. I’m sure she’s expecting you to be by her side.”

Wife?! Despite the direness of the situation, a strange spark of happiness came to life in her chest. Was she Lena’s wife in this fantasy?

She tested the waters. “Yeah. Never a good idea to get on Lena’s bad side.”

Her suspicions were confirmed when the Martian nodded. “Angering the ruler of a planet is always foolish, even if you are married to her. Especially if you are married to her.”

So Lena ruled the world in this fantasy. Because of course she does. And, apparently, Kara was ruling it right at her side. Supergirl supposed she should have expected it, but still…

“I’m off,” the Martian said. “The Mars colony won’t build itself. Good luck today.”

She nodded as the other hero flew off, a sadness overtaking her. There was no telling what kind of life the Martian would have lived had he survived, but to see what could never be right in front of her…because of her failure…

Kara shook her head. Lena was the one in danger right now, and she could still be saved. Supergirl felt around her pocket, finding an L-Phone that unlocked with her fingerprint. Perfect. There was only one place to start her search: the most useful and comprehensive database ever known to this sector of space.

Lena Kieran Luthor (born January 3, 1990), also known as Vanity, is an Earth-based politician, superhero, businesswoman, and philanthropist. After ascending to the position of L-Corp CEO following her father’s death, Luthor embarked on a worldwide campaign to increase her political, financial, and societal influence. During the summer of 2020, she employed her resources to thwart an attempted invasion by the Dominator armada and capitalized on her success to officially declare her control over the planet (an action that faced little overt opposition.) Known as the Protector of Earth and Its Colonies, Luthor has attracted widespread support from the planet’s populace despite significant criticism of the methods she employed in her rise to power.

Kara took a deep breath. Wikipedia had proven enlightening. She was in a world controlled by Lena, where her secret identity was still secret and Supergirl was publicly wed to the ruler of the planet. And Clark was alive. How would he even be in Lena’s fantasy?

This wasn’t good. She was dealing with a Black Mercy illusion more detailed than any Kara had ever heard of. The plant must have been drawing upon Lena’s own brainpower to project the fantasy, which meant that forcing the supervillain to reject it would be nearly impossible. All of the CEO’s capacity for logic and reasoning were at the Black Mercy’s disposal.

A ping sounded in the ceiling.

“Supergirl, you have a video call waiting for you in the lounge.” A voice sounded through the PA system.

Lena.

“On my way,” she called out.

\

“Please present identification,” an automated voice intoned.

Walking towards the conference screen, Supergirl placed her hand on the nearby touchpad. A green light immediately blinked beneath her fingers.

“Welcome, Supergirl. Displaying video call.”

Kara steeled herself to confront her girlfriend. Everything depended on easing her into the truth. If she approached Lena in the wrong way, the CEO might refuse to hear her out at all. Sweat actually began to leak through her fingers as the screen came to life. She. Would. Not. Lose. Lena.  

But it wasn’t Lena.

“Jeju?!”

Alura Zor-El smiled at her. “You don’t have to be so surprised, Kara. It’s been three rotations since we last spoke. I know you’re busy ruling the Earth, but did you really think your mother wouldn’t reach out and see how you were doing?” The image spoke in perfect Kryptonian. “Kara?”

She was kneeling on the floor, oblivious to the tears sliding down her cheeks. Mom is alive! Kara hadn’t been left to wander the stars alone, dumped on an unfamiliar planet with no one to turn to. Her mother was still watching out for her and everything would be…

It’s not real! It’s not real!

“I-I’m fine. Mom, how are you…where are you?”

The older woman rolled her eyes. “Still on Krypton. It wouldn’t be polite to leave while Kal and Lois are visiting, now would it? They’re out fishing with your father.”

This was impossible. Krypton was gone. Destroyed. Even in this fantasy world, it had to be. How else would Kara have arrived on Earth?

Unless…

“Sorry,” Kara managed. Her eyes were glued to her mother’s face, a visage that was still staring at her with all the love and concern that the hero could remember from her childhood. “I…I had a nightmare last night. About the pod.”

Alura’s face darkened with guilt. “I will never forgive myself for that. But you know how doomed the planet looked when we chose to send you and Kal to Earth. We couldn’t have counted on a miracle. At least…that’s what I tell myself.”

So Kara had Earth and Krypton in this fantasy.

“Like you said,” Alura continued. “It worked out in the end. You found love and helped save the Earth. Brought our worlds together. It was the will of Rao.”

There were so many questions in her mind. Was the Black Mercy now making a fantasy for Kara? If not, how did Lena’s brain even know what Alura had looked like? And shouldn’t her mother have aged by now?

But none of that mattered. She was speaking with jeju.

“Mom, I…I miss you. More than anything.”

Alura smiled sadly. “I miss you too. But you’re needed on Earth. If you’re feeling homesick, however, I’d be more than happy to have another guest for a few days. I know interstellar flight is expensive, but your wife has never had an issue with that before,” she noted with a wink.

This isn’t real. This is pointless. You are wasting time.

“How is dad?” she asked.

“Well, you talked to him yesterday. He’s fine. Gaining a little too much weight for my liking…he’ll have to go on a diet. Some of the hero worship is getting to him. I suppose being the savior of a planet made that inevitable.” Alura paused. “Why are you crying, little one?”

Kara forced herself to look away from her mother. This wasn’t fair! She couldn’t lose her parents again. Even if this wasn’t real. It felt real.

The hero looked up again. “Mom…I don’t blame you for the pod. I still remember screaming at you as you put me in…I can’t believe I did that. You were making the most painful and selfless choice I can imagine, and I just called you a coward. Did I even tell you I love you before it took off?”

“It doesn’t matter, Kara,” Alura said, her voice filled with warmth. “How could I have ever doubted that you love me? You were a young girl, forced into a spaceship as her planet burned. What else could have been expected but anger and panic?”

This was the mother Kara remembered. The one that Eliza had always tried to be. Someone who was there for her no matter what, and loved her unconditionally. Who had faith that Kara would be a beacon of light for all she let into her life.

BZZT!

Supergirl’s blast of heat vision fried the monitor in an instant. Lena was dying, and Kara couldn’t waste any more time. Anything she saw here was an illusion, nothing more. Even if the pain in her chest was so sharp it felt as if she was being pierced with a knife.

She had to be strong. This wasn’t even her fantasy. And if Kara had known this was all an illusion and still had been tempted…

I’m coming, Lena.

Logic

“Hi, this is Sam. I’m either out with my daughter or helping my boss take over the world. Leave a message and I’ll get back to you as soon as I can.”

Beep.

“Sam, it’s Alex. I’m in Lena’s apartment. She’s been attacked by a plant called a Black Mercy; it’s knocked her out and is sucking the life out of her. It creates a fantasy for its victim and Kara’s gone in to try and fix it. Please get here. Quickly!”

It was the third time that she’d tried to call the CFO. Alex understood that Sam had a daughter to take care of, but wasn’t an executive expected to be available for consultation at all times?

Her training as a DEO agent and an officer battled against her panic for Kara. What else could she do? No one else she knew could possibly know how to counteract a Black Mercy. There was no one who could assist her…

Assist. Lena’s assistant. Jess, if Alex was remembering correctly. The ex-officer didn’t have the assistant’s number, but she was willing to bet that Kara did. The prospect of anyone at L-Corp being able to help her was a longshot, but Alex refused to sit on her hands as a parasite killed her sister.

She reached into Kara’s pocket and pulled out the phone. Watching the steady rise and fall of her sister’s chest, she pressed down on the home button.

“Call Jess.”

\

At the familiar sound of her wife touching down on the balcony, Lena lifted her gaze away from her computer. As expected, Kara was walking towards her clad in her full heroic regalia.

“Lena, I-”

The CEO held up a hand to stop her. “Forgetting your manners so easily, Supergirl?”

Kara stared at her, eyes wide. “What do you mean?”

Lena gestured to the rug in front of her desk. “Kneel before your Empress before speaking to her. Unless you desire punishment, which I can easily provide.” She crossed her arms expectantly. “So? What’s it going to be?”

“I, uh, Lena…” Supergirl’s gaze flickered between the rug and the executive. “I didn’t expect, this, is, um…we need to…”

The CEO’s mask immediately slipped away. Clearly, Kara wasn’t in the mood to play today. Lena had been hoping for some fun after the press conference that had drained her earlier, but it looked like that wasn’t going to happen.

In a smooth motion, Lena vaulted over the desk and into her wife’s arms. “Kara, baby, what’s wrong? I haven’t seen you this worked up in a long time. Did something happen in the meeting today?”

Kara shook her head rapidly. Rao. There were tears in her eyes. The concern in Lena’s heart was rapidly changing into dread.

“Is someone hurt, or-”

“Just listen!” Kara demanded, her voice so desperate that Lena was taken aback. “I know what I’m about to say might seem crazy. You’re not going to want to believe it. But if you don’t listen, we’re both going to die.”

Die? Lena nodded slightly, forcing herself to remain calm. Clearly, something big was brewing. Another alien invasion?

“Of course,” the CEO replied. “Go ahead.”

Kara sighed deeply. “This place, this world…it’s wonderful, Lena. You’ve given me everything I’ve ever wanted in a life. It’s perfect. And that’s the problem. It’s not real. None of this is real. You’ve been attacked by a parasite called the Black Mercy, and it’s placed you inside a fantasy of your own imagination. I’ve come inside it to break you out.”

Lena’s fingers clenched. She had never heard of anything called the ‘Black Mercy’, or of any parasite that could force illusions upon a victim. Perhaps such a thing was theoretically possible, but no projects of that nature had ever come to the CEO’s attention.

This entire world was an illusion?

“That’s ridiculous, Kara. There are certain poisons that can induce vivid hallucinations, but what you’re talking about isn’t possible,” the CEO said firmly. “I have a well-detailed memory of my life, something that no hallucinogen could ever produce. The chicken at our wedding was a little dry. Three months ago, I had to buy you another television after you spilled your soda all over our old one.”

The hero was staring at Lena, rapidly shaking her head. “The Black Mercy is different; it was native only to Krypton. It can draw on the brainpower of its host; that’s what makes it so dangerous to you.” She stepped forward, placing her hands on Lena’s shoulders. “I need you to trust me. If you really care about me, you’ll reject this reality so we can build a new one. Together.”

“I do trust you, Kara. I believe that you believe what you’re saying. But tell me, what is more likely? That I’ve been infected with a parasite I’ve never heard of, one that’s capable of illusions more detailed than anything else in the universe? Or that you are under the influence of something nefarious?”

Supergirl paled. “Lena, I-”

Vanity’s suit materialized around the CEO. “It’s also possible you’re not my wife at all. Either stand down or get blasted.” Two red-sun cannons were mounted at Lena’s wrists, each aiming for the other woman’s chest.

“You wouldn’t shoot me!”

Lena scoffed. “Seriously? Of course I would. If you’re really my wife, then all that will happen is a temporary loss of your powers and some slight soreness. If you’re not my wife…then I don’t really care what happens, do I?”

\

“Kara said that removing the plant from either of them at this point would be fatal.”

Jess’s composure was rapidly breaking down. She was trained to assist a powerful executive and rub shoulders with some of the most influential people in the country, a process that necessitated a certain amount of steel. But this was different.

This was her first time in a life or death situation. She didn’t have Alex’s training as a soldier. True, working as Vanity’s secretary had not been the safest job in the world, but Jess had always assumed that she would be the one in danger. That, she might have been able to handle.

Not this.

Ms. Luthor had given her a great amount of latitude over the years. Nearly all of L-Corp’s resources were at Jess’s disposal. But there was nothing she could think of that could fix the situation; none of the alien employees within L-Corp had even heard of a Black Mercy.

So now she was watching the world’s last, best hope slowly having the life sucked out of her. It would have been a stretch to call her and Ms. Luthor friends, Jess was far too professional for that. That hadn’t stopped her from admiring her boss’s passion and commitment to making the world a better place.

The fact that Ms. Luthor had found out Jess was involved in a custody battle over her four-year-old son, hired her a lawyer without even asking first, and taken care of all court fees following Jess’s winning of full custody didn’t hurt. Nor did the regular raises she received simply for doing her job.

“I don’t…I don’t know what…where is Sam?”

Alex grimaced. “Still not answering. But we have time. Kara said that the Black Mercy usually takes at least a day to kill its victims. So as long as-”

“DEFENSES ACTIVATED!”

Machinery began to whirl in the apartment’s walls. Jess turned around just in time to see a salvo of red sun blasts and kryptonite missiles rocket towards a dark figure streaking across the sky.

The secretary screamed, the blood draining from her face. Reign, now floating a hundred meters outside the apartment windows, dodged much of the ordinance. A blast of red energy erupted from her eyes, eliminating one of the rows of turrets that had been uncovered on the roof.

“Damn it!” Alex swore as the rogue alien battled through the defenses, steadily making her way towards the penthouse. “She’ll kill them both. Call for reinforcements, everything L-Corp has! My friends, too. I’ll keep her busy.”

Jess wasn’t sure whether to be impressed by the ex-officer’s bravery or horrified at her stupidity. “She took down Lena! What chance do you have? She will kill you!”

Alex darted forward, opening one of the reinforced windows with the indoor mechanism. “I might surprise you.” She glanced back once more at her sister, and Jess realized that Reign would not be entering that penthouse until Alex Danvers was no longer breathing.

As the secretary reached for her phone, Alex leapt out the window.

\

“DNA tests confirm it beyond all doubt. You are Kara Zor-El,” Lena said. “Which means we need to find out what’s interfering with your memories and how to correct it.”

Kara sat up from the table and began to pace around the office. “We don’t have time for this! I agreed to let you test me, and now I need you to listen. We’re running out of time.”

“And I repeat, I’ve never heard of a Black Mercy. There are a thousand things, however, that could be damaging your own recollections. Tell me, Kara, how do you know that all of this isn’t real?” Lena gestured around the apartment. “Why should you trust your own memories but refuse to believe in mine?”

The hero clenched her fists.

“See? It’s far more likely that you’re under the influence of some telepath who has messed with your short-term memories. The odds of myself being infected by a plant that I’ve never heard of, from Krypton of all places, are remote. We could call your mother-”

“She’s dead! And Krypton is gone! It was destroyed when I was a child; that’s why I was sent here. My father didn’t stop it!” Desperation, clawing at her chest, was now joined by a fresh bout of pain.

With a skeptical smile, Lena shook her head. “Whatever has you under its influence hasn’t been keeping its facts straight. If Krypton was destroyed, how was I infected with a plant native to only Krypton?”

Kara winced. In truth, she had no idea. Perhaps the plant had been recreated on Earth, but she didn’t see how. Was it really her memories that had been altered with? Was this wonderful, glorious utopia really her reality?

No.

The hero could still feel, very faintly, the pain in her right palm. A small part of her mind was still connected with her real body. If Kara put all of her focus to it, she would be able to lift her hand from the thorn and exit the illusion.

Her words to Alex hadn’t been entirely truthful. If Kara didn’t leave the fantasy before Lena died, then she would die with her. Likewise, if her fantasy-self was killed before Kara left, her body would perish as well. Her mind would make it real.

Like in those confusing movies with all the leather outfits that Alex had made her watch.

But if she left of her own free will and took her hand off the thorn, Kara would be just fine. She’d lied to Alex so her sister wouldn’t be tempted to take her out before she saved Lena. Once someone had left the fantasy, it was impossible to re-enter.

Kara wasn’t leaving here alone.

“I can still feel the pain of the thorn in my hand; a small sliver of my mind is connected to my real body. I know this isn’t real! And I refuse to lose you. Please…”

“I would do anything for you, Kara, you know that. And that means I will save you from whatever is infecting your thoughts. Obviously, it’s also producing the sensation of pain you feel in your palm. There are plenty of telepaths capable of doing so,” Lena argued. “Doesn’t that sound more likely than a detailed fantasy you can enter merely by spiking your hand on a thorn?”

It sounded terrifying plausible. But this wasn’t real. It wasn’t.

There were tears in her eyes now. “Don’t you think I want this to be real?” Kara pleaded. “My family, my world…it’s perfect. Nothing in the real world could ever compare to this. Do you think I would reject this unless I was certain it was all a lie?”

Lena nodded, a fond smile breaking out amidst her worrying features. “Of course you would, if you were convinced it was the only way to save me.”

Slam! Supergirl’s foot beat into the floorboards, setting cracks spreading in the stone beneath. She wouldn’t be leaving this illusion without Lena. And that seemed to mean she wouldn’t be leaving at all.

“If I don’t take my hand off the thorn before you die, I’ll die with you! Is that what you want?”

Lena stared at her. “Kara, I love you more than anything. If that were really the case, then I would want you to abandon me.”

I love you. Kara didn’t know why those words affected her so much. She should have expected it, given that Lena had married her in this fantasy. Yet that simple phrase ignited so much happiness and longing within the hero that her breath slipped away.

“I love you too.” These words came easy, but they felt so right to say. The kind, beautiful, passionate, brilliant woman before her deserved nothing less. “That’s why I won’t leave you.”

The executive smiled brightly. “You don’t have to! We can call Sam and Alex back from their vacation. Ruby and Jonathan won’t be happy, but they can always take another one. We need to set your mind right.”

“Who the hell is Jonathan?” Kara demanded, her frustration boiling over.

Lena’s face shifted back into a concerned frown. “The son your sister and Sam adopted. Your godson? This is worse than I thought.”

“I don’t have a godson!”

 “Right. You have two. Or have you forgotten about Van-El too? Clark and Lois won’t be happy. We should probably call them in as well-”

Kara stomped over to Lena’s desk. “Clark. Is. Dead. My godchildren don’t exist. And this person…”  she snatched a photograph off the desk. A man the hero recognized as Lionel Luthor was smiling next to an aging brunette. “Probably doesn’t either.”

“Those are my parents, Kara,” Lena said, keeping her voice gentle. “You saw them at their last anniversary party, a few months before they died. If you hadn’t been there for me that year…”

Her shoulders slumping, Kara resorted to throwing out the big guns. “I’m sorry, Lena, but I never met them. Your parents weren’t married. Lionel had an affair with your mother and only acknowledged you after she died when you were four. Your stepmother Lillian hated you, and your brother Lex went mad and ended up killing Clark. Doesn’t any of this ring a bell?”

“Nope. I don’t know anyone named Lillian or Lex. If I was under a ‘Black Mercy’, don’t you think it would be sticking closer to the truth? These deviations from reality would make it more likely that the victim would reject the fantasy.”

Kara screamed internally.

“You don’t know how powerful this thing is! It can draw upon the victim’s brainpower. That’s why this fantasy is so detailed, and why you have such logical arguments against what I’m telling you,” Supergirl pleaded.

Lena didn’t even seem worried. If there was any fear in her face, it was only stemming from her concern that someone or something had meddled with Kara’s thoughts.

“I estimate that the odds of a plant that originates from a dead planet, can draw upon a victim’s own brainpower to create the most detailed illusion imaginable, and allows for others to enter the fantasy to exist to be roughly four quadrillion to one. The odds of you being confused by a telepath or mental alteration device are orders of magnitude higher.”

Kara almost had an urge to laugh bitterly. Lena Luthor’s mind had outsmarted her countless times, but it had been an immense relief to know that the supervillain had no intention of killing her. It was the most powerful weapon on Earth, but Lena Luthor’s intelligence had been sworn to never harm an innocent.

Now, her girlfriend’s powerful brain was about to murder both of them.

\

Alex collided with Reign right before the alien could take out the last of the penthouse’s defenses. Clutching her enemy in a vicelike grip, Alex allowed her momentum to slam them both into the roof of a building roughly a block away.

Concrete dust and sand erupted from the point of impact. The tall building shuddered beneath them, leading Alex to fear that it was about to collapse beneath them.

WHAM!

In that moment of hesitation, Reign’s fist slammed into her shoulder. The world spun as Alex was sent careening across the roof, landing only inches away from the edge.

“Careful now.”

Alex jumped to her feet. Reign was standing several meters away, having made no move to follow up her attack. Balling her fists and calming her nerves, the ex-officer forced herself into a ready position. Her shoulder felt like it was on fire.

“Leave,” she hissed at the alien. “Get off of Earth if you know what’s good for you.”

Reign scoffed, contemptuous but not openly hostile. “Your world will become ours, soon enough. That is its destiny. But your sister need not perish. The same may be said for you.”

All of Alex’s muscles were tensed, awaiting the burst of superspeed from her opponent. “You want to kill us all, no matter what you say. We will never let you take our planet. And I’m not letting you near my sister.”

“You should,” Reign intoned. “I can save her from the Black Mercy. If she remains inside the illusion when the Luthor dies, she will perish. That cannot be allowed to happen.”

Ha! “I know better. If Kara leaves the illusion now, she’ll die. You get past me and you’ll kill both of them.”

Reign shook her head, a gesture Alex found strangely familiar. “Kara Zor-El is not my enemy. Let me pass and you will see for yourself.”

Alex’s eyes narrowed. “Never.”

Their eyes met, Reign’s glinting with an amused resignation. Seconds passed, and Alex knew she was being invited to make the first move.

Strike first, she had been taught. Always strike first.

Alex darted forward, lashing out with an uppercut aimed at the alien’s chest. Reign merely leaned to the side, avoiding the blow with a movement so fast that the ex-officer could barely perceive it. Then a sweeping kick collided with both of Alex’s legs, knocking her feet out from under her.

Instinctively, Alex immediately rolled to the side and just managed to avoid the follow-up kick. She charged again at Reign, lashing out with three punches to the midsection. The alien dodged the first, deflected the second, and caught Alex’s wrist on the third.

No!  

Alex launched a high kick at her opponent, forcing her to release the hold before she could twist Alex’s arm. Reign launched a swipe at her face, one that the ex-officer barely dodged. Thinking quickly, Alex darted to the other side of the roof, hoping to get on her enemy’s blindside-

BZZT! Twin beams of red energy slammed into her chest, knocking her into the ground. Her skin escaped with some minor sizzling, but her clothes had caught fire. Alex leapt to her feet, snarling at the alien who still stood in the center of the roof.

She closed the distance between them, jumping into the air. If she could just land a blow to Reign’s-

“Ack!”

Faster than Alex’s eyes could see, Reign’s arm had darted out and seized her by the throat. Desperately struggling for breath, the ex-officer clawed at the fingers wrapped around her windpipe.

“Insufficient.”

Reign finally took off from the ground, keeping her hold on Alex’s throat as they rose dozens of meters into the air. Her vision darkening, Alex fruitlessly kicked at the alien’s legs.

No! No! Kara! I need to save Kara!  

“Several months remain. Time enough for you to make your choices. But what will you do, I wonder? Let’s see,” Reign intoned, her mouth set in a slight smirk.

Then she let go.

Terrifying weightlessness took her for a second. There was a brief spasm of pain as Alex slammed into the ground, and everything went black.

A Way Out
