“You have to get out of here!”

When Jess had deactivated the security controls on the elevator, she had been hoping for some reinforcements to show up. Unfortunately, the young man who’d just arrived was the only one of Kara Danvers’s friends who remained fully human.

Winn shook his head as the sounds of Alex’s clash with Reign filled the room. “She won’t last long. James and the others aren’t here yet,” he said desperately. “We have to move them!” He nodded at Kara and Lena, then jerked his head at the elevator.

Well. It was as good a plan as any. Jess was just about to nod in agreement when the sounds of battle stopped.

No point. Too late.

\

“If you really believe that, Kara, then try to leave,” Lena implored. “Once you fail, you’ll realize that this isn’t an illusion and we can work on isolating what’s manipulating you.”

Supergirl resisted pounding the floor in frustration. “I can’t! If I leave, I can’t come back in. The Black Mercy will reject me. I’m not going to watch you die!”

The CEO chuckled. “Well, isn’t that convenient,” she mused sarcastically.

Kara’s eyes began to water as she realized there was no saving Lena. She couldn’t use logic to break through the brainpower at the Black Mercy’s disposal.

I could leave. Continue protecting the Earth. It’s what she would want. She even said so!

No. Kara knew, in her heart of hearts, that Lena would never have left her if the situation was reversed. And Supergirl…no, Kara, didn’t leave the people she loved behind. Better to die than live knowing she’d left Lena to her death.

There had to be some way to win. Logic wouldn’t work. That was the only thing that had ever managed to break someone out of the Black Mercy’s grip. But the plant hadn’t ever been fully understood even by the Science Guild, and there had never been the chance for experimentation. What if there was another way to break the fantasy?

Fantasy.

“Come with me,” Lena pleaded. “We can stop whatever’s doing this to you, and you can see that all of this is real. Our life…the one we built together.”

Kara forced herself to ignore the words. A Black Mercy with Lena’s mind might be able to convince her of anything. It didn’t help that she wanted to believe it.

And that might be the key to fixing this.

Every victim of the Black Mercy was placed in a fantasy of their own making. Why? To ensure that they wholeheartedly accepted the illusion. Seeing all of their desires fulfilled placed the mind in a passive state, unable to resist the parasite’s influence.

But what if the fantasy became a nightmare? Would the brain suddenly reject it? Perhaps Kara was simply desperate, but it was the only plan she had. And it did make some sense. There had to be a reason every illusion created by the plant was always extremely pleasing to the victim.

I have to turn this into a nightmare.

What would work? Only something drastic would shock Lena’s mind out of the Black Mercy’s influence; the plant’s control was clearly running deep by this point. Supergirl could go on a rampage, destroying buildings and-

“No,” Kara hissed to herself. That wouldn’t work. “Give me a minute to think!” Lena, having taken a step closer, reluctantly moved back.

Lena would just believe that Kara was being controlled by a hostile force. Even if hundreds of innocent lives were lost, that wouldn’t be enough. The CEO’s subconscious could easily convince itself that things in the illusion were better than in reality. Hundreds dying because of a brainwashed Supergirl would be worth the price of world peace and the salvation of seven billion.

And Kara, even in an illusion, wouldn’t be able to harm innocents. She couldn’t take the risk. The risk that…

No! I know this is an illusion! I know it!

The Black Mercy’s poisonous logic was infecting her mind. When it came to philosophy and ethics, Kara was more than capable of debating her girlfriend. But in any argument over objective facts, such as whether reality was an illusion, she would never win against Lena’s brainpower.

She didn’t have much time.

I have to do something she can’t fix. She had to take the central element of Lena’s fantasy and burn it to the ground, so that even Lena could find no way of ever fixing it. But even if Kara was willing to destroy this Earth’s peace and prosperity, how could she manage it?

Then the hero looked down at the wedding band on her finger, thinking back to everything she had seen. And in a moment of affection and horror, Kara realized the truth.

A stable and prosperous Earth wasn’t the center of Lena Luthor’s fantasy.

\

Lena stood and watched as her wife seemingly debated with herself. The CEO was considering disabling Kara by force, but that was risky and didn’t seem necessary at the moment. Kara was delusional, but she wasn’t acting violently. Lena needed to try and resolve this peacefully.

Supergirl took a deep breath, meeting Lena’s gaze. A flurry of emotion swept by Kara’s eyes…fear, sadness, confusion…before the hero’s expression morphed into one of steely resolve.

“I…I can convince you.” Kara seemed to be struggling to speak. “I guess I probably have clearance to access your vaults, right? And there’s probably one at the Justice League space station.” At an uncertain nod from Lena, she continued. “Good. Uh, wait here. I’ll be back in five minutes.” 

The CEO took a harried step forward. “No. You’re a danger to yourself and others right now. I can’t let you go.”

A small smile. “Lena, look at me. We might disagree about the nature of reality right now, but otherwise we’re on the same page. Look into my eyes and tell me if you think I’m capable of hurting someone.”

Lena did.

“Alright, go,” the CEO conceded. “Five minutes. Then I’m coming after you.”

\

It took her seven minutes.

Seven minutes to fly into space, access the vault, and come back to Earth. By the time she touched down back in Lena’s office, the CEO was still sitting anxiously in her chair.

Kara’s chest was heaving with fear.

“You always were patient,” she said, trying to inject some humor into her words. “If…if this doesn’t work…” This isn’t happening. This can’t be happening.

“Kara, what’s going on?” Lena jumped to her feet.

Her eyes glistening, Kara forced herself to face her girlfriend. “Logic can’t break you out of the illusion. Maybe emotion can. If I’m not around, this might not be a fantasy for you anymore…”

“Not around…KARA, NO!”

The hero had revealed the lead-lined container she was holding. Inches of the substance coated the surface, fully suppressing the green glow they both knew was encased within.

“You won’t be able to save me, even with that big brain of yours. I might be able to pull my hand off the thorn, if I don’t black out from the pain, but that will just leave my fantasy counterpart to die in my place. Either way, your perfect life will be ended,” Kara said firmly, ignoring the trembling in her arms. “No more me. You’ll never be able to bring me back.”

Lena tensed, looking for a chance to seize the container. “No! If this really is an illusion, then just take your hand off the thorn now. Let me die. Don’t risk it! You don’t need me. Not like I need you!”

“You’re wrong. Lena, I can’t imagine a world without you in it. I know you’d want me to save myself. That’s why I love you so much,” she said, barely suppressing a sob. “My fantasy might not have had us ruling the world, but we would have been a family. Maybe on Krypton, maybe on Earth. But you and me. Always.”

Lena shook her head rapidly, her entire body pulsing with terror. “Kara, this is real. Don’t do this just because some telepath is messing with your mind!”

WHOOSH!

Kara unleashed a gigantic gust of her freeze breath, blowing the unprepared CEO across the room. As Lena’s back slammed into the wall, Supergirl ripped open the lead container. Her entire body immediately exploded with pain; it felt like razor-sharp needles with searing into every inch of her skin.

I can’t do this. Oh Rao, I can’t-

Her eyes found Lena, climbing to her feet with tears in her eyes. And Kara realized that she didn’t have a choice.

“If I don’t make it…” Kara began, gingerly positioning the sharp of kryptonite above her heart. “Tell them all that I love them, and that I have no regrets.”

The CEO jumped across the room, but Kara was quicker. By the time Lena had landed to her feet beside her, the hero had already plunged the kryptonite dagger into her chest.

Nothing Kara had endured had ever compared to this. Every centimeter the blade traveled through her organ ignited a supernova of pain. At any other time, a second of this agony would have been enough to knock her out instantly.

But that couldn’t happen now. Kara had to leave. She had to take her hand off the thorn and leave her fantasy-self to die in her place. Yet she couldn’t. As the hero had known would likely be the case, she couldn’t muster the concentration to focus on her physical body. Every iota of her mind was pain and agony and Lena’s tear-stricken, pleading face.

Supergirl tried to muster a few last words, but her lips couldn’t find the strength to move. With her last coherent thoughts, Kara tried to focus her mind of her friends. A good image to go out on-

Yank!

An impossible force tugged on her wrist. Her world of pain disappeared as her hand was ripped free of the Black Mercy’s thorn. The office had vanished, revealing a familiar penthouse. There was no time to take it in as the hand that had seized her wrist threw her aside.

Kara’s momentum carried her across the room. What’s happening? Where-?! The pain might have vanished, but her brain hadn’t yet got the memo. Tearing her free of the illusion had only worsened the strain on her mind.

Everything went black.

\

After tossing Kara aside, Reign had turned back to Lena. The alien’s eyes were brimming with red energy. Jess, recovering from her shock, dived between them.

“You can’t take her!”

Reign actually smirked in amusement. “Then die with your boss.” The glowing red eyes turned to her, and the secretary knew she was about to be scorched by twin beams of heat vision.

Jess searched for a noble thought to go out on, but all her brain could come up with was hopefully it will be quick.

“No!”

The secretary gasped in shock as Winn jumped to tackle her out of the way. It really was a shame. No human could move faster than a Kryptonian’s heat vision. Reign was just getting two targets for the price of one.

Yet her body felt the impact of Winn colliding with her. And when they both hit the floor, neither had been seared by heat vision. The blast hadn’t gone off.

Jess looked up to see Reign glaring at them, annoyance plain in her eyes.

\

“KARA!”

Lena fell to her knees as her wife choked on her own blood. This couldn’t be happening. Kara couldn’t die. Nothing mattered now. Nothing would ever matter again.

Her mind refused to accept it. Kara wasn’t dead! Kara couldn’t be dead because otherwise there was no point to going on living. The woman who had been her light in the darkness, who had believed in her when no one else did, could not be gone.

Kara had believed in her. Kara had chosen to be friends with her even after Lex killed Clark, defended her at every opportunity, even handed her kryptonite just as a gesture of trust. The hero had shown her that she didn’t have to sacrifice her happiness to save the world…that there might be a bit of light left over for Lena to keep for herself.

This reality wasn’t real. It wasn’t real because it couldn’t be real.

The illusion melted away in an instant. Lena’s eyes flickered open to a vision of her penthouse in chaos. She barely noticed the plant on her chest withering away into dust. All that mattered was Kara- unconscious on the floor- and Reign.

Reign, who was about to kill Jess and Winn. Reign, who had subjected her to an illusion of her perfect life only so it could be snatched away. Reign, who had forced to her watch as Kara died on the floor.

Her world went red.

She wasn’t aware of her mental command to instantly form her suit around her. Lena didn’t register herself rocketing forward, slamming into the off-guard alien and hurtling them both out the window. All she knew was rage.

Glowing with a sickly green light, Lena’s fists slammed into the alien’s face again and again. They crashed onto a rooftop, kicking up dust and asphalt as they skidded across the surface. “Do you have any idea what you’ve done?” the CEO hissed.

She lashed out again, assailing Reign with blows imbued with both kryptonite and red sun energy. Blood dripping from her nose, the alien finally lost her footing under the onslaught; Lena’s next right hook sent her enemy careening into the concrete.

Fierce exultation melding with her rage, the supervillain rushed forward to capitalize on the moment. Reign was going to pay. Lena was going to make her beg for death before-

WHAM!

Reign’s legs, balled up into her chest, suddenly darted out to deliver a devastating kick to Lena’s midsection. The wind completely knocked out of her lungs, the supervillain went sprawling across the roof.

She came back into her senses just in time for Reign to dart over to her in a burst of superspeed. Before Lena could react, the alien’s hands wrapped around her throat and began to squeeze.

“You should have stayed in whatever happy fantasy the Black Mercy granted you. At least then, your death would have been painless,” Reign snarled.

Lena’s own hands darted up, grasping the alien’s shoulders.

“Fry.”

All of her suit’s energy pouring into her hands, Lena unleashed a devastating amount of electricity into the alien. Reign screamed in agony as sizzling blue energy flooded into her body. As the fingers loosened around her throat and voltage crackled between them, the supervillain increased the discharge even further. Smoke now issued from Reign’s hair as the alien’s entire body was encased in electricity.

BZZT! Red energy erupted from Reign’s pupils. The concussive force knocked the two women apart, sending Lena falling over the roof’s edge and down towards the sidewalk hundreds of feet below.

SLAM!

Her entire body aching with pain, Lena suddenly became aware of panicked screaming as the remaining civilians in the area desperately tried to run away. In a moment of sheer terror, Lena realized that Reign wouldn’t hesitate to put their lives at risk. If that happened-

In her moment of hesitation, Reign’s feet collided with her forehead. Lena’s world slipped away as her body collapsed to the ground in a heap. Two punches slammed into her forehead before fingers wrapped around her throat once again, and this time the supervillain could do nothing but gasp in desperation as she fell into unconsciousness.

“NO!”

Two blue beams of energy slammed into Reign’s side, separating the two combatants once again. Then Kara was there, standing in front of Lena in her full civilian regatta.

In an instant, Reign was gone.

Supergirl stared off into the air, making certain that the rogue alien was truly gone. Then Lena felt herself being lifted gently off the ground and into the air, and she knew that everything was going to be okay.

Kara.

\

“You lied to me.”

Supergirl turned towards her sister. They were sitting in Kara’s apartment; Jess had sent a clean-up and repair crew to fix the mess in the penthouse. Sam and Winn, sitting on the other side of the room next to the still-unconscious Lena, were doing their best to pretend they weren’t listening.

“I couldn’t risk you pulling me out early. I’m not apologizing for that. If you thought you could guarantee my safety by pulling me out, you would have done it. I know exactly how much Lena’s life means to you,” Kara said firmly.

Alex winced. “I…suppose that’s fair. But you can’t blame me for being willing to choose you over her. I definitely don’t want Lena dead, but you’re my sister!” She laughed ironically. “Funny how it seems I can’t trust Supergirl, but it seems I can trust Reign.”

“She didn’t just let you live,” Winn said, apparently no longer deaf. “She went out of her way to save you.”

Sam nodded. “She didn’t seem to want to kill you, either,” she glanced at Alex. “Though it seems she was just fine giving you a beatdown. Are you feeling any better?”

Lifting the pack from her head, Alex groaned. “Can you grab me some more ice from the kitchen.”

“Anything for the brave hero.” Sam winked and got to her feet, heading for the refrigerator. The CFO had been horrified that she’d been out of contact during the attack- she’d left her phone off during a meeting, apparently- but she’d quickly arrived afterwards to help tend to the wounded.

Especially Alex.

“Chicks love the superheroes,” Winn muttered, earning him a pillow to the face when Sam’s back was turned.

“So what was it like? Lena’s fantasy?” Alex asked. “How did you manage to pull her out of it?”

Kara’s face turned bright red. There was no easy way to say ‘We were married, and by the way so were you and Sam. Also, I broke her out of it by killing myself and would have died had Reign not chosen that exact moment to come and pull me out of it.

Everyone looked at her curiously, Sam now returning from the kitchen.

The hero took a deep breath and shook her head. “I’m not telling. That’s way too personal. Lena’s thoughts should be her own. I had to go in to save her life, but I’m not spilling the details. If she wants to tell you, she can.”

Alex frowned. “Was it…?”

“It wasn’t bad. That much, I’ll say. Lena was ruling the world and we were all helping her. Everyone was happy." Lena had definitely never made any secret of that particular desire. "That’s the end of it.”

Kara was still trying to process it herself. Seeing everything she had ever wanted, even knowing it had been an illusion…it made returning to reality a difficult adjustment. Add to that the near-death experience and how close she had come to losing her girlfriend and Supergirl just wanted to go and huddle underneath her blankets for a few hours.

A gasp garnered the room’s attention. Lena had bolted upright and was quickly turning her head to look across the room. “How much of that was a dream?”

“None of it, unfortunately,” Sam said. “It’s good to have you back, boss. But I think these two deserve a little time alone together, wouldn’t you agree? Alex, Winn, let’s go hang out in my apartment. I have some more ice there. Good with you, Ms. Luthor?”

Lena blinked rapidly. “Ah…yes. Thank you, Sam. And you too, Winn. I saw you stand in between Jess and Reign. That must have taken some willpower. Jess…gods, I need to give her a raise.”

Alex’s mouth opened to interject, probably to say ‘I fought Reign to save your sorry ass,’ but the ex-officer apparently thought better of it. Lena had no way of knowing that Alex had been there, Kara realized. Of course, that probably wouldn’t stop Alex from telling her about it later.

It was only when the elevator door closed and Sam, Alex, and Winn vanished from view that Kara realized how hard her heart was racing. An illusion created by an alien parasite wasn’t exactly the ideal place for a couple to exchange their first ‘I love you’s’.

Supergirl had utterly invaded Lena’s privacy. It had been necessary, yes, but still. The CEO had always preferred to keep some small part of herself hidden from view. Now that was gone. Kara knew Lena’s heart’s desire, and she knew that it revolved around her.

“Kara,” Lena’s voice cracked. The poised façade had already crumbled away. “We need to talk. But…hold me first…please?”

All too happy to fulfill that request, Kara sat down on the couch and enveloped her girlfriend in the most encompassing hug she could muster. “Are you okay?” the hero whispered.

“…No,” Lena managed. “But you’re alive and I’m with you. So I’ll get better. As long as you’re here.” There was an undercurrent of fear in the supervillain’s voice, as if she was afraid that the revelations of the Black Mercy were going to scare Kara away.

Kara placed a light kiss on Lena’s forehead, smoothly running her fingers over the CEO’s arms. “I’m here and I’m not going anywhere,” she said. “I promise.”

Chapter End Notes

I wonder if some of you will recognize the TQM homage in here. :)

Drastic Measures

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Holding Lena’s hand gently in her fingers, Kara placed a light kiss on the CEO’s knuckles. The supervillain wasn’t crying, but Kara knew that was only the case due to a remarkable amount of self-control.

“Let it out, Lena. I’ve seen footage of Black Mercy victims before. Bottling it up isn’t going to help you,” Kara said firmly. “There’s no shame in feeling upset.”

Lena laughed bitterly. “What are you, a counselor? No. Just my counselor, I suppose. Always there for me. Just not in the way I want.”

Kara maneuvered herself on the couch so that she could look into Lena’s face. “What are you talking about? I’m dating you and I’m not going anywhere! What else could you ask for?”

“Ask for? Kara, I’m not asking for anything. If you’re with me, it should only be because you want to be. But now you know what I want. Us. Together. You figured it out, of course, that’s why you stabbed yourself. I might be your girlfriend, but you’re the center of my world,” Lena replied, her face turning bright red. “I’m so in love with you it’s embarrassing.”

“Lena-”

“This is a mistake. We are a mistake,” the supervillain said, tears brimming in your eyes. “Ever since we got close all I’ve brought you is pain. I made you a target. Maggie Sawyer is dead, you lost your secret identity, Metallo, the red kryptonite…it was all because you were close to me. Yes, you were a hero before, but you weren’t in real danger. Not like this.”

Kara shook her head emphatically. “Lena, none of that was your fault! Maybe you could have noticed the Red K sooner, but you didn’t plant it. That was Cadmus!”

“Lillian made you a priority because we were becoming friends. I should have known this would happen. The day you interviewed me should have been the last time we spoke until I took over the world. But you had to be just so warm and accepting and Kara that I couldn’t stay away. I didn’t think about the consequences until it was too late.”

“Neither did I!” Kara protested. “It wasn’t your fault!”

Lena ignored her. “I tried not to let myself believe it. When you came to me the night Maggie Sawyer died I told myself you didn’t trust me. Then you came into my office handing me Kryptonite and I was a goner. When you showed up the next day at my apartment with flowers you paid for using your dinner budget…you had me without even trying. I was selfish and couldn’t let you go. Look at the results.”

Yes, attacks against Supergirl had ramped up ever since Lena had come into her life, but none of the blame fell on the CEO. Classic Lena. Obsessed with control, thinks everything she doesn’t stop is her fault to begin with.

“Maybe you did make me more of a target,” Kara admitted. “But you couldn’t have known that. Even your big brain can’t think of everything. All you wanted was a friend. You can’t blame yourself from wanting to be human, Lena!”

The supervillain sighed. “It doesn’t matter. It’s too late now. I don’t have the strength to push you away, and it wouldn’t help in this case anyway. Everyone already knows what you mean to me.”

“Just stop it, Lena!” Kara jumped to her feet. “You don’t run the world yet, and you’ll never be able to control everything. You’re not responsible for everything that goes wrong. Even the smartest woman in the world is entitled to make a few mistakes. No, not even mistakes! You can’t expect yourself to predict everything that every single person might try to do!”

In an instant, the CEO had gotten to her feet as well. Then Lena was kissing her fiercely, and all Kara could focus on was the feeling of her girlfriend’s lips against her own. They fell back onto the couch, the hero wrapping her arms around the villain’s shoulders.

When they finally came up for air, it was Lena who spoke first. “That’s exactly what I’m talking about. You’re so nice that it’s addictive. You sucked me in and now you have me forever.”

Kara blushed. “Well, I wouldn’t go that far…”

“You saw what I want. My world isn’t complete unless you’re right there with me, Kara. I think about us all the time. I want you to be my wife. I want you at my side every second of every day. One of my fantasies is us having a routine where you kneel when you come into my office before we have sex on my desk. The only way I’ll ever really be happy is if we get married, have kids, and grow old together.”

Kara hadn’t had the same detailed fantasies Lena had had. Her mind lived more in the present. But the world she had just been in, with the two of them as close as could be, had been perfect. Supergirl might not have had her entire future planned out, but she couldn’t see herself with anyone except the  brilliant, generous, driven woman now in her arms. Being with anyone else, or with no one at all, just seemed…empty in comparison.

No, not empty. Miserable.

“I love you, Lena. I thought I made that clear.”

Her girlfriend frowned. “I’m not holding you to what you said in order to get me out of there. God, I’m so mad at you for killing yourself to save me and I can’t even yell at you for it because I know you would just do the same thing all over again.”

“Yes, I would.” Kara leaned forward, staring into her girlfriend’s eyes. “And I love you, Lena Luthor. I love how you spend every waking moment thinking of ways to protect the world, even if I don’t agree with all your methods. I love noticing the spark that lights up your eyes when you get a new idea for some diabolical invention. Rao, I even love the smirk that shows up on your face when you’ve proven how smart you are for the millionth time.”

The hero was rambling now, but she didn’t want to stop. “I love it so much when you dote on me, and not just with the money even though the way you wave your influence and finances around is really sexy and makes me want to call myself a sugar baby and kiss you. Everything you’ve given me has had such thought put into it that I honestly can’t decide what touched me the most.”

Lena shook her head, as if she couldn’t believe what she was hearing. “You can’t love me, Kara. Not like that.”

“And why not?” Supergirl challenged. 

The villain’s fists were tightly balled up. “Because you’re better than me. Yes, I do a lot of good for a lot of people, but not like you. I have to actively reign in my darker impulses and compel myself to make the world a better place. For you, it’s instinctive. You don’t have to remind yourself to do good things or ignore your baser instincts to do what’s right. At your core, you’re good. It comes as easy to you as breathing.”

Kara let a moment of silence pass. “Then why do you think that you’re right about taking over the world and I’m wrong?”

“Because people like you aren’t the norm, Kara. Your way of thinking is wonderful and commendable, but it will also get people killed. Someone has to be in charge who’s willing to do the wrong thing in order to serve the greater good. I have to be willing to do the things your heart would never let you do.”

Supergirl wasn’t sure whether she was being praised or insulted. “Like what?”

“My plans put lives at risk, even if I don’t target innocents,” Lena explained. “I do that because I’m trying to maximize the chances of keeping as many people alive as possible. You would never do that. You might be willing to accept me doing that, but you couldn’t make those decisions yourself. You would always keep trying to find a perfect way forward. That makes you a better person than me…and it makes me more suited for command.”

“I-”

“Imagine you’re human,” Lena said. “No powers. You have a gun on you. There’s a person in front of you threatening to blow up a hospital, and he’s got the detonator in his hands. He doesn’t notice you yet. Do you shoot? Only a headshot will make sure he doesn’t hit the button.”

Kara’s fingers twitched nervously. “If I had to, maybe. But I’d try to talk him down first. I don’t know the full story yet. Maybe he’s insane, or someone’s threatening him.”

“I know. You might be right. But there’s a good chance that if he sees you he’ll push the button immediately. Supergirl would be brave enough to try and save everyone. I would just pull the trigger. I’m cold enough to do that. I wouldn’t sleep easily for weeks, but I would do it. Take something like that on a larger scale. If I pulled the metaphorical trigger, could you honestly stand by me?”

Could she? Kara would definitely be angry if Lena killed someone in any situation other than immediate self-defense. But if it was to save innocents?

“I wouldn’t abandon you, because I know your heart would have been in the right place. Who’s to say your way of thinking isn’t more moral than mine? There’s no objective rule for what qualifies as ‘good’,” the hero noted.

Lena’s eyes suddenly looked tired. Frowning, she laid her head against the hero’s chest. “Ethical dilemmas aside, I know you’re better than me. I…I’ve never told you about what happened to my mother, did I?”

“Your real mother?” Kara shook her head, calmly running her fingers through her girlfriend’s hair. “I know she died when you were four. That’s all.”

“She drowned. We went out to the lake to go for a swim. She went out into the water first…then she disappeared. I just froze. It wasn’t until some people found me an hour later that I reacted. Then I watched as her body was fished out of the water.”

Kara had never seen the CEO so vulnerable. She couldn’t tell if Lena was crying, but her voice was as small and terrified as the hero had ever heard it. Tears began to drip down Kara’s own face as she pictured the event, but she knew she had to let her girlfriend finish.

“I didn’t do anything. When I got shipped to the Luthors I knew it was my fault. No, maybe I wasn’t as bad as them but I deserved the life they gave me. It was a more than fair punishment.”

“You were four, Lena,” Kara whispered, still stroking the long dark hair in front of her.

The supervillain let out a strangled cough. “I could have yelled for help. That’s what a good person would have done. That’s what you would have done. Instead I just watched her die. I had the power to save her and I did nothing.”

And then you vowed to never let someone die again when you had the power to save them. And when you realized you had the power to achieve world domination, you knew what you had to do.

“You were a child and you were scared when the person you loved most certainly vanished. That’s not your fault.”

“I’m not saying most people wouldn’t have done the same,” Lena replied, her voice regaining some its volume. “But you would have. Even at that age, your instinct would have been to save your mother.”

Would it have been? Kara could hardly remember her thought process from when she was four. Who’s to say she wouldn’t have frozen up just like Lena?

But she didn’t say that. Arguing with her girlfriend wouldn’t help at this stage. Instead, Kara leaned down to whisper into Lena’s ear. “You’re a good person, Lee. You know that, or else you wouldn’t think yourself worthy of ruling the world. If you really do trust my instincts so much, then listen to them. Because every fiber of my being tells me that you’re amazing.”

Lena scoffed lightly, but Kara could still feel her smile against her chest. “I didn’t say I trust all of your instincts. Anyone who knows you would agree you’re far too trusting.”

“Maybe everyone else is too cynical. And besides, you haven’t let me down yet. I didn’t trust you totally at first, remember? Not until I saw how great you were…misguided world domination plots aside.”

The brief burst of happiness seemed to deflate from the supervillain’s chest. “That’s what you think now. But I’m terrified, Kara. One day you’re going to see me for what I am and leave me. I won’t even blame you when it happens. I’m just going to enjoy you for as long as I can.”

The hero sighed. “What’s it going to take for you to believe that I’m not going to leave you?”

“Nothing springs to mind,” Lena replied.

Kara thought for several moments. An idea slowly occurred to her. By Earth’s standards, she was crazy. But Kara had grown up on Krypton, where matches were decided by the Matrix and the parties might never have met before. And she decided she didn’t really care what Earth would think.

“Lena, you could agree to marry me.”

The supervillain sat up instantly, her eyes staring wide at Kara. “What?”

“Agree to marry me. I know it’s what you want…and it’s the same thing that I want. Not yet, of course. Not until one of us convinces the other about the ‘world domination’ thing and Reign isn’t a threat any longer. When those things happen, promise to marry me.”

Lena sighed. “You don’t need to try and make me feel better. We’ve been dating for what, two weeks? I might be so emotionally dependent on you that I already know I want to spend the rest of my life with you, but-”

“I can’t imagine a life without you, Lena. When I stabbed myself with that Kryptonite, I wasn’t thinking about the good that Lena Luthor could do for the world, or the fact that Supergirl is sworn to protect life. I just couldn’t lose you.”

“And I appreciate that more than you will ever know,” Lena said warmly. “But that’s not the same thing as wanting to marry me.”

“No,” Kara agreed. “But wanting to believe that the illusion was real and loving every time you called me your wife is. Part of the reason I stabbed myself because I was afraid if I waited any longer I would convince myself that you were right and that the illusion was reality.”

The supervillain’s eyes fell to their interlocked hands. “I can’t ask you to do this…not just to make me feel better.

“Lena, I want to be your wife. I grew up on a world where some couples didn’t even meet before they were matched. This is an eternity of courtship by comparison. Normally, I would have been willing to wait, but that doesn’t mean I would like to. Seeing you like this doesn’t make me want to marry you…it just makes me brave enough to admit it.”

“Kara-“

“I saw your fantasy. You gave me everything I wanted. My planet…my mother. Even when you were being taken over by a Black Mercy you were still thinking of me. Even everyone else- Sam and Alex- you gave them the best life you could. If that isn’t an instinct to do good, I don’t know what is! How could I not love you after seeing all of that?”

“It wasn’t real,” Lena whispered.

“It’s what you wanted to be real,” Kara shot back. “I’m not agreeing to help you take over the world. Just because your plan worked out in a fantasy doesn’t mean it will happen like that in real life. But I got a glimpse inside your heart, Lena Luthor. It was a complete invasion of your privacy and something that should never have happened, yet I treasure it.”

Lena offered her a small, bemused smile. “You went in to save my life. I think the trespassing can be forgiven. And…I don’t mind that you saw. I’m not ashamed of loving you, Kara.”

“And I’m not ashamed to love you, Lena. Buy me an engagement ring and I’ll show it to the whole world. I’d buy you one if I could afford it without using your money but since I can’t, it looks like you’ll be the one who has to make the purchase.

A storm of emotions battled in the CEO’s eyes, as if the ingrained self-doubt was fighting desperately to keep the supervillain from agreeing to Kara’s offer. “I won’t hold you to that. I can’t.”

It looked like drastic measures were necessary. It wouldn’t be easy, but it was a sacrifice Supergirl was willing to make. Anything for Lena Luthor.

She placed a hand across her chest. “I, Kara Zor-El Danvers of Krypton and Earth, swear upon the memory and legacy of my family that I will not eat another potsticker until I am married to Lena Kieran Luthor.”

Lena gasped. “You…you mean it. You actually mean it! That means…that means we’re engaged!” she shouted, as if not quite able to believe it. Supergirl had never heard her girlfriend sound so happy.

Kara went bright red. “Well, I wouldn’t say that exactly, since we can’t set a date yet. More like engaged to be engaged. But you can call me your fiancé if you want. I rather like the sound of it.”

“Oh fuck the semantics.” Lena’s smiling, tear-stricken face met Kara’s in another intense kiss. And even though Supergirl knew that there might be hell to pay for this decision…and the potstickers, Rao the potsickers!...not one part of her regretted it.

Lena, I might never be able to show you how wonderful you are, but by Rao I swear I will spend the rest of my life trying.

Chapter End Notes

WARNING: Fluff Overload.

I thought they deserved some happiness together after everything they've been through. And I have to admit, this was cathartic to write.

Choices

“Engaged?”

Kara nodded nervously. “Well, more like engaged to be engaged, but yeah. Nothing will happen until things have calmed down and we’ve settled everything out.”

Alex’s face was impeccably neutral. “By ‘settling everything out’, you mean when either she’s ruling the world or you’ve managed to talk her out of it?”

“That’s about the size of it, yes.”

The hero couldn’t help but be agitated. Despite their many disagreements over Lena in recent months, there would always be a part of Kara that yearned for her big sister’s approval. That wasn’t to say that she would think about dropping their engagement plans if Alex demanded it, but Kara would be considerably happier going forward if she knew she at least had her sister’s reluctant support.

Several seconds of silence passed before Alex spoke. “You’re not just doing this because you feel bad about whatever you saw in there?”

Well, that was a fair question.

“No. But it did help me realize what I want,” Kara admitted. “Lena gave me the go ahead to tell you what the fantasy was. She and I were together. Married…that is. We were happy. She was so in love with me that stabbing myself broke her out of it-”

“You stabbed yourself?!” Now, Alex was angry.

Kara’s hand sheepishly rubbed the back of her neck. “It was the only way. I wasn’t leaving there without her. And it worked.”

The ex-officer took a deep, calming breath. “I know I’ve never been able to convince you to put yourself first, but did you think about what would happen if you died? The world needs Supergirl. I need my sister!”

“The world needs Lena too! Even if it didn’t…Supergirl doesn’t leave people she cares about behind. Neither does Kara Zor-El!”

Some of the emotion faded from Alex’s eyes. “I know. Sometimes I wish she would. I just…” her hands were shaking now. “You have to be more careful. Maybe you could have found another way. I know everything worked out this time, but next-”

“Next time I won’t be alone. The Black Mercy only works on any individual once. This won’t happen again.”

Alex sighed. “Something will happen. Something always happens. That’s the way your world works. Even with the Harun-el, I can’t protect you.”

With the look of fear in her sister’s eyes, Kara was really starting to regret letting slip her act of near suicide. Trying to change the subject, she spoke again. “So? Isn’t this the part where you tell me how marrying Lena is a horrible idea?”

“I know how things worked on Krypton,” Alex replied. “Quick marriages are normal to you. If you’re really sure you love her-”

“I am!” Kara affirmed. “She wants so much to make the world a better place…even if we don’t agree on how to do that. She’s kind and pretty and always looks out for me. Did you know, in her fantasy Krypton was still alive. So was Clark. She wanted me to be happy. It was such a perfect world for me I almost fell for the illusion…I wanted to. And it wasn’t just me. Her fantasy was a happy life for everyone. Even you,” the hero noted wryly.

Alex frowned, shock plain in her eyes. “I’m sorry you had to let them go again,” she whispered.

“Me too. But you can’t blame Lena for that,” Kara said firmly.

Her sister nodded. “No, I can’t. And it’s good to have confirmation that she wants what’s best for you. But just because things worked out between you in her fantasy doesn’t mean that will happen in the real world. It was a fantasy, after all. In real life you could get tired of each other…feelings could fade. You know that, right?”

Kara couldn’t see herself not being in love with Lena. Arguing, even fighting? Yes, absolutely. But no longer wanting to be with the CEO? Never.

“That won’t happen,” Supergirl declared.

Alex stared at her for several moments, her eyes unreadable. “Well, I can’t say I share your confidence, but it’s your decision to make. If you want to be engaged with her, then go for it.”

The hero placed her hands on her hips, fuming with indignation. “Is it too much to ask that you accept one of my decisions for just once in your life?” she demanded. “Lena and I love each other and if you don’t like that then-” Kara froze. “Wait…did you just say you were fine with it?” she asked in a small voice.

“Yeah,” Alex replied simply.”

Kara’s arms flapped inelegantly through the air. “But you’ve never liked her! You think she’s ‘an arrogant B-word’! I…I’m not still in the Black Mercy, am I?”

“Maybe I don’t like her. But that doesn’t matter. You’ve found someone who makes you happy, has been proven to love you back, and is capable of protecting you. That’s all I could ask for.”

Arms still gesticulating wildly, Kara stared at her sister. “But you don’t trust her!”

Alex shrugged. “That was before she saved your life about a dozen times and had a fantasy of marrying you. I think we can agree she has your best interests at heart. And I do owe her the benefit of the doubt after…well, you remember.”

The gesticulating arms now coalesced in a hug around the ex-officer. “Thanks, sis!” It was a small point in the grand scheme of things, but knowing that this is one fight she wouldn’t have to battle felt like having a two ton weight lifted off her chest.

Returning the hug, the ex-officer placed a comforting hand on Kara’s back. “So I guess congratulations are in order. And also some consolation. I can’t imagine James and Lucy will be happy about this and I don’t envy you having to tell them.”

Kara winced, pulling back to look Alex in the eyes. “Can’t you do it for me?” she asked, biting her lip.

“Sorry, Supergirl, but I’ve become immune to your pout. I’ll be there with you, but you have to do the talking.”

\

Alex stepped out of the elevator and into Lena’s apartment.

The CEO was sitting at her kitchen table, hunched over her laptop and surrounded by a sea of papers. Even less than twelve hours after being brought to within an inch of her life, she was already back to work.

“I have to admit your construction crews work fast,” Alex nodded at the repairs. She released a sigh. “I got your text; you wanted to see me?”

Lena shook her head. “Actually, I was wondering why you wanted to see me.”

The ex-officer frowned. “Did Kara tell you that? I don’t have anything to say to you about the engagement, other than you better treat her well if you don’t want me to destroy your office. But otherwise I’m fine with it.”

“I haven’t spoken to Kara since she went to India to help with the earthquake. And I’d appreciate if you stopped dodging the issue. You were the one who found me with the Black Mercy,” Lena said, tapping her finger on the granite impatiently. “This morning, you stole Kara’s keycard to get up here. Why?”

Alex would have rather died a thousand deaths than say what she was about to say. But she would sacrifice anything for her sister, including her pride. There wasn’t any point in drawing it out further.

“I want in.”

The supervillain tilted her head quizzically. “In?” she repeated. “In on what?”

Oh god, please kill me. “On L-Corp. Your plans. Whatever you want to call it. I’m one of the few people injected with Harun-el. That makes me useful. I’m offering to work for you.”

And there it was, the inevitable sheen of arrogance in Lena’s eyes. There was none of the surprise, however, that Alex had been expecting. “Oh? I was under the impression that you disagreed with my efforts for world domination. You tried to kill me, if I recall-”

“I tried to kill you because I thought you were a threat to Kara!” Alex shot back. “I couldn’t think of another way to stop you. I thought that any world run by a Luthor was one in which a Super couldn’t survive.”

Lena nodded. “And now?”

The ex-officer resisted the urge to drop her gaze. “Now I think that a world run by you might be necessary for Supergirl to survive. Every major government has been after her for years…recent events have just made them bolder about it. Her identity would have been revealed eventually; the only reason Eliza and I haven’t been carted off by the government is because of whatever hold you have on the President.” She took a breath. “You’ve stepped up for Kara time and again, even when it would have been easier for you to cut her loose.”

“You don’t think I’m trying to manipulate her to get her on my side?”

“I know you are. But you love her and want what’s best for her; I can’t say the same for any of the governments out there. If I had lingering doubts about your feelings, the Black Mercy erased them. There’s no way you could have planned that,” Alex noted.

Lena resisted a noticeable urge to chuckle. “I understand, but after everything that’s happened I can’t help but be skeptical. You’ve really done a complete one-eighty on all of this? One minute I’m a threat to world peace and the next I’m Earth’s only hope?”

“The other day, I was thinking about why I didn’t want you to control the world, and I suddenly realized…all of my reasons are gone. You don’t want to hurt Kara, and you’re at least better than the people in power right now,” Alex admitted. “Yeah, it could all blow up in your face and make everything worse, but we’re screwed anyway. Sam’s given me the details about what’s happening out there.” She pointed out the window, up at the stars. “I’ve spoken with several aliens to confirm what she’s saying. We’re going to be invaded soon. If we don’t take a chance on you, we’re already screwed. Why else would Reign want you dead so badly?”

“Maybe she’s just afraid of the competition,” Lena replied with a smirk.

Alex glared at the CEO. The less time she had to look at the other woman’s self-satisfied face, the better. “Don’t play Devil’s Advocate against yourself; I’m not in the mood. You got me. I was wrong and you were right. Maybe Kara has a point, and your approach could so with some changes, but that’s not my concern. I’m a pragmatist and I’m looking for my best option, not a perfect one.”

“Very well.” Lena’s hand smoothly retrieved a small packet of papers within the pile and slid them to Alex. “There’s your contract. Read it and tell me if you have any questions.”

What?  

Alex’s eyes widened. “You keep random employment contracts around just on the off chance someone might come in looking for a job?”

“No. I’ve been keeping your specific contract around ever since I finished writing it up a few hours ago. I knew why you wanted to see me, Alex.” The smirk was back. “Or, at least, I had a good guess. I overheard you telling Kara you would support her even if she decided to join me, and I know you’ve been talking to Sam about what’s going on in the universe. Even the way you look at me has been different lately. Dislike, yes, but there’s no fear in your eyes now…no worrying about what I might do. Add that all together with the fact that your priority is Kara’s safety and the way governments have been going after her, and it was a fairly simple deduction.”

There was really nothing to say to that, so Alex deflected. “You’re…not worried I’m going to try and bring you down from the inside? Leak things to the press and all that.”

Now, Lena did laugh. “You’re a smart woman Alex, and I know that. Even an idiot could see that weakening my position only makes Kara more vulnerable.”

She’s even more annoying when she’s right.

The ex-officer stared at the contract, unable to bring her vision to a focus. “So…what is it that you want me to do?”

The mirth faded from Lena’s face. “While I was under the Black Mercy, some of my more secure networks were attacked. I don’t know what was stolen, if anything, but it shows my operation is vulnerable. So, for now, you’re Sam’s chief of security and troubleshooter. Keep her safe and handle things for her that a regular human couldn’t. Anything else is up to her.”

Alex couldn’t help the small smile that broke out on her face. Either Lena didn’t think it was worth pointing out, or she didn’t notice it.

“Sure, but I wouldn’t be able to protect her from everything. If Reign goes after her, I won’t be able to stop her,” Alex pointed out.

The CEO nodded. “But you might be able to buy her enough time to call in reinforcements. Besides, it’s not Reign I’m worried about. Her focus seems to be primarily on me, not my staff. Hopefully it stays that way. There’s a lot of other people out there, however, who would be all too happy to target my support network.”

The ex-officer frowned. That did make sense. “Fine, but I have two conditions.”

Lena blinked. “And those are?”

“One, I’m not helping you try and convince Kara to join you. Join us, I suppose.” Wow, this is going to be an adjustment. “I’m telling her my decision…better to ask forgiveness than permission…but I’m not going to tell her to follow me. It’s entirely up to her.”

“Understood.”

Alex frowned. “Second, I’m not calling you Ms. Luthor. Ever. You don’t like it, don’t have me around for important meetings.”

“Well, you did save my life today, so I suppose that’s a fair trade,” Lena agreed.

The ex-officer frowned. “Just to clarify, I was fighting to save Kara. Not you. I thought that Reign would kill my sister if she had the chance.”

“I know that. But if you hadn’t found me in the first place, it might have been too late. And if you hadn’t stalled her, Reign would have pulled Kara out before she could save me. So I owe you,” Lena affirmed. “Unfortunately.”

Alex couldn’t resist a thoughtful smirk. “Is that the main reason why you aren’t gloating right now?”

“Pretty much,” Lena agreed. “But I’m sure my gratitude will wear off soon enough and then I can ask you to repeat ‘I was wrong, you were right, and thanks for giving me a job even after the attempted murder’ every time I see you.”

It’s for Kara. It’s for Kara, Alex reminded herself. And as painful as this has been…it could have been worse.

The CEO stood up. “Here. Almost forgot.” She fished a keycard out of her pocket, holding it out to Alex. “A key to your complementary apartment. You’re on Sam’s floor; I’ll sleep easier if I know you’re in hearing range of her apartment.”

“I have an apartment.” 

Lena narrowed her eyes. “You’re saying you’re willing to bend your pride enough to work for me, but you won’t take a nice apartment out of the bargain? One that lets you stay close to your new boss? I thought you were a pragmatist?”

Well, I suppose staying closer to Sam couldn’t hurt…

“You did what?!”

Kara’s ears had to be broken. That was the only explanation for the fact that Alex Danvers had just told her that she was going to work for Lena Luthor and help her take over the world. Alex Danvers hated Lena Luthor and thought her plans were insane. Alex Danvers considered Lena Luthor supremely arrogant and a massive threat to global stability.

“I told Lena I would work for her and help her achieve world domination,” Alex repeated in a deadpan voice.

The superhero frowned. “Looks like my hearing is still broken. Either that, or my sister has been replaced by a clone. Because I know my sister really doesn’t like Lena and would never help her try to overthrow global governments.”

“And when was the last time I said that?” the ex-officer questioned. “Before Lena took down Cadmus and the DEO, or before those global governments proved they would never tolerate you no matter what?”

Kara realized her mouth was gaped open. Forcing it closed, she stared into her sister’s eyes. “None of that changes the fact that her plans are going to backfire horribly, or that they cross the line in a dozen ways.”

“Like what?” Alex demanded. “Locking up dangerous people? What the hell does she do that a major government doesn’t? Besides actually fighting for alien rights, that is.”

“I-”

“We’ve assumed her plans will backfire, but where is the evidence of that?” Alex continued fiercely. “So far they’ve pretty much gone exactly as she said. Kaznia-”

Kara slammed her palm into the dresser, sprouting cracks in the wood. “People are dead in Kaznia! Militants have launched suicide attacks on her bases!” the hero retorted, vividly remembering the recent news reports. “Didn’t you know that?”

“Of course I do. And I also know that the death rate throughout the country overall is down dramatically. Lena never promised that everything would be perfect if her plans go into effect, just that things would be better.”

The absurdity of the moment was so great that the hero had to resist the urge to laugh. “This is a trick, right? You’re working with Lois or something to gain inside info so you can bring her down later.”

“Yeah, I want to bring her down,” Alex drawled. “That way, the next time my sister is in trouble, her best backup will be in prison. That’s exactly that I want.”

Kara forced herself to calm down. The realization that this wasn’t a joke was slowly sinking in. If Alex joined Lena…who was left on her side?

“And you suddenly decided to completely change your opinion…when, exactly?” the hero questioned through gritted teeth.

A flicker of annoyance passed through Alex’s eyes. “It wasn’t sudden. When was the last time I said Lena’s plans were a bad idea? I’ve been considering it for a while. I wasn’t going to say something until I was sure; telling her she was right and I was wrong wasn’t exactly a pleasant experience.”

“If this is about Sam-”

Now, her sister was annoyed. “Sam showed me the evidence. Earth is going to be invaded, and a few powerful individuals aren’t going to be enough to protect us. Lena couldn’t beat Reign by herself. And me…” the ex-officer failed to completely suppress a shudder. “The only reason she didn’t snap my neck is because she didn’t want to.”

“We can beat Reign!”

Alex nodded. “Yeah, probably. Eventually. But an alien fleet? No. It’s inevitable. If humanity isn’t united, we’re toast. We have to take a chance.”

Kara’s shoulders slumped. “You’re really okay with what she’s doing? The mind control, the prisons, the thefts… I can’t believe you’d agree with that.”

“Why?” Alex’s eyes narrowed. “You don’t seem too upset with Lena when she does it; when is the wedding, by the way? And yeah, I’m fine with punishing the guilty to save the planet.”

The irony was laughable. Kara had always hoped that Alex would look past her initial prejudice and see Lena for the good person that she was. Now Alex had, and this was the result.

It wasn’t the nature of the plans that Alex had been opposed to. It was that she thought Lena was a danger to me, and the fact that Alex simply didn’t like her. Mitigate that dislike and take away the perceived danger to me, and Alex joins right up.

In hindsight, maybe Kara should have seen this coming. Alex had been less hostile to Lena lately, and her sister was no stranger to the idea that the ends could justify the means.

“Well, she must be happy,” Kara noted sourly. “You were a big player in her organization in the Mercy’s illusion. I thought that was the least likely thing about it. Shows what I know.”

“I’m not going to try and convince you to side with us,” Alex said. “You can make your own choices. It might be the case that you’re too good a person to cross some lines, and we’re worse for doing it. But maybe people like you need people like us to survive.”

Kara crossed her arms. “I know Earth isn’t safe,” she said. “But I’m going to protect it on my terms or die trying. I won’t let fear compromise who I am.”

“Yeah, I know,” Alex agreed. “That’s why I’m doing this.”

Supergirl threw up her arms. “It makes sense now. After my identity was revealed, you told me you would support me if I decided to join Lena. I should have thought about that more. Why else would you have said that unless you were going to serve her yourself?”

“I serve Earth, Kara. And you. If working for Lena is the best way to do that, then I can accept that. Even if it means you hate me.”

Kara sighed. “I could never hate you. You’re right; if I can love Lena despite her plans then I can accept you joining in. But I don’t like it.”

“I’m not asking you to,” Alex said. “And look at it this way: everyone else is going to be so mad at me for going to work for Lena that they won’t have time to be upset with you for agreeing to marry her.”

The Dark Side

“You wanted to see me, Ms. Luthor?”

“Yes, Jess, please sit down.” Her boss indicated the chair in front of her desk, which Jess dutifully sat in. “I assume everything is prepared for the press conference later today?”

The secretary nodded. “I’ve received confirmation that everything is in place. Ms. Sakai is ready to counter the backlash should it arise. Many alien employees have volunteered to give statements on your behalf.”

Lena nodded, though Jess could see the twinge of worry in her eyes. Despite their preparations, this announcement was certain to arouse suspicion, fear, and even hatred from the alien community. Relying on paid employees to give statements could only do so much to staunch the bleeding.

“That’s good,” the CEO said, moving past the issue. “But that’s not the real reason I asked you here. I wanted to talk about you. Or, more specifically, your work for me.”

The secretary frowned nervously. “Have I done something wrong?”

“No,” Lena said firmly. “The problem is that you’re still manning the front desk and taking my calls when you’re qualified for far more difficult work. I’m not trying to demean the excellent job you’ve done here, but there are less qualified people who could handle it while you move into a management position.”

Jess sighed and shook her head. “I’m comfortable where I am, Ms. Luthor. Honestly.”

“You have a son to take care of,” Lena reminded her. “This time next year you could be earning triple your salary. I have little doubt you’d end up a department head soon after that. As much as I would love to increase your current salary to that level, I can’t do that without being unfair to the other employees. Even L-Corp can’t afford to pay every office worker with an executive’s salary. Not yet, anyway.”

“I’m earning more than enough, Ms. Luthor. Luke and I have everything we need. I can’t ask more more…especially not after you paid for my custody hearings,” Jess said earnestly. Part of her still couldn’t believe that her boss had done that. They were friendly, certainly, but far from close friends. Lena had long since chosen to isolate herself into her work, until Kara Danvers arrived and broke down her walls in less than a week.

The supervillain shook her head. “For now. But this was never meant to be a permanent position. You can’t sacrifice your future just to be my secretary forever. It’s a hard job, yes, but there are plenty of people who would be happy to do it.”

“Do you really want me gone?” Jess asked quietly.

Lena almost looked offended. “Of course not! You’ve never let me down. But at this point I’m just taking advantage of you by keeping you in a low position. And I hate to see talent go to waste.”

“I appreciate your concerns, Ms. Luthor. If there’s nothing else, I’ll let you prepare for the press conference.” Jess moved to get up.

“Stop,” Lena ordered firmly. “I’m forcing you into a promotion unless you can convince me otherwise. I can’t imagine you enjoy being a secretary so much that you’d forgo a six-figure salary hike.”

A higher salary would be nice. It would mean a larger apartment and a guaranteed future for her son. Jess knew that if she allowed herself to rise through the ranks, a seven-figure salary eventually awaited her.

Finally, Jess decided to come clean. “I don’t trust anyone else to do the job,” she said simply.

Her boss frowned. “You take phone calls, organize meetings, and help plan my schedule. We both know there are other people who could do that work. Maybe not as well as you, but they would manage.”

Jess hadn’t meant to sound conceited. “That’s not what I was talking about. I said that I don’t trust anyone else to do the job. I know there are people who could do the work as well as me…maybe even better. But I don’t know them. Anyone who takes the job could be a mole. You don’t need the best employee to do my job, but you need someone absolutely loyal.”

A flicker of understanding shone in Lena’s eyes. “You’ve been offered bribes to rat on me, haven’t you?”

“Every week,” Jess answered. “Not from anyone too sinister, just other companies or governments that want to see you taken down a peg, or just want some increased access. I don’t know if your next secretary would stay loyal to you, but I know that I will. That’s why I’m staying. I believe in what you’re doing, and I won’t let that be compromised by having a rat control your calls and your access.”

A moment of silence passed before Lena spoke again. “I see your point. And no one could doubt your loyalty, not since you stood between me and Reign’s heat vision.”

Jess shuddered as terrifying memories broke to the surface. “I didn’t know you knew about that.”

“I talked to Kara’s friend Winn, yesterday. He gave me some of the details about what happened. He was rather impressed with you, I think.”

The secretary offered her boss a small, puzzled smile. “He called you?”

“I called him,” Lena clarified. “I wanted the most neutral person I could get to tell me the truth of how the rest of Kara’s friends were reacting to recent developments.”

Jess nodded, noting her boss’s stony expression and accepting the unspoken request not to probe further.

“Christmas is coming up,” Lena said. “End of the year bonuses are private, and I don’t think anyone would react too strongly to a larger bonus anyway given that my secretary helped save my life a few days ago. Even if some stock options were included.”

Jess could have declined and said such a gesture wasn’t necessary. But she wouldn’t have been able to do so honestly, not when she had the realities of childcare to consider. “Thanks, Ms. Luthor.”

“If we’re going to make this a permanent position, perhaps we should consider getting you some additional protection. You stick around my office for too long, and some people might start considering you one of my close associates.”

The secretary frowned. “I know that, but I’m not a fan of having a security team follow me around all day.” Jess would do it, if it would keep Luke safe, but she didn’t think his childhood would benefit from being under the constant gaze of security professionals.

“That’s not what I’m talking about,” Lena replied. “The Harun-El. I want to test you for compatibility and inject you with a dose.”

Jess’s mouth gaped open. She knew how difficult the substance was to make, in spite of L-Corp’s best efforts. Only Lena, L-Corp’s top operatives, and Supergirl’s closest friends had received the substance.

“I…I never thought about that before,” the secretary admitted. “What does a compatibility test have to do with it?”

Lena pursed her lips. “Harun-El binds to human DNA. If the protein structure of that DNA is compatible, there’s no danger. If not, the binding process can induce severe brain trauma and, eventually, death. Most people are compatible, but some aren’t. Winn was one.”

The secretary found herself suppressing a small wince. That couldn’t have been a pleasant revelation.

“Protein structure?” Jess questioned.

Her boss nodded. “If there isn’t sufficient room for the Harun-El to bind on the DNA helix, the process will cause the host’s DNA to break down. Even among people who are compatible, there’s different levels of tolerance. Take too much and you will die. That’s why no one with Harun-El has full Kryptonian abilities. No one has enough room in their DNA structure for that much Harun-El to bind safely.”

“But if I take the test, the process will be one hundred percent safe?” Jess questioned.

“Yes; the test can isolate exactly how much Harun-El the subject can safely be injected with. No downsides have been observed in any of those who have received it.”

“Not yet,” Jess found herself noting. “But if you’re sure it’s safe-”

The office phone began to ring. Glancing apologetically at Jess, the CEO picked it up.

“Hello? What? Yes, I suppose I have a few minutes. Send her to my office.”

\

Of all the people Jess had been expecting, Lois Lane was not one of them.

The secretary barely had time to return to her desk before Lois had arrived. The reporter politely greeted Jess before stepping into Lena’s office and closing the door behind her, leaving Jess to guess at what was discussed. This, of course, was a typical feature of her job, but the nature of Lois’s arrival definitely had her curious.

That curiosity was not abated when Lois left Lena’s office several minutes later and turned to Jess. “Lena tells me you’re considering a Harun-El treatment?”

Jess nodded, knowing that Lois was one of those who had injected the substance. “I am. I’m just worried that it could make me more of a target. I have a son to worry about.”

The reporter shrugged. “Then don’t tell anyone. Let it be a nasty surprise if anyone ever tries to ambush you.” Jess’s vision lost track of the other woman as Lois stepped behind her chair and placed a hand on her shoulder. “At the end of the day, it’s your decision, but I don’t think your boss would have offered if she thought it would place you in more danger.”

Huh? Since when is Lois Lane a fan of Lena Luthor? More than ever, Jess wanted to know what had just been discussed in the CEO’s office, but it wasn’t her place to ask.

The secretary spun around in her chair, using her foot to slide her purse off to the side. “Do you feel normal after taking it?” she questioned.

A wistful look appeared on Lois’s face. “I haven’t felt normal since the day I met Clark. Smallville actually thought he could hide his secret from me, but it took me about three minutes to realize I was sharing a workspace with the city’s new Superhero. Idiot,” she chuckled fondly.

Jess’s gaze darted back to Lena’s office. A protective instinct settled in her voice. “Please don’t tell me you blame Ms. Luthor for-”

“I don’t. Your boss wouldn’t be alive if I did.” Lois crossed her arms. “Killing Clark lost Lex his life. Watching his sister using his company to support alien refugees and dating Supergirl…I couldn’t think of a better way to spit on his grave.”

Jess could hear the venom in her words. She hadn’t thought she would ever meet someone who hated Lex more than Lena did, but Lois had just proved her wrong.

“Good luck today,” Lois went on to say. “After this press conference, everyone in this building is going to need it. Now if you’ll excuse me, I have an appointment with Mr. Colville.”

The VP of Finance? Jess nearly started with surprise. Why would Lois Lane need a meeting with Thomas Colville? Why would she want an interview with an L-Corp executive when she could get one with Lena herself?

Jess was curious, but she resisted the urge to react. It wasn’t her department, and she had more than enough to worry about at the moment.

“Thanks,” Alex said.

Sitting behind her desk, Sam raised an eyebrow. “Thanks? For what? I haven’t even given you a paycheck yet,” she pointed out playfully.

“For not rubbing it in,” Alex answered. She’d received so much grief from James and Lucy that Lois’s silence on the matter had only been the barest compensation. “I’ve had enough to deal with this week.”

The CFO stood up. “I’m well aware of that,” she said, walking over to Alex. “It takes strength to admit you’ve changed your opinion, especially when you know some people are going to be smug about it. Oh, Ms. Luthor’s great, but we both know she’ll never let you forget it.” Sam’s voice was sympathetic. “The fact that you decided to be an evil minion with me anyway…”

Alex groaned. “I’m not even an evil minion. You’re an evil minion. I am an evil minion’s evil minion. Not exactly a resume builder.”

Sam broke out into laughter. “And they say security personnel have to be all doom and gloom,” the CFO replied, still chuckling. She placed a warm hand on Alex’s arm. “For what it’s worth, I’m glad to have you here.”

The security officer could do little more than mumble her thanks as warmth spread into her cheeks. There was a warm tingling in her arm that sprouted from Sam’s touch. Is that a side effect of the Harun-El?

Alex’s brain inwardly sighed at the thought. You’re pathetic, Danvers.

“Come on, sit down,” Sam said gently. “Ms. Luthor’s press conference is about to start and I’m honestly terrified at what the reaction was going to be.”

Alex didn’t blame her. Ever since she had been told what Lena was about to announce, the thought of the public’s response made her nervous. It was a part of Lena’s agenda that Alex was fully comfortable with, but only because she knew that the Luthor didn’t have nefarious intentions in mind. Had this announcement been made a year ago, Alex would have been the first to warn that Lex’s sister was about to continue his plans for genocide.

\

Lena was outside of L-Corp, standing on an erected stage and facing a crowd filled with reporters. And for a brief moment the entire gathering had been stunned into silence.

Then the journalists began frantically asking their questions. The CEO turned to one at random and spoke his name. “Mr. Collins?”

The man stood up. “Ms. Luthor, are you in the process of constructing a block on alien entry to the planet?”

Lena shook her head. “No. As I just stated, I am constructing the first stage of a defense grid that is designed to detect large-scale movement of extraplanetary forces. Alien refugees will not be affected. This warning system is designed for the sole purpose of warning us of potential invasion forces.”

Cries of “Ms. Luthor!” echoed throughout the audience. Lena pointed at a woman, who eagerly got to her feet. “Ms. Luthor, are you enacting your brother’s plan for a human-exclusive Earth?”

“Absolutely not,” Lena replied, her voice tinged with steel. “This warning system is designed to protect all humans and aliens who wish to live on Earth peacefully. It was the stories of many alien refugees now employed by L-Corp that inspired the creation of this system. Dozens of worlds have been lost to conquest and plunder. I intend to make sure Earth is not one of them.”

Another reporter jumped to his feet. “Ms. Luthor, couldn’t this system easily be repurposed to target and intercept alien refugees?”

Anger boiled within the CEO. It was her most ambitious project yet, possible only now with the vast amount of resources L-Corp had acquired. Eventually, the defense grid would evolve beyond the capability to warn and would be able to actually threaten invading alien fleets. The L-Shield was the most expensive human undertaking in history, and potentially the most vital. And all these drooling imbeciles wanted to know was whether Lena was intent on continuing a genocide?

“Perhaps,” Lena growled. “Just like all of the nuclear weapons stationed around the globe could be used to wipe out humanity in a matter of hours. We can’t allow ridiculous hypotheticals to stand in the way of progress.”

“Ms. Luthor, what do you say to the human supremacist groups praising your decision on Twitter right now?”

Lena grinned viciously. “Everyone has the right to their opinions, as long as they don’t commit violence, but I would gladly save a single alien refugee before I helped a dozen members of any of those groups.”

“Ms. Luthor, are you saying you are pro-alien? How can you claim that in light of this announcement?”

“I am pro-peaceful alien. Most beings coming to this planet want nothing more than a new life. If you’re a human who gets nervous about the alien situation, I understand. Aliens are new. They’re different. And humans have never been quick about adapting to change,” Lena said. “I can work with people who are uncomfortable about aliens; I think most of them will come around. But I will never stand beside those who are consumed by fear and hatred. They can join my brother on the ash heap of history.”

A flurry of questions. “Ms. Luthor, we all know who you are. You lie to us on a daily basis. Why should anyone trust you now?”

Lena nodded. “I have never sought to conceal who I am or what I do,” she said carefully. “Everyone knows what I want and what I stand for. This is no different. Several alien employees of L-Corp have volunteered to speak on behalf of the L-Shield. Many of them have worked on it.”

“Ms. Luthor, with all due respect, these aliens work for you. Why should we take the word of anyone on your payroll?”

The supervillain’s hands began to shake in frustration. Her earpiece was buzzing with the words of the head of her PR department, warning her that much of Twitter was declaring her to have been a bigot all along. She was about to hiss to the crowd that, “Well, I’m sorry, but so many of the aliens in this city work for me that good luck finding one who doesn’t,” when a hush fell over the crowd.

Lena had been so distracted she hadn’t even noticed Supergirl floating to the ground beside her.

“We all know Lena Luthor is a supervillain trying to take over the world,” Kara spoke to the crowd. “I don’t support that in any way. But that doesn’t change the fact that she’s a good person who means well. Lena has nothing against aliens; she’s nothing like her brother. If she says this system isn’t a threat to refugees, then I believe her.”

The mob of reporters stared at her. “But…Ms.- Supergirl,” the first to recover spoke. “How can we be sure of that? And how do we know she isn’t controlling your mind?”

Supergirl frowned. “If she was controlling my mind, I would be telling everyone that her taking over the world is a good thing.”

Another reporter spoke. “What makes you think that she isn’t anti-alien? You don’t have any proof of that. For all you know, she could be playing you. Her brother kept his true intentions hidden for years before he made his move.”

Lena had never seen such anger on Kara’s face. “Her brother? Lex never employed thousands of aliens or supported an Alien Amnesty Act. Judge her for being a villain, fine, but not by her last name.”

“Then give us a reason to!”

“I just gave you two!” Kara fumed. She glanced between the skeptical reporters and Lena’s silent visage. Indecision briefly illuminated her eyes before it was consumed by furious conviction. “Fine. You want proof she isn’t anti-alien? Here!”

Lena barely had time to react before the hero kissed her. Their lips met as thousands watched and dozens of cameras flashed. The CEO was far too surprised to melt into the kiss, but neither did she recoil or turn away.

Kara pulled back, facing the reporters. “I encourage you to listen to the rest of L-Corp’s speakers and hear what they have to say. In the meantime, I’m taking my girlfriend back to her office.”

Lena numbly accepted Supergirl’s outstretched hand, barely comprehending the moment. As the hero lifted her into the sky, her face was a blend of a dopey smile and a stricken look of terror.

Did you really just do that?!

/

Alex stared at the computer screen, dumbfound. “Did Kara really just-”

Incredibly, Sam began to laugh. “Oh God, she did. That was brilliant! Did you see the look on Lena’s face? Twitter must be blowing up!”

“Do you realize the danger they’ll be in?”

The CFO shrugged. “They’re already the most targeted people on the planet. At least now Ms. Luthor might not receive so many death threats from alien supporters.”

“What do you mean?”

“Anyone can hire an alien refugee, or publicly support Alien Amnesty. All of that can be an act by someone waiting for the right time to strike. The look on Lena’s face when Kara suddenly kissed her? The complete lack of disgust? That can’t be faked.”

Alex realized she was right. Social media was going to be dominated by pictures of Lena’s befuddled expression. She actually found herself amused by the fact that Lena Luthor had, for a brief moment, looked like an idiot to the entire world.

That didn’t mean that she was comfortable with the idea of her sister publicly dating Lena Luthor. Yet perhaps Sam had a point. How much more of a target could she be?

Her phone buzzed. Lois Lane.

“Sam, it’s Lois. Do you mind if I take this?”

Her boss chuckled, as if surprised Alex had even asked. “Go ahead. In fact, put her on speaker. I’m curious what she has to say.”

Alex did so. “Lois? What’s the reaction?”

The reporter was equally straight to the point. “Most people seem to think that Supergirl was pissed off that her girlfriend was getting a lot of hate online, and showed up at the press conference as a spur of the moment decision.”

“Then they might be right for once,” Alex murmured. Kara had probably just improved Lena Luthor’s reputation more than she realized. For a moment, Alex felt a twinge of annoyance at her sister for improving a supervillain’s pubic image.

Then Alex remembered that she had joined the Dark Side, and that she now wanted Lena Luthor to be trusted by the public.

“What do you think, Lois?” the security chief asked. “How bad is this going to be?”

Lois audibly shrugged. “Not any worse than it already is. It was common knowledge already that Supergirl didn’t want to arrest Lena Luthor. It’s going to be a media firestorm that a superhero is dating a supervillain, but Kara isn’t a politician. She’s free to ignore reporters if she wants to.”

A twinge of relief settled in Alex’s chest. “I still can’t believe she did that.”

“I can,” Lois surprised. “Is it any wonder that Kara and Lena are moving fast? They’ve nearly died so many times that they probably want to enjoy the good in their lives while they can. Near death experiences have a way of reshaping perspective. No one likes to leave unfinished business behind.”

Alex didn’t like dwelling on the possibility of her sister dying, but she understood Lois’s point.

“In fact, I’m surprised the same hasn’t happened to you,” the reporter continued. “You’ve faced your own share of peril in recent months. You and your new boss make heart-eyes at each other every time you meet. Why don’t you follow your sister’s example and just kiss her?”

Alex went stark white. A glance at Sam revealed the opposite reaction; the CFO’s cheeks were glowing red. Belatedly, Alex realized that she had never told Lois that she was on speaker.

“I’ll…keep that in mind.” The security chief’s eyes were rooted to the floor. “Any updates on the media reaction, contact me. I’ve got to go. See you, Lois,” she said, shutting her L-Phone off without waiting for a reply.

Dead silence permeated the room.

Still silence.

I’m going to have to say something.

“Sam, you know Lois…she likes to tease. We should get back to work.”

A pause. “I think it’s actually time for lunch,” Sam said slowly. “I’m going out to eat for an hour. I have a date I’m meeting at Kwong’s Cuisine.”

What? Alex tried not to let her boss see how painful the thought of Sam sharing a lunch at a fancy restaurant- with someone else- was to her. “Oh. Yeah. Have fun.”

Sam took a step forward. “That is, if my date is interested. Is she?”

Alex looked up, staring at the CFO. As the implications became clear, Alex distracted herself from her racing heartbeat by reaching for her purse.

Lois is right. We could all die tomorrow. I need to text her 'thanks'.

“Yes, she is. Let’s go.”
