Getting out of her taxi, Jess walked into her apartment building. She’d been sent home early, probably to allow Supergirl and her boss to have a private argument. Lena would be berating Kara for putting herself at risk by putting their relationship in the spotlight, and Kara would shoot back that it had been her choice and she was already in danger.

Odds were good that they would make up by the end of the day, as Lena would realize that Kara had done her reputation a huge favor and Kara would realize that her girlfriend’s anger was born out of worry. Either way, it wasn’t Jess’s business.

What was her business was the syringe of Harun-El in her purse. Her compatibility test had come back positive. All she had to do was inject herself and she’d be superhuman. Lena had given her the syringe, telling her to do it in the most comfortable setting possible. That would be her own home.

“Jess.”

The secretary had been so consumed by her thoughts that she hadn’t noticed the familiar face standing on the stairs. “What are you doing here?” she asked.

Her visitor frowned. “I need you to leave your cell phone on the stairs. Then you’re coming with me for a few hours.”

“Excuse me?” Jess demanded. “I have a son upstairs I need to get to.”

The visitor wasn’t moved. “He’ll be fine. And I’m sorry, Jess, but I wasn’t offering you a choice. Let’s go.”

Investigation

Supergirl barely had time to set Lena down on her office balcony before the CEO was storming out of her arms and pushing open the glass doors. “Jess!” she called. “Go home for today.”

The secretary stepped into the office. “Ms. Luthor, what about the-”

“Go,” Lena repeated. “Make your decision tonight. Inject yourself someplace comfortable…the transformation isn’t entirely pleasant.”

The confusion in Jess’s eyes vanished as they darted between the superhero and supervillain standing in the office. Hurriedly, she returned to the outer room and closed the door behind her.

Kara inwardly flinched as Lena’s gaze turned to her. “You are a child.”

The superhero crossed her arms. “Excuse me?” Kara demanded. After just having put her reputation on the line to protect her girlfriend, anger had been the last thing that she expected.

“You just act, doing whatever your emotions say, without even thinking of the consequences!” Lena hissed, wringing her arms in exasperation. “You’re going to be more of a target than ever now, and you don’t exactly have a secret identity anymore, remember?”

Now the hero’s own indignation was rising to the surface. “I doubt I can be a bigger target than I already am,” she drawled. “People already knew I didn’t hate you.”

“They suspected,” Lena countered. “Now they know, and more importantly, now they know it’s personal. You’re now the number one target for all of my enemies. Did that occur to you? Did you stop and think for one second before ‘flying off to my rescue’?”

Talk about ungrateful! “Why in Rao’s name are you so upset?” Kara demanded. “I just provided the world with proof that Supergirl trusts you. Another step closer to world domination; isn’t that right?”

Lena sent her a vicious smile. “Yes, that’s right. But you didn’t think about that either, did you? Not until it was too late. Your fan club is quite big, and it’s not going to oppose me any longer. Aliens have just seen their biggest champion publicly endorse me. I couldn’t have asked for more.”

“Then why are you upset?” Kara replied with a scowl.

“Because you are in danger!” the supervillain repeated. “My goals mean nothing if you have to die to make them happen.”

Supergirl wasn’t sure to be flattered or insulted. “I’m not going to die.”

“You saw someone you cared about getting some tough questions from the press; that was all that it took for you to leap into action and give a massive advantage to a supervillain planning on world domination!” Lena exclaimed. “You didn’t think. And you can be damn sure I’m going to use what you’ve given me. Supergirl’s endorsement is going to be my newest recruiting tool.”

Kara was incredulous. “You’re going to try and punish me?”

“I’m going to give you a reminder that your actions have consequences,” Lena shot back.

The hero crossed her arms. “That’s an easy way to rationalize using your girlfriend’s selfless moment of weakness against her wishes.”

“Should have thought of that earlier, huh?” Lena’s eye twitched.

What else should I expect from a supervillain? Kara thought bitterly. Her girlfriend meant well, but at that moment Supergirl was resisting the urge to burn her desk with a blast of heat vision.

“You’re the best person I know, Kara,” the CEO said, calming down slightly. “But you never think. It’s why you still won’t side with me. You base your entire life around emotion. Taking over the world feels wrong to you, so you won’t do it. All you do is fight criminals and rogue aliens like a glorified attack dog. If you thought even a few months ahead, you would have realized from the beginning that your efforts were doomed to failure. The minute you meet a force more powerful than you…you’re done.”

Supergirl narrowed her eyes. “Oh, am I?”

Lena smiled proudly. “Well, you would have been, if you didn’t have me to show up and do the hard thinking for you. Thanks to me, you’ve been able to survive so far. But keeping you alive would be a lot easier for me if you would just grow up and think ahead.”

“I’m the child?” Kara spat back. “You’re the one who acts based on emotion. You want to take over the world because you’re scared. You’re afraid that if you don’t have all the power, you won’t be able to save everyone. Just like you couldn’t-”

The hero stopped herself. Far too late.”

A bitter chuckle filled the office. “Did you mean to say that my guilt over what happened to my mother fuels my actions? I took psychology in college too, you know. A semester of it, anyway. You’re not entirely wrong. Perhaps my guilt initially spurred me to take this path. But I wouldn’t have continued if my logic told me otherwise.”

“You’re really good at rationalizing, aren’t you?” Kara noted. “But logic would show that you can’t save everyone. Even when you hold all the cards. Did our raid on the DEO not teach you anything? You’re just as human as the rest of us, Lena! So let me live with my own decisions, and maybe stop trying to make all of humanity’s choices for them!”

A moment of silence passed.

“Go,” Lena said, nodding at the balcony door. “I have work to do, and you’re scheduled to visit the Children’s Hospital. I’ll see you tonight for our dinner. I suggest we do not resume this conversation in the near future.”

Kara sighed. There was no more point in arguing.

As far as Alex was aware, first dates were supposed to consist mostly of awkward small talk. If you got lucky, the night would end with some slightly deeper conversation before a chaste farewell kiss.

What was not supposed to happen was your date grabbing you before dessert could be served and pulling you into an intense kiss for the entire restaurant to look at. That was also not to be followed with your date nonchalantly tossing some bills on the table before virtually dragging you out of the establishment. Most importantly, you weren’t supposed to make out with your date on the way to work as the driver raises the visor and tries to pretend you don’t exist.

All of those rules were broken.

How could Alex resist? Sam was sweet, generous, and just confident enough to be sexy without being an arrogant bitch. The fact that she was incredibly hot also didn’t hurt.

Okay, there’s no doubt about it now. I’m into women.

 True, they were moving a little fast, but what did it matter? They all lived dangerous lives and there was no telling when it all might end. Plus, with the crazy world that Alex had entered, her options for dating were going to be rather limited. She wasn’t going to let go of a prize catch if she could help it.

“We’re going to have to…file a report with HR,” Sam moaned as they briefly broke apart.

Alex frowned, moving across the leather seat and seizing her boss in another kiss. “I’m not too worried,” she managed to get out. “I…have…connections.”

“Oh, do you?”

“My sister is dating the CEO.”

Jess tested her bonds. If she’d been injected with the Harun-El, the ropes would have snapped like a twig. Unfortunately, the syringe was currently lying on the table in front of her, meaning the secretary had no way to break out of the dingy motel room she’d been placed in.

“You have to know you won’t get away with this,” she warned her captor. Not an ounce of fear was in her voice. “I wouldn’t be worried at all if my son wasn’t home alone.”

A shrug from the kidnapper. “He’ll be fine. You’ll be found missing within a few hours and your boss will send someone to watch him. The worst he’ll experience is a late dinner.”

“You’d better hope so,” Jess hissed, leaning forward in her chair. “Either way, you’re going to regret this,” the secretary promised.

“Only if I fail,” the other individual replied. “You’re not the only person who has someone to protect.”

“Mommy, is Ms. Alex your friend now?”

Sam smiled at her daughter. Even at the age of twelve, she knew Ruby would see through to the truth soon enough. “Actually, darling, Alex is my girlfriend now,” she corrected. “We’re going to be trying that out for a bit…if that’s alright with you.”

Across the dinner table, Alex nodded.

“Already?” Ruby questioned, though she didn’t look displeased. “A lot of people would say that’s pretty quick. Isn’t that what you said when my friends started dating?”

The CFO shook her head. “Your friends are twelve. Alex and I are not, and as you like to remind me, I won’t live forever. If it doesn’t work out, then there’s no harm done. There’s no contract involved.”

After their eventful date this afternoon, Sam had proposed a dinner in her apartment. The first test in any relationship she entered was Ruby’s approval. If her new girlfriend couldn’t get along with her daughter, there was no point in continuing further.

She hadn’t been surprised to see Ruby take to Alex. The ex-police officer and current chief of security was certainly more ‘’badass’’ (as Ruby would put it) than herself. Even an intelligent twelve-year-old was bored by a job that mostly involved phone calls and spreadsheets.

“Ruby, I’m helping my boss complete a hostile takeover! Want to come look?”

“That’s great, Mama! But I’m watching CSI right now.”

“Good,” Ruby said decisively. She turned to Alex. “I’m sure you’ll make her happy. But if you don’t, you’ll have to answer to me,” she said, folding her arms.

Alex laughed. “I wouldn’t dream of it. Your Mom is amazing. And I wouldn’t want to cross you, Ruby. Diamonds aren’t the only gems that can cut steel, you know.”

Sam watched as her daughter took a second to digest the sentence. Then a wide smile broke on the girl’s face as she accepted the compliment.

This is what Sam had needed. Someone mature and decisive, who could be tough and show a softer side. The good looks only sealed the deal.

True, Alex had attempted to kill Sam’s boss…but there hadn’t been any harm done, right? Part of Sam couldn’t even help but respect her girlfriend’s protective instincts when it came to family. She would have been willing to kill in a second to eliminate a threat to her daughter.

She had always put Ruby first. Sam had been adopted by an unloving parent, and when she became pregnant as a teenager she had refused to let her daughter suffer the same fate. Raising Ruby had made her life more difficult in those early years, but it had never been a burden. Without Ruby, Sam Arias had no reason to live.

That said, part of her had missed having a social life. Now that her daughter was older and they were financially secure, it was time to have a little fun for herself.

Now if only her damn headache would go away, her day would be perfect.

\

“You know why I worry about you.”

Kara frowned at her girlfriend from across the dinner table. “That doesn’t mean you can scold me like a child whenever you want. I’m just as capable of taking care of myself as you are.”

The supervillain shook her head. “No, you’re not. You act without thinking, and you shackle yourself to principles that are only going to get you killed. Maybe get all of us killed.”

“You know something, Lena? You’re not always right.”

“I’m right about this,” the CEO scowled. “You act based entirely on emotion. It’s why you put yourself in the line of fire today, and it’s why you still won’t join me even when you know I’m right. In fact, it’s also why you refuse to kill even your worst opponents. Abandoning your precious code is too much for you.”

“I believe that humanity deserves to make its own destiny!” Supergirl shot back. “And that killing, by definition, is wrong. There’s always a better way.”

Supergirl had faced hundreds of enemies during her career. Many of them would have been only too glad to choke the life out of her. Kara had defeated them all without lowering herself to that level, even if it had meant suffering a few more bruises.

The villain sighed. “I have one principle, Kara. One. To protect and enrich innocent lives. Anything else other than that is just ego-stroking.”

“So what makes someone guilty?” Kara demanded. “Is there a firm rule in place, handed down by the gods? Or is it entirely up to you?”

Lena frowned. “I would kill the guilty if it was necessary to save the innocent. In those situations, it’s usually pretty easy to distinguish the two. And if not, I’d use my best judgment. In the end, that’s all anyone can do.”

It was times like this that Supergirl knew her life would be a lot easier if she’d found a girlfriend without a warped ideology.

“Life is precious, Lena. Some people can be considered evil, and there are plenty of examples of beings who cause more harm than good,” Kara admitted. “But I think there’s a spark of goodness in everyone, no matter how depraved they might seem. History is full of examples of the worst people…terrorists, warlords, slavers…coming back to the light. Everyone deserves that chance.”

“Full of examples?” Lena scoffed. “There have been some, I’ll grant you. And I agree that redemption can be earned. But I wouldn’t put innocent lives in danger to save someone still determined to do them harm. So far, I’ve been able to imprison anyone who poses a threat, but I have a feeling that won’t work forever. Do you see Reign staying put in a cage?”

Kara’s eyes narrowed. “Reign is a monster, but she could be one of my people!” the alien protested. “We could try to redeem her. Don’t you wish you’d had that same chance with Lex?”

All of the fire suddenly drained out of the CEO’s eyes. “Lex killed your cousin,” she said softly.

“And I hate him for it,” Kara agreed. “Imagine, though, if he could have seen the error of his ways. Maybe it could have happened. Beneath all his madness, he still thought he was doing the right thing; most people always do. What if he could have realized he was in the wrong? It might have taken decades, maybe it never would have worked, we won’t ever know. That’s what happens when people are killed: all hope for them is extinguished.”

Lena was staring at her in awe. “You…would have been willing to forgive him?”

The hero sighed. “It wouldn’t have been easy, and I definitely would have been suspicious. But if he was really remorseful, I would have been prepared to try.”

The CEO’s mask had faded away, and a truly remorseful expression stood in its place. “Kara, I see your point. I’ll try my best to capture Reign,” she promised. “If I can’t, and I have the opportunity to kill her, then I’m sorry. I won’t hold back.”

“I won’t let you kill her,” Supergirl replied. “I’ve never needed to kill to protect people and I’m not going to let you cross that line, either.”

“Then we’ll come to blows yet again,” Lena pointed out.

She’d been hoping that her days of battling Supergirl were over. Vanity’s days of liberating criminals and stealing from companies were mostly over. L-Corp had gained such a foothold in the global economy that it no longer needed her help. All competitors in the areas of technology and finance had been either absorbed or rendered irrelevant. Any individual or organization that wanted to succeed needed to rely on L-Corp products and services. There was no longer any real choice.

Phase 1 was complete.

Lena cast a regretful look at Kara. Phase 2 would be a lot easier if Supergirl was openly supporting her efforts, but that didn’t look like it was going to happen soon.

“You say you want me around to keep you on the moral path,” Kara said. “Yet you never listen to me.”

The villain nodded, accepting the point. “I don’t agree with your adherence to principle to such an extent. I’ll hear you out on that front, but that doesn’t mean I’ll ever agree.”

Lena had heard her girlfriend out…countless times. Was it her fault that the hero had never managed to convince her?

“You inspire me,” Lena said. “For me, doing good is a choice. A duty. For you, it’s automatic. Natural. I saw the footage of you handing out presents to those kids today. I’ve seen a lot of footage of you doing charity work. You’re not there because it’s the right thing to do. You’re there because you enjoy it. Doing good makes you feel good. It’s like another source of solar energy for you.”

Kara said nothing, but the CEO could see the surprise in her gaze.

“I’m smarter than you, Kara. That’s why I can see the bigger picture and why you’re the one who naively sticks to an outdated code. Yet...you’re better than me. You make me want to do everything in my power to help people. I want you to be proud of me,” she admitted, letting her mental walls crumble completely. “I’m sorry that doesn’t translate into agreeing with your way of doings things. I wish we were on the same side. I really do.”

The hero smiled sadly. “We usually are.”

“I hope it stays that way,” Lena replied. What if, when she took over the world, Kara never agreed with her? Could their relationship survive that? There was no happiness for her without Kara. The Black Mercy had proven that well enough.

My happiness doesn’t matter, Lena reminded herself. The world matters. Kara matters. Even if we fell apart, she’d survive. If I have to let her go to save her…I will.

It wasn’t until several hours later that Sam’s headache finally vanished. If these migraines didn’t stop coming, Sam would have to go see a doctor. They’d been a problem since she was a child, but over the years they’d gotten steadily worse.

For the moment, that could wait. Sam was curled up on the couch with a wine glass in hand, laughing as Alex told one of her stories from her time on the force. Apparently, the officer had thought jumping off of a building was a good idea. Yes, she’d seen her superhero sister flying nearby, but it had nearly given her first partner a heart attack.

“She’s lucky to have you,” Sam said, smiling wistfully at Alex. “I would have loved to have had a sister when I was adopted. My mother, well…she couldn’t wait to get rid of me.”

Alex shot her a sympathetic glance. “It wasn’t always like that. I resented her at first. She took up all of my parents’ time as she adjusted to Earth and she was an alien. Anything we did, I couldn’t compete. She was stronger. Faster. Nicer.”

“I’ve always liked Supergirl,” Sam said, wrapping an arm around her girlfriend’s neck. “But she’s not my favorite. Lena Luthor might be into the idealistic, saintlike type, but I prefer someone with a little more…fire. Kara might serve as an example, but it’s people like you who get the job done.” She punctuated the statement with a kiss.

“Ruby’s sleeping in the other room,” Alex reminded her ruefully after a few more seconds.

Sam nodded. “If it wasn’t for your super-hearing, I wouldn’t believe it,” the CFO noted. “She’s always had a bad habit of eavesdropping.”

“She’s just a curious girl,” Alex said, with a defensiveness that both surprised and pleased Sam. “And she wants you to be happy. If I had a daughter, I’d want one like that. Asking questions, never sitting still.”

Sam chuckled. “Be careful what you wish for. Now that you’re around, prepare to get most of those questions yourself. After all, you have a much cooler job than mine…even though you work for me.”

“Are you jealous?”

The CFO frowned. “No,” she denied flatly.

Alex grinned. “Sam, she adores you. I’m not usually scared by threats, especially when they’re made by little girls, but when Ruby told me not to hurt you…” she shuddered playfully. “Anyone could see how loyal she is to you. That’s something that had to be earned.”

Sam let her feelings be known through another passionate kiss.

It wasn’t until a few minutes later that her good mood finally began to fade. That was when Alex was interrupted by a call from her cell phone.

“It’s Lois,” Alex said, annoyance plain in her voice.

The CFO resisted the urge to scowl. “Answer it,” she replied reluctantly.

Alex did so. “Hey, Lois,” she spoke into the phone.

For a solid minute, the CFO watched as Alex listened intently into her cell. By the end of Lois’s words, the expression of annoyance had morphed into one of concern.

Alex lowered the phone. “Jess is missing,” she said quickly. “Lois has been trying to reach her for over an hour and hasn’t gotten any response. When she called Jess’s apartment, her son answered the phone and said she never came home from work.

A black pit of dread settled in Sam’s stomach. “Oh God,” she breathed. “Where is Lois now? Ask her why she was trying to talk to Jess-”

“She’s here,” Alex interrupted. “At the bottom of the building. She wants to compare notes in person. Can you give her clearance to come up?”

\

“Have you called Lena?” Sam asked.

Pacing in the middle of the apartment’s living room, Lois shook her head. “I tried. No response. I don’t think she has my number flagged as a priority contact.”

“I’ll do it,” Alex announced. The security officer walked off into the other room, phone in hand. “I’ll make sure she sends someone over to check on her son.” The worry was plain on her face, but Alex’s eyes were narrowed in focus.

Sending her girlfriend an unconscious admiring smile, Sam turned back to the reporter. “Why were you trying to reach her, anyway?”

Lois frowned. “Perry White sent me to National City to get a report on some of L-Corp’s investments. You can’t take over the technological sector and not expect to make waves,” she replied with an admonishing glare. “In fact, I was going to be asking you for an interview tomorrow.”

“And how does Jess factor into this?”

“I talked to her when I was at L-Corp earlier. She told me Lena had offered her an infusion of Harun-El. I was calling to ask whether she’d decided to take it,” Lois revealed.

Sam immediately leapt to her feet, following Alex into the sitting room and leaving Lois behind. The situation had just escalating from troubling to catastrophic. Her boss needed to know.

Jess’s captor walked into the room without preamble. “Your boss knows you’re missing,” the words came immediately. “Kara volunteered to watch him for the night.”

“Then he’s safe, but he must be worried sick!” the secretary protested. “How long do you plan to keep me here?”

Lois crossed her arms. “I am sorry about this. But Lena has a mole within her inner circle, and I have to find out who it is. If she goes down, Kara falls with her. I didn’t plan on kidnapping you, but the Harun-El forced my hand. If you are the mole, I can’t risk her enemies getting ahold of it.”

“I’m not a mole!” Jess hissed. “Ms. Luthor has been great to me! Why would I want to hurt her?”

Lois shrugged. “I don’t know. But I didn’t win two Pulitzer Prizes by taking things for granted. If you’re guilty, I’ll find out. It won’t be long til my program hacks your phone.”

“You’re crazy.” Jess would have opened her phone herself; she had nothing to hide. Yet she didn’t trust Lois any more than Lois trusted her. Recent events hadn’t helped in that regard. Kidnapping people based on hunches was not the mark of a stable woman.

Another shrug. “What matters is that I’m right. You, Sam, and Colville are my top suspects. I asked Perry to give me a reason to interview Colville and I placed a bug on him. Your disappearance gave me an excuse to come up to Sam’s apartment and place bugs on both her and her residence. It won’t be long until the truth comes out.”

“And you’re caught and arrested for kidnapping,” Jess pointed out viciously.

“Once I find out who the mole is, I’ll come clean,” Lois promised. “I accept the consequences.”

 

Plans Within Plans

L-Corp had a mole.

It was obvious, really. The death of Maggie Sawyer’s killer, right as the investigation was closing in, was the biggest clue. Reign’s arrival during the raid on the DEO was the second. Kara’s identity leaking at the perfect time was the final straw.

To be honest with herself, Lois wasn’t entirely sure where she stood on Lena Luthor or her plans to control the world. The villain certainly wasn’t her brother, and the fact that she cared about Kara was obvious, but world domination was certainly a Luthor-esque plan. There were a thousand ways it could go wrong, and Lena didn’t seem willing to acknowledge any of them.

Yet that was all moot. Kara’s fate had become entwined with Lena Luthor’s, for better or worse. If Lena was taken down, Supergirl wouldn’t be far behind her. Even Lois could admit that Lena’s resources had become virtually indispensable.

When Lena had refused to listen, Lois had made her own plans. The reveal that Jess had been given a syringe of Harun-el just accelerated her plans. Getting an interview with Colville and access to Jess’s office had been easy; Perry White was always willing to do her a favor.

Sam had been trickier. Lois hadn’t had an excuse to interview her immediately, and her kidnapping of Jess had given her a small timeframe. So she’d seized her chance when Supergirl had kissed Lena during that press conference. She’d called Alex, knowing that she would be in Sam’s presence, and advised her to make a move.

Evidently, either her hope that Alex had had the phone on speaker had been well-placed, or Alex had taken her advice. The end result was that she was spending time together with Sam after work. When Lois had ‘reported’ Jess’s disappearance, it had been all too easy to place listening devices on both Sam and in her apartment.

Jess was still tugging at her bonds. “If you think Ms. Luthor will appreciate any of this, you’re sorely mistaken. My boss doesn’t like it when people go behind her back.”

“I really don’t give a damn,” Lois replied smoothly. “I’m doing this for Kara, not her.”

A flash of sympathy illuminated Jess’s eyes. “I am sorry you lost Clark, you know. I get why you want to protect his cousin. But kidnapping and lies aren’t something he would have approved of.”

“Oh really?” Lois demanded. “Did you ever even meet him? Clark was willing to make tough choices. So many people always forget that. All they remember is the symbol. No one will ever know just how much it cost him to go after Lex that day. He knew innocents would be put at risk, but it was the only way to save thousands of lives.”

Jess was silent.

Lois sighed. “Everyone remembers Superman. History has already forgotten Clark Kent. And that’s how Smallville would have wanted it; he would have been happy to see his legend still giving people hope. Me? I would trade it all in an instant to have him back for a few minutes.”

Wow, I’m really opening up to my kidnapping victim. Is reverse Stockholm syndrome a thing? Maybe I should write an article about that.

“You couldn’t save him,” Jess said simply. “Now you’re trying to save Kara to redeem yourself.”

Lois scoffed. “Clark’s death wasn’t my fault. Nothing on Earth could have convinced him not to try and stop Lex, and I knew that. Even if I’d knocked him out with kryptonite, he never would have forgiven himself. It would have been a fate worse than death for him.”

“So why are you feeling so guilty?” the secretary demanded.

She crossed her arms, placing the syringe of Harun-el in her pocket. “Eat your dinner, Jess. I’ll call Kara and make sure everything’s fine with Luke.”

\

“Thanks, Supergirl. All we need to do now is the wiring.”

Kara winced. Despite having just used her superspeed to finish the construction of a building, the hero wasn’t even winded. However, some things would always be beyond her.

“I’m afraid that’s not within my capabilities. Good luck!” She shot off into the air.

Even if crime fighting was her main forte, Supergirl was happy to help the citizens of National City in any way she could. Especially when they were constructing a new homeless shelter open to both humans and aliens. On some occasions, she worked with charities on a pre-scheduled basis. Sometimes, it was just spontaneous.

She had just started her next patrol of the city when her phone began to ring. Seeing it was Lena, the hero eagerly answered the call. “Any news on Jess?” she asked hopefully.

The CEO’s voice was flat. “No. It’s been nearly twenty-four hours. No sign of who took her, and no ransom demand.”

“You were expecting a ransom demand for your secretary?”

“No,” sighed Lena. “But I was hoping for one. It would mean that the kidnapper was just interested in targeting one of my associates for a quick score, instead of trying to interrogate her for all of my secrets.”

Kara frowned. “Or taking the Harun-el,” she reminded her girlfriend.

“It’s worse than you think,” Lena replied. “That syringe is made of enhanced Nth metal, so it can pierce through Kryptonian skin. Otherwise, the needle could get trapped inside during the transfusion.”

Supergirl nearly froze in midair. “So anyone who duplicates your formula could come at me with knives that would actually work?”

A pause. “No, probably not. Even I haven’t made enough of the substance for that to be practical. But the technological applications are impressive.”

Kara frowned. They were getting distracted from the important issue. “Shouldn’t we be worried about Jess, not your fancy technology?”

It was as if a dam had burst open.

“You think I’m not worried?!” Lena demanded. “Fine, let’s talk about Jess. Right now, she’s probably being strapped down and tortured for all my secrets! And since my scanning of all L-Phone communications has failed, her son might be growing up an orphan! My mind keeps going over ways to tell him that his mother is never coming home because I sent her out into the world with valuable technology without having her escorted by security. Is that what you would rather talk about?”

Even as Kara winced guiltily, the tirade stopped.

“I’m sorry,” Lena apologized numbly. “This isn’t your fault. Just keep doing your patrols and listening for the sound of her voice. I’m going through all of the footage I have of her yesterday. If there’s a clue there, I’ll find it.”

\

Using the superspeed granted by the Harun-el, Lois had placed herself a mile away from the city. Standing in the outskirts of the desert was much less uncomfortable when one had Kryptonian powers.

She’d left her phone back at the motel. No sense in allowing anyone at L-Corp to track her, just in case. All the reporter had on her was the Harun-el in her pocket and a PDA tuned only to the bugs she’d placed on Sam and Colville. So far, there had been nothing incriminatory, but all of Lois’s instincts were telling her to wait.

A small smile appeared on her lips. Lois had conducted quite a few stakeouts with Clark in those early days. Patience had never been his strong suit. It had been during one of those investigations, spying on the meeting place of suspected human traffickers, that Lois had finally dropped the bomb.

“Fine. Go get them, Superman. I’ll wait here.”

The familiar mix of happiness and anguish appeared that always accompanied her thoughts of Clark. Yes, part of her was doing this for him. Kara was the last of his legacy.

Unlike what some might suggest, however, there were other reasons as well. Lois was her own woman, and that meant that she took responsibility for her mistakes. Kara Zor-El had been her biggest mistake of all.

Clark might have taken her in. Lois had sensed that he was on the fence. But she had strongly voiced the opinion that Kara would have been better off with the Danvers. Her fiancé had quickly made his decision after that.

Lois had made some good arguments. Yet if she was being honest with herself, her reasoning had come down to one factor: she’d been a young woman trying to ascend to the top of the Daily Planet while also about to marry the love of her life. She hadn’t needed a kid to worry about on top of everything else.

It had worked out for Kara, in the end. There was no point in dwelling on what might have been. But until the present day, Lois had never told the young hero just how much of a role she had played on Clark’s decision. Maybe she never would.

Sitting at her desk. Talking with Lois. Ordering lunch. Sitting at her desk. Going to the bathroom. Sitting at her desk. Lena ran through the footage again. Everything seemed completely innocuous, yet the CEO couldn’t stop searching.

She was missing something.

Jess had been kidnapped the day she had received the Harun-el. Lena knew that wasn’t a coincidence. The odds were simply astronomical.

BANG! Her hand slammed against the desk. It didn’t make any sense. No one Lena suspected of being an enemy had even been near Jess the previous day. Only Lois knew about the Harun-el, and Lena knew she wasn’t stupid enough to talk about that with anyone outside their circle.

“Not just a mole. Someone high up. Someone you trust.”

The memory popped into the supervillain’s brain, unbidden by her conscious mind. Yes, Lois had been certain that Lena had a mole. And her instincts were driving the supervillain to remember that because…

Lois thought Jess might be a mole. She wanted to do something in case she gave the Harun-el to our enemies.

“Lois!” the villain hissed. Why hadn’t she realized it before? Lois had been one of the few people to see Jess the previous day, and the only one to know about the Harun-el besides Kara. Sam had told her that Lois was the one to report the secretary was missing. It all added up.

Seconds later, her phone was in her hand. Kara’s number had been dialed.

“You ladies are all set. Anything else?”

Reign suppressed a scowl. “No thanks,” she said, adopting the tone often used by Samantha Arias. “We’ll call you if we need anything.”

The server nodded, closing the door behind them.

Reign looked at Purity and Pestilence. A private room in a restaurant was a strange choice for their rare in-person conversations, but there was a reason for the madness. It was the last place Lena Luthor or any of her lackeys would expect their enemies to meet. And if caught, Reign could just claim to have been enjoying a meal with two old friends who were visiting the city.  

“So, our next move,” Reign commenced immediately. “Luthor survived the Black Mercy, but we have obtained everything we need. All we have to do now is kill her.”

Purity frowned. “That’s proven difficult. Do you really believe that she remains a threat, if alive?”

“The Mistress does,” Reign replied. “The Queen thinks that with her death, our forces are certain to suffer less casualties. We are not taking any chances.”

“Allow me to unleash the Blight,” Pestilence cut in. “Human society will collapse under the weight of its own dead. Luthor will have no one to follow her.”

Reign stared at her. Even closed in civilian attire, the glare was intimidating. “No. We need the humans. Their deaths serve no purpose. Better to allow Luthor to continue to operate than lose a billion potential servants.”

Pestilence scowled petulantly but made no further comment.

“There is also the matter of Kara Zor-El,” Reign continued. “The Queen would prefer her subdued before hostilities begin.”

Pestilence perked up again. “Then why don’t we go get her? Right now? She couldn’t hope to beat you, much less all three of us!”

“For the same reason we aren’t all going to snap Luthor’s neck,” Reign replied impatiently. “There’s already an armada of drones operational. Any attack on Luthor or Kara risks provoking a massive force, one we may not be able to defeat. I will not risk using our trump card until the final moment.”

Purity coughed. “Reign is right,” she agreed. “In the meantime, I hope the two of you have finally subdued your hosts.”

“Grace Parker has…harmonized with me,” Pestilence reported. “We have a similar mindset. What about Samantha Arias?”

Reign repressed another scowl. She was the most powerful of the Worldkillers, their leader…yet the last to gain full control of her body. “Her pregnancy delayed my takeover,” the alien reported. “Though she has no idea of my presence, her subconscious continues to fight me.”

The body still belonged to Samantha. Apart from Reign’s brief periods of control, she was confined to the role of an observer. The Worldkiller had been forced to endure countless hours of watching Ruby Arias play with her mother, desperately aching to unleash a blast of heat vision. Thankfully, their positions would soon be reversed. Reign would be in perpetual control of her body, and Samantha Arias would be imprisoned as an impotent bystander.

Samantha’s phone began to ring. Kara Danvers. She ignored it. The search for the secretary did not concern her.

“You could obtain some Harun-el,” Purity pointed out. “Remember what the Mistress said? Her scientists are almost certain that an infusion of black kryptonite would split you apart from your host.”

A shake of her head. “It’s too risky. If Samantha escapes me, or her body is discovered, my position within L-Corp will be gone.”

Another chime sounded from Samantha’s phone. With a bored glance, Reign lifted the device from her pocket to look.

Sam, it’s Kara. Lois is the one who took Jess. Lena directed me to Lois’s phone signal and I found her. Jess says Lois thinks there’s a mole in L-Corp. She placed bugs on both you and Colville. I’d be careful what you say.  

Jess is fine. Still looking for Lois.

 For the first time in Reign’s existence, the Worldkiller felt fear.

She fixed her allies with a hard stare, placing a finger to her lips. Wordlessly, she held out the message for them to read. No sooner had their eyes trailed over the words then the blood drained from their faces.

Thankfully, both of them were smart enough to keep their mouths shut.

Reign made a circling gesture with her hand. Keep talking.

As Purity began to speak some irrelevant drivel, Reign’s mind was spinning. Rapidly, she typed words into her phone in the Notes app.

Search my clothes for a bug.

As Purity continued to talk, Pestilence’s eyes roamed over Reign’s body. Ten seconds later, the plague-bringer was pointing at the folds of Samantha’s favorite jacket.

She input more words into the phone.

I have to find that reporter before she speaks to anyone else. She won’t stop listening if she thinks she can still find valuable information. Keep talking. Say anything. Make up fake plans. I’ll find her.

At two nods from her allies, Reign gingerly slipped off the jacket.

\

Lois’s mind was spinning.

Sam wasn’t a mole. Instead, there was a hostile alien personality that was taking over her body. It seemed too ridiculous to be true, but the words were coming into the PDA loud and clear.

Reign wasn’t alone. She had at least two compatriots, one of whom apparently had the ability to bring about a plague. They were working for an invasion force that was set to arrive sometime in the near future.

Who were they? What did they want? Lois continued listening intently, hoping to pick up more clues. Even under the dire circumstances, it was still fascinating.

They didn’t want to kill Kara. Why? Who was this Mistress/Queen that they kept talking about? Every thought just brought about further questions.

Most importantly, there was a way to free Sam from her torment. Harun-el. All I have to do is inject Sam when she isn’t on guard. That should be easy enough.

Reign seemed to be their leader. Taking her down would go a long way to resolving the entire situation. Strangely, the alien hadn’t talked for several minutes, leaving Purity and Pestilence to discuss a raid on some L-Corp facilities in Kaznia.

I was right. There is a mole. Of course, Lois admitted to herself. Lena was also right. Still, this means I owe Jess about a million favors-

One second, Lois was alone in the outskirts of the desert. The next, her PDA exploded.

Gaping in shock, the reporter looked upward for the source of the twin red beams that had destroyed her equipment. Reign was floating above her, her eyes flaming with both triumph and rage.

For the first time in two years, Lois began to quake with fear. She was alone, and no one knew where she was. Her phone was sitting in a motel room miles away, and the most powerful alien on Earth now wanted her blood.

“How…how did you find me?” the reporter heard herself gasp.

“I followed the voices of my companions to your device. I know them well.”

Lois stared upwards in disbelief. The bug had been microscopic. Even a Kryptonian wouldn’t have been able to find it unless they had known it was there.

Reign smiled viciously. “You can thank Lena Luthor for figuring out your little scheme, and Kara Zor-El for telling me just in time. Fortunately, they won’t have to live with the guilt of your death. They won’t know what happened to you. All your secrets follow you into the grave.”

She forced herself to slow her breathing. Lois Lane didn’t give up that easily. And she never, ever, failed to report the facts. Her eyes flicked over her shoulder. All she had to do was make it to civilization. How far was she from the city?

“A shame,” Reign said, descending to the ground several feet away. “You were on the list. You’ve doomed yourself through your actions, and there is no escape.”

Consequences

Lois clenched her teeth. What hope did she have? Even with the Harun-el running in her veins, she couldn’t hope to defeat Reign. Trying to run probably wouldn’t work out any better. Reign was definitely faster than she was.

A cold, unfamiliar emotion trailed down her spine. This wasn’t fear. This was terror.

There was the syringe in her pocket. If she could stab the alien with the hardened nth metal needle, it would split Sam from Reign. But what exactly would that entail?

It might not even slow Reign down. What if she just splits from Sam and keeps attacking? Or it might kill them both. Damn it…there’s too many unknowns here! I can’t risk it. Then again, what choice do I have?!

“This isn’t entirely your fault,” Reign continued. “You have your friends to thank. If Lena hadn’t figured out your scheme and Kara hadn’t been so quick to alert me, you would have won. So close. Instead-”

The alien darted forward. Lois was ready; she’d already started to run. Unfortunately, that bought her less than a second before Reign tackled her into the ground with the force of a bulldozer.

I don’t think so.

Being a superhero’s girlfriend had taught her a few tricks. Lois launched her forehead backwards, slamming into the alien’s face and eliciting a satisfying grunt of pain. The reporter turned around, scrambling back to her feet-

SLAM! Reign recovered and renewed her tackle, slamming Lois back into the ground. A hand reached around her throat, squeezing it shut. The reporter heaved against her enemy, but her lower body was now pinned beneath the alien’s knees.

Lois struggled desperately, slamming her fist repeatedly into Reign’s stomach, but the Kryptonian’s lips only tightened in anger.

“You’re even weaker than Alex Danvers. Less Harun-el in your system? Don’t worry, it will be over soon.”

As her vision blackened, Lois’s thoughts turned to the syringe in her pocket. If she could just reach it! Yet her arms were both pinned, and the alien’s grip on her throat was only growing tighter…

\

Reign smiled viciously as her enemy fell into unconsciousness.

To think that a pathetic human had come so close to unraveling so many of her plans. If Lois had managed to communicate the truth, Reign would have found herself ambushed and separated from her host within the day. The thought only spurred her to tighten her grip even further.

Any second now, the reporter’s neck would snap and-

NO!  

A tremendous spasm of pain erupted in her forehead. Reign collapsed to the ground, rolling away from the unconscious reporter and clutching at her temple. She’d never felt pain like this. Never. What the hell was happening?

And then the answer popped into her head. Through the pain, the Worldkiller smiled. So, the inevitable confrontation had finally come.

Sam awoke in total darkness.

She was floating in the middle of a pitch-black void. Weightless, yet nearly motionless. Panic permeated her entire being, yet there was some strange sense of familiarity about her surroundings.

I’ve been here before. In a dream, maybe? Or is this a dream?

Light exploded into her vision as an image appeared in front of her. It was two dimensional, almost like a television screen, yet Sam felt as if he could reach into it. She raised her arms, stretching through the empty blackness towards the projection.

Her limbs felt like they were made of lead. Inch by inch, they reached for the screen. On it, Lois Lane was lying on the ground in the middle of the desert. It looked like she was looking through someone’s eyes, staring down at the reporter.

Then her fingertips brushed the projection.

Sam’s mind split into two. Half of her was still floating in the void, helpless. The rest of her was back in her body and staring down at Lois Lane. She tried to move, but her limbs barely obeyed her. Collapsing to her knees, she cried out in fear. “What is happening to me?!”

A foreign will clamped down on her lips, preventing Sam from moving them more than millimeters. Then they spoke of their own accord. “There is no you. Not anymore.”

That same foreign will crashed into her consciousness, knocking all of Sam out of her body and back into the void.

On the screen, the image shifted as her physical body collapsed into the ground. The last thing that could be seen was the ground rocketing up towards her vision before the eyelids clamped shut. Within the void, the encompassing darkness returned.

Then, to her left, two red pupils illuminated the area around her. There was someone else here with her! As Sam’s eyes took in the sight, all she could do was choke in shock.

She was looking at herself! The doppelganger’s eyes blazed with red energy, and she was clad in a dark supersuit, but it was the body of Sam Arias. There was no doubt.

“Who are you?!” the CFO demanded. “Where are we?!”

Her clone shrugged. “This is nothing more than a representation of our shared consciousness. Where I’ve been waiting for years, seeing through your eyes.”

Nausea sprouted in her chest. This…this foreign presence had been staring through her vision for years? Why? How?

“As my power grew, I was able to assume control for brief periods,” the clone gestured towards the blackened monitor. “Each time, you would wait here, unconscious. Your mind would make fake memories all on its own. Since you’ve now managed to awaken here, it proves that this is finally your permanent home. You will watch me for the rest of eternity.”

Sam spasmed in the darkness, but the center of her body was rooted in place. “T-this is impossible! I’m Samantha Arias! There’s nothing else inside me! I…I’m going insane!”

“No, not insane,” the other individual smiled. “Your panic is perfectly understandable given the situation you’re in. You’re going to watch as I assume your life and fulfill my destiny.”

Her horror magnified. “Ruby-”

The clone smiled. “Her situation will be no worse than the rest of humanity’s. Though I wonder how long it will take for her to realize her mother is gone forever? Or…should I instead make her believe that she was never loved from the start?”

“You!” The CFO reached out, desperate to claw out the other woman’s eyes, but the clone was safely out of reach. “Lay a finger on my daughter and you’ll wish you never left this place.”

“Don’t give me any headaches and perhaps I’ll tell her the truth one day,” the clone said. “I’m sure you still have many questions. But watching that screen will make everything clear in time. It’s quite a puzzle to put together, and I wouldn’t want to deprive you of your only source of entertainment for the rest of eternity.”

Suspended helplessly in her new prison, the CFO watched as the clone reached for the monitor. Sam tried to touch it first, but her limbs would barely budge. That same foreign will kept her in place.

Sensing her struggle, the clone sent her a small smile. Then her fingertips touched the surface of the monitor, and the doppelganger vanished completely. Leaving Sam alone.

Forever.

Ow…  

Coughing violently, Lois returned to consciousness. The Harun-el in her system might have prevented any bruising, but her throat was still a hotbed of pain. Her eyes flickered open, revealing the sun still shining brightly overhead.

I’m alive? She didn’t kill me? I have to-

 Reign was on the ground in front of her, slowly stirring. Lois didn’t know what had incapacitated the Worldkiller, but it didn’t matter. This was her chance! Taking the syringe out of her pocket, Lois advanced on her enemy without delay.

Reign’s eyelids open half a second too early.

“You!” The Kryptonian’s hand shot up, seizing Lois’s arm. The needlepoint clutched in her fingers was an inch away from the alien’s skin. Reign’s eyes widened in surprise. “What is…ah, Jess’s Harun-el. You were trying to split me from Samantha. How convenient for you. Or it would have been, I suppose.”

Lois’s free limbs lashed out, but Reign calmly absorbed her blows. “Yes, Black Kryptonite does interfere with the spell keeping me attached to my host. You’ve really come close to victory several times today. Unfortunately for you, destiny favors the righteous.”

The alien’s other arm slammed into Lois’s shoulder, sending the reporter back onto the ground. Screaming with fury, Lois desperately tried to throw her enemy off.

“Spell?! There’s no such thing as magic!” she heard herself hissing.

Reign smirked. “There are primal forces at the very heart of our universe. My people are simply advanced enough to access their power. The dark magic that birthed the Worldkillers was only one of our achievements.”

“KARA!” Lois yelled.

A spark of alarm in her eyes, Reign looked up. As Lois continued to struggle beneath her, the alien shrugged. “She must not be listening for you. A shame. Kryptonian hearing is only good if-”

Lois spit in her face.

“Ah!” The alien reeled back, reflexively wiping the moisture out of her eyes. With all of her strength, Lois heaved Reign off of her and rolled to her feet.

Lois leapt forward, intent on plunging the Harun-el into her enemy’s chest. Reign recovered just in time, jumping into the air and hovering a dozen feet above the ground. Her eyes brimmed with red energy.

BLAST!

The twin beams of light exploded at Lois’s feet, sending the reporter sprawling across the ground. By the time she knew what was happening, Reign was already on her. An iron grip was once again closing around her throat, and the arm that held the syringe was pinned beneath one of the alien’s knees.

Her trapped arm brushing against her own leg, Lois tried to angle the needle upward, but the distance between her hand and Reign’s skin was too great. Within seconds she would be unconscious and as good as dead.

Unless…

Reign smiled softly as her grip tightened on her enemy’s throat. All she would have to do is burn the body to a crisp and dispose of the ashes. No one would ever hear of Lois Lane again. Luthor and her cronies might be suspicious, but there would be nothing tying trusted CFO Samantha Arias to the disappearance.

“AHHH!”

A scream erupted beneath her. The next second, Reign was being hurled through the air by a strength she had never before experienced. She stopped her momentum only after several seconds, coming to a halt in midair and assessing her foe.

Lois was climbing to her feet. But how? Only a real Kryptonian should ever have been able to wield that strength! The Harun-el would never be able to-

The Harun-el. Lois had injected herself. The double dosage had vastly increased her strength, but her time was now at an end. All Reign would have to do is hold her in place and…

Two bright blue beams slammed into the Worldkiller, sending her rocketing back through the air. By the time she stopped herself, skidding across the ground, Lois Lane had already vanished from sight.

Reign looked around, extending her vision in every direction, but there was nothing. The Harun-el had enhanced Lois’s abilities. How long would it take to snap her mind? Long enough for her to find a friendly face?

If she had flown away, chasing after her was a lost cause. It was time to get to L-Corp. There, she could present herself an alibi and report her side of the story if Lois indeed managed to find help. And if the reporter was able to prove her claims? Then it would give Reign one last opportunity to snap Lena Luthor’s neck.

Lois had heard the warnings. She knew the danger of having too much Harun-el in her system. Her DNA would be overloaded, quickly leading to brain trauma and condemning her to death. But what else was there? At least her death might mean something.

The second she injected the needle into herself and hit the plunger, her world became a firestorm of pain.

She wasn’t aware of throwing Reign aside and blasting her with heat vision, or of her own sudden launch into the sky. It wasn’t until Lois was thousands of feet above the Earth’s surface that the thinning air finally jolted her back to reality.

Weightless. Suspended in the air. Was this what he…what Clark felt like when he flew?  

The agony was almost all consuming. Her entire body felt like it was on fire; the white-hot flames sprouting from her brain. Lois had to do something. She had to tell them…tell them that Sam was her, and that the Harun-stuff could split her.

“Need to find someone. Lucy! She’s in the city, right? Visiting!” Her hearing called out as she flew back down to Earth, seeking her sister’s voice.

And she needed to find her sister to tell her something! What was it? Her. The woman was her and nobody knew it! The Harun could fix that. Everyone needed to know!

So much pain…

Lena looked up as Sam walked into her office, clad in her typical business suit.

“I just got Kara’s message,” the CFO reported. “I’m sorry; I was catching up with some old friends at the new sushi place that just opened up. Any news?”

“Nothing,” the villain sighed. “Kara is bringing Jess back here, but we have no idea where Lois is.” Lena mentally berated herself yet again. She should have noticed sooner. The signs had been right in front of her!

“I’m sure she means well,” Sam replied reassuringly. “What’s the worst that can happen? She can take care of herself, and she’d not going to do anything that could hurt Kara.”

Lena nodded, resisting the urge to shudder. “I know. But I have a bad feeling about this.”

Lucy was sitting in James’s office, calmly discussing the latest news from CatCo. Even if she only had a few more hours to spend in National City, it was hard to resist spending a few hours talking with an old friend. At one time, she’d thought they could have been more. Maybe, one day, if they were living in the same city again…

“Trying to stay clear of L-Corp related news is like trying to avoid heat in a forest fire,” James was saying. “The last thing we want is to take a stance on what Lena is doing; we could turn off half of our readers in an instant. And-”

BOOM!

The window exploded. Shards of glass hurtled into the room, the sheer force of the impact knocking James’s desk onto the floor. Standing…floating...in the middle of the chaos was Lois, her hands clutching her head tightly.

“What the hell?” James sputtered, having been knocked off his chair. His eyes widened as he beheld the intruder. “Lois? What are you-”

Lois collapsed to her knees, groaning with pain. “I have to…have to tell you. The alien. She is the world…killer. She’s her!”

“You need help,” Lucy declared. “We need to get help! What happened to you?”

She moved towards her sister, who was now spasming wildly on the floor. “Injected myself with the…secretary’s Harun. Had too. You need to know. It can fix her. Split her! You need to split the…the…!”

Lucy was barely listening to her sister’s nonsense. All she knew was that Lois was in serious trouble, and it was getting worse. “Lois, please.” Gently but firmly, she placed her hands on her sister’s body. “James, get help!”

He was already rapidly dialing numbers into his phone. CatCo employees were congregating outside of the office, staring into the bizarre scene, but Lucy only had eyes for one person.

“Lois?” her sister moaned. “No, it wasn’t her. That…wasn’t…the name. I need the name! What…was it?! You’re not listening!” The reporter thrashed around again, rolling away from Lucy’s touch and towards the shattered window.

Tears of incredulous terror streaking down her face, Lucy moved after her sister.

“Ahhh! It’s burning. Everything is burning!” A blast of blue energy erupted from her eyes, launching out of the window and into the sky. A stampede of feet ensued as employees desperately tried to clear the area.

Her legs jerking uncontrollably, Lois convulsed onto her knees. A gush of vomit spilled from her mouth. No! Not vomit. Blood.

Oh my god! This was more than bad. It was…this couldn’t be happening!

“She is her, she is her,” Lois was whispered repeatedly. “Black…kryptonite. Split it! Fix it!” Another torrent of blood fell from her lips, rolling across the hardwood floor. “Split…split what? I don’t…forget. I…why am I…”

James knelt by her side. His hands were shaking. “Lena’s coming. We’ll fix what the Harun-el did to you. Just hang on! Lois, you can’t…”

Lois took a shuddering breath. As Lucy’s heart rate spiked ever higher, her sister’s body began to calm down. The spasms subsided into intermittent twitching. Blood steadily flowed from her nostrils, even as her breathing began to slow.

“NO!” Lucy shouted, lifting the reporter out of the pool of blood. “Get something to staunch the bleeding!”

Her sister’s eyes were wandering, unfocused. “It’s over. I can see him.”

“You can’t go!” Lucy sobbed. “I won’t let you. I need you, sis.  We promised to protect each other! Clark wanted you to live! That’s what you deserve! You’re...you're all I have left!”

A small smile appeared on Lois’s lips. “He always said hope…hope…bigger than anyone. Any person. Eternal,” she said, her breath shuddering. “What a farmboy…” she scoffed, her eyes faintly glinting with amusement.

And that was the end.

\

They were sitting in the couches of Lena’s office. Lena, Kara, Jess, Sam, and all of the Superfriends. Lucy was so silent she could have been mistaken for catatonic. The rest were choking back tears, or doing their best to pretend that their world hadn’t just been crushed.

Kara was sitting on the couch next to Lena, still sobbing into the CEO’s shoulder. The villain would have given anything to erase a fraction of that pain, but even with all the power in the world she was helpless.

In the three hours since Lois’s death, Sam had volunteered to investigate the situation. It made sense. Sam was empathetic enough to be motivated, but not close enough to Lois to be emotionally compromised.

More importantly, she had Lena’s complete trust.

Lois had been investigating potential moles within L-Corp right before her death. The simplest situation wasn’t always the correct one, but it had to be considered first. Lena had needed someone she trusted to investigate the matter, and they had all been on Lois’s list of suspects.

Footage from the restaurant and L-Corp had Sam on film for all but fifteen minutes of that day. Lena had tested her CFO’s DNA personally. She was a human, and a human could never make it from the restaurant to L-Corp in fifteen minutes with time to spare. Sam was accounted for during Lois’s death, and that was all that Lena had needed.

“Her system was infused with triple the Harun-el her DNA could accommodate,” Sam was explaining. “It burned through her within minutes.”

“It doesn’t make sense!” Winn stood up off his chair. “Why would Lois take more of it? We all knew how dangerous it was!”

Everyone looked to Sam. Even Kara raised her head to stare at the CFO curiously.

“It didn’t make sense to me, either,” Sam said. “Not until I went into our archives and uncovered some new information.” Reaching into her purse, she pulled out two folded-up pieces of paper. “This is Lois’s compatibility report concerning the Harun-el. And this is our record of how much she was injected with. They don’t match.”

Lena reached out, seizing both of the papers. This…this couldn’t be right. According to the numbers, Lois had been injected with two percent more Harun-el than she had been cleared for.

Sam sighed sadly. “It wasn’t enough to kill her, but it did unbalance her mentally. Enough to lead her to making rash decisions like kidnapping Jess…or injecting herself with more Harun-el once she got her hands on it.”

Jess gasped. “What about…?”

“Everyone else is clear,” Sam assured her. “Their dosages match their compatibility. Lois was the only discrepancy.”

Kara took a shuddering breath. “How did this happen?” she demanded pleadingly. “Who the hell could mix up something that important?”

All eyes turned to Lena. They were waiting for the name of the scientist responsible, but the answer was closer than any of them realized.  

No. I couldn’t have! I double checked everything! She reminded herself. But Lena had been out of sorts that day, hadn’t she? Kara’s identity had just been exposed, and Reign had used her to murder the last Martian. Had that been enough for her to…?

“I prepare every dosage of Harun-el myself,” Lena whispered. “I…I made that sample. These reports don’t match, but I couldn’t have….I couldn’t…”

She didn’t raise her gaze. At that moment, Lena would have traded everything she owned…all of her plans…if it meant she would never have to look into Kara’s furious, accusatory stare.

Chapter End Notes

I am capable of more cruelty than I realized.

Nonsense

She was watching from above.

It was a crisp winter morning in Metropolis. In the city’s central park, a funeral was currently being held for one of the nation’s most famous reporters. The details of her death were unknown by the public, and attendance at the event had been restricted to those who knew Ms. Lane personally. Even still, it was quite a crowd.

Lena wasn’t there. She had no right to stand amidst the mourners, all of whom were there because of her carelessness. Yet she refused to wait in National City as the woman she had killed was laid to rest. Instead, Vanity was perched on the roof of a far-off skyscraper, watching from a distance.

Kara had probably seen her. Supergirl’s vision was more than capable of spotting a supervillain sitting half a mile away. So far, however, the hero had done nothing to acknowledge her presence. As painful as that was for Lena, the alternative would have felt even worse.

Her only company was the mocking voice of her dead brother, helpfully called up by Lena’s own imagination.

You’ve surpassed me, sis. I might have killed Superman, but you’re the one who’s destroyed what he loved most! You are a Luthor after all.

Lena grit her teeth as she watched the casket be lowered into the ground. No. She was nothing like Lex. Her brother had killed out of malice and jealousy. Lena had simply made a mistake.

Because her life meant nothing to you. All you care about is ruling the world. Just like I did. You might be willing to accept aliens in your regime, but only because you want to have their abilities under your control. I’m proud of you, sister!

The worst part was that the voice was right. Lex would have been proud.

\

I never thought supervillain strategy meetings would be so boring.

Why Alex had even been included in this meeting of Lena’s inner circle, the security chief didn’t know. Yes, she was Supergirl’s sister, and yes Lena trusted her despite their previous animosity, but still.

Most of Lena’s trusted associates and high-ranking L-Corp executives were still there, except for Thomas Colville. The VP of finance was home after having caught a rather nasty bout of flu that had been going around. The longer this meeting went on, the more Alex envied him.

“Vanity’s primary objective has been fulfilled,” Lena was saying at the head of the table. “There’s no longer much intellectual property out there that’s worth stealing. From now on, I’ll be saving the suit for emergency situations and concentrating on our other efforts.”

Alex supposed learning the details of Lena’s plan for world domination had been interesting. It was a two-pronged approach: subvert, blackmail, and replace prominent world leaders while simultaneously gaining primacy in every technological and financial market.

Two separate strategies that nevertheless supported one another. The more powerful figures under her control, the easier it was for L-Corp to expand its market and financial influence. And the more influential L-Corp became, the easier it was to find the weaknesses of politicians and powerbrokers and exploit them.

Lena’s brilliant mind had made L-Corp’s expansion trivially easy at times. The patents she’d unveiled in every field made the company’s products irresistible to anyone hoping to remain competitive in the modern world. Stealing the ideas and data of rival corporations had all but eliminated any obstacles in the market.

L-Corp wasn’t simply a company any longer. In the span of a year, it had become the linchpin of human society. With an unassailable position in every market and an ever-rising stock price, there was simply no escaping its influence. As impressive as it was, even as an employee of L-Corp, the security chief couldn’t help but view the company’s rise as somewhat unsettling.

Alex glanced at Lena, the woman whose net worth had crossed into the trillions and been ballooning ever since. At least it’s a benevolent dictatorship. Most of the CEO’s money was either being funneled into charitable organizations or reinvested back into L-Corp’s projects.

World domination wasn’t yet in her grasp, but it was slowly coming into view. With Kaznia as a model, L-Corp would soon be announcing plans to take control of other struggling nations throughout the world. Cooperation, either willing or otherwise, from their current leadership would keep things running smoothly enough.

The developed nations were quickly falling more and more under L-Corp’s control thanks to the two-tiered strategy. By the end of the next year, Lena would be powerful and popular enough to push through Constitutional changes in nearly every nation that mattered. By that time, any dissenters who wanted to resist would find armed rebellion almost in possible; the world’s strongest militaries would be running entirely on L-Corp technology.

One would think that having her wildest ambitions coming true would make Lena Luthor happy. But Alex had never seen the supervillain look so miserable. She was hiding it as best she could today, but the dull gaze and flat voice were giving the game away.

Was it partially Lena’s fault that Lois was dead? Maybe. Lucy and James certainly felt that way. Alex herself hadn’t been sure of what to think for a few days. Sam hadn’t made any move to push their relationship forward in the past week, which Alex silently appreciated. They would both still be there when Alex’s thoughts cleared.

And now, mostly, they had. Which meant that it was time for her to fix this mess.

\

“Alex, you don’t have an appointment,” Lena heard Jess say reluctantly.

“Your boss has been moping for seven days,” Alex’s voice replied back. “If you don’t think she needs a wakeup call, then don’t let me in.”

There was a pause outside. Even as the CEO mentally willed her secretary to do her job, Jess’s voice cut through the silence. “No. I can’t let you in. I’m sorry, but I have my orders and no one gets into Ms. Luthor’s office without an appointment while I’m here.”

Thank you, Jess.  

Unfortunately, Jess continued speaking. “Oh, look at that.” Through the frosted glass, Lena could see her secretary make a show of checking her watch. “It’s time for break. I’m off to lunch; see you later Alex.” Jess stood up, heading for the elevator.

Say goodbye to your raise.

“Lena.” Alex burst through the door. “Call your driver. You’re going to Kara’s apartment and putting an end to this nonsense.”

The supervillain frowned. “She doesn’t want to talk to me, and I don’t blame her. If Kara wants to find me, she knows where to look. I’m giving her as much space as she needs.”

Alex rolled her eyes. “You’ve been living in your office safehouse for a week. Kara’s in her apartment. The apartment you gave her. Doesn’t that sound kind of strange to you?”

“Gifts aren’t conditional,” Lena replied, glaring hard into the other woman’s eyes. “She needs a place to stay, and she wouldn’t feel comfortable sleeping a floor below a woman she hates.”

“Kara doesn’t hate you!”

Lena sighed. “Of course she does. I don’t blame her. I didn’t want Lois dead, but I was careless enough to let it happen. Just like with J’onn Jonz. Like with-” she stopped herself. Kara was the only one who knew that Lena Luthor had all but let her mother die, and it was going to stay that way.

“We don’t even know that for sure,” Alex pointed out. “And even if you made a mistake…Lois would have understood. The Martian had just been murdered and Kara’s identity was exposed. You were giving her friends the most valuable substance on Earth so that they wouldn’t be targets. A slight miscalculation-”

“Isn’t forgivable,” the villain interrupted. “Not from me. I’m Lena Luthor, genius trillionaire CEO who’s going to rule the world and save it from invasion. I don’t make stupid mistakes. I’m not supposed to.”

Alex smiled sadly, taking a seat in front of Lena’s desk. “Impossibly high IQ or not, you’re only human.”

“Yeah,” Lena whispered, the words coming out seemingly of their own accord. “I can’t even protect people from my own experiments, yet I’m going to defend the entire planet. Maybe you were right the first time.”

The security chief sent her a confused frown. “About what?”

Lena’s eyes fell to the pristine white carpet. Of all the people to say this to…but who else was there? Kara didn’t even want to be near her.

“Me and my big plan,” Lena replied bitterly. “I definitely can take over the world, but maybe I’m not fit for the job. Lois Lane died because I was careless. So did J’onn Jonz. I can’t use stupidity as an excuse, clearly. Perhaps I’m more like Lex than I thought…obsessed with control, and uncaring of the little people who get hurt along the way. Kara knows that now. Why do you think she hates me?”

One second, Alex was sitting peacefully in her chair. The next, she had seized a mostly-full water bottle and hurled its contents at the CEO.

Drenched, Lena stood up from her chair and furiously wiped the moisture from her eyes.

“There was a time I would have given anything to separate you from Kara and stop you from taking over the world,” Alex sighed. “Oh, the irony. Lena, you’re not perfect, but everyone knew that already. Sure, you might fuck it up, but if you don’t take over the world…humanity is already dead.”

Well, that might be true, but if Lena screwed up…

“L-Corp believes in you. Hell, you convinced me, and I tried to shoot you a few months ago!” Alex’s arms lifted in exasperation. “You won’t be ruling the world alone, so stop acting like everything will be your fault.”

Lena couldn’t help but smile slightly. “I suppose I did win you over. A lot faster than I expected, too.”

Alex jumped to her feet. “Then call your driver and get to your girlfriend. Better yet, just put your suit on and fly over to her. I’m sick of the two of you pointlessly moping around.”

The CEO’s smile faded. “Nothing would make me happier than to have her back, but I won’t force her into it. If she hasn’t come to see me, it’s because she doesn’t want to. Don’t believe me? Then go ask her yourself.”

“Where is she?” Reign seethed.

Purity winced. “She hasn’t reported in, and the illness is spreading. It looks like…she’s gone rogue. We have no way of tracking her.”

Bitch! Pestilence had always been the most impatient of the Worldkillers, but Reign had never expected her to desert. How could anyone with a part their glorious, divine-given mission choose to   abandon it for the simple pleasure of slaughter?

“She must have decided that she would never be able to unleash her full power if we kept to the plan,” Purity noted.

Reign clenched her fists. “We need chattel. Killing them en masse won’t advance our aims. She must be stopped.”

“How?”

The Worldkiller took a deep breath. This development was doubly troubling. If Pestilence went unchecked, there was no telling how many humans would be killed by the Blight. There was no chance that Luthor would be among them, thanks to the artificial black kryptonite in her veins. If anything, a plague might even enhance Luthor’s position. The panic would make it far easier to seize control. 

And without Pestilence’s powers on their side, taking Luthor down would be significantly harder. That meant more potential casualties when the colonization began. 

“We kill her,” Reign decided. “The magic that powers her abilities won’t be destroyed so easily. It will flow into the nearest vessel of Yuda Kal.”

Purity frowned. “But how do we kill her? You’ll never receive her power if we don’t track her down. She’s been careful to remain in hiding. So?”

Reign nodded. “So we get some help.”
