Knock! Knock!

Kara groaned. After taking down two rogue aliens in the space of an hour, all she’d wanted to do was relax in the comfort of her apartment alone. Unfortunately, judging by what her vision saw on the other side of the door, Alex seemed to have other plans.

The hero hopped off the couch and walked over to the door. “Is this important, Alex?” she asked glumly as she let her sister in. “I’ve had a long day.”

“You could say it’s important.” Alex’s voice was deadly firm. “It’s time for this nonsense to end. Go fly to your girlfriend’s office and let her know that everything is fine. A week of moping around is enough.”

Kara grimaced, falling back into a chair. “Alex, I can’t. After Lois…”

Alex was standing over her, arms at her sides. “Lois wouldn’t have wanted you to break things off with her. She wanted you to be happy,” her sister reminded her. “I know who you are Kara, and that’s someone who will miss Lois for the rest of your life. But you’re not the kind of person who will hold a grudge against a good person who might have accidentally contributed to her death. Especially not a person you love.”

“You don’t know me,” Kara said softly. Her hands trembling slightly, she forced them down onto her knees. Alex didn’t understand. She couldn’t.

The security chief sat down across from her. “You’re telling me you’re angry at Lena? I don’t buy it. If you were angry, you would have confronted her. You wouldn’t be hiding in your apartment while she sleeps in her office! That’s not Kara Danvers.”

Supergirl stood up, her frustration boiling over. “I’m more than Kara Danvers! I’m Kara Zor-el, and I have a legacy on my shoulders. I’m all that’s left of Krypton, and I can’t go back on my mission! I’d never forgive myself.”

Alex was incredulous. “Your mission? Protecting the Earth is your mission! Avoiding Lena doesn’t have anything to do with that!”

“My parents didn’t tell me to protect the world,” Kara revealed. “They told me to protect Kal, and I promised them that I would. That was the last thing I ever said to them. Then my pod got knocked off course, and he died before I could become a hero.” She sighed, slumping into her chair. “That wasn’t my fault. But I can still protect Kal by upholding his legacy. If I don’t, he died in vain…and I lied to my parents right before they died.”

There was a long pause.

“Kara.” Alex leaned forward, forcing the hero to look up. “I get it.You think you have to follow Clark’s example. He loved Lois more than anything. We both know he never would have forgiven Lena for playing a part in her death. You think that by doing so, you’re betraying him.” It wasn’t a question.

Supergirl forced her gaze back to the floor. “I know you think it’s stupid. But on Krypton, family was more important than anything. They’re all gone, Alex. I have to make them proud. If I still uphold their example, their lives meant something. If I don’t, I fail…Krypton might as well never have existed at all.”

“You failed a long time ago.”

Kara’s eyes shot up to meet her sister’s, bristling with shock and anger. “Excuse me?” she demanded.

“Clark would be so disappointed in you. Superman would never have become friends with Lena Luthor. He put principles above everything. Truth, justice, and the American way, remember?” Alex replied hotly. “He would have hated Lena and done everything he could have to arrest her. You…you might not agree with everything she does, but you’ve forgiven her for all of it. You love her. Hell, you even let her keep imprisoning people and get away with controlling the leader of the free world. Clark would have died before he let that happen.”

Heat was brimming in Kara’s pupils. “Kal protected people. That’s what I do! He wouldn’t have-”

“Gone after Lena?” Alex finished for her. “Oh yes he would have, and you know it. And unlike you, he never would have given up. He was a great hero, Kara, but he was the model of idealism. He wouldn’t have tolerated Lena’s methods for a second. And he would be horrified to see you do the same.”

Kara stepped forward menacingly. “Get out!” she snarled.

Alex shook her head. “You need a reality check. Clark is dead. Krypton is gone. They both did amazing things, and the universe was better because they existed. But they’re gone now. Everything dies eventually,” she said, her voice softening slightly. “Kara Zor-el is still here. She needs to live her life for herself, and do what she thinks is right.”

“And it would be right to dishonor my promise to my parents and the memory of my cousin?” Clark would never have been friends with Lena, Alex was right about that, but he might have stopped trying to arrest her once he saw all the good she did for world. But he never would have forgiven her for Lois’s death. If Kara did so, she would be turning her back on his legacy and spitting on his grave.

“They got their chance to live their lives and do what they thought was right. You deserve the same. You can’t spend the rest of your life living in the past!” the security chief rebutted. “Dying doesn’t give someone the right to dictate the lives of the living. Those of us who survive have to move forward with our own lives.”

Billions of souls had died when Krypton exploded. The planet was now a chunk of scattered, barren rocks. One of the two survivors was dead. If the other moved on…

“Maybe that’s true for most people, Alex, but I have the legacy of an entire planet on my shoulders. And the legacy of a hero who died saving the Earth. I can’t ignore that.”

Alex huffed. “Clark’s legacy isn’t yours. It doesn’t belong to you just because you’re his cousin. It survives in everyone he saved. It spreads when those people have their own effect on the world. Just like Krypton’s. All of the beings throughout the universe who were influenced by the Kryptonians and influenced others in turn...that’s Krypton’s legacy, even if people don’t remember it.”

“I won’t let my world be forgotten, Alex. I-”

“That’s not up to you, either,” her sister interjected. “It will be forgotten, one day. Just like Earth. But just because the memory of something is gone doesn’t mean that it didn’t matter, Kara! You get to make your own legacy now. That’s what Lois did! She loved Clark more than anyone, and she was willing to work with Lena even when she knew it was something he would have hated. She would have forgiven Lena for her own death.”

Kara’s hand unconsciously rested upon the hidden crest on her chest. “Lois wasn’t his family.”

“She would have been,” Alex said. “And I’m sorry to say this, but she had a better claim on his legacy than you do. You were born into his family. He chose her to be a part of his.”

Supergirl slouched back into her chair. A lot of what her sister made sense, yet she couldn’t just turn her back on her family, could she? Kara had tried to come to Earth and lose herself in humanity, but Kara Danvers had never really worked. Blending in had never felt completely right to her. Earth was amazing, but it wasn’t her home. She wanted to escape the burden of Krypton’s memory, but it had never been possible.

Could she do it now? If Kara Zor-el let go of her heritage, what would be left? An alien refugee lost and adrift on a planet that had never felt right, constantly trying to do good deeds in order to try and fill the void left by a dead family and a vanished civilization? As long as Kara upheld the legacy of her people, Krypton still lived. She couldn’t survive without it.

Can I?

“Alex…I need some time to think.”

Turning away from her sister, Kara moved towards the window. Opening the glass, she stared out into the city below.

“Where are you going?” Her sister’s concerned voice followed her.

Kara frowned. It was a good question.

“Somewhere quiet,” she decided.

Nightmare

“Hey Alex. Come in.”

“Thanks,” Alex replied, stepping into her boss’s apartment. Something about her nervous energy must have leaked through her exterior, because Sam immediately frowned.

“Is something wrong?”

The security chief fell down into the sofa. “Of course. Lena and my sister. Kara’s going through a lot right now. I hope…I think she’ll work it out in the end, but I hate seeing her suffer like this. Lena isn’t any better. She’s just throwing herself into work for the sake of distraction.”

Sam sat down across from her. “I know,” the CFO said. “She’s working so much she’s having to find busy work. Can you imagine how hard that is when you’re a CEO who’s trying to take over the world? I think she’s making a backup for her suit.”

Huh? “I thought she already had backups?”

Her boss shook her head. “That’s what she likes to say. But right now, all of her replacements are nowhere near as sophisticated as the real thing. Basically for ‘emergencies only’. I think she inflated their capabilities to dissuade Kara from trying to steal her suit in the first place.”

“That would make sense,” Alex agreed. “But you would think having one suit would be enough for the moment. Kara’s the only one who would be able to get close enough to steal it, and I don’t find that likely anymore. So…she’s just trying to bury herself in work.”

Sam nodded. “Pretty much. But aside from worrying about your sister,” she said, changing the subject, “How are you feeling?”

When your sister is Supergirl, who has time to worry about anything else? “I’ve been better. Lois still has me in shock…it hasn’t sunk in yet.” As her chest panged, Alex looked around the room for a distraction. “Where’s Ruby?”

“At a friend’s house for the night. I wanted to speak with you…alone. We need to talk.”

Panic flared in Alex’s mind. There was no way that her girlfriend saying those words, in that tone, could mean anything good.

Sam sighed. “Our company is about to go into the final stages of its plan for world domination. I have a daughter hitting puberty. You had a family friend just die and you’re spending half your time worrying about your sister. I think…” she trailed off briefly, standing up. “I think you and I have enough to be worrying about without dealing with…us.”

No! Alex wouldn’t give up the one bright spot in her life so easily. Not now.

“Sam, it’s fine,” Alex said hurriedly. “We can handle it. I can handle it. I know I’ve been out of sorts since Lois died, but I’ve enjoyed every minute with you. This-” she gestured in the air between them- “Keeps me going.”

Sheer terror was keeping the security chief sitting on the couch. She couldn’t feel her legs.

That terror only intensified as Sam turned away. “You have no idea how much this hurts me, Alex. Really, you don’t. But I have to make decisions that are best for my company, my boss, and most importantly my daughter.”

Sheer indignation finally gave Alex the energy to rise. “How is us being together bad for Ruby?” she demanded, springing to her feet. “She wants you to be happy. She worries about you. How will this make her feel any better?”

“Ruby needs to focus on herself,” Sam replied, turning back. There was a cold edge to her voice now. “And I need to focus on her. I can’t do that if I’m both working as the CFO of the largest company in the world and dating my chief of security. I’m sorry, Alex. It’s over.”

Alex would not cry. She would not punch a hole in the apartment’s wall just to let out some of her anger. Instead, she focused her gaze on Sam. “I can’t believe someone so smart could be so stupid!” she vented. “You want me gone? Fine, I’m gone.” This is a nightmare, right? It has to be a nightmare. “I’ll talk to Lena tomorrow morning about being reassigned. Goodbye, Ms. Arias.”

She turned away, storming out of the apartment.

Well, that was fun.

Reign smirked to herself as Alex Danvers disappeared down the hallway. It would have been even more entertaining to let her down hard, saying that she was ending their relationship purely because she’d grown to hate the security chief. Unfortunately, that would have sent a few too many red flags to Lena Luthor.

With their plans coming to fruition, she couldn’t have Alex Danvers snooping around her life. The woman might be on the list, but that in no way forced the Worldkiller to spare her emotions. Now all Reign would have to do was continue to keep Sam’s annoying daughter at arm’s length and there would be no other complications.

Her cell phone buzzed. Pulling out the device from her pocket, Reign entered her incredibly long password at superspeed before reading the message.

I found her.

\

Perhaps it wasn’t monument Kal would have wanted, but it was one he deserved.

He would have hated it, Kara knew. Superman would have wanted an average grave situated in a cemetery like any other. But this memorial wasn’t for him, not really. It was for the citizens of Metropolis. The giant obelisk in the center of the park, emblazoned with the El family crest on its largest side, was meant to be an enduring symbol of hope for all who could see it.

Kara was sitting on a high rooftop on the perimeter of the park, staring at the crest of her family etched in marble. The last remnant of Krypton in this city. But in the end, stone was just stone. If Kara turned her back on her cousin’s ideals, would it be all that was left?

Supergirl sighed, turning her eyes to stare at the moon shining brightly above. Kal had always been a man of principle. Hadn’t he? That was always how he had presented himself to humanity. Had that been real, or just another mask? How often had he sat on these same rooftops, doubting himself?

Lois would have known. But Kara had never asked.

If she forgave Lena for what had happened to Lois, Kara would be turning her back on her cousin’s memory. It wasn’t easy standing in Kal’s shadow, but that didn’t mean she had any right to step away. Not when she was now the last scion of a world that was nothing but dust.

Of course…Kal hadn’t seemed to feel the same way. He hadn’t raised her himself, had he? Superman had left the only other survivor of his planet with another family. It had all worked out in the end, but had it been the right decision without the benefit of hindsight?

Kal had seen himself as a citizen of Earth, not a refugee from Krypton. Kara envied him. It would be a much easier existence. Less stressful. Peaceful.

Selfish.

“Kara Zor-El,” a voice echoed behind her.

Supergirl whipped around. Reign was touching down onto the gravel several meters away. Before Kara’s brain could even process the situation, twin blue blasts were streaming from her eyes. Reign met the attack with her own burst of heat vision.

Red and blue met in the center of the rooftop. Then, slowly, the point of intersection was slowly pushed back towards Kara. Supergirl unleashed all the energy she could muster, but the concussive force of Reign’s blast was too great.

Kara suddenly broke off her heat vision and dropped to the ground. Reign’s attack sailed above her, streaming out into the night. With a burst of superspeed, Kara closed the distance between them instantly.

WHAM! Supergirl’s fist lashed out at the villain’s midsection. Reign lowered her forearm to block, but the impact sent her skidding back several meters.

“I’m not here to fight!” Reign called out. “Do you really wish to face me here? There are innocents in every building, and our clash would destroy half of this city. See for yourself.” The alien nodded at a point over Kara’s shoulder.

Keeping one eye on Reign, Kara’s gaze slowly peeled around. Her vision was instantly directed to a sprout of flames. Reign’s blast had scorched the monument, melting and igniting some of the stone at the top of the obelisk.

Shaking with rage, Supergirl restrained herself. She could try to take the fight elsewhere, but there was no guarantee she would succeed. Reign was at least as strong and fast as she was, and Kara knew from Lena that the alien had no qualms about threatening innocents.

“What the hell do you want?!” the hero demanded.

Reign frowned. “Why such anger, Kara Zor-El? Are you not happy to meet another of your race?”

She IS a Kryptonian!

Kara’s teeth clenched. “Not when she threatens innocent people, murders captive aliens, and attempts to assassinate my girlfriend on multiple occasions. Who are you, and what do you want with this planet?”

“To remake it anew. Krypton is not as dead as you might think, daughter of Alura. It will rise again on this planet,” Reign replied. There was no derision or anger in her words. Instead, her voice seemed…happy?

The hero gasped. “What are you talking about? Are there others? How many?”

Reign could be lying; her claims were outlandish. But she spoke with such certainty, such…earnestness, that Kara couldn’t help but believe her just for a moment.

Reign smiled. “You will soon see, in time. But suffice it to say that your expectations will not be disappointed.”

Kara came back to herself.

“This planet isn’t ours. I…there’s nothing I would want more than for Krypton to return, but not…I’m not allowing you to sweep humanity aside,” the hero declared.

The other alien shook her head. “Krypton will arise with humanity. The galaxy is on the brink of utter ruin. The remnants of Krypton and humanity need each other.”

This is the woman who tried to kill Lena! Kara’s mind reminded her.

Supergirl forced any trace of eagerness out of her tone. “You lie. You’ve spent the last month trying to murder Lena! She’s the best humanity has to offer. If you’re afraid of such a dangerous universe, why are you obsessed with destroying the strongest mind we have?”

“Lena Luthor is dangerous,” Reign replied. “She would never willingly share Earth with another race. She might welcome scattered refugees, but she would never trust a large migration of a superpowered race.”

Large migration?  

Kara shook her head. “You’re a murderer. You killed J’onn Jonz. Right in front of me!”

Reign frowned. “I did. It was far too dangerous to leave him under Luthor’s control. Sacrifices must be made, Kara Zor-El. Our people have always understood that. Your vitriol is understandable, but it is misplaced. I have only targeted those who were threats, and I have never harmed any of your loved ones.”

“You were going to murder people just to keep Lena from escaping you!”

“I knew she wouldn’t allow that.” The alien shrugged. “In any case, I see you will need some more time to convince. That is not why I am here tonight. To state it simply, I need your help. Your’s and Luthor’s.”

Kara gasped.

“I was sent to this planet with two others,” Reign continued. “We are to prepare this planet for Krypton’s rebirth. But one of my partners has gone rogue. She has grown to relish in destruction, and she will no longer be controlled.”

Supergirl forced herself to move past her questions about Krypton. If only three were sent here, where are the rest? Reign is definitely saying that there’s more. Are they still on Krypton? No, it blew up, I saw it! 

“So kill her,” Kara replied disdainfully. “That’s what you do, isn’t it?”

Reign ignored the jab. “I cannot find her. Her powers don’t require her to come out of hiding. She is a walking plague, Kara Zor-El. With a single touch, she can spread her deadly virus to any human on the planet. As she wills it, the virus will spread.”

What?! A walking virus? If that was true, it was a catastrophe. Kara had never heard of such a power, but she had seen enough in her life to know that anything was possible.

“When does she plan to start?” the hero asked, dreading the answer.

Reign confirmed her fears. “She already has. Pestilence went rogue last night. Within a matter of hours, the disease will make itself apparent. Not all who catch it will die, but there is no vaccine. If she isn’t stopped, millions will die. Possibly more.”

The hero’s blood went cold. “How do we stop it?”

“The virus is driven by her will. Kill her, and the infection will disappear. I am entrusting the task to you. I can provide you with facial recognition data that should allow Luthor’s satellites to track her down.”

Kara frowned. If the only way to stop this Pestilence was to kill her, then… For now, it didn’t matter. The first step was finding her. “You expect Lena and I to chase her down.”

Reign shook her head. “Just you. Pestilence’s top speed will likely be roughly equal to yours. Luthor would not be able to maintain the pursuit. I will assist, if I can.”

Eyes narrowed in distrust, Kara stared at the other alien. “It doesn’t matter if this information is true or not. You’re a murderer. I wouldn’t trust you as far as I can throw you. I might be willing to believe you, but only because I think you don’t want the Earth devastated. You want to conqueror it for yourself.”

“I want a new Krypton,” Reign asserted. “We can share this world with humanity. Are you really so eager to turn your back on the last hope for our people?”

A New Krypton. Survivors. It was all too good to be true. After the Pestilence matter was resolved, Kara might be willing to hear Reign out, but she wasn’t getting her hopes up.

Was she?

\

Lena hadn’t appreciated being woken up at two in the morning, but calls from over a dozen agents couldn’t be ignored. Now she was in her office, typing furiously at her computer screen as reports continued to come over her second monitor.

This can’t be happening.

A familiar sound caused her to turn around.

Despite the rapidly developing nightmare that the CEO was finding herself in, the sight of Kara standing on her balcony was enough to bring her a brief burst of happiness. After so many days…had her girlfriend finally decided to forgive her.

Focus! You have bigger problems right now!

“Lena, you need to know-”

The supervillain stopped her. “As great as it is to see you, unless it’s worse than a possible plague, I’m going to have to cut you off. I’m getting reports from across the globe that there’s…it’s bad, Kara. My people don’t recognize what it is and it’s cropping up everywhere.”

Further reports were still coming in on her computer and cell phone. The constant buzzing only added to her rapidly developing panic.

Strangely, Kara didn’t seem surprised.

“I know what it is,” the hero replied. The indecision and awkwardness of Kara Danvers were nowhere to be seen. Supergirl was standing before her, ready and determined. “I know how to stop it.”

Lena stared at her. “How?”

Supergirl’s tone was unwavering. “Reign came to see me. She didn’t come to this planet alone, and one of her allies appears to have gone rogue.”

“Reign?!” Lena’s jaw dropped. There was no way that her girlfriend had just had a conversation with the alien who had attempted to murder her on several occasions. It didn’t make sense.

“She came to me in a populated area. I couldn’t fight her. Then she told me about Pestilence. She has the power to transmit a virus with a single touch, then it propagates unchecked. Millions could die,” Kara reported, her fists clenched. “I didn’t know whether to believe her, but I couldn’t take that chance. It looks like she was telling the truth.” The hero gestured to the computer.

Lena frowned. “Kara, tell me everything.”

\

“The news hasn’t picked up on it yet, but they will by morning,” Lena was saying. “The first patients are already starting to be hospitalized. It won’t be long before they realize these incidents are connected, and that we’re dealing with something new and incredibly dangerous.”

She was sitting at her desk, speaking to her top executives and agents through her computer screen. Most of them were in their nightclothes, but professionalism was the least of their current concerns. Sam, Kara, and Alex were sitting in the chairs nearby. All of them seemed to be at a loss for words.

A male voice spoke through the screen. “You have to make an announcement,” the Vice President of her media division reported. “With your clout, you might be able to buy us some time to track down the source of this virus.”

Lena nodded. “I’m inclined to agree, Rodriguez. Draft a statement and tell your subordinates to get everything ready immediately. I want to be in front of the cameras in ten minutes. Do your best to minimize the damage.”

With a nod, he logged off.

“Minimize the damage?” Kara asked.

Lena bit her lip. As she hesitated, the head of her sign division quickly spoke up from his space on the monitor. “This will set back human-alien relations back years. An alien disease ravaging the planet? Even if we get past this, calls to deport and block offworld immigrants are going to increase tenfold.”

Sam was keeping her expression neutral. Alex looked pained. Supergirl’s heroic visage cracked instantly, revealing nothing less than mortification.

“We don’t have a choice,” the voice of the (imposter) President spoke up. “Downplaying this virus or lying about its cause could cost countless lives. We beat this first, then we deal with the ramifications.”

Across the screen, L-Corp’s top people nodded grimly. The multiple aliens among them issued no protest, even as Lena could see the anguish in their eyes.

“Any progress on the search?” Lena demanded.

A woman’s voice came onto the screen. “The virus has appeared on every continent except Antarctica. This Pestilence is clearly moving from location to location at rapid speed. We’ve input the picture provided by Ms. Danvers into our satellites and are using all our resources to track rapidly moving objects. It’s only a matter of time.”

Lena grit her teeth. “Time is something we might not have. We don’t know how long this disease takes to kill, but based on the progression observed in the victims so far, it could be a matter of hours before we see our first fatality.”

The CEO sighed heavily. “I want everyone reassembled once my announcement is over. Until then, begin establishing a quarantine in whatever zones of influence you have. Yes, Olivia, that includes the entire United States. Do everything you can. Pamela, that goes for you too. Every leader under your control…I don’t care what their situation is.”

A chorus of affirmative responses sounded from the monitor.

“All L-Corp properties and subsidiaries are to go into immediate quarantine. Only one individual in a room if at all possible. Exceptions for any department working to track down Pestilence and contain the virus.”

As the various individuals logged off, Alex spoke up. “We don’t seem to be in quarantine,” she said flatly, gesturing between the four of them.

“There’s only one human in the room, Alex,” Kara pointed out before Lena could respond. “Reign told me. Those with Harun-el won’t be affected. Neither will true Kryptonians.”

Sam looked at Kara skeptically. “That’s if we can trust her.”

What is this world coming to? In a matter of hours, a plague was spreading across the planet and Lena’s best chance to stop it was relying on the words of her worst enemy. Maybe this really is a nightmare.

“So far, she’s been right,” Lena spoke up. “As it is, Sam, I imagine you want to go check on your daughter. Stay as far away as possible and make sure Ruby stays in her room,” she advised. “We have no idea who’s already infected.” 

The danger to them was more pronounced than most. Colville, originally thought to be suffering from a bout of flu, was showing symptoms of an unknown virus. If his case showed one thing, it was that the incubation period and progression of the disease could vary tremendously. He had been feeling sick for days; Lena’s reports discussed healthy people becoming seriously ill within minutes.

It was nothing like Lena had ever seen before. At first, an infected person seemed to exhibit only typical signs of illness…coughing, high temperatures, weakness. But as time passed, all of the body’s internal systems began to slow down. The virus left no outward signs of sickness, but it seemed to attack all of the body’s essential functions at once.

“I’ll be back,” Sam promised as she prepared to leave.

The CEO shook her head. “No. This isn’t your area of expertise, Sam. There’s nothing you can do. Stay with Ruby. More to the point, I’m going to need another normal human in this room right after my press conference and I don’t want to break quarantine.”

Strangely, Alex looked relieved at the news that the CFO would be leaving.

\

“Why did you call him here?”

They were alone in one L-Corp’s meeting rooms, Lena having told Kara that she wanted to speak privately. Kara still couldn’t fathom why.

“It doesn’t matter right now. Kara, is there anything more important than stopping Pestilence?” Lena asked. 

Supergirl shook her head. “Of course not. Why are you asking-”

“Absolutely nothing?”

The hero resisted the urge to sigh in exasperation. “No, nothing. Why are you talking like this? We need to-”

“My conference is in five minutes,” Lena cut her off. “We can’t do anything about Pestilence herself until we pinpoint her location. But when that happens, you might be the only person who can catch up to her. Don’t hesitate. Every second she’s alive, someone else might die. Kill her, Kara.”

No…

It might not be the only way. Maybe if Supergirl knocked Pestilence unconscious and took her to Lena, the CEO would be able to reverse the virus. Maybe she could threaten the alien into stopping the plague. Maybe she could…

But there was nothing she could do that wouldn’t risk innocent lives.

Staring into Lena’s firm, uncompromising gaze, Supergirl realized that even her principles had a limit. She couldn’t risk more people dying to possibly save a mass murderer. Innocent lives had to come first.

Or maybe that was the right principle to follow all along.

“…I will,” Kara promised. They weren’t dealing with hypotheticals any longer. This was an existential threat that needed to be eliminated. Supergirl would do anything to make sure that happened.

Even sacrifice her soul.

The CEO nodded. “You’ll be connected to L-Corp’s information network. All leads on Pestilence’s location will be filtered and delivered to you. I’ll be trying to keep up with you, but don’t wait for me. You’re much faster.”

Even as the world was falling apart, Lena Luthor’s presence still provided some comfort. The villain’s cool, unflinching determination was a lifeline in a raging storm. Despite all of their ideological differences, Kara couldn’t help but thank the universe for her girlfriend’s existence.

“You sound like a superhero,” Kara couldn’t help but say.

Lena shook her head. “I’m not a superhero.”

“Of course you-”

“I’m not a superhero because I never needed to be one,” Lena interrupted. “Because Supergirl has been flying around, saving people and stopping disasters, Vanity never needed to enter that role. Saved me a lot of time to work on taking over the world.” The CEO allowed her the tiniest of smiles.

Refusing to resist the affection welling up inside her, Kara leaned forward and kissed her girlfriend. “If I don’t make it back, I want you to know that I love you. I always will.”

The supervillain’s eyes widened. Half of the tension seemed to melt off her shoulders.

“Oh Supergirl,” Lena sighed, trying and failing to disguise her voice cracking. “Such a walking cliché. It would be pathetic except for how well you manage to pull it off.” She reached out, pulling Kara back in for another kiss. “Now go save the world. Vanity will be right behind you.”

Kara closed her eyes, forcefully blocking off a small flow of tears. “Any advice?” she asked.

A nod at her wrist. “Remember the password.”

Chapter End Notes

This is the second time I've written about girlfriends breaking up because one of them was secretly possessed by an evil personality. Hopefully it works out this time!

Principle

Chapter Notes

Happy Thanksgiving, everyone!

“Kara, we have a possible match,” Lena’s voice spoke in her earpiece. “Continue flying north at top speed; adjust your course five degrees to the right.”

“Understood,” the hero replied. How Lena was coordinating her directions while simultaneously flying herself and overseeing the pandemic response, Supergirl wasn’t certain. “How far behind are you?”

Lena’s voice sighed. “Five hundred kilometers and growing. You’re significantly faster than my best speed. Don’t wait for me.”

Kara nodded to herself. She would feel much safer with her girlfriend at her side, but Supergirl was no stranger to battling powerful aliens. Of course, normally there wasn’t such a time constraint involved…nor did Kara usually have to kill them.

“How are things on the ground?”

“You mean across the world?” Lena’s tone was tinged with desperation. “Nations where I have more influence are going into lockdowns. A lot of people are skeptical, but there’s always been an undercurrent of fear that something like this could happen. That’s helping things along. Places where I’m not yet in power…many are denying anything is wrong. Some leaders are saying it’s a hoax. Others are choosing to ignore the problem entirely. Ten more degrees to the right, Kara.”

Kara’s mind flashed back to Krypton’s last days. Accusations and denial of the exploding core were what had led to her world’s destruction. That could not happen again.

The hero gritted her teeth. “Any rioting?”

“Yes,” Lena replied. “Right now, a lot of people are processing the situation. L-Corp is doing our best to coordinate a response with local governments. But it’s bad, Kara. The longer this goes on, the worse it’s going to get.”

Even when flying at the speed of sound, the dread in her stomach felt like an impossible weight. “Any deaths yet?”

The answer was immediate. “No. Not that we’re aware of. But conditions are getting worse. The second you can end this, do it. Adjust three degrees to the left.”

“I will.”

A brief moment of static before Lena’s voice returned. “We have a positive ID on your target. Satellite surveillance confirms it.”

Determination settled in her chest. “How long until contact?”

“Minutes,” Lena replied. “You’re slightly faster than she is, according to our readings. Pestilence doesn’t know where you are, which means she’s not running from you in a straight line. Hopefully she doesn’t notice until you’re right on top of her.”

Minutes. Supergirl had faced difficult situations before, but never had all of human civilization potentially been at risk. I am the last daughter of Krypton, and I will not let this world be destroyed by a perversion of our people.

“Kara, we’re tracking another object heading for your position. Flying faster than you are. I think we can guess who it is.”

Reign. “How did she find me?”

“I don’t know, and right now it doesn’t matter. Cooperate with her to take down Pestilence. Reign clearly doesn’t want you dead, and right now that’s enough for me. Keep your guard up and be ready for anything the minute Pestilence is down,” Lena ordered. “I-”

The voice broke off into static.

“Lena? Lena?”

“…I’m fine, Kara. Continue your pursuit at all costs.”

\

Lena shouldn’t have been surprised.

Another heat signature was flying through the air, heading for Vanity’s position at a speed faster than the supervillain could have ever hoped to match.

Of course. Reign had mentioned being sent to Earth with two others. One was Pestilence. The other must be the one currently heading for her suit’s position.

They intend to kill me while Kara is busy.

Leave it to her enemies to make the most of an opportunity. They knew, just like Lena did, that she couldn’t call Kara back. She couldn’t even tell her girlfriend what was happening. Kara’s entire focus must be kept on stopping Pestilence, even if that meant cooperating with the alien who had planned yet another assassination attempt on Lena.

Lena’s fists clenched tightly. The chase was on.

\

They were high above Canada’s boreal forest before Pestilence noticed Supergirl’s imminent approach. By that time, only a few miles of distance separated them.

Kara didn’t hesitate. Still flying at top speed after her foe, she unleashed a burst of heat vision. The twin beams narrowly missed as Pestilence continued flying north.

“Come on.” Supergirl fired again, this time in a continuous stream. Pestilence weaved through the air, dodging the torrent of energy but forced to take attention and speed away from her northbound flight. The gap between them continued to close.

BZZT! A red blast rocketed through the sky, catching the off-guard Pestilence in the side. Smoke trailing from her form, the alien lost nearly half her altitude before righting herself again.

Reign was flying in, approaching them quickly from the left. Relief and revulsion swept through the hero in equal measure as she saw her unlikely ally approaching.

\

“I am Purity, Lena Luthor. And you shall not escape!”

Vanity dodged as her pursuer let loose another burst of purple heat vision. Moving eastward over the Atlantic Ocean as fast as possible, the distance between them nevertheless was shrinking rapidly.

No sooner had the thought entered Lena’s head then a sonic scream erupted from Purity. An annoying power, and one she was glad Kara didn’t possess. The edge of the sonic waves crashed into Vanity, nearly sending the suit out of its flight and into a tumble.

Opening the leg compartments, the suit let loose a torrent of hovering, black mines. No sooner had Purity reached them then they erupted, sending a cloud of smoke issuing over the north Atlantic.

Unfortunately, Purity could clearly see through smoke, and the concussive force of the mines barely slowed her down.

“Kara Zor-El is thousands of miles away,” Purity’s voice boomed. “Your time has come. Fight me, and at least you will enjoy the reward of an honorable death.”

There was no choice but to fight. Purity would catch up within a minute. Fortunately, there was now an ideal place to make a stand. Engey island, located a bit north of Iceland, was now within view. A small, uninhabited circle of Earth less than half a kilometer in diameter.

It was as good a place as any.

\

Pestilence was still fleeing northward through the Canadian tundra. The winter air grew steadily colder as darkness fell around them. They were close enough to the artic circle that night had already fallen, and a steady snowfall had begun.

None of those things were a barrier to Supergirl.

Whipping her head around as she flew, Pestilence fired a burst of green heat vision at her pursuers. Reign and Supergirl dodged, both firing back. Reign missed, but Kara scored a glancing blow that slowed down their enemy’s flight even further.

Almost there.

\

“So disappointing.”

Purity touched down on the island rock, glancing at the pitiful supervillain before her. Lena Luthor was crumpled on the ground, barely able to move.

The fight had lasted only minutes. The Luthor had unleashed her full array of red sun and kryptonite blasts, but Purity was more than a mere Kryptonian. Kara Zor-El could be easily brought down with her natural weaknesses, but it would take far more than that to bring down a Worldkiller. The attacks had bruised, but Purity still possessed most of her power.

“We must thank Pestilence. Even going rogue, she has still served our cause well,” the alien mused. “Reign will soon kill her and reclaim the power, and you won’t even live to see it. Any last words, Luthor?”

Without waiting for an answer, Purity moved forward. One quick snap of the neck, and it would be done.

Then she stopped dead in her tracks as the suit’s visor opened.

For several moments, Purity stared forward in silent disbelief. Lena Luthor wasn’t there. Purity was looking into an empty suit.

As her fury and panic began to rise, an impish male voice echoed from the empty vessel. “Lena Luthor isn’t available right now. She’ll be happy to get back to you after she finishes saving the world. Please leave a message after the explosion.”

BOOM!  

Purity had no time to react before the world was engulfed in green light. All of the suit’s nanites simultaneously combusted, discharging every ounce of their energy into a kryptonite blast that engulfed the entire island.

The world went black.

\

BZZT!

 Reign’s next burst of heat vision hit Pestilence directly, downing the rogue Worldkiller into the icy tundra. Exultation rippling through Kara, the hero dived downward, ready to finish off their enemy.

“AAGH!”

Supergirl stopped as a bloodcurdling scream erupted from Reign. The Worldkiller writhed in midair, cradling her face in her fingers. Kara whirled around, looking for the source of the attack, but saw nothing.

Huh?

Reign righted herself. Even at a distance, Kara could see the cold fury in her face. The Worldkiller’s gaze rapidly switched from Supergirl to the recovering Pestilence. A moment later, her face was set in stone as a decision was made.

Without another word, Reign was gone. The alien disappeared over the horizon in an instant, flying east at her top speed. Leaving Supergirl alone with-

Reign doesn’t matter. I have to finish Pestilence! Now!

Kara rocketed towards the ground, fist extended, but Pestilence recovered just in time. The rogue alien rolled to the side, leaving Supergirl’s fist to collide with the snow-covered earth. A shockwave radiated from the point of impact, buffeting both aliens.

“Hurry Kara,” Lena’s voice spoke in her earpiece. “Patients around the world are starting to go into critical condition!”

“Stop this!” Supergirl yelled as Pestilence climbed to her feet. “People are dying. End your virus, or I will kill you!”

Pestilence laughed. Save for her dark supersuit, she was unassuming in appearance. A young Asian woman, she could have been just out of college. But her eyes gleaned with malice.

“I’m having far too much fun, Kara Zor-El,” the alien taunted. “Kill me?” She stretched out her hands, allowing long, sharp, golden claws to extend from her fingers. “I have all of your powers and more.”

Kara was already sick of this woman. “I don’t give a damn.”

The two aliens collided, sending out another shockwave. Kara kneed her opponent in the groin, only to withdraw as a clawed hand swiped at her neck. Instinctively, Supergirl knew that those talons were a threat even to her invulnerable skin.

A blast of green energy caught the hero full in the temple. Supergirl tumbled backwards through the snow, her earpiece frying. She jumped to her feet, afraid Pestilence would have taken the opportunity to flee, only to see another green blast barreling towards her.

Kara rocketed up a hundred feet into the air, allowing the beams to incinerate the snow beneath her. Pestilence rose up after her, claws outstretched, only to stop as Kara slammed her hands together.

The resulting thunderclap slammed into the Worldkiller. Pestilence barely had a second to right herself before twin blue beams collided with her forehead, slamming her back down into the ground.

Before Supergirl could close the distance between them, Pestilence fired another green blast. This time, Kara altered her course into the ground, spinning rapidly as she did so.

Now a makeshift drill, the hero tunneled through the snow and into the earth. Using her X-ray vision, Kara emerged right under the shocked Worldkiller’s feet.

WHAM! The devastating uppercut caught Pestilence right below the chin. Kara could even hear the sound of teeth cracking.

Supergirl followed Pestilence’s momentum, slamming her foot into the Worldkiller’s shin as they sped through the air. Fear for the alien’s impending victims flooded through the hero as she slammed her fist into the side of her opponent’s face.

Pain!  

A horrible agony erupted on the side of Kara’s right leg. As they’d grappled, two of Pestilence’s claws had scraped right through her skin. Both wounded, the two combatants crashed to the ground. Drops of blood began to stain the snow.

Kara moved forward…only to stop as horrible wave of nausea sprouted in her body. It was only through pure determination that Supergirl remained on her feet as dizziness took hold.

Pestilence was climbing to her feet, spitting out blood of her own. “Even your immune system can’t withstand direct contact with my virus,” she gloated. “Now all I have to do is-”

Kara rocketed at her opponent, slamming her with a vicious headbutt. Ignoring the pain, Supergirl punched her enemy twice in the gut before unleashing another blast of heat vision. She grabbed her enemy by the shoulders, holding the Worldkiller in place.

So close. I have to finish her!

A flailing claw sunk into Supergirl’s forearm. Kara acknowledged the pain, turning it into fuel for a continuous blast of heat vision aimed straight at Pestilence’s skull. The beams of energy pounded against the Worldkiller’s skin, blackening the nearly invulnerable exterior.

Pestilence howled in agony.

Kara was feeling sicker by the minute. The virus was rapidly overpowering her immune system, draining her. Yet she didn’t allow her blurry vision to interrupt her aim or weaken her grip. The sight of smoke rising from her enemy’s blistering forehead filled her with nausea of a different sort, but Supergirl refused to stop.

They fell to the ground with a crash once again. Pestilence crumpled to the ground as Kara barely maintained her feet. Finally breaking off the twin beams of energy, Supergirl seized the dazed alien from behind. One hand went to Pestilence’s chin. The other to her opposite temple.

One snap and it would be over. But she hesitated.

Heroes don’t kill, Kara. We have to find a better way. It’s what separates us from them. Clark’s voice filled her mind, sending shudders into Supergirl’s hands. Murder is never justice.

As Supergirl’s hands trembled, Pestilence’s arm moved in a blur.

White hot agony burned into the hero as Pestilence’s claws scraped along her side. Kara’s knees buckled instantly, sending her crashing into the snow.

She barely noticed as blood gushed out of the open wound. Vomit spilled from her mouth as her body wretched with illness. Pestilence was nothing but a vague shape before her as the alien climbed to her feet.

“Even with all of your power, you are still weak.”

Kara struggled to rise, but she could barely even move her fingers. Her mouth wouldn’t even respond to her commands. The nausea was all-consuming.

Barely conscious, she was just able to hear the approaching sound of a jet engine.

\

Jess glanced at her boss. It didn’t matter that the secretary was now protected by the Harun-el; she had never felt less safe. Monitors throughout the office played live news footage, continuing to detail rapidly rising hospitalization numbers.

Even if L-Corp hadn’t released the news by now, human civilization would already have been consumed by panic. There was no longer any denying the catastrophe. L-Corp was doing all it could to handle the situation; even providing the facts to the public was sustaining a degree of hope that a quick fix was possible.

But it wasn’t enough. Jess only had to glance outside to see that. It may have been noon, but National City had never looked so dark. Most people were in their homes, huddling with their families. Looters taking advantage of the chaos were prowling the streets, smashing windows and stealing supplies.

How did this happen?

 Luke was in the other room. With her newly enhanced hearing, she could hear his quiet cries. What kind of world was he growing up in? What would be left for him once he was ready to step out into adult society?

Her phone buzzed. Glancing at the message, Jess sighed before walking over to her boss.

“Ms. Luthor, we’re getting unconfirmed reports that a small number of those hospitalized have passed away.”

\

“You’re one mile from her position. Eject.”

Those were the last words Alex heard before the entire bottom portion of her jet opened. Cold air rushed around her as she sped hundreds of feet towards the surface. Her forward momentum carried her over the dark, snowy tundra.

She had to give Lena’s calculations credit. Alex skid across the ground halted her only a dozen meters from her sister’s position. Where Kara was-

Bleeding out on the ground as an alien stood over her.

Alex didn’t hesitate. She charged forward with all of her speed, hitting the wounded and off-guard Pestilence with a right hook to the cheek.

Wounded. But not beaten. Pestilence climbed to her feet as Alex stood protectively in front of her sister. A small smirk appeared on the alien’s lips. Then, she began to laugh.

“You?” she jeered. “Not nearly enough. Where’s Luthor?”

Alex stared at her enemy. Lena was where she needed to be, in her office. The simple truth was that Lena was the only one who could coordinate the response to the plague, find and track Pestilence’s position, and direct the drone fleets around the world heading their way as reinforcements. Not to mention helping Winn remotely control her Vanity suit to draw off the inevitable assassin.

Which left Alex, the only superpowered L-Corp employee capable of flying a jet (thanks to DEO training), as Kara’s backup. At least until the drones arrived.

“Delta squadron is five minutes out,” Lena’s voice reported.

Shit. We’ll be corpses for three minutes by then.

Pestilence was hurt. Horrifying third degree burns stretched across her forehead. But that didn’t stop her from darting forward, lashing out with a clawed hand that Alex barely dodged. She suppressed an inward shiver. If those claws could wound Kara, what could they do to her?

Kara, who was bleeding out in the snow. If Lena’s drones couldn’t provide sufficient medical attention, her sister was already dead.

Pure rage and adrenaline were all that allowed her to dodge a green blast of energy. Then she was on Pestilence, slamming an elbow into her badly wounded forehead. Even with her strength only half that of a real Kryptonian’s, the blow still elicited a cry of pain.

A taloned hand lashed out at Alex’s side. She jumped back, but a golden claw still scraped across her stomach. A thick line of blood sprouted from the wound, filling the security chief with pain.

But no illness.

“Harun-el,” Pestilence hissed. “That heresy provides you complete immunity from my virus. But it will not save you. Nothing can.”

Her eyes blazed again. Alex dodged the blast of energy, but she was too slow to react as the alien lashed out with a kick to her knee. She lashed out with another punch…only to have her blow knocked aside by her enemy’s superior strength.

More than anything else, the resulting exchange filled her with frustration. As Alex barely managed to block and dodge the enraged alien’s blows, it galled her that all of her training…all of Lena’s Harun-el, were nowhere near enough.

They couldn’t save her. And she couldn’t save Kara.

As Alex recoiled in pain from absorbing a kick to her forearm, a slash of claws managed to graze her forehead. As blood blinded her vision, another talon stabbed into her leg. Alex had barely started to scream in pain before a backhanded blow slammed into her face.

“Blind? How fitting,” Pestilence snarled viciously. “If only you knew what she really is. You’ve been living a lie for months. Killing you will be a mercy.”

Another blow slammed into her head, and everything went dark.

\

Alex…

Swimming in and out of consciousness, Kara had watched as her sister was pulverized. More bile issued through her throat as she struggled to move…to speak.

She is going to die because of me.

Kara’s vision blurred further as the seconds ticked by. She could almost see her cousin standing above her, frowning in disapproval.

As Alex suffered another blow to the head, Clark’s voice again sounded in her mind. ‘Do not soil our people’s legacy. My legacy. Being a hero is never easy, but true strength is found in the darkest times. Don’t let yourself forget what is right.’

Blood trailing down her forehead, Alex was stabbed in the leg by a claw. Pestilence was taunting her. And as Kara’s eyes shifted between the vision of her dead cousin and her dying sister, she finally understood what really mattered.

I owe you, Clark. You were my hero. I will never forget our people. But they’re gone now. Whatever I owe the dead is nothing compared to my responsibility to the people still here. And I have to do what I think is right.

Another blow from Pestilence knocked Alex off her feet. Kara’s sister collapsed into the snow, unconscious.

‘Kara, we stand for truth and justice.’ Clark’s voice implored.

No. You did. I stand for…

The hero called forth the last of her energy. “Hope, help, and compassion for all.” As the words, faint as they were, echoed into the air, Kara’s bracelet stirred.

A massive yellow light burst from Kara’s arm, encompassing Supergirl, Alex, Pestilence, and the surrounding half mile in a sea of bright energy. Pestilence reared back from Alex, withdrawing the intended deathblow and shielding her eyes.

As the light faded, Kara rose to her feet. As the radiation seeped into her body, her immune system renewed its fight against the deadly infection. The flow of blood on her side slowed to a trickle as her skin began to heal itself.

“You seriously intend to fight me in that condition?” Pestilence demanded.

Supergirl stared at her enemy. “You are a threat to my family, my friends, and my world. Protecting them is the only thing that matters.”

She charged forward.

Her kick slammed into Pestilence’s chest, sending the alien skidding backwards. The Worldkiller came forward, raising a clawed hand to slash at Kara’s arm.

Supergirl didn’t hesitate.

BZZT! A burst of blue heat vision sliced into the outstretched claws. Two of them fell into the snow. As Pestilence screamed in fury, a roundhouse kick by Kara was already on its way. The blow connected right with her burned forehead, knocking the rogue alien to the ground.

By the time Pestilence started to rise, it was too late. Supergirl was already on her, using one hand to pin the Worldkiller’s uninjured arm and the other to keep her legs at bay. Pestilence’s eyes blazed with green energy, but the blast went wide as Kara ducked to the ground. She kept up her hold.

Pestilence grunted, reaching out with her free hand and seizing Supergirl by the throat. “I’m not done.”

Supergirl raised her free hand. And her enemy gasped in horror as she saw one of her own severed claws clenched firmly in the hero’s fist.

“Yes, you are.”

Kara’s hand plunged downward, sending the tip of the claw right through her enemy’s chest. Even as blood spurted upward, she continued to push the claw deeper.

Pestilence let out a horrifying scream as the weapon pierced her heart. Her hand fell from the hero’s throat.

Kara forced herself to continue. Even as tears fell from her eyes, she didn’t stop. It wasn’t until Pestilence let loose a final, ragged breath that the hero finally let go.

Adrenaline fading, she collapsed into the snow.

It’s over.

As the yellow sun energy began to dissipate, the hero felt her strength beginning to slip away again. Fortunately, her wounds weren’t opening up any further. And this time, there was no nausea. The virus was gone.

Were we too late? Was I too late? How many are dead because of me?

Even as Kara laid in the snow, absorbed in mental agony, she watched as a sickly green mist floated up from Pestilence’s body. At first, it seemed to slowly drift up into the sky.

Then, as if captured by a powerful magnet, it sped at Alex’s unconscious form. Kara cried out, but she could do nothing but watch as the mist seemed to sink into her sister’s skin.

And just as fast as it had appeared, the smoke was gone.

“Alex…”

Just as Kara finally began to slip into unconsciousness, she heard the oncoming sound of her girlfriend’s drone fleet.

Turning Point
