Reign was seething.

She’d made it in time to stop Purity from being carried away by Luthor’s drones. It would take days for the defeated Worldkiller to heal; kryptonite poisoning had seeped into her veins. But it wasn’t Purity that Reign was worried about.

Pestilence’s power was gone. The dark energy that had given the rogue Worldkiller the power over plague had seeped into the unwitting form of Alex Danvers. A human who had received a bastardized transfusion of the Rock of Yuda Kal now possessed the full power of a Worldkiller, whether she realized it or not.

What a sickening thought.

Reign would have enjoyed killing her, but Alex Danvers was on the list. Taking action would require a direct communication with her Mistress, and her Goddess. She only hoped that she would be given to snuff out the life of the usurper.

\

Kara opened her eyes.

She was lying on soft sheets. Bright yellow light was issuing from the ceiling above her. And prone on the hospital bed next to her was-

“Alex!” The hero moved to get up, but a familiar arm intercepted her.

“Lena?” Her girlfriend was standing over her, looking down with both concern and relief. As Kara reflexively tried to stand up again, the supervillain gently pushed her back onto the bed.

“Relax,” Lena said soothingly. “She’s fine. All her readings are normal. You were the one I was more worried about. Pestilence gave you a beating.”

Supergirl’s face fell. The memories came flooding back to her. She was a killer now. It had been necessary, but her skin went green with revulsion at the thought. Lena must have noticed, because she began speaking quickly.

“You’ve been out for fifteen hours. I had you both moved to one of my National City safehouses,” Lena spoke.

Kara nodded, trying to shake off the cobwebs from her memory. “What happened? Why weren’t you there with us?” she asked. Her tone wasn’t accusatory. If Lena hadn’t been there, she had had a good reason. Kara just couldn’t fathom what it was.

The CEO bit her lip. “I knew Reign would try to have me killed while you were distracted. So I recruited Winn to help pilot the suit remotely; I needed someone I could trust who was competent at fighting games,” she explained. “I didn’t have a backup suit, and I was needed to coordinate the whole thing. Your reinforcements, the response around the world…all of it. I’m sorry I wasn’t there for you.”

“You were.” Kara’s hand intertwined with one of Lena’s. “You’ve always been there for me. Our best chance was for you to stay back; you knew that. And it worked out, didn’t it?”

Lena smiled sadly. Instantly, dread settled in Kara’s stomach. Pestilence might have been dead, but there was no telling how much damage she had wreaked on the planet.

“How bad is it?” the hero demanded.

“Not too bad,” Lena replied quickly. “Things were crazy for a while, but the human race is remarkably resilient. As soon as Pestilence died, the virus disappeared. L-Corp got the word out immediately. There was some rioting, but things have calmed down. Some people even slept through the entire thing.”

Kara’s hand was trembling slightly. As Lena’s fingers tightened over her own, Supergirl forced herself to ask the question. “Any deaths?”

Her worst fears were confirmed as the CEO dipped her head. “A small number. Probably less than a hundred, although we don’t have all of the information in yet.”

“A small number,” Supergirl repeated angrily. “Any number is too high!”

Lena’s face hardened. “Kara, it could have been millions. You stopped that from happening! Hasn’t being Supergirl taught you that you can’t save everyone? All you can do is try your best, and you did.”

That was a lie. Kara could have killed Pestilence sooner. But she’d squandered her chance. How many had died because Pestilence had lived for a few minutes longer? And Alex…the hero shivered at the memory. Alex had suffered for Kara’s mistake.

Forcing her thoughts away from that torment for as long as she could, Kara turned back to her girlfriend. “How much anti-alien backlash?”

“Not as much as there might have been,” Lena replied heavily. The tone of voice was so hesitant that Kara’s eyes narrowed in confusion.

“You sound guilty,” Supergirl pointed out. “Why? It’s not your fault.”

Lena shook her head. “No. But I made a choice to try and stop it. I knew you wouldn’t like it…but it had to be done. I hope you can forgive me,” she said, her voice shuddering. Keeping her gaze locked into Kara’s eyes with visible effort, the CEO continued. “I released the footage of you fighting Pestilence, and killing her. Hundreds of millions of views already.”

Supergirl’s face went white. “Rao. They saw me…” she stared down at her hands, remembering stabbing the rogue Worldkiller with her own claw. She was a murderer for all the world to see.

“They did,” Lena said. “And they needed to. The human race saw a powerful alien saving their civilization. Anyone defending aliens on Earth now has an easy argument that there are good aliens out there, and that we need you. L-Corp has already released a statement on the matter, and the governments and officials under my control have done the same. It’s made stopping any burgeoning anti-alien laws that much easier.” Finally, her eyes fell to their still-interlocked fingers. “I know I used you. And I’m sorry.”

The world had seen Supergirl take a life. The very thought made Kara want to vomit. Yet she knew just how bad the backlash might have been otherwise.

Hope. Help. Compassion for all.

“I know,” Kara replied. “And I hate it. But I’m glad you did. The first and only principle that matters is protecting innocent life, right?” she reminded her girlfriend. “Aliens would have died if you hadn’t done that. I can’t blame you for it.” The hero scoffed. “If anything, you should be blaming me. You were right. Killing is sometimes the only way to save the innocent. I convinced myself otherwise. But even with all my powers, sometimes there’s no other way. If I had accepted that sooner, maybe Alex wouldn’t be lying in a hospital bed.”

Lena shook her head vigorously. “If killing was easy for you, you wouldn’t be…well, you. Alex will be fine, and you saved the world.”

“Not yet,” Kara said. “People still need me.” She attempted to rise again, but a wave of weakness pushed her back onto the bed before Lena’s hand could do the same.

“Right now, people need you to get better. You’re in no shape to be flying around,” Lena replied firmly. “L-Corp is handling things for now, and there hasn’t been too much damage.”

The hero frowned. News of a pandemic should have sent shockwaves through the global economy. Even if the crisis had been averted, the economic damage would have led to widespread chaos. How was Lena telling her otherwise?

“I had Olivia suspend all trading for the day.” Her girlfriend seemed to have the ability to read minds. “The economic hit won’t be too bad. We expect the market to fall tomorrow, but it won’t collapse,” Lena explained. “Good thing, too. I would have lost a few hundred billion dollars before all was said and done.”

Kara couldn’t help but smile, even as a conflicting thought occurred to her. “You’re going to milk this for all it’s worth, aren’t you?”

Lena grinned back. “I’m going to make sure the people of Earth know the truth: that it was L-Corp’s growing power that all but saved civilization. Everyone’s going to know that without my actions, both legal and otherwise, we would have been screwed. Supergirl was our hero, but she couldn’t have found Pestilence without my satellites.” There was a pregnant pause. “Is any of that unfair?”

The Black Mercy. Kara couldn’t help but think back to the details of Lena’s fantasy under the parasite. In that illusionary world, it had been her efforts against an alien invasion that cemented her control over Earth. Would the same thing happen now?

“I’m fine with being a symbol against anti-alien sentiment,” Supergirl answered. “But I didn’t kill Pestilence so I could be your company mascot.”

The CEO’s gaze darkened. “No, you did it to save the world. So did I. What do you think I’m trying to do now?” she demanded. “Kara, this was one powerful alien that nearly destroyed our civilization. If L-Corp doesn’t gain control of the planet in time to shore up our defenses, we’re doomed. Maybe you’re just too stubborn to realize it, but I have a feeling that a lot of people are about to come around.”

Kara sighed. “Did you come here to argue?”

“I came to watch over you,” Lena answered. “I wanted to give you fair warning about what was going to happen. How you react is entirely up to you.” The steel in her voice vanished. “Focus on recovering. Alex should be waking up soon. Afterwards, when you’re ready…we can have a long talk.”

The hero couldn’t help but shift nervously.

Lena’s eyes fell to the bedsheets. “I don’t know if our relationship can survive, Kara. Maybe you can’t forgive me for what happened to Lois, or you can’t accept that I’m going to use our defeat of Pestilence to increase my influence,” she said sadly. “All I know is that I’m going to do everything in my power to ensure you don’t lose another world. What happens between us…is entirely up to you,” the CEO continued, her voice cracking. Lena’s eyes were glistening. “Whatever you decide, I’ll understand. Either way, you were the best thing that has ever happened to me.”

In one fluid motion, the Luthor rose to her feet and planted a gentle kiss on Kara’s forehead. She left the room, leaving nothing further said.

\

“So, your sugar mama gave you a bracelet that makes you even stronger?”

Kara huffed impatiently into the phone. “Winn. No…it doesn’t work like that. It just acts as a temporary recharge, letting loose the maximum amount of yellow radiation my cells can take in at once,” the hero explained. “And Lena is not my sugar mama. I’d have dated her even if she was poor.” 

Oh, wouldn’t that have made things so much easier. No dreams of world conquest to come between us.

“Fair point,” her friend responded. After he’d finished giving her the details of his remote controlling of Lena’s suit, Winn had regaled her with details of the fight. To her relief, he’d been considerate enough to avoid asking about the end of it.

“Kara,” Alex interrupted from the other bed. “Tell Winn to remind James that my flight training wasn’t a thousand wasted hours in the end. Since, you know, it helped us save the world and all!”

If the phone hadn’t been made of nth metal, it would have cracked in her grip. “Winn, Alex wants me to tell you to remind James-”

“Yeah, yeah, flight training saved the world, I got it. Any idea when Lena is allowing you two to have visitors? Lucy was talking about a hospital game of monopoly,” Winn answered.

Kara had told him that Lena had advised her to remain as isolated as possible. With her powers at a low ebb, it was possible her immune system was vulnerable. After all, it had never had to adapt to the diseases present on Earth.

It was a lie. Supergirl hated lying, but the last thing she wanted was more company. There was simply too much on her mind.

“I’ll let you know,” she responded.

After the call ended, Kara turned to her sister. It was a relief to see Alex conscious and talking again. The hero had been grateful that her only comment on Supergirl’s killing of Pestilence was, “It had to be done,” accompanied by a sympathetic look.

In the two hours since she’d awoken, the security chief had been busy on her computer. Why, Kara wasn’t quite sure. Alex’s job was protecting Sam, not organizing recovery efforts.

“Something wrong? You seem out of it,” the hero commented.

Alex shook her head unconvincingly. “No, I…everything’s fine. I’ve just been emailing Sam. Obviously, she’s pretty busy. There’s a lot of money being moved around today.”

Eyes narrowed, Kara considered this. Yes, Sam was undoubtedly busy. Even before the recent crisis, she had volunteered to oversee an investigation into Lois’s death…not that anything was expected to come of it. Still, there was something else going on with Alex that her sister wasn’t sharing.

For now, Kara would watch and wait.

“I’m surprised you switched to L-Corp’s email,” the hero commented. “I thought you were pretty attached to your old one?”

Alex shrugged. “It’s company policy,” she explained. “All top-level L-Corp employees have to use the company’s email servers. Lena barely even pretends that there’s any privacy. Even the messages we delete stay on her server.”

Typical Lena. “She’s obsessed with control,” Kara replied moodily.

Alex scoffed. “She’s trying to save our lives. I don’t like knowing my boss can access all my emails, but Lena needs to be able to trust the people she delegates to. Some of them have…interesting pasts, as you well know.”

“Oh, I didn’t forget,” the hero responded. “You know, life was so much simpler when you wanted to shoot Lena Luthor rather than work for her.”

No. Life was so much simpler before she met Lena. When Kara had known who her enemies were and what she wanted the future of Earth to be. She’d been certain of what was right and how to achieve it.

You were also vulnerable, alone, and helpless against any threat you couldn’t just beat into a pulp.

Kara suppressed a groan. Why did her life have to be so confusing?

A start from Alex redirected the hero’s attention. Her sister was staring at her computer screen, wearing a solemn look on her face. But as soon as she noticed Kara’s gaze, the security chief immediately clicked out of her current window.

“What was that?” Kara questioned.

Alex’s eyes shifted to the side. “Nothing,” she said quickly. “Just some reports that Sam sent me. Losses in production were a little higher than expected; nothing to worry about.”

Kara’s fists clenched. “I’m not in the mood to play games, Alex,” she said firmly. “What are you hiding? Did something happen?”

“Nothing happened!” her sister protested. “Calm the fuck down and take a deep breath. You don’t need to be worried about my work.”

“There’s something on that monitor you don’t want me to see.” Shakily, Kara climbed to her feet. “I can hear your heart racing. Show me, or I swear by Rao I will burn that computer to a crisp before you can blink.”

Lena. Alex. Kara had had enough of uncertainty. Now a new question had been placed in front of her, and the hero wasn’t about to let her sister hide the answer away.

Alex bit her lip. “Fine. I suppose you’ll find out soon enough anyway. Here, have a look,” she said, tossing the laptop onto Kara’s bed. “Just…don’t overreact.”

Sitting back down, Kara grabbed the computer and quickly located the window Alex had closed. Her eyes ran greedily over the page, searching for information. It didn’t seem to be anything important, just a list of names and times. Times of…

Times of death.

There were nearly a hundred names on the digital sheet, all of them known victims of Pestilence’s virus. According to the listed locations, there had been victims around the world. People of all age groups had fallen to the short-lived plague.

“Kara, it could have been-”

“Quiet,” the hero hissed.

Every name on the list was equally tragic. But it was reading the last two dozen that drove Kara into tears. All of them had passed away in the last five minutes of Pestilence’s life, the few minutes that had been won thanks to Supergirl’s hesitation.  

They were a monument to her mistakes. A reward for her precious principles.

Tobias Glover, aged nine. Chika Feliciana, aged seventeen. Mei Carran, aged sixty. Johanna Macie, aged thirty-two. Thorvald Uttar, aged eighty-four.

Each name at the bottom of the list was another gut punch, but Kara forced herself to read them all. Even as Alex protested, she clicked on each name to view the accompanying picture. The details were harrowing. There were promising college students with athletic scholarships, workers in the primes of their lives, and seniors spending retirement with their grandchildren. All of them had had a future to look forward to…until Pestilence.

Until Supergirl had hesitated.

“That list would be millions of names long if it hadn’t been for you,” Alex tried again. “You know you can’t save everyone. This isn’t the first time people have died on your watch, and it won’t be the last.”

Kara shook her head. “People have died because I was too slow, or because I didn’t notice something in time. This isn’t that. These are people who are dead because of a conscious choice I made! I should have snapped her damn neck when I had the chance!”

The hero was barely aware of being wrapped in Alex’s embrace, or being led back onto the bed. The faces of Pestilence’s victims continued to swim in her mind. If Kara had just chosen the safety of innocent lives over her idealism, how many people would still have been breathing?

“You’re a hero,” Alex said soothingly. “Not a Goddess. You can’t save everyone, and you will make mistakes. The people of Earth are lucky that one of the strongest aliens on the planet has made them priority number one. But you can’t protect them all, no matter how fast you fly or what choices you make. All you can do is your best.”

Several moments of silence passed. Slowly, Kara’s breathing began to settle back down. 

“I have to go,” she said. “Where is my suit?”

\

“Ms. Luthor, Ms. Danvers is here to see you,” Jess’s voice spoke over the intercom.  

Lena froze, slowly putting down her bottle of wine. “Send her in,” the CEO replied. She forced herself to breathe, ignoring her rapidly rising heartbeat. If Kara was here already, after not even a day of consideration, this couldn’t be good news.

The door opened to admit Supergirl. Kara was clad in her full heroic outfit, her glasses and civilian attire nowhere to be seen. She walked into the room and stood before Lena’s desk, somehow looking both purposeful and hesitant.

“Kara, why are you-”

“Lena,” her girlfriend interrupted. “I have some things to say. Just…let me talk, okay? Once I’m done, you can say whatever you want.”

Moisture was forming on the tips of Lena’s fingers. “Okay,” she managed. This was it. No more dinners, movie nights, or stargazing. Kara Danvers was out of her life…another sacrifice in her quest to save the Earth.

How ironic. The only thing that makes this sacrifice worth it is the very thing I’m giving up. Kara’s life was worth infinitely more than Lena’s happiness. Now all that was left was to see it through.  

“You were right,” Kara said.

What?

“I let my ideals…my principles, get in the way of doing what was right. There are over a dozen people who are dead because I didn’t kill her when I had the chance,” Kara breathed. “Yeah, I made Alex show me the casualty list.”

That had been one thing that the CEO had wanted to avoid. “Kara, I-”

“I’m not done!” the hero continued. “I’ve been clinging to my principles for so long, trying to live up to my cousin’s example. I thought that not doing so would dishonor my people,” Kara admitted. “And…maybe it does. But Krypton is dead. I can’t bring it back. There are people alive right now who will die if I make a mistake like that again.”

Lena resisted the urge to speak.

Kara sighed. Then, she looked directly into the villain’s eyes. “I’m not the protector of Krypton’s legacy. I’m just Kara Zor-El Danvers, an alien refugee who has to do what she thinks is right. And I refuse to let people die again just because of my ideals.”

“Pestilence killed them,” Lena spoke softly. “Not you.”

Kara nodded. “She was a monster. And people died because I didn’t end her life in time. One of them was five, Lena. A five-year-old boy!” Her hands were wringing in frustration. “Never again. You know what, I’m perfectly okay with you taking credit for all of this. You know why?”

The CEO went silent again. This was the last thing she had expected to hear.

“Because you deserve it! If you hadn’t made L-Corp powerful enough to maintain its own satellite network and maintain a drone fleet, we’d never have found Pestilence,” Kara said, her voice hard. “Millions of people would be dying right now as human civilization collapsed.” She paused, rapidly pacing back and forth. “I want to stand for hope, help, and compassion for all. Without what you’re doing…there’s no hope there. Earth will be finished in a few decades at most. The universe has gotten too dangerous…I mean, is it any wonder so many alien refugees are on this planet, or that so many of them want to work for you?”

Lena felt like the wind had been knocked out of her. Was this really happening?

“I don’t know if your plan will work,” the hero admitted. “All I know is that it gives us a chance. A divided Earth won’t be able to handle what’s coming for us. You were right the whole time; I’m sorry I was too stubborn to see it.”

Not again. “Kara, while I would love to take you seriously, you’re grieving right now. You’re not thinking clearly.”

The hero grit her teeth. “No. I’m thinking more clearly than I have since I arrived on this planet! I finally see what’s really important…it only took a few dozen deaths on my conscience for that to happen.” Kara took a breath, forcing herself to continue. “I don’t know if Lois’s death was your fault or not, Lena. Either way, I forgive you. You might have made a mistake with a test tube…I let people die because I was selfish.”

“Selfish?” Lena demanded.

“Yeah,” her girlfriend agreed. “Pretending that I could be a personification of Kal’s legacy, and Krypton’s legacy, helped me ignore how much I’d lost. And how alone I am.”

Lena stood up, her expression fierce. “You have me. You have your friends, your sister. And the people of Earth adore you. Kara, you’ve lost more than anyone I’ve ever met, but you are not alone.”

A sad smile. “No. And I want to protect what I still have. Not as the heir to Krypton and Superman, but as Kara Zor-El. And that means admitting you were right,” the hero said. “I don’t agree with everything you do, and our debates aren’t over. But as long as you don’t ask me to break my own morals…I’m yours to command, Ms. Luthor.”

As the supervillain watched, barely able to comprehend what she was seeing, Kara Zor-El dropped to one knee before her. The superhero’s cape pooled in front of her desk.

“No Red-K this time,” Kara said. “Just me, you, and a world we’re going to bring into a new future together.”

Lena’s mouth gaped open. At first, she’d been so certain Kara would come around to her way of thinking. Over time, that hope had faded. Now, it was happening. Supergirl was hers. And with the heroic icon working under her, it was only a matter of time before the rest of the world followed.  

Less importantly for the future of Earth, but more important to Lena, was the fact that she could keep Kara Danvers as her fiancé.

“Kara,” she said slowly. “Get up and kiss me.”

In a flash of superspeed, the hero was standing next to her. “Yes ma’am,” Kara agreed. Then, for the first time, their lips met without any ideological differences wedged between them.

It made the taste all the sweeter.

Welcome to the Dark Side

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“I can’t believe this!”

The hero frowned. “I’m sorry, Lucy,” Kara replied. “It wasn’t an easy decision to make, but this is the way it’s going to be. If Lena doesn’t succeed-”

“I’ve heard enough.” Lucy stomped away, towards the apartment door. “If you want to be a minion for a world-enslaving dictator, that’s your business.”

This was going just as Kara had expected it to. Horribly. “Lucy, that’s not what she wants!”

Lucy turned back. “That’s exactly what Luthor wants. All she cares about is control, and you’re going to give it to her. What happened to hope, Kara? Was all that talk of ‘faith in humanity’ just for show?” she fumed.

“Of course not!” Kara shot back.

The other woman scowled. “Then why are you giving up on it?” she demanded. “You’re signing off our future to a megalomaniac because you don’t think we can do it ourselves. Am I wrong?”

Kara frowned. “I believe that most people, humans and aliens, are inherently good. That won’t save the Earth from getting invaded by a superior force.”

“And you think Lena Luthor is going to save us all?” Lucy hissed. “Tell that to my sister.”

Without another word, Lucy turned and stormed out of the hero’s apartment. Kara watched her go. She wasn’t surprised at the other woman’s anger and, honestly, hadn’t expected anything less. With time, Kara believed that Lucy would come around.

A lot of time.

She turned to James and Winn. It was the former she was worried about. “Do you think that Lois’s death is Lena’s fault?” she found herself asking.

James sighed. “I don’t know. Lois was saying some weird things that day. Maybe Sam’s investigation will…” he broke off forlornly. “If it was Lena’s fault, well, I know it wasn’t intentional. I can’t deny that part of me is bitter at her for it.”

Kara dipped her head. “I know what you’re going to say,” she prompted. “Go ahead, tell me that Clark would be ashamed of me and that I’m a disgrace to his legacy.”

Here eyes widened in surprise as the photographer shook his head. “Clark wouldn’t be ashamed of you,” he replied easily. “You’re trying to protect people and your heart is in the right place. That would have been enough for him.”

“But he would have been disappointed?” Kara pressed him.

“He would have been worried,” her friend clarified. “Just like I am. You’re making the wrong choice. I know Lena has done a lot of good for the world, but this is going too far. One person can’t control everything, no matter how smart they are.”

She couldn’t quite hide her relief at his gentle tone. Of all her friends, it was James who reminded her of Clark the most. If he didn’t hate Kara for her choice…it felt like confirmation that Clark wouldn’t have hated her either.

Disappointment and disagreement, she could handle.

“Lena isn’t going to control everything,” Kara said calmly. “Despite what Lucy thinks, she doesn’t want to be a dictator. Lena wants to steer the world to prosperity, not take away everyone’s freedom.”

James nodded. “I know that. Lucy is…” he trailed off, wincing. “Understandably not in the best state of mind right now. She’s wrong about Lena in a lot of ways. But that doesn’t mean I think helping Lena take over the world is a good idea.”

Kara said nothing.

The photographer sighed. “Clark and I talked a lot about Krypton, you know.”

“Kal was only a baby when…when we left,” the hero pointed out.

Her mind was reeling. She didn’t mind that her cousin had talked to a trusted friend about their planet. Yet why hadn’t he talked to her?

“His parents placed their journals in his pod,” James explained. “They talked a lot about how Krypton was destroyed.”

Her gut clenched in a familiar pain. “The core imploded,” she gritted out.

“It could have been stopped,” the photographer said. “There were warning signs and potential countermeasures that could have been used. If the Council hadn’t been so certain that everything was fine, things could have been different.”

Kara placed a hand to her temple. “I remember,” she said. “My parents were some of those convinced by the Council. My aunt Astra disagreed. Why does this matter? What does it have to do with Lena?”

“Krypton was destroyed because all authority was placed in one body. A body that ended up making the wrong choice. All control was centralized.”

“In five years, my mother would have been on that Council,” Kara muttered. As a rising member of the Science Guild, Alura Zor-El had been all but destined to act as the guild’s representative on the Council.

James looked uncomfortable, but he was determined to continue. “I’m sure they meant well. At least, I can safely assume they didn’t want their planet destroyed. And it happened on their watch anyway. Clark always thought that if power wasn’t so concentrated on Krypton…if scientists and local governments had been given more freedom, the world might have been saved.” The photographer settled onto the sofa. “That was at least a Council. Lena is one person. If she succeeds at taking over the world, her mistakes become Earth’s mistakes. There’s no accountability and no safeguards.”

The hero’s eyes widened in understanding. So that was why Clark had refused all involvement in politics. He’d never given any statements or endorsements. Her cousin had been afraid that people would rely on his opinions, and his failures would be magnified.

“I get it, James,” Kara answered. “It’s a fair point. You know what else I’ve heard? Half of L-Corp’s alien employees have come from worlds where the opposite happened. Their planets were too divided to stand against external threats, and they fell one by one.”

“Those planets didn’t have Supergirl,” her friend argued. “They didn’t have Lena Luthor organizing people and advancing technology…things she could still do without going for world domination.”

Supergirl was very familiar with this argument. It was one she had made herself, countless times. Her mind had argued both sides of the issue as she’d made her decision, and it was a choice she was going to stick with.

“They had their own heroes and their own scientists. It wasn’t enough,” Kara said.

James wasn’t deterred. “And what happens if Lena dies, or is killed? It’s nearly happened more than once. Say she takes over the world and is assassinated? Then what? Are you going to take charge?”

“I don’t know,” Kara admitted. All of Lena’s plans depended on the CEO’s survival. If there were any contingencies, Kara was unaware of them. “I think if she dies, Earth is screwed. If her reign collapses, Earth is screwed. If she doesn’t gain control of most of the planet, Earth is screwed.” She shook her head. “Her plan isn’t a guarantee, but it’s the only hope we have. We’re outgunned and outnumbered by hostile forces, and galactic civilization is falling apart. Something will come for us, and we need to be ready.”

“Are you comfortable working with criminals, mind controlling enemies, blackmail, extortion, and imprisoning people without trial?” he demanded.

Kara shook her head. “No. Definitely not. But as long as Lena only targets the guilty, I can live with it for the sake of saving the Earth.”

The photographer turned to Winn. “What do you think?”

Winn shrugged. “Lena’s gained a lot of power in a short time. She’s done a lot of things that would make it hard for me to sleep at night. And if she hadn’t, Pestilence would have killed hundreds of millions of people. That was one powerful alien.” He paused, looking at James. “I think Kara’s right about this one.”

James sighed. “Okay.”

Kara frowned at him quizzically. “Okay?” she demanded.

“Yeah,” he replied. “I think this is a bad idea. Morally and practically. I hope you and Alex- and you-,” he nodded at Winn, “Come to your senses. That doesn’t mean I have to hate you, or that we can’t be friends.”

Kara let out a bewildered chuckle. “Seriously?” she asked. Supergirl’s steel faded into Kara Danvers’ rambling. “I’m technically a villain now. And a hero too, I guess, but still. Clark would have never been friends with a villain! How could you…?”

“Clark had a soft side just like everyone else,” James said. “He’d never befriend a killer, but a misguided minion he could probably tolerate. I don’t know why this is so strange to you,” he mused. “Isn’t this exactly what you did with Lena after you first met?”

The hero frowned. “Well, I…yeah,” she admitted. “So…we’re good?”

Her friend frowned. “I am horrified and disappointed, but…yes. We’re good!”

She jumped forward, enveloping him in a hug. Whatever their disagreements, James had stuck by her from the minute she’d become Supergirl, and his company would have been a painful loss. Their embrace only ended upon a hesitant cough from Winn.

“So, if you’re seeing Lena today?” the techie asked. “Think you could tell her I’m open for employment?”

\

“Hey, darling!” Lena stood up from her desk as Kara flew in from the balcony. “How did it go?”

The hero bit her lip. “Better than expected,” Kara admitted. “James is disappointed, but he doesn’t hate me for it. Lucy is, obviously, furious. And Winn…”

“Wants to join,” Lena finished for her. “Don’t worry, our tech operations could use him. It’d be nice to have someone we trust available to operate my suit remotely if need be. Now, as for you…”

Oh. Right. Kara was officially working for her girlfriend now. Which meant a job title, salary, and duties. Her feet began fidgeting, even as she told herself she had no reason to be nervous.

“How does Senior Vice President sound?”

“S-senior Vice President?” Kara sputtered.

The CEO grinned. “I did want you to be my second-in-command, remember? And I usually get what I want.” She stepped closer to the superhero, lightly running her fingers over Kara’s biceps. “I don’t intend to have you get involved with corporate matters. It’s not your area of expertise, obiously. You’re going to be a symbol, but one who has real authority if you need it.”

Kara suppressed a shiver as she melted into her girlfriend’s touch. Lena was radiating poise and confidence. It was almost intoxicating. “So…what will I actually be doing?”

“The usual, most of the time,” Lena answered. “Taking down villains, rescuing cats from trees, visiting hospitals. You’ll be making statements that make it clear you support me. When I need you, you’ll assist with peacekeeping efforts around the globe. Sometimes, with some particularly heavy construction, you’ll help me construct the L-Shield.”

The hero intended to answer with a cheeky ‘Oh, will I? I guess you’re the boss.’ Lena’s fingers running through her hair were making thinking difficult, however, and the best she managed was, “Uh huh, yeah.”

“Nothing overtly criminal,” Lena continued. “It’s not necessary at this stage, and you don’t have a secret identity any longer.”

Kara nodded. “So I’m going to be a glorified construction worker?” She smiled teasingly.

“Once in a while,” Lena admitted. She ran her hand lightly over the hero’s chest. “First day on the job and you’re being insubordinate already?” the CEO demanded. “I’ll have to think of an appropriate remand.”

I’ve never seen her so…happy. Years of tension seemed to have vanished from Lena’s shoulders over the last twenty-four hours. It didn’t take a genius to figure out the cause, and the confirmation that Lena cared about their relationship that much was enough to make Kara grin.

“Oh, and you’ll be wearing this.” The supervillain tapped an unfamiliar bracelet on her wrist. Instantly, a flow of nanites covered her body. Within a second, Lena was wearing a Supergirl suit.

It looked much the same as Kara’s own. The coloration was identical, the cape was still present, and her house crest was still proudly emblazoned on her chest. New, however, were the L-Corp symbols adorning her shoulders. Lena spun around, revealing a larger L-Corp crest adorning the back of her cape.

Oh, and the skirt had been replaced with pants.

“You’ll be wearing this from now on,” the villain said, turning back around. “It’s activated with a tap of the bracelet. Nearly perfect protection from red sun radiation and kryptonite. Using your code phrase, whether the suit is on or still in the bracelet, will imbue you with yellow sun radiation.”

Kara really wished her brain was focused on the details of the suit, instead of the fact that Lena was wearing her suit and looked damn hot doing so.

Her girlfriend seemed to mistake her awe for hesitation. “We can make changes if you want,” Lena said, biting her lip for the first time that day. “I thought it was time for an upgrade from the skirt, and-”

She interrupted the CEO with a searing kiss. “It’s perfect,” Kara said. “Is this my present for finally coming over to the dark side?”

“Not really.” Lena’s face was now burning red, something Kara took immense pride in. “I’ve been working on this for a while. The timing was simply convenient. The L-Corp logos are a recent addition, of course, though I can’t deny having thought about them for a while.” She tapped the bracelet again; the nanites instantly receded, leaving behind Lena’s business suit.

The hero wordlessly reached out, accepting the device. Now she knew why Lena had been willing to remove Kara’s other bracelet yesterday, despite the yellow sun capabilities.

“It only works if you tap it here,” Lena indicated. “And it only responds to your touch or mine. Speaking of a present for coming to the dark side…”

“Is it cookies?” Kara blurted out.

Lena rolled her eyes playfully. “No, though I did order some with our lunch. It should be here in a minute. I meant a salary. Do you want one?”

“No,” the hero answered instantly. “Supergirl doesn’t work for money. I wouldn’t feel comfortable taking it. You gave me an apartment and your credit card because you liked me, way before I started working for you, so I’m okay with those,” she explained. “I don’t need much, and I use your card to buy what I do need. That’s enough.”

Her boss chuckled. “As expected,” she said. “So be it. You’ll be the most underpaid Vice President in the history of business. If you change your mind, well, an eight-figure salary is always yours if you want it.”

“Lena!” Kara slapped the CEO on the arm. “What in Rao’s name would I need that kind of money for? You already pay for my apartment, and most…okay, all, of my caloric intake. What else would I need?”

Lena shrugged. “Maybe a vacation, for one thing.”

“I can fly anywhere in the world within minutes,” Kara pointed out. “Besides…” she leaned closer to  her boss, not quite pressing their lips together. “If I was going to go on vacation, I’d figure you’d be coming with me. And since you usually insist on paying for everything…”

Lena leaned back in mock offense. “Good to see you’re dating me for the right reasons,” she drawled. “I mean, you’re right, but still.”

\

“I know what a lot of people might think,” Kara spoke into the sea of microphones. Camera flashes accompanied her every word, reflecting off of her crisp new suit. “It’s true that I’m in a relationship with Lena Luthor. I’ve always believed she was a good person who was misguided. Recent events have made me realize I was the one who was misguided,” she said awkwardly.

Speaking to the press was never her strong suit.

“I stopped Pestilence. I was only able to do so because L-Corp gave me the resources to track her down. If it hadn’t been for Lena Luthor, millions would be dead by now,” Kara said firmly. “I’ve spoken with alien refugees from dozens of worlds. Krypton was destroyed by a natural disaster. Galactic civilization is in shambles. Since then, countless planets have fallen to hostile forces,” she continued.

“Are you giving into fear, Supergirl?” a reporter called out.

Kara shook her head. “I’m not trying to scare you. I’m trying to give you hope. Lena Luthor’s methods have worked so far. She’s accomplished things most of the planet would have never thought possible. The entire developed world has seen an increase in the stand of living thanks to her. Within the next few months, L-Corp will be focusing fully on developing nations. Poverty is going to be a memory. We’ll keep the Earth safe and make it better than ever.”

“You’ve backtracked on supporting Ms. Luthor before, Ms. Danvers. How do we know this time will be any different?”

The hero’s fingers clenched under the table. “Last time, I was under the influence of a rare type of kryptonite. I wasn’t thinking clearly, to say the least. Lena didn’t know at first, and when she found out, it was her research that brought me back.”

“You now fully support Ms. Luthor’s criminal enterprises, Supergirl?”

The hero stared down the cameras. “As an employee of L-Corp, I officially deny that my boss has engaged in any illegal activity,” she said, intentionally rolling her eyes. “If you’re asking whether I’m completely comfortable with every aspect of L-Corp…no, I’m not. But I’ve accepted them as necessary to save our planet.”

Another reporter cut in. "Supergirl what happened to the skirt?"

At least some people are asking the important questions. 

\

Reign forced herself to turn away from the television screen. It was the most sickening press conference she had ever seen. In spite of all of her efforts, all of her scheming…Kara Zor-El was now officially pledging her allegiance to Lena Luthor for the entire world to see.

It represented nothing less than Reign’s abject failure.

She looked back at her communicator, staring at her superior’s face. “Mistress, I fear that things have become much more difficult. With Kara Zor-El now Luthor’s puppet, and permission to reclaim Pestilence’s powers from Alex Danvers denied, the future is uncertain.”

“How quickly you lose faith,” her Mistress replied. “Our arrival is only months away. The key to Luthor’s defense network is at your disposal. Most importantly, do not forget the vast power that our leader possesses. Nothing on Earth could hope to stop it.”

At that, Reign allowed herself a grin. How cathartic it would be to watch Lena Luthor fall beneath the greatest power in the universe. All of her preparations, allies, and technology would be nothing before the deadliest force galactic civilization had ever known.

The Omega Effect.
