New Recruits?

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Lena had failed.

Her plan had been simple. In the past week since the new phase of their relationship had begun, the hero had renewed her quest of having Lena watch every Disney movie that had ever been released.

Unfortunately, this included the direct-to-video sequels.

The CEO had tried to argue that her ownership of a controlling stake in the Disney corporation was enough to fulfill her Disney-quota. Kara had merely shaken her head.

She could agree with Kara that it was a shame Lillian had banned any Disney throughout her childhood. Some of the movies were fantastic and truly inspirational. Others, however, were just bad. Kara enjoyed them all, minus the overt racism and sexism. Alex had explained to Lena that Disney films had been one of Kara’s first means of introduction to human culture…Eliza having wanted to get her off to an optimistic start.

Which meant Lena couldn’t bring herself to refuse watching them all. The only thing she could do- and did, with relish- was use her stake in the company to prevent them from releasing any more direct-to-video films. Forever.

Of course, being a good girlfriend had its rewards. More than once, both women had fallen asleep on Lena’s sofa during the end credits. Sleeping beside Kara was wonderful, so much so that the CEO had begun trying to get them to both fall asleep after every movie.

This time, she’d failed. Even as Lena had closed her eyes and willfully begun to nod off, Kara was still well awake. There was a gentle sigh from the hero before Lena was lifted into her arms and carried into her bedroom.

It was only when Kara was moving to leave, after placing a kiss on the CEO’s forehead, that Lena found her courage.

“Don’t leave me.”

Her girlfriend frowned. “I’m just going downstairs to get some rest. Big day tomorrow. Why? Is something wrong?”

Lena bit her lip. How could she explain her nightmares? That nearly every night, her dreams tormented her with images. Her mother drowning. The Earth falling to invasion. Kara bleeding out on the ground right in front of her eyes.

Damn the Black Mercy to hell.

 “I need a hug,” the world-conquering supervillain pleaded. “Just stay with me tonight. Those clothes are comfortable enough.”

Something in Lena’s eyes must have shown through, because Kara nodded. Gingerly scooting the CEO over, she eased herself into the bed. Lena felt a wave of calm wash over her as Supergirl’s arms wrapped around her from behind.

There would be no nightmares tonight.

\

Kara woke up alone.

She was lying on an unfamiliar bed, her hair was a mess, and the lack of teeth brushing had made her mouth grimy. As the memories of the previous night came back to her, the hero pushed herself off the sheets.

As Kara made her way into the bathroom and rinsed out her mouth, her thoughts turned to Lena. It hadn’t been since the aftermath of the Black Mercy’s attack that she had seen the CEO so vulnerable. It didn’t make sense. Everything had been calm since Pestilence’s attack.

The sound of sizzling permeated through the air, luring Kara towards the apartment’s kitchen. Lena was standing in front of the stove, still in her nightgown. A steadily browning pancake was resting in the pan, as a stack of them sat on a plate nearby. There was a full pot of coffee already made, with a cup clearly having been laid out for Kara.

“Morning,” the CEO said easily.

Nope. She’s not dodging the question this easily. “Lena, this looks great, but we need to talk. Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?”

“Nothing I’m not used to,” the CEO replied as she flipped the pancake. “Can you grab the butter and syrup from the refrigerator?”

Distracting Kara with her favorite breakfast food was clever, but it wouldn’t be enough. “Nice try,” the hero said, nevertheless moving to the fridge and doing as requested. “I saw the look on your face last night.”

“Can we just drop it?” Lena’s voice had a hard edge to it.

Placing the syrup on the table, Kara crossed her arms. “You’ve been having nightmares, haven’t you?”

The villain scowled. “Of course I have. It’s already been established that I have a guilt complex and a borderline god complex. I’m trying to take over the world, remember? Did you really expect me to sleep peacefully?”

Kara shifted awkwardly. Lena had been through a lot. “Have…have you ever considered going to therapy? I’m sure you could afford a session or two.”

Her girlfriend groaned. “No point. I know every trick in the book,” she said. “I know a therapist’s response to everything I could say before I even say it. I’m sure I would be interesting for one of them to study, but it wouldn’t do me any good.” She paused. “I usually could handle the nightmares. It wasn’t until after I saw you bleeding out, when we were in the Black Mercy…”

Kara winced.

“I swear, if you apologize for stabbing yourself to save my life, I will punch you,” Lena warned with a small smile.

The hero thought back to last night, remembering Lena grabbing her wrist. “Did sleeping with me help?”

Lena dipped her head. “More than you can imagine. Having a physical reminder that you’re safe, and that I’m not alone…it quiets the thoughts in my head.”

The  hero glanced around the apartment. True, they hadn’t been dating for very long, but they were already in a preliminary engagement. Any excuse for her to spend more time with her girlfriend was a win-win, anyway.

“Let’s move in together,” Kara said. “We can take out part of the floor between our apartments and add a set of stairs. It’s a lot of space for the two of us, but I’d hate to give up all those features you added just for me,” she said. The sun lamps, high thread sheets, and regular high-calorie deliveries had been amazing.

The villain’s jaw was slightly gaped open. “You want to move in with me…just because I told you I’m having nightmares?”

Kara nodded. “Yes! Well, there are other reasons, I guess. I like spending time with you, in case you haven’t noticed. Obviously. Since we’re dating and all,” she breathed. “Also…” she broke off as a shiver ran through her. Some memories were best kept buried. “I’m not a huge fan of sleeping alone, either. It reminds me of…you know.”

She could see in Lena’s eyes that her girlfriend understood. Hypersleep or not, decades spent in a pod drifting through space had been traumatizing. After so much time trapped with nothing but her own thoughts, was it any wonder Kara never enjoyed being alone?

“Okay,” Lena agreed. The relief in her voice was palpable. “I’ll make the arrangements today. We can sleep in your room for now while they install sun lamps up here.”

Kara frowned. “Why don’t we just live down in my place full time? We can just keep this floor as a loft.”

“That won’t do,” Lena said, chuckling. “Remember, I’m a CEO who is taking over the world. It’s expected of me to sleep in the penthouse. Don’t worry; I’ll make sure all the adjustments made for you downstairs are added up here. Now, are you going to help me eat these pancakes?”

“Me help you?” Kara demanded. “I’ll let you have one if you’re lucky,” she said with a wink. “Remember, I have an important mission today. I need to be at my best.”

Lena chuckled. “So do I.”

\

Ding dong!

The door to the suburban house opened to reveal a young man. He was good looking but unremarkable in terms of appearance, with dark brown hair and hazel eyes. His face was friendly, but he frowned in confusion upon looking at Kara.

“Yes? You…look familiar.”

The hero nodded. “Yeah, losing your secret identity will do that to you. I’m Supergirl,” she said easily. “And you’re Barry Allen. Anyway, I was looking for the Flash and I know who you are, so I was hoping we could-”

BOOM! The air rippled around her as Barry morphed into a red blur. Before Kara could blink, he was zipping past her and disappearing down the street.

We’re off to a great start.

\

Immediately after she teleported into the cave, unsurprised words greeted her.

“I knew you would come eventually.”

Lena stared into the darkness. “I knew you would know that,” she said flatly. “Now let’s get down to business. I’ve left Wayne Enterprises alone out of respect for all your good work, both in the suit and out. But now it’s time for you to join the fold.”

There was another reason, both obvious and left unsaid. The hero’s sidekick had been brutally murdered by his arch-enemy several months ago. Since then, sightings of the caped hero had gone down significantly. Only in the last few weeks had he resumed his regular patrols of Gotham.

“You’re not evil, Ms. Luthor,” the superhero spoke. He was sitting in front of his sprawl of computer monitors, fully decked out in his supersuit. “You’re just deluded. Let me make one thing clear…I will never work with you. Your compassion doesn’t excuse your obsession with power. And you are a killer.”

Lena allowed the nanites to retract from her body, leaving only her business suit behind. “I’ve never taken a life directly. If you’re referring to Supergirl killing Pestilence, well, it was necessary.”

“I’m sure it was,” the hero countered. “Just like everything else you do; it will all be necessary. When you rule the Earth through fear, it will be necessary. Killing more people and holding the rest hostage under your guns will be necessary,” he said, his voice dripping with venom. “I’ve seen your kind many times before, Ms. Luthor, and it always ends the same way.”

The CEO crossed her arms. This was definitely going worse than expected. “I’m here to ask for your help defending the Earth, not to trade thinly veiled threats.”

“Heroes defend the Earth,” he replied. “Villains want to rule it. You’re not your brother; you act rationally and you have patience. That makes you far more dangerous.” The hero glared at her from underneath his cowl. “I know what happens if you ‘win’. You’ll spend the rest of your existence desperately clinging onto power. Humanity hates being controlled, and it will never just sit back and obey you. You’ll keep crossing lines to maintain your rule, all for the ‘common good’, until one day you wake up and realize you’re just as bad as the monsters you wanted to protect us from.”

Lena’s fists clenched. “Fine. There’s no convincing you for now,” the villain said. “Keep working on your own. I have no interest in stopping your work as a vigilante or a philanthropist. If you interfere with my plans, however, I can’t guarantee such restraint. I’ll buy out your company and leave you nothing except this manor and your trust fund.”

He smirked. “Here’s my counteroffer.” His finger twitched.

PAIN!

Lena dropped to her knees. White hot knives were burrowing through her eardrums and penetrating her skull. She rolled across the floor in agony, all other thoughts forgotten. It felt like the blades of sound were slicing through her brain tissue, setting her skull on fire.

The hero rose from his chair, completely unaffected.

It was extremely high-pitched sound. Inaudible to human ears. Too high pitched to be picked up even by her suit’s passive sensors.

Her hands reflexively covered her ears, but there was no escape from the all-encompassing noise. The Vanity suit could be activated through mental command alone and would have blocked the sound, but the pain was so great she couldn’t even begin to focus her thoughts. Vocal activation was similarly impossible.

The only sound Lena could make was a constant scream. 

\

Using her own superspeed, Kara changed into her supersuit within milliseconds and took off after him. He was fast. Faster than Kara? Yes, definitely. Faster than Reign? Probably. But he wasn’t quite fast enough to disappear from her telescopic vision instantly.

Supergirl flew behind him. She fought back the urge to yell that she wasn’t there to fight; there was no way he would be able to hear her. As they zoomed through the Ohio suburbs, Kara felt their speed begin to equalize. Evidently, he was slowing himself down enough to not cause damage to the streets. The airborne hero had no such concerns to worry about.

She kept pace with him as they continued north. The ground beneath them shifted into water as they headed over Lake Erie. The Flash sped across the water effortlessly, only to come to an instant stop upon a small, uninhabited island.

Kara touched down nearby, holding up her hands to quell any semblance of hostility. “I’m not here to fight,” she said. “I just want to talk.”

The other hero glanced at her cautiously. “Well, that’s a relief,” he said. His voice sounded sincere. “If we were going to fight, I wanted to do it away from civilization.”

Her regard for him instantly increased. Their information hadn’t been able to confirm whether the Flash was a reckless glory hound or a mature superhero. He simply hadn’t yet faced any opponents that forced him to truly test his abilities.

Rogue aliens were far more likely to appear in California than the Midwest. Why? Kara wasn’t certain, but the data bore her out.

“It’s nice to meet you. I was a big fan. But I have to admit, I was hoping you wouldn’t show up,” he said.

Huh?

“I was wondering if Luthor would come for me eventually,” Barry admitted. “I’m not interested in tangling with her. I’d almost certainly lose and end up dead or being dissected. And even if I won, well, L-Corp is too big to fail now, isn’t it? Is that why you signed up?”

Kara looked at him curiously. “I realized she was the Earth’s best chance to survive. It wasn’t a choice I made easily. What about you?” she questioned. “Why try to avoid her?”

Barry chuckled, but there was a clear undercurrent of worry on his face. “I’m not interested in world conquest,” he replied. “I want to help people in the best way I can, however I can. Central City needed a hero, so I stepped in.”

“Good,” Supergirl replied. “Unfortunately, that’s not always going to be enough. Earth’s defenders need to come together and cooperate.”

The Flash sighed. “Look, I can tell you made the choice you did for the best of reasons,” he said sympathetically. “But I’m never going to be comfortable helping take down governments and manipulating an entire planet.”

“Neither am I.” Kara crossed her arms. “I’m just even less comfortable leaving our planet vulnerable to an alien invasion.” She took a moment to laugh inwardly at the irony. How many times had she participated in the same exact argument from the other side?”

Barry didn’t look convinced. “Why do you want me?” he asked. “I’m the Fastest Man Alive, but you and Luthor already have all the firepower you need. I’m good with tech, but I don’t have anything you guys don’t.”

“We have enough firepower to take control of the Earth,” Kara said. “We might not have enough for what’s coming. Lena wants the heroes of the world to unite and work together.”

“Under her thumb,” Barry pointed out.

Kara dipped her head in acknowledgment. “She’d be in charge, yes. That doesn’t mean all of us wouldn’t have the freedom to do as we wished or leave at any time. All of her resources would be at our disposal,” the hero said, making no effort to hide her enthusiasm for the idea. “We could form a network so sophisticated that the supervillains wouldn’t have a chance.”

If there was one benefit to Lena having been under the Black Mercy, it was placing this idea in the forefront of her mind. The world of her fantasy had been protected by a ‘Justice League’ that had virtually eliminated large scale crime on Earth. There was no reason not to try and make it a reality.

“And where would those villains go?” Barry asked. “To a hidden prison without trial.”

“Only if we couldn’t find enough evidence to convict them,” Supergirl countered. “Look,” she said with a smile. “I’m not expecting you to join up with us after one conversation. Right now, I just want to convince you that we’re not evil.”

He gave her a small grin in return. “Well, you haven’t blackmailed or threatened me, which you easily could have. You haven’t even tried offering me money.”

“We are willing to do that,” Supergirl admitted. “But I was hoping that wouldn’t make the difference. We’d gain a supporter, but I’d respect you a lot less.”

Barry nodded. “Good,” he echoed.

“Here’s what I want you to take.” She stepped forward, reaching for the L-Phone in her pocket. “This will let you get in touch with me or Lena instantly. You need anything to help you fight a villain- technology, backup, tracking, advice from a super-genius…it’s all right there. Even money, if it’s to help you fight crime.”

He shot her a hesitant look. “What’s the catch?” he demanded. “Other than the tracking device that I know is on that phone.”

“You want that on there,” Kara said. “If you ever get taken down in a surprise attack, who is going to save you? If we know where you are, we could help you. I have one in my bracelet, and it’s saved my life multiple times.” She paused. “We didn’t need help finding you today, and we could have knocked you out and placed a tracker under your skin without you noticing.”

“I suppose,” Barry agreed, still not reaching for the phone.

Kara took another step forward. “We’re not asking for anything right now. You’re right, we don’t need you to take over the world, and we’re not ready to form an organization of heroes yet. Right now, we just want to be able to communicate with Earth’s strongest heroes…and make sure they stay alive. If something apocalyptic comes up, we’ll call you and expect you to come, but wouldn’t you want to be there if that happened?” The hero glanced down at her hands. “We could have used you fighting Pestilence.”

He winced. “Yeah, that looked ugly,” he said in agreement.

“I was only able to stop her because I had access to Lena’s network,” Kara added. “We all should have the same resource if a crisis occurs. For now, it’s limited cooperation and an agreement to fight the next apocalypse. Is that good enough?”

Barry stared at her for a long time.

“Okay,” he answered, taking the phone at last. “I don’t see why you would go through all this if you didn’t mean it. Don’t take this as an endorsement of Luthor’s world domination or try and present it to the media that way.” He frowned. “Please?”

Kara could have laughed. “Deal,” she agreed.

\

The entire ordeal lasted five seconds.

It was enough time for the hero to fire his grappling hook pistol at her wrist with expert precision. Her bracelet, usually bound to her wrist via her thoughts, caught easily. As Lena continued to squirm in agony, it flew off  her skin landed in his outstretched palm. Her vision began to blacken.

Clever. He’d predicted her arrival and prepared for it. The hero had capitalized on one of her few vulnerabilities and managed to capitalize. Somehow, he’d known that her enhanced hearing was better at picking up high-pitched frequencies than her suit.

Lena’s heart rate hit one-hundred and eighty beats per minute.

It was a last-ditch failsafe in her bracelet. Independent of her thoughts, the suit would come to her and activate if her brainwaves detected a dangerously high heartrate. Before her unwilling host could even think about storing her bracelet, it zoomed out of his palm and back onto the villain’s wrist. Instantly, it activated.

Blissful relief swept through her body as the Vanity suit covered her ears. The automatic sound-filtering of the nanites immediately kicked in.

The aftermath left her trembling on the ground, squirming as residual spasms of pain flared up in her skull. Now in control of her suit again, Lena mentally commanded the nanites above her mouth to retract a second before she vomited directly over the cave floor.

“How?” the hero demanded. 

Struggling onto her hands and knees, Lena glared at him. There was no point in remaining. Nothing more was needed to be said, and the villain certainly wasn’t in the right state of mind.

In a flash, she teleported out of the cave.

Chapter End Notes

Time Skip coming up soon.

Ups and Downs

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Okay, I’m ready.”

The first humanoid drone stepped out onto the wide training floor. Alex stared it down impassively. The injections she’d recently received had temporarily decreased the effect of the Harun-El on her DNA. She’d been left strong enough to become more comfortable with her superhuman abilities but was now too weak to destroy the drones outright.

Nth metal was expensive, after all.

Her opponent rocketed towards her. Every single drone in L-Corp’s armada was capable of flight. More importantly, they’d been programmed with a wide array of fighting techniques. With Alex’s strength and speed now only slightly greater than the drone’s own, it would be a tough fight.

The drone feinted with a jab before continuing with its momentum into a swinging kick. It was a fast move, but Alex dodged it easily. It came up again with a haymaker aimed at her gut, but the security chief simply leaned to the side.

I did take those injections, right?

 Perhaps she was simply growing more used to her powers. Alex knew that at full strength, her current Harun-El levels would enable her to crack the drone’s endoskeleton. That was exactly what she was aiming for.

As her body tensed with anticipation, Alex’s mind cast around for motivation. Instantly, an image of Sam popped into her thoughts. Snarling, Alex cast her fist forward, channeling all of her rage, frustration, and disappointment into the blow.

The drone exploded.

Well, not exactly. The metal crumpled the instant Alex’s fist made contact with its exterior. Countless cracks spread throughout the endoskeleton, shattering the carapace. All that was left was a pile of metal shards and wiring scattered across the floor.

What?

Even at her full power, that shouldn’t have been possible. Only Kara herself should have been capable of such a feet.

“Can someone tell me what the hell just happened?”

Judging by the silence in her earpiece, it seemed that the observing technicians were at just as much of a loss.

Am I stronger than we thought? Did those injections somehow strengthen the Harun-El instead of weakening it?

It was insane, but unless the drone was defective, nothing else made sense. She glanced skyward, looking at the reinforced ceiling dozens of meters above. Under her current Harun-el levels, she shouldn’t be able to reach it.

It was as good a test as any. Tensing her legs, Alex called forth all her strength before jumping upwards.

Ah! Only a desperate reversal of momentum prevented her from smashing through the ceiling. Instead, she slammed into it like a pancake. Alex shook her head, shaking off chunks of concrete and steel.

“Ma’am?” Her earpiece beckoned. “Ms. Danvers, you appear to be floating.”

Alex looked down at the ground. She wasn’t stuck to the ceiling. Her body was levitating right under it, allowing her to look down at the floor far below. Her stomach jolted at the strange sensation. She’d always envied her sister’s ability to fly (who wouldn’t). But experiencing it for herself…

Concentrating, Alex willed herself to float towards the ground. The fluttering in her chest steadily decreased as the floor approached. She found herself instinctively using her arms to propel herself downwards, as if she was swimming, but it clearly wasn’t necessary. Flight was controlled by thought alone.

The second she touched the ground, Alex ran over to where she’d left her phone. Ignoring the voice in her ear, she scrolled though her contacts. Her first instinct was to call her sister, but in this situation the scientist was more desperately needed.

Ring. Ring.

 “H-hello?” Lena’s voice spoke through the phone.

“It’s Alex,” the security chief replied. “You okay? You sound…off.” There’d been a certain hesitance in the CEO’s voice, something Alex wasn’t used to hearing.

A strange sound came though, as if Lena was wiping her mouth. “I’m fine. I just had a rather unpleasant encounter. What’s going on?”

Alex took a breath. “Something is happening with my powers. I took the injections and still smashed one of your drones to paste. When I jumped up…I flew, Lena! I was hovering in midair and everything! I thought you said that was impossible?”

“It is impossible!” Lena immediately replied. “Human DNA can’t take on enough Harun-El to accomplish flight. Are you certain you were flying?”

“Dead certain.”

Several seconds passed. All Alex could hear over the phone was the villain’s heavy breathing. What the hell is going on.

“Alex, listen carefully. You need to quarantine yourself immediately. Contact anyone you’ve recently been in close contact with and have them do the same. No exceptions. Do it. Now,” Lena ordered.

The security chief’s eyes narrowed in confusion. “Why? I don’t understand.”

“No. But I think I do,” Lena replied. “Quarantine yourself now. Do not go outside. Do not have physical contact with anyone. Tell any L-Corp employees with you to do the same. Failure to comply will result in immediate termination of their employment.”

“Lena-”

“No arguing!” the CEO’s voice retorted. “Millions of lives could be at stake. I’ll explain when I get to you. Find a room and isolate yourself immediately.”

This can’t be good.

\

Lena’s mind was spinning. The dots were connecting, and not in a way that provided reassurance.

Could it have been possible for Pestilence’s powers to have transferred to Alex? It didn’t seem possible, but then, even Lena herself didn’t understand all of the secrets of Harun-El. Perhaps the substance had acted as a magnet of sorts…

No. Superpowers are not a physical object. They live and die with their owners.

Except for the fact that Alex could now float in the air. Alex, who had been infused with Harun-El and been right next to Pestilence when she died. Lena remembered Reign’s determination to bring Pestilence down. Had part of her reasoning been a fear that the Worldkiller’s power would fall into Lena’s hands?

The powers of the Worldkillers were different from Kara’s. They were stronger and more varied. Was it possible that they came from a source other than that of the sun? If Kara died, her powers would die with her. Perhaps the abilities of a Worldkiller were different in that respect as well.

Harun-el had given its bearers immunity from Pestilence’s powers. Pestilence had referred to the substance as ‘heresy’ during her fight with Alex. The obvious conclusion was that there was a link between the Worldkillers and Harun-el itself.

Maybe their powers are, at least partially, a product of Harun-el? Instead of fading, if they transferred to the nearest source of Harun-el…

In the five seconds after learning that Alex could fly, these were the thoughts that had gone through her mind. The idea seemed ludicrous, but Lena had long since learned to trust her instincts.

She ordered Alex to go into quarantine. If Alex had Pestilence’s powers, without having full control over them, could she release another virus. Lena could not allow the world to go through that. Not again.

\

“You’re joking.”

Lena turned to glare at her. “Does this look like a joke to you?” she demanded, keeping her eyes glued on the window. Inside, Kara’s sister was currently floating in midair. Twin beams of green energy were streaming from Alex’s eyes, obliterating the target in front of her.

“No, it’s just…I can’t believe it!” Kara breathed. “She looks like a Kryptonian. I never thought I would see something like that again.” An image of Clark appeared in her mind.

The CEO looked at her curiously. “Aren’t you worried? Somehow, your sister has gained the powers of a Worldkiller that nearly destroyed human civilization.”

“Alex wouldn’t do that,” Kara pointed out. Wasn’t that obvious?

“Not intentionally,” Lena agreed. “But if she can’t control her abilities, that might happen if we don’t keep her contained.”

Supergirl was still staring at her sister in awe. “She seems to have pretty good control right now,” Kara argued. “How did this happen? And how can she have such control? It took me years to figure out how to fly and control my heat vision!” Ever since they’d been kids, Kara had always feared that Alex was jealous of her powers.

Now it might be the other way around!

 Lena sighed, replying with what Kara knew were her girlfriend’s three least favorite words in the English language. “I don’t know,” the villain admitted. “It might have something to do with her fact that her powers don’t seem to come from the sun…she developed them instantly, not gradually like you did. I’m just theorizing at this point.”

Supergirl wrapped an encouraging arm around her. “You’ll figure it out,” Kara promised. “You always do.” Lena shook her head in exasperation, but the hero didn’t miss how her heartrate calmed down slightly. Or how she leaned into Kara’s embrace.

“I better,” Lena said. “If Alex can’t control her abilities, she’s going to have to spend all her time in quarantine until I learn how they work.

Kara gulped.

“Okay Alex.” The CEO spoke into the comms. “That room is completely sealed. The only things alive in there are you and that potted plant. I want you to try and infect it with Pestilence’s powers.”

Alex was still floating through the air, now doing loops. Her normally reserved demeanor was entirely gone. Learning that she had just received potentially civilization-ending powers had done nothing to erase the smile from her face.

“Alright,” she said, floating over to the plant.

Lena nodded. “Pestilence’s powers worked by sapping living organisms of their energy and rotting them from the inside. I want you to see if you can control when the virus operates, how powerful it is, and -most importantly- if you can make it disappear when you want.”

They didn’t have to wait long for the results. Within minutes, the leaves on the plant had turned into a sickly brown color. Kara looked at the experiment in horror. Lena was staring at the results intently while Alex seemed…interested.

“Can you stop it now?” the CEO asked.

Alex snapped her fingers. The decay on the plant instantly stopped spreading. Within another few minutes, it was clear the plant was beginning to recover.

“For the record, the snap wasn’t necessary,” Alex said. “I feel…connected to the virus. I can sense where it is, how strong it is, and how fast it spreads. All I have to do is want it to disappear, and it does.”

Kara breathed a sigh of relief. Yet the knowledge that her sister wouldn’t have to be quarantined did nothing to dissipate her jealousy. “It took me a month to learn how to float. Float, Lena. It’s not fair,” she whined petulantly.

Her girlfriend chuckled. “Supergirl, you might be the first alien to receive godlike abilities from sunlight to complain that the distribution of superpowers is unfair.” Through her amusement, Lena’s relief was evident. And there was something else there too. Was that a glint of eagerness in her eyes?

Oh, yeah. That’s right. I’m dating a supervillain.

\

Despite the promising start, Lena insisted on five hours of various tests before she allowed Alex to leave her confinement. Even after the security chief had demonstrated enough control over her abilities to the villain’s satisfaction, it was clear that Lena’s curiosity was far from sated.

Kara glanced at her sister sympathetically. Alex had hours of serving as Lena’s lab rat ahead of her.

Supergirl was sitting on L-Corp’s balcony, watching as Alex zoomed away through the air. L-Corp would be having a press conference tomorrow about a new superhero, Kara was sure. Hopefully, they would be able to keep the details about how those power had been obtained under wraps.

“She’s going to be floating everywhere for weeks,” the hero said in-between pizza slices. “It’s a hard habit to break. And if her powers are anything like mine, her caloric intake is going to skyrocket over the next few weeks.”

Lena glanced up from her phone, pausing her efforts to complete her latest corporate buyout. “Believe me, I’m aware,” she said, glancing pointedly at the boxes of pizza surrounding the hero. “I assure you that I pay your sister well enough to afford all the food she requires. Anyway…” she smiled at Kara. “I hear congratulations are in order.”

“For what?”

“Your first successful mission for L-Corp,” Lena clarified. “The Flash might not be on our side quite yet, but the fact that he’s willing to work with us is a big development. I wish I had been as lucky today.”

Kara raised an eyebrow. “What happened?”

“He slipped past my defenses and I ended up puking my guts out on the cave floor.” At the hero’s look of horror, she continued. “Don’t look so horrified. One of my contingencies kicked in. If I’d wanted to beat the shit out of him, I could have.”

Despite her girlfriend’s projected confidence, Supergirl couldn’t suppress a tinge of fear. The only people to have gotten the better of Lena had done so through both luck and overwhelming power. Hearing that she’d been brought low by an entirely mortal man was…unsettling.

“So I guess he’s not working with us.”

“No,” Lena agreed. “It’s a shame, he really does have a lot of potential. Deep down, he’s a good person. He’s devoted his entire life to helping others and constantly places himself at tremendous risk. Not unlike someone else I know,” she glanced at Kara meaningfully. “Unfortunately, his perspective was warped through tragedy…he’s never been able to overcome it.”

Kara bit her lip.

The CEO placed a hand over Kara’s own. “It’s a loss, but nothing is going to stop us. Now that you and I are working together, there’s no limit to what we can achieve.”

She nodded. “If Clark and Lex had worked together, things would be so much better now. Instead it was all sacrificed for a stupid and petty feud. I’m…I’m glad things are different with us.” Kara couldn’t help but smile as she said those words. The hero felt imbued with hope.

“This planet is going to be ours, and we’re going to make it better for everyone,” Lena said. “A lot of this is going to be covered at the company meeting tomorrow, but I think my Senior VP deserves some advanced notice.” She grinned teasingly.

Kara wolfed down another slice of pizza. “Go on. Tell me how we’re going to achieve world domination.”

The CEO ran a finger along Kara’s arm. “We already have Kaznia. In a few months, I think at least twenty smaller nations will have followed suit. People have seen now what L-Corp can accomplish. Some leaders of poorer countries will join us willingly. Dictators will be convinced just like they were in Kaznia.”

Kara shuddered. She still wasn’t a fan of Lena’s methods, but she’d seen what happened in Kaznia. A nation of poverty and rubble was rapidly being rebuilt. If that could be spread to other countries, Supergirl was all for it.

“In the U.S., Europe, China, Russia, India, Japan…L-Corp is growing ever more popular. Thanks in no small part to your endorsement. We have so many bargaining chips now, thanks to our dominance in the technological and finance markets,” Lena explained. “Leaders who don’t want to work with us will be easily swept aside.”

“Swept aside?”

The CEO nodded. “Forced out of office by either the populace or their own governments. L-Corp’s technology is now decades ahead of our closest competitors. There’s so much we can offer now. Soon, we’ll be beginning localized terraforming efforts.” Lena’s eyes were shining now. “Imagine half of the Sahara Desert turning green, Kara. Widespread settlements across Greenland, even Antarctica. Free and clean energy for any who want it. How many people are going to say no to these things?”

Not many. “Vanity’s mission wasn’t just to steal ideas from other companies,” Kara realized. “It was to help ensure you had a monopoly on all aliens coming to be employed on Earth.”

Lena nodded. “A lot of them had information on technology humans have barely dreamt of. It’s taken me months to understand some of it. Now I’m at the point where I can start implementing it…and improving it.”

“Months, she says,” Kara scoffed playfully. “It’s taken her months to figure out alien technology, implement it, and surpass it. Truly shameful.”

It was the villain’s mind that had gotten them this far. That impossibly high IQ that forced her to develop new computer chess programs just so she could have a semblance of a challenge. Lena could plan and develop new technology faster than her closest peers could even fathom.

The hero winced inwardly. Her girlfriend’s intelligence was impressive. And sexy. Even still, the power base that it was developing was fragile. Lena could take over the world and gain control of its resources, all she had to do was offer humanity safer, easier, and more comfortable lives. As long as she granted basic freedoms to those who had none and preserved them for those that did, most would follow her.

But if she died, it would all crumble. Kara wasn’t sure how to vocalize that thought, and her mind refused to even try. The world needed Lena Luthor’s intelligence. Kara Danvers needed Lena Luthor.

Beep. Beep. The CEO’s phone rang.

“Hello?” Lena spoke into it. She listened quietly for a few seconds. “Alright, I’ll go take a look.” As she put her foot down, the Vanity suit materialized over her body. “Come on, Kara. There’s something we need to go look at.”

\

Supergirl stared at the ground. “Rao. What is this?”

They were floating hundreds of feet above the Gobi Desert. The sand below had been irrevocably altered. A trail of heat had scorched a symbol into the sea of sand. An entire square mile had been claimed by the ominous visage.

Lena was levitating beside her. After several moments, the villain retracted the nanites around her head. Kara was startled to see her girlfriend’s skin as pale as it had ever been. “Reign did this,” the villain said. “She’s sending us a message.”

“What?”

The CEO stared at the ground. “Do you have any idea what that symbol is? I never thought…I didn’t think he would target Earth. I’ve never met an alien who liked talking about it, about him, but I’ve heard the stories.” Lena visibly shivered.

Kara didn’t recognize it. Krypton had been relatively isolated from the rest of the galaxy before its destruction. She’d seen the symbol before on Earth, as a Greek letter, but the hero didn’t think that was what Lena was referring to.

“That is the crest of the worst evil in the universe,” Lena spoke softly. “He exists as the manifestation of tyranny. His only goal is to spread misery, terror, and subjugation as far as he can. Across the entire universe, his name is a synonym of fear. They say he’s wiped out an entire pantheon of gods and stolen their power for his own. He rules over a literal hellscape…imagine a concentration camp stretching across an entire planet. And now he’s coming for us.”

Supergirl trembled. “You think Reign is working for this thing?”

“That’s the message we’ve been given. He’s…a thousand times worse than Lex. He’s cruel, sadistic, evil to the core, but still rational and patient. The scariest thing about him isn’t that he’s insane, Kara,” Lena spoke. “It’s that he is entirely in his right mind, and his only objective is to engulf the universe in pain.”

“You’re placing a lot of faith in stories,” the hero pointed out.

Lena glared at her. “Nearly identical stories, that I’ve heard from aliens who live within ten billion lightyears of his planet. The Green Lanterns and New Genesis together were barely enough to keep him in check. Now that the Lanterns are gone…”

Not since Kara had stabbed herself with Lena’s Black Mercy hallucination had she seen such fear on her girlfriend’s face. “So what do we do?”

The CEO swallowed. “We take over this planet, we finish the L-Shield, and we prepare every defense imaginable. We’ll redouble our efforts to recruit every metahuman and powerful alien on Earth into an army of heroes. Then, when he arrives, we pray that all of our efforts were enough to give us a ghost of a chance.”

A bead of sweat was dripping down Kara’s forehead as she nodded. Now, more than ever, she was certain that joining Lena had been the right decision. Hopefully, it would be enough. She looked down at the symbol again, imprinting it into her mind.

“I can’t believe I agreed to do this.”

Kara merely smiled. “Even supervillains need to take a break once in a while,” she pointed out. “Besides, out of all of us, you’re the one who has the nicest place.”

“We’re the ones who have the nicest place,” the CEO corrected. “You moved in with me, remember?” She leaned forward, catching Kara’s lips in a kiss that only remained chaste because of the apartment’s current visitor.

Eliza looked up from her baking. “You two are so adorable. Please pretend I’m not here,” she said.

“Too late for that,” the superhero replied.

Lena’s eyes didn’t quite comprehend what they were seeing. It had been days since they had been presented with evidence that an alien dictator had his sights set on Earth. Yet somehow, the CEO had been pressured into helping Kara host a holiday party even as her world domination schemes continued apace.

How did this happen? She thought to herself.

Her girlfriend turned back towards her, wearing a beaming smile, and wrapped her in a hug. “I really appreciate this, Lena, you know that,” Kara said, her eyes shining with affection.

Oh, right. Now I remember.  

Now Eliza was in their kitchen, baking a large dinner despite Lena’s repeated insistence that she was more than happy to hire a caterer. Apparently, tradition was tradition, trillionaire girlfriends be dammed.

It did smell rather good.

“Are you sure about this?” Lena asked. “I know there’s no way Lucy will come if I’m hosting. She’s always hated me, and now she blames me for…what happened.”

“I’m sure,” the superhero replied immediately.

Eliza’s head popped over the counter. “Lucy refused to step foot in the same room as you,” the elder woman supplied. “Kara said that she would be spending Christmas with you, and that anyone who refused to spend the holiday with you wasn’t welcome to spend the holiday with her, either.”

“Eliza!” Kara’s face was bright red.

Lena should have expected it by now, but the involuntary admission still brought a warm glow to her chest.

“No one else was going to let you be left out,” the hero finally managed. “You’re stuck with us now. We all agreed that James would step out a little early to go check on Lucy, but we weren’t going to let her ruin the holiday for you.”

 

Lena found herself leaning unconsciously into her girlfriend’s embrace. “You know, I haven’t exactly had a real holiday party in over twenty years.”

“Yes.” Supergirl’s eyes were blazing with determination. “And anyone who wants to mess up this day for us is going to have to do so over my dead body.”

Beep!

Kara glanced down at her cell phone, sighing. “Apparently, there’s an alien gang attempting to hold up the bank,” the hero said. “I’ve gotta go.”

The CEO’s face fell with disappointment, but she allowed Kara to reluctantly slip out of their hug. “Don’t forget to call in drones if you need back up!” Lena yelled after her as Kara flew out the window.

She turned to Eliza. “A bank holdup. How original.” she rolled her eyes. “How does anyone think they’re going to get away with something like that when Supergirl lives in the same zip code?”

The older woman shrugged. “Maybe they’re new to this planet,” she offered. “If not, well, it’s never easy to understand the mind of a criminal.”

“Technically, I am a criminal,” Lena pointed out.

Eliza nodded. “Point taken. But this is an opportunity I’ve been looking for.” She lowered her head, checking on the status of the oven. “I wanted to make sure you got something Kara for Christmas.”

The CEO frowned. “Of course I did.”

“That’s not what I meant,” Eliza said plainly. “Everyone knows you could snap your fingers and buy her something extravagant within the blink of an eye. I’m asking if you got her something personal. I hope you didn’t just buy her a company or something like that.”

Lena smiled to herself. “I got her something crude, handmade, and constructed without the aid of any assistants or secretaries. I don’t know if she’ll like it, but I think she’ll appreciate the gesture.” She paused, looking at Eliza. “Kara was the first person in years not to see me as a boss, CEO, or supervillain. Oh, sure, she acknowledged what I was, but she treated me like me. I’m going to treat her just like she deserves.”

It’d been hard to resist the urge to buy her girlfriend a billion-dollar gift. Since her adoption, Lena had been taught to equate money with affection. The villain’s awareness of the mindset hadn’t been enough to shake her of it completely. So, as an afterthought to her real gift, Lena had caved to temptation.

“And I bought her a company as well,” Lena admitted. “I couldn’t resist.”

\

“The plane is dropping fast. Thirty seconds until contact with the ground.”  

“I’ve got it!” Alex dove under the rapidly descending jetliner, placing her weight underneath the body of the plane carefully. Too little strength wouldn’t be enough to stop its fall. Too much could rip a hole through the hull and seriously injure the passengers.

Her earpiece chimed in again. “There’s an open stretch of land a mile ahead. Keep the plane falling slowly and let it glide onto the ground.”

The new superhero nodded to herself. “Understood, Liam,” she replied to her supervisor. “We’re in a remote part of India, so I wouldn’t count on a quick local response. I’d call in some L-Corp evac and medical teams just in case.”

“Already done. Luckily the boss has gained some traction with the Indian government this month, or that might have caused us some difficulties.”

In the days following her acquisition of full-blown superpowers, Alex had become a full-time hero. She’d leapt at the chance; it was time someone stepped in to take some of the burden off of Kara. With both of them capable of supersonic flight, they could now work in shifts and cover different parts of the globe.

Alex glanced down at her jumpsuit, barely straining under the weight of the plane. The suit was all black. It was something that Alex had insisted on. Other than a dark green cape, the only feature of note was the large L-Corp logo emblazed on her chest. That was something Lena had insisted on.

It was a fun, demanding, and fulfilling job, just as Kara had always said it was. And, as an added bonus, it transferred Alex into a position where she almost never needed to interact with Sam. That open wound was still painful, made even more so by the fact that the CFO had been unusually cold with her as of late.

Was I just a casual fling to her? Or is she forcing herself to remain distant from me because she thinks that it’s for the best? Both alternatives made Alex’s stomach drop.

Thankfully her earpiece cut in. A different voice popped up this time, one markedly different from her supervisors. “Hey, it’s Winn. You heading over to the party soon or what? I know you’re busy being….do you have a name yet?” 

Her superhero code name. “Not yet,” she admitted. “The geniuses in charge of my image haven’t settled on one yet. You have any suggestions?”

“A few! I’ll see you at the penthouse. We can talk then. You almost done with whatever you’re doing?”  

The new hero looked ahead at the field. The plane was descending smoothly under her guidance, heading right for where Alex intended. “Almost,” she replied. “See you in ten minutes.”

\

It wasn’t often that Lena Luthor found herself in a room with ten people she could trust completely.

Alex. Winn. James. Eliza. Sam. Ruby. Jess, holding her son Luke in her arms. And, of course, Kara. The supervillain might still have issues with some of them, but she knew without a doubt that each was a good person. All of them wanted the best both for Earth and (equally as importantly) Kara Danvers.

Handing out gifts was nothing new for Lena. She’d participated in countless charity events since she’d become a CEO, the most recent of which having been the previous day at the Children’s Hospital. Sometimes it was a bittersweet feeling, knowing that there were some people who could never be made whole with a simple gift.

Sometimes, it was downright painful. No amount of money would ever be enough to bring true joy to a child suffering from a terminal illness. Those were occasions Lena dreaded, and her reasoning to make a personal appearance stemmed entirely from good PR.

This was not one of those times.

“Yes!” Winn ripped off the rest of the wrapping paper. “The new L-Force console!”

James chuckled. “You could have bought one yourself, you know,” he reminded his friend. “Lena isn’t exactly jacking up the price on those things.”

“But this one’s custom made!” the techie read the details of the box. “A more powerful hard drive, more RAM, nice!”

“And every game available on the system already downloaded in,” Jess chimed in.

The CEO glanced at her secretary in confusion. “Really?” Lena asked. “I didn’t know that was possible. I don’t really know much about gaming…except for Chess, of course.”

“I may have taken some liberties with my position, Ms. Luthor,” Jess replied apologetically. “Since you had me handle the details of most of your gifts, I took the opportunity to tell our gaming department to add some features to Mr. Schott’s new device. I don’t technically have authority over them, but…”

Winn stared at her. “You didn’t have to do that.”

“Well, you did stand between me and a homicidal ultrapowerful alien a few weeks ago,” Jess reminded him, her face turning slightly red. “I thought it would be nice to return the favor in some small way.”

A tug on Lena’s arm pulled her away from the discussion. “Come with me,” Kara said, all but dragging her towards the balcony. “I wanted to give you your gift.”

Uncertain why Kara wanted to exchange presents alone, Lena was nonetheless powerless to resist the requests of her girlfriend and followed eagerly. They stepped out into the chilly winter air, closing the glass doors behind them before sitting down on two of the outdoor chairs.

The superhero’s hands were fiddling expectantly. “On my planet, marriages weren’t proposed with rings. When the matrix selected a match, the pair would be presented with a set of bracelets engraved with both family crests,” she explained nervously. “I know we weren’t selected through a matrix, but I wanted to keep some part of the tradition.”

As Lena watched, her fiancé produced a small black, satin box and laid it on the table before them. Smiling despite herself, the CEO reached forward and unlatched it to reveal two metal circlets. Both shone with the familiar sheen of nth metal.

“Usually, both crests are inlaid in the bracelets,” Kara explained. “I wanted to do something different.”

The villain looked more closely. Both circlets were engraved with a single symbol. It looked like the familiar House of El crest, but it was interspersed with the L-Corp logo. Lena wasn’t sure how her girlfriend had managed it, but the melded crest looked…

“It’s perfect.” Lena reached out for one of the bracelets, holding it closer. “I…I can’t get over the irony. Oh, Lex is rolling in his grave. I can’t wait to show Lillian.” She couldn’t resist the grin breaking out on her face. Kara’s family had meant everything to her. The fact that the hero was willing to distort their symbol with the Luthor logo…

On impulse, Lena reached out to clasp the bracelet on her wrist. She stopped as Kara’s hand darted out, gently grasping her own. “The new partners are supposed to put on each other’s,” the hero explained.

“Okay,” was all the CEO managed to say. She reached out, slipping one circlet onto Kara’s wrist and sliding it up next to the bracelet that was already there. Calmly holding her own wrist out, she then allowed Kara to do the same.

Kara chuckled nervously. “I may have used your credit card for these. Nth metal is outrageously expensive, and having it engraved is even worse. Don’t be too surprised if the bill this month is ten times higher than it should be.” Her face seemed to shrink. “Or a hundred,” she admitted in a whisper that Lena would have heard even without her enhanced hearing.

“Don’t worry,” the CEO replied, shooting her fiancé a sultry grin. “I like seeing my woman spend my money.”

“W-ell…” Kara stuttered, her face burning bright red. “I’m glad you approve. As long as you know that I’d like you even if you didn’t have a nickel. Which, I admit, is unlikely since someone as smart as you would probably never be broke…”

Lena held up a finger. “As much as I enjoy watching this, if you don’t stop rambling, I’ll never get the chance to give you your gift.”

Kara’s fingers clenched tightly in excitement, and in that moment Lena knew she’d been absolutely right to make something personal. The hero wouldn’t have been pleased with anything else, regardless of what she might have said.

The villain scrolled a finger over her black bracelet. “I’m having it delivered,” she explained. “While it’s coming, I might as well tell you about your other gift. I decided to buy Catco under your name,” she explained. “It will run itself for now, but if you ever want to go back to reporting…or even be the Editor-in-Chief, now you can just hire yourself. It’s too dangerous for now, but in the future-”

Kara cut her off with a fierce kiss. “Just how did I end up with the most extra girlfriend on this planet?” she demanded. “That’s my other gift? What’s the main one? Please tell me you didn’t buy me a country!”

Lena shrugged teasingly. “I tried, but that deal fell through. So I came up with a replacement myself. Here it is now.”

A sleek black drone sailed over the balcony, precisely dropping a wrapped package in Lena’s hand before disappearing from sight. The pattern of paper covering the gift was neat, not creative, but the CEO hoped what was inside might make up for that.

“Open it.” She handed it to Kara.

The superhero did so eagerly, discarding the paper with a quick flourish. With a gasp, she stared down at the covered sheet of nth metal that had been revealed. “You…you made this?”

It was a series of laminated photographs, all of them stuck to a panel of nth metal with industrial grade superglue. Each and every single one was of Kara. There were pictures of her spending time with Lena, Alex, Winn, James, Clark, and Eliza. Others showed Supergirl flying around the city, either on patrol or helping rescue citizens. One had her in full Supergirl uniform visiting children at the hospital.

The pictures were arrayed as neatly as Lena’s hands could managed, but there was no rhyme or reason in an organization. It was the exact kind of gift that should never have been given by a Luthor: crude, uncoordinated, and impractical.

Lena had hoped that Kara would like it. She hadn’t expected her to cry.

“It’s…me. All of me.” The hero’s eyes were welling with tears. “You made this all yourself?”

“I asked Winn and Eliza for help finding photos, and I had a drone discretely take a few others,” the CEO admitted. “The handiwork was mine, yes. Is…is something wrong?”

Kara stared at her. “You didn’t separate Kara Danvers and Supergirl.”

Lena glanced again at the collage, trying to hide her frustration with herself. It looked like she had gone overboard with the anti-Luthor gift policy. “No. I guess it didn’t occur to me. Should I? I can redo it if you want me to. All I’d have to do is dissolve the glue and-”

“NO!” Her girlfriend interrupted. “That’s…no, you shouldn’t change it. I feel I’ve spent my entire time on Earth juggling two different people,” Kara said fervently. “I wanted to help people and to live a normal life, and I always had to keep those things separated. You’re the first person to make me feel that I don’t have to.”

Lena smiled with relief.

“Can I have a hug?” Kara asked.

“You don’t need to ask-”

The hero caught her in a crushing embrace, one that Lena quickly returned. She lost track of time, simply enjoying the feeling of her girlfriend’s proximity. She found herself burying her face in Kara’s hair, enjoying the hero’s scent.

Knock! Knock!  

They broke apart reluctantly. Alex, standing at the balcony door, shifted the glass panel aside and stepped out into the night. “Sorry to interrupt,” she said. “Although you should probably know that at least half the people here have superhearing and can hear your entire conversation.”

“I find myself not caring,” Lena replied. “Is there another reason you’re interrupting us?”

Some of the confidence seemed to fall off of Alex’s shoulders. “I’ve realized…I never actually formally apologized for the attempt to kill you,” she said hesitantly. “I know this seems sudden, but with everything going on today…it felt like the right time.”

The CEO felt Kara’s body tense against her.

Lena frowned. In truth, the incident had ceased to bother her a while ago. “I can’t blame you for being willing to kill for Kara,” she admitted. “I would do the same, after all.”

“That’s not what I’m apologizing for,” Alex replied. “I’m sorry that you were a threat. All I saw was a villain with the last name Luthor; I ignored all of the signs that you were different from Lex. I should have taken more time to judge your intentions. Maggie had just been killed and I was devastated, but that’s no excuse for how I acted.”

“You weren’t the first, and you won’t be the last,” the CEO replied. “Obviously, you’ve come around on that point. If you’re asking for forgiveness from me, then you have it. We all make mistakes. Even me,” Lena replied with a slight smirk.

Alex turned her gaze towards Kara, remaining hesitant. “You said before that you weren’t ready to forgive me,” she spoke to her sister. “I respect that…but I was wondering if you’ve changed your mind.”

Supergirl spent several seconds staring at her sister.

“I’ll never be okay with what you did,” Kara said. The hero sighed. “But I know it came from a place of love. You wanted to protect me and avenge someone you cared about. I…I’m trying Alex. I want to forgive you.” Her eyes were becoming misty. “You’ve grown a lot since then, you’ve learned from that mistake. I…”

“Forgiveness isn’t an on/off switch,” Alex interrupted. “It’s a process. I just…I miss you. We see each other all the time, but it’s not the same. I was just hoping you’ve come close enough to forgiving me so that we could…you know…be sisters again.”

Lena forced herself to remain quiet. She knew how much it hurt Kara to have a strained relationship with her sister, but the hero couldn’t be forced into repairing it. Even as the most powerful woman in the world, it wasn’t Lena Luthor’s place to interfere.

“Okay.” Kara’s gaze slowly lifted from the ground. “I’ll try. We’ll try. We can have a sister’s night tomorrow and see how it goes. Maybe we can-”

“Adorable.”

Lena whirled around. An all-too familiar woman was hovering several yards above her balcony, clad in a dark purple suit. “Purity,” the CEO hissed, her nanosuit forming around her. “All recovered from the explosion, I see. Where’s your boss?”

“Reign is occupied at the moment,” the alien replied. Kara and Alex were both tensed for combat, but the Worldkiller held up a hand. “I’m not here to fight. Reign and I have come to the conclusion that your forces have grown too strong.”

Lena smirked. With all of her drone fleets and Alex now having Pestilence’s powers, even two Worldkillers couldn’t defeat them. “So you’re here to surrender?”

“Hardly.” Purity’s lips were curled up in amusement. “You only have the upper hand for now. The preparations are complete. When almighty Darkseid arrives on this planet, your pathetic resistance will be crushed under our heel. You have no idea what is awaiting you.”

The supervillain refused to let any fear show. “Yes, we got your message already. So why are you here, then?”

Purity ignored her, turning to Alex. “So, you now have our rogue sister’s powers. They will not protect you. We have seen abilities transfer before; energy always outlives its conduit. Once you perish, we will have the Plaguebringer on our side once again.”

“Give it your best shot.” Alex floated up into the air menacingly.

“I am not here to fight,” Purity scoffed. “But I will if I must. How many do you think will die if we brawl in this populated urban center?” She turned to Lena. “You may think yourself ruthless, but you are weak. You know that within seconds I will disappear and assume a disguise amongst the helpless masses of this city. Yet you will not pursue out of fear for their worthless lives.”

Supergirl clenched her fists. “Our weakness is our care for others,” she acknowledged. “Your weakness is your care for no one. Unlike you, we can unite. It doesn’t matter how much power Darkseid brings to this planet; we will come together and crush him. His power will crumble beneath him as his followers desert him. His omega beams won’t save him when I place my boot on his neck,” the hero promised. “Give that message to your master.”

Purity laughed. “You don’t understand just how fortunate you are, Kara Zor-El. Make your petty threats if you must. There aren’t enough forces on this planet to stand against us. Enjoy the coming months. They are all you have left.”

The Worldkiller disappeared in a burst of speed.

Lena stared at the empty space before them, eyes narrowed in suspicion. “She’s playing us,” the CEO declared to the other two. “She wouldn’t come here just to threaten us.”

“What else did she gain by coming here?” Alex demanded, clearly seething.

“Intel? Misdirection? I don’t know,” Lena admitted. “Unfortunately, I get the feeling that she was telling the truth. She honestly believes that Earth can’t stand against what’s coming.”

Kara jumped into the air. “Then we’ll prove her wrong!” she promised.

Lena nodded, forcing herself to smile. “That’s what I like to hear,” she said, sounding far more confident than she felt. I don’t know if I can save the Earth, but I will not surrender it until my dying breath.  

\

An unfathomable distance away, the lost city of Argo hurtled through space.

“Several months until we complete our journey to the Milky Way,” her trusted subordinate informed her. “Our supply of Harun-el is running thin, but projections state that it will be enough.”

“Thank you, Selena,” she replied. The head of Argo’s High Council turned away from the monitor, looking out into the reaches of space. Her city was weak, running on borrowed time, but it represented the last hope for countless millions.

Be strong, Kara. I am coming. Alura Zor-El promised.
