Time-Skip of several months next chapter!

Six Months Later

Chapter Notes

We have a winner! I've decided to go RedDevilLola's suggestion for Alex's superhero name, though with a slightly different spelling. Thanks for the suggestions, everyone!

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Lena clutched the teddy bear tightly to her chest.

“Girl, come over here.”

She cautiously made her way over to the dinner table, her bear still in her hands. Even at four years old, she knew the stuffed animal wasn’t real. It was a collection of cloth, synthetic fiber, and straw wool. There was no consciousness inside it.

She just didn’t care.

Lillian was sitting at the head of the table, glowering down at her. It was the first time the two of them had been alone together since Lena’s adoption the week prior. Lionel had taken Lex with him on a business trip to Japan, leaving the newly adopted girl behind to ‘get to know her new mother.’

There was no highchair. With difficulty, Lena tugged back a chair in the middle of the table and scrambled up into it. She sat down, missing her old booster seat. The Luthors’ table was just low enough to lift her arms over and reach for the food meticulously prepared by the family’s servants.  

The room was dimly lit, with only a simmering fireplace and scattered lamps providing light. Even still, Lena could see Lillian continue to glower at her. Dropping her gaze to the ground, the girl wordlessly grabbed her bear and placed it in the seat beside her.

“Enough.”  

Lena flinched as Lillian abruptly sat up from her chair. The girl’s heart pounded ever faster as the Luthor matriarch took slow, deliberate steps in her direction.

“For better or worse, you are a Luthor now.” Lillian placed an imperious hand on the rim of Lena’s chair. “You are not a child. This thing…” she gestured to the bear “Is an inanimate object. Give it to me.”

“No!” Finding her voice, Lena hopped up in her seat. “I’ll keep it in my room, but please don’t get rid of it! Mommy gave it to me!”  

She realized her mistake instantly. Lena had never seen Lillian lose her composure, but her lips never failed to twinge with displeasure whenever Lena’s mother was mentioned. There were two possibilities: Lionel wasn’t telling the full truth about his reasons for adopting Lena, or Lillian resented any other woman having influence over her future daughter.

Either way, the result was the same. Lillian’s eyes flared as she stared down at Lena. “Your mother is dead,” she said calmly. “She drowned because you were too weak to save her. I’m sure even you can realize that.”

  Lena fought against the tears swelling in her eyes. What could she say? Lillian was right, after all.

Lillian’s fingers snatched the bear off of the chair. “Weakness never goes unpunished.” She moved towards the fireplace, never taking her eyes off of Lena. “If you’re going to be a Luthor, you’ll need to learn that lesson. I’m going to make sure you will.”

“Please!” Lena jumped off the chair, falling to the floor. Ignoring the pain in her knees, she fixed the older woman with pleading eyes. “Please don’t!”

Lillian held the bear above the flames, clearly relishing the moment. “Please don’t?” she repeated mockingly. “Begging will never get you anything in this world, my dear. Do you want to stop me? If you want your toy back, you’ll need to fight for it.”

The frustration and despair of the past week boiling over, Lena did just that. She ran headlong at her tormentor, planning to jump up and snatch her mother’s gift from Lillian’s long fingers.  

Lillian’s foot lashed out, slamming into Lena’s stomach. The wind knocked out of her, the girl skidded back across the floor and slammed into a table leg. Her back exploded with pain as her soft flesh collided with the heavy wood.

“This is all for your own good,” the Luthor matriarch said, seemingly serene. “The weak can’t protect the things they care about.”  

The bear fell into the flames.  

/

“Wake up. Lena, wake up!”

The CEO opened her eyes. She was in her bed. Kara was staring down at her; concern was etched in the superhero’s face.

“What’s wrong?” the superhero asked.

Not in the mood for such a conversation, Lena shrugged. “Nothing.”

“Don’t lie to me,” Kara said, her voice both firm and warm.

The Kryptonian looked so worried that the villain mentally gave in. “I wasn’t sleeping well,” she admitted. “How did you know?”

“Girlfriends tend to know each other’s secrets,” Kara replied. She flashed Lena a cheeky smile before growing serious again. "So, tell me about it. Bad dream?”

Lena shook her head. “A memory,” she said. “There are downsides to having perfect recall. If Lillian is good at anything, it’s leaving psychological scars.” A familiar rush of satisfaction swept through her at the thought that the woman who had made her childhood a living hell was well and truly incarcerated.

“Oh dear,” Kara responded. “Do you want to talk about it?”

The supervillain’s eyes swept out the window. The moon was still shining brightly in the sky, illuminating the early summer landscape of National City.

“No. I want to go back to sleep.”

Her fiancé kissed her on the cheek. “Okay.” Kara hugged Lena tightly, burying her face into the CEO’s neck. If there was one thing Harun-el was good for, it was allowing cuddles with your clingy Kryptonian lover.

Even after lived together for over six months, sleeping with Kara Zor-El was something Lena still hadn’t wrapped her head around. The hero could always be counted on to hog the blankets, so much so that Lena had had to make custom sheets just so she could remain covered most nights. Then there were the frequent occasions the CEO would make up three feet in the air, perched on top of her girlfriend’s floating body.

And, of course, there was always Supergirl duty. Lena’s concurrent hobby of taking over the world was just as timing, if not more so, but it was a rare thing for her to have to schedule meetings in the middle of the night. Unfortunately, random crimes and natural disasters were not so predictable.

Still, Lena wouldn’t have treated her bedmate for anything in the world. And when Alex had told her that Kara only ever floated in her sleep when she felt completely safe and happy…and that she had never been sleep floating on a regular basis before…well. People might have been confused the next day when Lena couldn’t stop smiling and ended up buying Kara a flower store packed with all of her favorite floral arrangements, but they would just have to wonder.

The second a cute alien had walked into her life, adorably thinking a pair of glasses could conceal her identity from the planet’s foremost supergenius …well, Lena had been hooked instantly. And after said alien insisted on treating her with understanding and compassion despite their family rivalry, well…

Part of her wished she hadn’t met Kara until after she’d completely taken over the world. Having a girlfriend was a distraction, one she could ill afford. Thankfully, Lena could recognize that letting Kara go would only create a larger mental burden.

Some things were simply too precious to give up.

Smiling with warm determination, she clutched Kara tightly to her chest.

\

“We’re in the middle of cleanup,” Alex reported. “No signs of biological agents. All heavy explosives have been accounted for.”

“Acknowledged. Good work, Sentinel,” her earpiece responded.

It was a routine machine. Alex and her team had been dispatched to Zambesi, a large African country that had recently fallen under L-Corp’s official control. Rife was lawlessness and feuding factions, it was taking quite a bit of effort to bring it into normalcy.

Today, they were bringing down a former government base. An army depot in the middle of nowhere, it had been seized by a faction of terrorists several years previously. With rumors of biological weapons floating around, finding it had been a top priority.

Alex was floating from above, watching to make sure no vehicles attempted to make a quick escape. She smiled as a blur sped across the ground, rounding up militants and binding them with magnetic cuffs.

In seconds, the entirety of the enemy force was lying on the ground in their restraints. The Zambesian Purification Brigade had been neutralized in a matter of minutes.

“It’s over,” Alex spoke again. “Barry got them all, and there are no other threats. Tell Canary and Elongated Man that we don’t need any backup today.”

“Understood.”

As the Flash finished rounding up the last of their targets, Alex landed next to him. “Nice work,” she said.

Her fellow hero turned to her. His efforts had hardly even winded him, but there was a heaviness in his eyes. “What’s going to happen to them after today?” the Flash demanded.

Alex shrugged. “L-Corp’s already refurbished some Zambesian prisons. I imagine they’ll go there unless they can prove they have an innocent reason for working with a terrorist organization.” She glanced at him curiously. “You have a problem with that?”

Barry looked like he wanted to vomit. “We have med teams on the way, right?”

“Yeah.”

“Good,” he said. “Some of the captives in there were being tortured. A few of the more lucid ones spoke to me. There are people who have been held here for years. Experimented on. I can’t even imagine…” he trailed off.

Scum. Alex hoped that their medical facilities would be able to help the survivors, but there were some injuries that couldn’t be healed. She made a mental note to have get more trauma specialists on hand as soon as possible.

She took another look at Barry. The green tint on his face contrasted horribly with his red outfit, but it didn’t look like he was having any more doubts about joining up. Lifting her head, she couldn’t resist a fearful look at the looming sky.

Worse is coming. The thought came suddenly, unwelcome but irresistible. This could be the fate of the entire Earth if we fail. How much longer do we have?

\

“Since when did I become a construction crew?” Kara demanded.

“Since you agreed to serve me and help me take over the world,” her favorite supervillain spoke into her helmet. “Remember? You, kneeling before me in my office? Me graciously accepting you into my employ despite your having fought against me for months?”

“Yeah, yeah,” Kara responded.

“You’ve helped me subvert and replace a dozen governments over the last few months,” Lena pointed out. “You’re really going to tell me that it’s delivering supplies that  is the breaking point for you?”

“It just seems like a waste of my talents to lug materials into space when your shuttles could do it for you.” The hero touched down on the artificial satellite, stepping inside the field of artificial gravity. Her breathing helmet remained in place, providing her a steady supply of oxygen.

Lena sounded amused. “Eventually, they could. But you’re saving me literally thousands of hours in manpower. Besides, it’s good PR to have you helping the L-Shield. A lot of people still think it’s an anti-alien project.”

Supergirl had to concede the point. The monitoring system was already in place. No large craft could even enter their galaxy without being picked up by L-Corp software. Even minuscule craft were spotted by the time they arrived on (or left) Earth, which was rather often. The next phase would create a massive forcefield around the planet, capable of stopping any invasion force upon activation.

In theory.

Ten generators on artificial satellites, powered by a rudimentary form of Harun-el, would create the shield. With help from Supergirl, the project had entered into its final phase.

“Now that you’re finished, I need you to fly down to my office,” Lena’s voice came through again. “Your boss has an urgent project on hand that requires some of your special skills.”

Urgent project. I wonder what that could be? “Can it wait a few minutes?” Kara asked. “Some of the crew is coming over. I think they want to meet me. Can you imagine how lonely it must be to spend weeks up in space at a time?”

Lena let out an audible growl of frustration. “Sure. Go brighten a few days, Supergirl.”

“What project are you working on anyway?” Kara asked. “Can’t you just ask Alex for help? She’s just as powerful as me.”

“I…unbelievable. You’re lucky you’re adorable.”

\

Lena glanced up as Alex flew into her office. “Kara said you needed help with something?” the elder Danvers sister questioned.

“Oh, Rao,” the CEO murmured. “I wanted her help. Just hers. I swear, sometimes your sister is as dense as steel. Maybe that’s how she got her nickname.”

She inwardly groaned as the superhero started laughing at her. “Sorry, Lena,” Alex said, pretending to wipe a tear from her eye. “But I’m afraid you’re stuck with her at this point. You have any more stories like this? It’s never too early to start preparing Maid of Honor material.”

Lena was spared from further mortification as her intercom buzzed. “Ms. Luthor?” Jess’s voice prompted. “You have a visitor.”

Using her x-ray vision to peer through the wall, Lena’s eyes widened in slight surprise. “Send her in. Thanks Jess.”

The door opened to admit Ruby Arias, who immediately started marching towards Lena’s desk purposefully.

“Ruby. What can I do for you?” the supervillain questioned. The thirteen-year-old paused in front of her desk, barely sparing Alex a glance.

“I need you to stop overworking my mom.”

Lena’s eyes blinked in confusion. She’d always made a point to give her employees adequate rest time and had heard no complaints from Sam herself. “What makes you think she’s overworked?” the CEO asked.

The teenager stamped a foot down on the carpet. “She’s not herself! Whenever mom’s not at work, she’s out running side jobs for you or cooped up in her room. She barely talks to me anymore!” Ruby protested, the pain in her eyes clear to see. “It’s been months since she’s even made dinner. I have to order takeout every night.”

“I…Ruby, I’m sorry,” Lena said. “I don’t understand. Are you sure it’s work?  I haven’t given her any extra jobs since she became CFO. Nothing’s changed.”

“Well, maybe it’s too much work as it is!” the young girl shot back. “Mom always says she’s too busy. She was too busy months ago to spend time with Alex, who I know she really liked.” Ruby gave Alex a sympathetic glance.

Lena bit her lip. She hadn’t had any close friends since Kara had entered her life, but Sam had certainly been the closest to qualifying. Clearly, something was wrong. It can’t be her workload. She’s had the same weekly schedule for years. Is it just stress?

“Ruby,” the CEO replied slowly. “I don’t know what to tell you. I haven’t given her any new work in a while.”

The teenager huffed. “You’re her boss. You must have done something. I just…I want my mom back.”

A motion from the couch drew her attention. The next second, to Lena’s astonishment, Alex had Ruby wrapped in an embrace. “I know it’s hard,” the hero said. “But if there’s one thing I know about Sam, it’s that she loves you. Things have just been pretty crazy lately.”

“I’ll talk with your mother,” Lena promised. “If there’s anything I can do to help, I will. And do you know why?” As Ruby shook her head, the villain continued. “Your mom and I both worked at L-Corp when Lex went crazy. We both were subpoenaed to testify at his trial. I was…in a dark place back then. The morning I was due to first speak, I was staying on the tenth floor to my hotel. All I could think about was how stupid I had been. People had died because I refused to see someone I trusted for what they truly were.”

Ruby frowned. “What does this have to do with my mom?”

“Well, I was in such a daze I barely noticed myself walking towards the elevator. Some careless breakfast waitress had left a few ice cubes lying on the carpet. I slipped on one, caught myself on the railing, and was half a second from pitching over and falling a hundred feet down into the lobby. I didn’t have any Harun-el back then, but I did have your mom. She’d been waiting for the elevator. When I was about to go over, she jumped forward and grabbed me by the back of my shirt. Saved my life.”

Alex and Ruby were both looking at her in shock. “I never knew that,” Alex said.

“Well, that’s the thing,” Lena continued. “Sam never made an issue of it. She never mentioned it again. After I became CFO, she never brought it up to try and gain an advantage with me,” the villain explained. “And that’s why I would never intentionally hurt her. If I am overworking her, we’ll fix it,” Lena promised.

There was a moment’s pause.

“Was mom CFO back then?”

Lena shook her head. “Only a secretary. But just because she didn’t angle for a promotion didn’t mean I couldn’t give her one. Trust is a rare commodity in the business world.”

\

Jess watched as Winn sat down across the café table from her. Even in the middle of the city, the restaurant was slow at 9pm. Just as Jess had hoped for.

“You wanted to meet with me?” he asked.

She’d seen him plenty of times at game nights, of course. Due to a lack of privacy, however, those had been out of the question. Asking him to meet her at L-Corp seemed way too formal. Texting or calling him was definitely too informal.

This was perfect. Public enough to not make it seem like a big deal, private enough so that none of their friends could possibly overhear them. The only issue was how to begin.

“Is something wrong?” Winn prompted.

The secretary shook her head, realizing she’d been zoning out. “No,” she said quickly. “I just wanted to talk to you. I…”

She raged inwardly. How could she possibly say, ‘Hey, I think you’re cute and funny and I want to go on a date with you. Only, I’ve been hesitating because I’m not sure if I’m attracted to you just because you saved my life and did something really brave. You’d think that would have gone away by now, but I can’t be sure. So can we take this slow. Also, are you interested in me? I should probably ask you that.

He shot her a small smile. “You know, I’m not supposed to spend too much time on my own,” he said. “Supergirl’s enemies and all that. Do you think you’ll manage to find the words within the next quarter-century?”

Jess laughed. “Don’t worry,” she said. “I’m perfectly capable of protecting you.”

“No. You’re really not,” a new voice said genially.

They looked up to see a dark-skinned woman approaching their booth. By the time either one of them could react, she had comfortably taken a seat next to Winn. Reaching down for the drink menu, the newcomer made a show of looking through the options.

“Who the hell are you?” Jess demanded.

The other woman smiled. A faint purple glow simmered in her eyes. “My name is Purity,” she said. “You may have heard of me. I’m sorry to interrupt your date, but I’m afraid Mr. Schott needs to come with me.”

“Excuse me?” Winn sputtered.

Purity shot him a pitiless smile. “We have need of your services,” she said. The Worldkiller frowned slightly. “Well, actually, putting it that way gives you too much credit. It’s more like we need information, and you’re the one who has it.”

“He’s not going with you!” Jess stood up. Her hand itched to reach for her phone, but she knew the alien would incinerate it with a blast of heat vision before her finger even pressed the home key. “I’m not afraid of you.”

Strictly speaking, that was a lie. But Jess was far from defenseless. If she could hold out against the Worldkiller long enough, someone from L-Corp would notice. Lena could have reinforcements sent her way within minutes.

“Unfortunately, Ms. Huang, you’ve been added to the list. I’m not supposed to kill you,” Purity conceded reluctantly. “But I’m more than happy to apply some blunt force trauma.”

Jess tensed, ready to jump at the alien who would dare threaten her and her friends. A moment before she could, however, Winn held out an arm in front of Purity.

“Winn?”

The techie’s limbs were trembling. With a gulp, he stared down Jess. “You fight her here and people will die,” he said. “We can’t…that can’t happen.” His face was white with fear, but that did nothing to disguise the determination in his voice. “I can’t live knowing that innocent bystanders died just so I could be safe.”

Jess’s mouth gaped open. “You can’t!” The secretary refused to let it happen. Her body was infused with Harun-el. She worked directly underneath the most powerful woman in the world. There was no way someone could just kidnap a friend right in front of her!

Purity simply smiled, watching their conversation with a passing interest. She made no move to interfere.

“We know these things don’t care about innocent lives.” Winn shot Purity a look of venom. “We’re in the middle of the city. One punch from her could send an entire building crashing down!” His breathing was growing more rapid now. “If it was you, or Kara, or Alex, I would say to try to get away. You’re too important…you know too much. Me? What could I know that would help them?”

They both glanced at the Worldkiller. Purity simply offered them a coy shrug.

The pavement cracked underneath Jess’s feet. “They’ll kill you!” she hissed.

“I don’t think so,” Winn replied. “Reign wouldn’t kill me, remember?”

Oh, yes, how Jess remembered. That didn’t mean he would be remotely safe. Torture was still very much on the table. If they thought he had information they could use, there might be no end to the torment. Especially if he really didn’t have anything to give them.

By the look in his eyes, she could tell that Winn understood that very same fact. Still, he remained firm. “Fight her and I’ll never forgive you,” he said. “Hundreds could die.” The techie reached out, grabbing her hand. “I can’t tell you how much I appreciate you willing to fight for me, but now isn’t the right time. You know it too.”

No! No!  

“Well, I hate to leave before ordering, but Mr. Schott and I must be off.” Purity stood up, seizing her captive by the wrist.

It was only the thought of a city block in ruins, search and rescue teams shifting through the debris, that stopped the secretary from launching herself at the Worldkiller. “I’m going to kill you,” Jess promised.

Purity simply smirked.

They both knew that the second the Worldkiller was out of sight, Jess would reach for her phone and call Lena. The fact that Purity seemed content to let it happen was a bad sign. Somehow, she had an escape ready, one too fast for even L-Corp to trace.

“See you around.” Dragging Winn behind her, Purity stepped out into the city. By the time Jess had reached for her phone, they had vanished amidst the crowd.

Chapter End Notes

I want to bring in some other DC heroes to round out the cast. Not for major roles, but to play a part in future battles. Anyone have preferences/ideas? I plan to go with the most request ones.

See the end of the chapter for notes

“How nice of you to visit, daughter of mine.”

Lena sent her prisoner a withering glare. “I’ve kept you down here for months. You think you would stop pretending that we were ever a family by now.”

Lillian smiled coldly. “I never wanted you, but you are Lionel’s daughter. Lex considered you his sister. Even after the many, many times you’ve disappoint me, I still haven’t given up hope for you.”

“And why is that?” The CEO crossed her arms, doing her best to suppress her revulsion for the woman sitting in the cell before her. Now, more than ever, she needed Lillian to cooperate.

“You’re intelligent,” the prisoner spoke. “Sentimental, but intelligent. Eventually, you’re going to realize that half measures won’t cut it. They might keep Supergirl in your arms, but they’re not going to save this planet.”

Even in dire situations, proving Lillian wrong still brought a perverse joy to Lena. “Kara joined up months ago. Supergirl takes orders from me, now,” the CEO crooned.

The only sign of surprise was a slight crinkle in Lillian’s forehead. “And there it is,” the prisoner announced. “That desire for power that’s going to come between you. Does it make you feel good to have Supergirl as a minion? I believe it does.”

“Supergirl is my minion. Kara Zor-El is my fiancé,” Lena replied calmly. She paused, pretending to examine her fingernails. “Why wouldn’t we work together? We have the same goals.”

“But not the same standards.” Lillian shook her head in exasperation. “You’ve been able to play by her rules so far. That’s not going to last. Earth will require more from you. If you want to control this planet and keep it safe, you’re going to need to kill. Control. How will darling Kara feel about that?”

Lena raised an eyebrow. “I’ve been fine so far,” she pointed out.

It was true. The answer to the question of whether Lena Luthor ruled the world certainly wasn’t a yes. But it wasn’t a definite no, either. By monopolizing all advanced alien technology and combining it with Lena’s intellect, the company was essentially running the world’s economy. Half of the world’s leaders were under her control or freely working with her. Thirty-one countries were now controlled by L-Corp directly.

Lillian nodded. “So far,” she agreed. “Until an alien fleet arrives in the Milky Way and Earth suddenly isn’t so cooperative. People won’t unite behind you; they’ll try to save themselves. You’ll need force to keep them in line. Executions of those who resist you. How will Kara feel about that?”

The supervillain refused to let any emotion show. “Speaking of alien fleets, that brings me to the reason why I’ve come here today.” Even in the dim light of the cell, she could see Lillian’s eyes spark with interest. “I’ve been fighting advance agents of an alien force for months. One of them just kidnapped a friend of mine. I need you to tell me everything you know about them.”

For the first time, Lillian seemed genuinely angry. “You think I would work with an invading force? Absurd. Aliens are a disease. You don’t cure the sickness by working with it.”

“It really is sad that bigotry is your noblest quality,” Lena replied. “And no, I don’t think you would knowingly work with an alien force.” She stood up, beginning to pace around the room. “Cadmus developed Red Kryptonite.”

The prisoner frowned. “So?”

“It fit your mission. Cadmus would have loved to see Supergirl disgraced. The only problem was that it was impossible,” Lena said. “Cadmus could never have made RedK on its own.”

“And how do you know that?”

Lena stopped in her pacing to stare into Lillian’s eyes. “Because I couldn’t have. Not unless you gave me a decade. I could synthesize more now, but from scratch, no. If it was beyond my ability, well, your scientists might as well have been banging rocks together.” She leaned towards the paneling. “Someone gave you the formula to make it.”

“Even if that was true,” Lillian said, pursing her lips. “What makes you think they’d be connected to the aliens you’ve been dealing with?”

The CEO could see the glint in the other woman’s eyes. Lillian knew something. “My organization has a mole. I don’t know who it is, but I know they exist. This mole ordered Maggie Sawyer’s death and made sure it was covered up. They tipped Reign off about my raid on the DEO and leaked Kara’s identity to the world.”

“So what?” Lillian demanded. “What does that have to do with me?”

Lena ignored the question. “These Worldkillers we’ve been fighting have an interest in Kara. I don’t know why, but they do. More importantly, they also have a connection to Krypton, meaning they’re also the only ones who would have known about RedK.”

“Why would they give it to Cadmus?”

“For the same reason they killed Maggie Sawyer,” the CEO finally answered. “They wanted to drive a wedge between Kara and me. The Worldkillers have been trying to get us at each other’s throats since the start.”

Skeptical laughter broke out from Lillian. “You’re basing a lot on a simple hunch. How do you know that you don’t just have more than one spy at L-Corp?”

It was a point worth acknowledging. Taking over the world brought more than one set of enemies. But Lena’s brain was excellent at sensing patterns. The search for Maggie’s killer and the raid on the DEO were at the same level of security clearance; a single mole would have found them both. But then there was the Worldkillers’ interest in Kara, and the fact that Maggie Sawyer’s death lined up with their apparent goal of bringing Supergirl to their side instead of Lena’s…

“Stop dodging,” the CEO demanded. “Someone outside of Cadmus gave the formula for RedK. Tell me who it was and I might be able to track the Worldkillers down. Or do you not want to stop hostile aliens from taking over the planet?”

Deep down, Lena knew the Worldkillers had been behind the RedK. Whether they wanted to cover their tracks or because they lacked the resources to develop it themselves was immaterial. What exactly they hoped to obtain with Kara, the CEO didn’t know. She wasn’t expecting to like the answer.

Lillian shook her head. “I wouldn’t know. One of our scientists claimed to have discover RedK. It’s possible she was contacted by outside agents. Unfortunately, she’s not one of the scientists you’ve captured.”

Resisting the urge to smash the paneling, Lena stared at her adoptive mother. “Then tell me who she is. If I don’t stop the Worldkillers, their alien master is going to take over the world. Isn’t that what you want to stop?”

The prisoner shrugged. “As long as you maintain your alien-loving attitude, Earth is already lost. Even if you prevent an outright invasion, waves of refugees will arrive. You let them in and they will consume our planet. Our culture will be drowned in a wave of alien garbage. That’s worse than an outright invasion; it gives humanity no chance to fight back.”

Lena’s eyes were burning with hatred.

“You could try and torture it out of me,” Lillian offered. “But I doubt your pet alien would much like that.”

“Don’t tempt me.”

The prisoner sighed with annoyance. “If you desire your alien slut so much, fine. I can live with that disappointment. Brainwash her to serve you. You’ll have Supergirl in your bed and more than willing to do your bidding. One powerful alien could be useful, if under your complete control.”

Rao. “You are sick,” the CEO hissed. She turned towards the door. “I’m restricting your meals to once a day. If you’re ready to talk, let the warden know.”

“You think hunger will be enough to break me?”

Lena swiveled to face her prisoner. “Do you want to be tortured? Are you a masochist now?”

“Save me the sardonic humor,” Lillian scoffed. “I am proving my point: half measures aren’t going to save the world. If you want to protect humanity, you can’t hold back. Kill and torture when you have to. Brainwash people who are too foolish to get in line. And keep alien refugees away from this planet.”

“I don’t kill and brainwash the innocent because it’s wrong,” Lena said. “I don’t keep out alien refugees because it would be wrong and because there’s nothing to gain from it. Peaceful aliens only make us stronger.”

“In the short term, perhaps,” Lillian acknowledged. “What happens when they grow so numerous our resources begin to dwindle?”

Torturing Lillian was growing more and more appealing by the second. “You sound just like those right-wing nuts who thought immigration would destroy the developed nations before aliens became the hot button issue. The parallels are so striking only a moron would miss them.”

“Earth has enough resources for humans.” Lillian crossed her arms. “Not the entire universe. How are you going to feed all of the refugees who come here?”

The supervillain turned back to the door with an air of finality. “I’ll find a way,” she said, stepping through the threshold. “I always do.”

\

“He could be anywhere by now,” Alex lamented.

Kara shook her head firmly. “No. He’s still out there, somewhere. We’re going to bring him home, no matter how long it takes.”

The hero twisted her head as the door to Lena’s office opened, revealing the CEO herself. Kara stood up on her toes in anticipation. “What did Lillian say?”

Her heart plummeted as Lena shook her head. “She won’t budge,” the villain admitted. “She knows the identity of the scientists the Worldkillers might have contacted, but she won’t give the name up.”

Alex leapt to her feet. “Offer her a deal. Better accommodations, five-star meals, a DVD player. Anything.”

“The only deal she would be interested in is her freedom,” Lena countered, giving Alex a skeptical look. “Lillian is a fanatic. She doesn’t care about her own comforts. All she wants is an alien-free world, and she would never help a ‘traitor’ like me who is letting them in.”

Kara watched as her sister bunched up her fists. “Then make her talk,” Alex hissed.

“We can’t torture people,” Supergirl interjected quickly. “Especially not on a mere suspicion. We don’t even know if the Worldkillers were behind the RedK. Lillian might not have anything useful.”

Alex was fuming. “Winn is probably getting tortured right now!”

Supergirl closed her eyes, resisting the images attempting to break through her imagination. She felt like she was being suffocated. Winn was not being tortured. It couldn’t happen.

“Kara,” her sister continued. “If Lena was the one who was captured, or me…wouldn’t you be willing to do anything to save us? We owe Winn the same. I know that if you were the one captured and I had a guilty party with information, I wouldn’t hesitate.”

SLAM! Both women turned to Lena. The CEO’s fist had just made an indent on the wall. “Lillian is my prisoner, and I’m in charge here,” she said intensely.

Alex placed her hands on her hips. “You are,” she agreed. “You’re the one who wants to take on the burden for ruling the world. So make a decision.”

Supergirl stared at the air between them. They were desperate; Lena’s scans had failed to turn up the faintest hint of where Winn was being held. Yet this…this was beyond the pale. Torturing Lillian Luthor out of the hope that she could name a scientist who might have a connection with the Worldkillers?

Winn is your friend’, Kara’s mind supplied unhelpfully. ‘He’s been captured because of his connection to you. How could you abandon him?’ Despite herself, tears began to prick at her eyes.

“Lena?” the hero prompted tentatively.

There was a long pause.

“We don’t have to,” the CEO finally said. “Not yet. I’m contacting Pamela; we’re going to try and put Lillian under mind control. She’ll tell us everything.”

Kara could have sighed in relief. Mind control wasn’t something she was a big fan of, but at least it wasn’t painful or permanent. Lillian was as guilty as anyone Lena had already put under her control, no one could deny that.

Without even realizing it, the hero had moved over to her girlfriend’s position. Lena opened her arms, allowing Kara to melt into her embrace.

“We’ll find him,” Lena whispered into Kara’s hair. “I promise.”

Alex rose to her feet. “Good,” she agreed. She stepped into the center of the room. “What if she’s resistant, though? I know only one in a hundred are, but still…we’re not always lucky.”

Lena met her stare, still running a hand soothingly along Kara’s back. “Then we’ll see. In the meantime, L-Corp will continue searching. I don’t care where on Earth they’re keeping him; no one can evade me forever.”

\

The bag lifted off his head to reveal a sterile hallway.

Winn had seen enough movies to know what to do next. Mindful of the firm hand on his back, the techie carefully swept his gaze from left to right, searching for exits. Unfortunately, he received far more questions than answers.

Wherever he had been taken while unconscious, it wasn’t in National City.

The hallway was a strange blend of white and gray. Several doors were etched onto both sides of the hall, each with a strange sheen of glass serving as a window in its center. Winn tried to get a look inside some of the rooms, but his captor was moving him too fast. All he knew was that it was a style of architecture he had never seen before. Strange swirls and patterns caught at the corner of his eyes.

“Thinking of a way out?” Purity asked, still standing behind him.

Winn frowned, ignoring the heart beating against his chest. “Eventually,” he agreed. “I’d like to stick around for a while, though. I have to admit that this place looks interesting.”

The doors had no handles, and they clearly didn’t swing outwards. Fingerpad scanners rested alongside each one, all of them brimming with an infrared light.

Behind him, he could feel the Worldkiller smile. “Focus your limited brainpower on coping with your situation, not on fruitless escape attempts. To return home, you’d need to escape this facility…which is currently staffed by over a dozen individuals each roughly ten thousand times stronger and faster than yourself. Then you’d need to make your way to the nearest ship roughly ten miles away while evading capture. And if you got that far, well, hopefully you’d manage to pilot it on your first attempt without crashing and dying a horrible death.”

His stomach plummeted, nearly sending him stumbling forward. He couldn’t really be on another planet, could he? The thought both elated and terrified him.

“We’ve held a Martian here. A Lantern.” Without warning, Purity stopped in her tracks and slammed his face into the nearest door. Inside, Winn could see a holding cell seemingly made of energy. On a table next to it rested a dark ring adorned with an alien symbol. “And two New Gods.” She dragged him back away from the wall. “So what do you think your chances of escape are?”

Winn scowled, wiping a smear of blood from underneath his nose. “Less than one hundred percent,” he muttered.

Purity chuckled. “Well, zero is less than one hundred percent, so I suppose you’re technically correct.” She stopped him in front of the next door.

Immediately, he flinched. This time, thankfully, Purity didn’t smash his nose into the glass. The alien placed her hand on the scanner. After an affirmative beep, the door slid open with an electronic hiss.

With a casual shove that nevertheless sent Winn reeling, Purity forced him inside.

The techie looked around at what presumably were going to be his accommodations. Which, unfortunately, looked less than accommodating. The amenities consisted of a hard metal slab of a bed and a strange alien contraption that must be their equivalent of a toilet.

At least there was no cell made of energy barriers. Apparently, he didn’t rate as a maximum-security prisoner. Not that it mattered. Winn instinctively knew that he could spend the rest of his life slamming against the door and never hope to make a dent.

“Look,” he said. “Can you just tell me why you’ve brought me here? Because honestly, I’m at a bit of a loss from what you could want with me.” The confusion in his voice was entirely genuine.

His captor smirked, resting her arms on an interrogation table. “I don’t blame you. You are rather worthless. Unfortunately, Kara Zor-El has taken an interest in you. As fruitful as our efforts on Earth have been, our plans for Kara have been ineffective. We need to know how she thinks.”

“And you brought me?” Winn demanded.

“You were the first to learn her secret,” the alien replied. “She trusts you. You will tell us her strengths, her weaknesses, and her fears. And if all else fails, you will make a convenient hostage.”

In spite of his dire situation, a fierce protectiveness welled up within him. “I can’t escape here. That doesn’t mean I’m going to help you.”

“You can put on a brave face all you like, Mr. Schott. There is no hiding your terror.”

Winn shook his head. “I’m not hiding it. I am terrified. But I’m not going to betray my friends. Especially for an alien cult that’s going to kill me as soon as they’re done with me, anyway.”

Purity held up her hand and flicked her finger. The compressed pocket of air emanating from the easy action was enough to knock Winn on his ass. Painfully.

“Oh, no. You’re one of the lucky ones. I can’t even damage you permanently without explicit authorization,” Purity revealed. She smiled down at him, her face gentle. “I’ll be sticking with more elegant methods…direct targeting of your pain receptors. I’ll try to keep you conscious, but if you pass out, well…we’ve got time. Mistress Selena has given me a month to work with you.”

Climbing to his feet unsteadily, Winn stared his captor down. He’d suspected such a thing was coming, not that it really softened the blow. “Before you torture me into insanity, I have a question of my own,” he said, trying to keep his voice steady. “What do you want with Kara?”

Purity gave him his answer.

All of the blood rushed out of his face. Before, he had been terrified for himself. He still was. But Winn was now mortified for Kara.

\

It was Lena’s crowning achievement.

The L-Shield was the most gargantuan construction project in human history. Its creation had been possible only through marshalling an invaluable amount of resources, technology, and manpower gathered throughout the planet. If Vanity hadn’t used her talents to make L-Corp the economic and political centerpiece of Earth, it would have taken a century to complete.

Years ago, the International Space Station had been built for roughly one hundred and fifty billion dollars. The cost of the L-Shield had been estimated at twenty trillion.

Lena had roughly doubled Earth’s GDP in the last two years, combining both her inexplicable brainpower and control over alien technology to jumpstart the global economy. Roughly one fourth of that increase had been funneled into the L-Shield. The network of satellites that would power the global energy shield, the weapons platforms defending the satellites, and the monitoring systems tracking any and all incursions into their solar system had been deemed impossible by many.

If L-Corp hadn’t gained a foothold in every major government on Earth, the network probably would have been nuked out of orbit during construction.

“How long do you plan on keeping the shield active for?”

Lena turned to the other occupant in her office. Princess Koriand’r was a recent addition to Earth, having fled her home planet of Tamaran following its fall to an interplanetary foe known as the Citdael. Having escaped slavery at the hands of her enemies, the exiled Princess had found her way to Earth alone.

She had come to Lena of her own violation a few months ago. Having seen her home planet fall, she was determined to prevent the same from happening to Earth. The Princess had agreed to lend L-Corp her services, asking only that the company help her locate fellow survivors from Tamaran in exchange.

Lena had quickly agreed, though the search had not yet been successful in spite of her best efforts. Though desperate to help at least some of her people, Koriand’r had been surprisingly patient. The alien was nothing if not understanding.

Koriand’r was useful for Lena’s purposes in a multitude of ways. Her status as an alien refugee made her a perfect spokesperson for both advocating the L-Shield’s necessity and assuring alien supporters that it would not be used to deter peaceful refugees.

A combination of solar energy and experimentation she had endured during slavery also had imbued the Princess with a combination of flight, super strength, and energy blasts. Already, she was operating as a superhero under the alias ‘Starfire’.

“There are two shields,” the CEO answered her guest. “One is an invisible barrier that is always active; it protects the Earth from an external telepathic attack. Any hostile force attempting to spy on us or take control of an individual on Earth will be blocked. The second is an energy field that blocks anything but sunlight.” Lena paused, smiling reassuringly. “It’s only to be activated in emergencies, I promise. My girlfriend would never forgive me otherwise.”

Starfire frowned. “I am sorry about her friend. Have you had any of the luck in trying to locate him?”

Folding her arms, Lena stared wistfully out the window. “It’s just ‘luck’, and no, I haven’t. It’s been two weeks, and not a thing.” Her gut twisted at the thought. Winn was out there somewhere, suffering at the hands of a Worldkiller. Kara’s recent depression and constant hunt to look for him served as an ever-present reminder of Lena’s failure.

“You will find him!” The alien smiled, floating over to Lena’s desk and taking the villain’s hands in hers. “On my short time on this planet, I have come to admire your abundant mental strength. I have faith you will not fail!”

“…Thanks,” Lena replied, gently prying her fingers out of the Princess’s grip. How these alien women can remain so optimistic after they’ve lost their planets, I will never understand.

A sudden beep sounded from her computer monitor, making Starfire jump in midair. “Lena, your device is angry!”

“It’s an alert,” the CEO replied. She clicked on the red message…and her eyes widened in shock. Live footage from one of her telescopes observing the edge of the galaxy was showing her a moving object, roughly one fourth the size of Earth.

Moving. Object.

 Her eyes focused in on the image. It looked like a domed city resting on the surface of a decaying asteroid. Many of the buildings had sustained what looked like heavy damage, but Lena could already tell they were crafted from a style of alien architecture she had never seen before.

Lena’s hands were a blur, rapidly dialing the number of the head of her aerospace division. “Give me details,” she spoke into the phone immediately. “When did we find this?”

“We didn’t. They found us. They’ve been broadcasting a massive telecommunications signal that our probes have recently picked up. It’s on a constant frequency compatible with one of our receptors. We can initiate video contact at any time.”

Her mouth gaped open. Hands falling to her sides, she did her best to process her thoughts. There are living individuals on that asteroid. They know who we are. They want to talk.

“Do it,” Lena responded. “Run it directly through my personal computer. Then alert all department heads for any emergency meeting. We’re about to get either a threat of invasion or a desperate plea for help.”

“Understood.”

Even expecting it, the CEO still nearly jolted in shock when a video image appeared on her computer. Two women were looking into the screen. One was dressed in a dark suit adorned with a Kryptonian family crest. The other was wearing a light blue dress with an interweaving pattern below the shoulders giving way to…

El mayarah.

Chapter End Notes

Wondering how everyone feels about how to deal with Lillian.

Light

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Kara, I need you to come in now.”  

Supergirl furrowed her eyes, even though she knew there was no way Lena could even see her. “I’m on patrol at the moment, covering North Africa. Don’t you remember?”

“Yes, I have your schedule memorized.” Lena’s voice was heavy with exasperation, but it was also tinged with an unplaceable emotional energy. “I’m sending Starfire to take over patrol for you. You need to come to my office, now.”

The retort ‘You’re not the boss of me’ sprung to Kara’s lips, only for the hero to remember that she was, in fact, speaking with her boss. More importantly, Lena founded more concerned than stern.

“Okay.”

\

Supergirl touched down on Lena’s office balcony minutes later. Inside, Lena immediately stood up from her desk and motioned to the computer. The CEO’s entire body was radiating with a strange intensity.

“Kara…we have a visitor.”

Missing the glow of sunlight as she stepped inside, Supergirl moved closer to the screen. “What are you-?” Her eyes lifted to the screen.

“Jeju?!” Alura Zor-El’s face was plastered on the monitor of Lena’s computer, looking at her expectantly. Slam! Kara’s knees fell to the floor with enough force to crack the wood.

What is this? “Lena…what…is this a program…?”

“It’s me, daughter.” Kara’s heart leapt as she heard her mother’s voice for the first time in decades. “I’ve missed you so much.”

This was a dream. It had to be a dream. Kara climbed to her feet and leaned towards the monitor. “Y-you can’t be alive…” she stuttered, tears dripping down her face. The hero was barely conscious of Lena behind her, placing a soothing hand on her back. “Krypton was destroyed. I saw it from my pod!”

“Most of our planet was lost,” Alura replied. There was no mistaking the sorrow in her words. “Argo City survived. We protected it with an energy shield; we’ve been drifting through space ever since.”

Kara’s heart felt like it was bursting out of her chest. She wanted to believe it…no. Kara couldn’t go through that loss again. She had to resist being sucked in by the mirage in front of her. “This doesn’t make sense! You sent me away because you knew we were doomed!”

Alura shook her head. “That was the hardest choice I ever had to make. We weren’t sure the shield would work. We…couldn’t take a chance on your life. It didn’t matter how painful it would be, even if we would never see you again…we had to give you your best odds.”

“Kara,” Lena whispered gently. “I think she’s telling the truth.”

And now this projection of Alura had the smartest person in the world supporting her story. “Y-your face. You’d be seventy years old by now.” She stared at her mother’s face, failing to find anything other than the smallest wrinkles. “You look forty.”

“We spend most of our time in hypersleep,” the older woman explained patiently. “Resources on Argo are thin…and dwindling.”

Yes! Individuals in hypersleep didn’t require any food or water. That made sense! Kara look again at the monitor, her eyes roaming over every detail. The woman on the screen was Alura Zor-El. Nothing could make such a convincing fake.

Nothing except…  

“Lena,” Kara said slowly. “Did you grow up in a loving family?”

The supervillain blinked in confusion. “…No,” she replied. “You know that? Why are you-?”

“I’m not under a Black Mercy!” Kara all but hopped on her feet. “Rao, it’s really you. Jeju!”

Her heart all but stopped.

“Where’s dad?”

Slowly, sadly, Alura shook her head. “Only a fraction of our population made it. Zor-El sacrificed himself to activate the dome. He saved all of us. I’m sorry, starlight.”

Starlight. The familiar term of endearment felt like it was splitting her soul in two. Her brief, unspoken hope that her father was still alive had been shattered, but her mother was still on the screen. Alura Zor-El, alive and healthy, was speaking to her.

“Jeju, I…” Kara let out a long, happy breath. “Where have you been?”

“Drifting towards Earth,” Alura answered. “I lead our High Council now. If you think I wouldn’t have followed you the second I was able, you don’t know me,” she continued with a smile. “It didn’t take much convincing. Earth is suitable for our needs, as you’ve already found out. My people seek a partnership.”

Still flooded with happiness, Kara could only motion to Lena. “That’s her department.”

She stepped aside slightly, allowing the CEO to come into full view of the monitor. Stupidly, Kara allowed her eyes to roam outside of the windows, seeking a glimpse of the last remnant of Krypton.

I’m not alone. A twenty-year-old burden had just vanished from her shoulders.

“I haven’t formerly introduced myself,” the CEO spoke. Her voice was now businesslike. “I am Lena Luthor, Kara’s boss, girlfriend, and fiancé. I’m also in control of more than half of Earth’s economic assets and many of its governments.”

Alura looked at her strangely. “You are Earth’s leader, then?”

“Not entirely. I’ve taken it upon myself to safeguard this planet from all threats,” Lena replied. Her fingers drummed against the desk. “If you seek an alliance, I’m the one who can make that happen. Fortunately, I’m certain that my Senior Vice President here will put in a good word for you.” She smirked.

Kara wrapped an arm around Lena’s shoulder. “You could say that. And I’ll put in a good word for you too,” she interjected, placing a kiss on her girlfriend’s cheek.

“Ah-hem,” Alura interrupted. “I see you’ve done well for yourself, daughter. Are you…happy on this world?” Her eyes all but were pleading for validation.

The hero nodded vigorously. “I am! Things haven’t always been easy, but I’ve helped a lot of people. Nothing could replace what I had with you and dad, but I’ve found family here. Friends too.” At the word friend, a familiar pit sunk in her stomach. “One of them’s been kidnapped,” Kara continued, her voice growing lower. She glanced hopefully at her mother. “Maybe you can help us find him!”

Alura nodded. “I will. But you should know the news isn’t all good. Argo was attacked fifteen years ago.” The matriarch closed her eyes, as if replaying old memories. “A despotic conqueror took note of our potential and our weakness. His forces penetrated the dome. We would have been wiped out completely if two hundred of our number hadn’t sacrificed themselves to sabotage his planet’s reactor.”

The bones in Lena’s knuckles were as white as her desk. “Don’t tell me,” she hissed. “Darkseid.”

“I see you know of his threat,” Alura answered.

“His world of Apokolips is a literal hellscape. It travels throughout the universe, taking whatever will aid its conquests and wiping out the rest.”

“Why target you?” Kara asked.

“Darkseid targeted us because he could. He follows us because he saw our potential. By the time Apokolips launched its invasion, we had already been energized by a yellow sun. A thousand of us were able to hold off his forces and wipe out those who made it through our defenses. Though…” Alura winced, “Not without cost. He took prisoners. His agents learned that most of our population is in hypersleep and vulnerable. If Darkseid’s minions gained control of Argo, they could brainwash every one of them to follow his bidding. The universe wouldn’t stand a chance.”

There was a furious dance of contemplation in Lena’s eyes. “That answers one question.” She stated after a moment. “Darkseid has minions on Earth…Worldkillers. They have Kryptonian abilities.”

Even through a screen, Kara could see her mother’s body tense with anger. “Then that monster has used his prisoners to make a perversion of our people. And if he has advance agents on Earth, there is no hiding your world from his wrath.”

As much as Lena tried to hide it, Kara could see the fear in the supervillain’s eyes. “How much time do we have?” Lena asked.

“Argo will reach your solar system within two weeks. Apokolips has been slowly gaining on us for years. We predict contact within six months.”

Supergirl suppressed a gasp. “Wake up everyone in hypersleep, then!”

Her mother sighed. “There are two billion of them. We don’t have the resources. And this isn’t like your pod, Kara. The technology is crude in comparison. Waking them up will be a gradual process…it would take at least a year. We don’t even have enough Harun-el to supply the necessary power.”

“I can help with that,” Lena said. “It might take time, but I’ve been refining my process of making Harun-el. Not quickly enough to stop Darkseid, however.”

Alura’s eyes, briefly alight with hope, sagged with disappointment. “Then our only chance of victory is to unite. Apokolips nearly overwhelmed us within ours, and that was with two thousand of us. Only half of our waking population is left,” she explained. “We must use Earth’s resources in our defense. It’s all or nothing.”

Kara wasn’t surprised to see Lena nodding in return. “Agreed.”

“Then I formally issue you an invitation to Argo, Lena Luthor. A small personal spacecraft should be able to make the journey to our current position within thirty-six hours. Kara, of course, is welcome to come along as well.” She issued a beaming smile at her daughter.

“I accept,” the CEO replied. Kara grinned.

“Unfortunately, I don’t have any such craft,” Lena continued.

Kara frowned, very unpleasantly surprised. “What? Why?”

“We’ve had no need for long distance manned spaceflight. And I’ve been busy developing other things, as you well know.” Lena turned back to Alura. “If you have such a spacecraft, you’re welcome to bring yourself and your advisers to Earth so we may begin preparations. There might just be time for a reunion as well.”

Please tell me they have-  

“We do have such a spacecraft. And yes, there will be time for a reunion. It’s a condition of our alliance.” She sent Lena a calm yet firm look.

The supervillain dipped her head. “Understood.”

“Jeju.” Kara stepped towards the screen again. “You’re back. I…I’m sorry. I don’t know what to say. I still think I’m dreaming.”

“I feel the same way,” Alura replied. “And if I am, I never want to wake up again. I’ve regretted sending you away for so long…it’s good to see you’ve at least found some happiness.” She gestured at Lena before sighing. “I need to go. The sooner we start preparing for our trip, the sooner I’ll arrive on Earth. Expect our ship within forty-eight hours.”

Kara stared at the screen. It made sense, but it felt as if ending the signal would be saying goodbye to her mother yet again. This could all turn out to be a cruel lie. What if the ship blew up halfway to Earth? Alura could have a heart attack on the way. Or Darkseid could attack Argo now, ahead of schedule.”

“Starlight,” Alura interrupted, a knowing look in her eyes. “I’ve survived for the last twenty years. I will see you on Earth within forty-eight hours.”

The hero took a deep breath. “I know. I love you.”

“And I you.”

The signal ended.

Kara jumped into the air, spinning around and raising her arms. “Lena, it was really her! I can’t believe it! And she’s coming here!” The hero glided forward, taking her girlfriend into arms and hoisting her into the air. “You’re going to meet her!”

Lena was smiling back at her. Yet there was a hesitance in the villain’s eyes that made Kara deflate. Literally. Supergirl floated back towards the ground, glancing at the other woman uncertainly. “What’s wrong?”

“Kara, I…” Lena hesitated, sighing as her feet touched back onto the floor. Then she looked back up at the hero, her lips set in resolve. “Even hundreds of Kryptonians couldn’t defeat Darkseid. Despite all my brilliance…some things just can’t be overcome. We’re fighting an alien world thousands of years more advanced than us, and every facet of its technology is designed for the sole purpose of conquest. What chance do we have?”

Supergirl understood Lena’s doubt. But as long as she was breathing, she wouldn’t give up hope. Especially not now, with her mother alive and on their side. “We have you, me, and all of Argo with us. Besides, we’ve beaten this invasion before. How many times have the Worldkillers tried to kill you?” Kara pointed out, smiling brightly. “They wouldn’t have gone to so much effort unless they knew you were a threat to them…and we’ve stopped them at every turn.”

The CEO sat back in her chair. “They have a weakness, Kara. Reign has refused to kill you; she even tried to save you from the Black Mercy. For one reason or another, our enemy wants you alive.”

There was a fear in the supervillain’s eyes that Kara couldn’t place. Suppressing a shiver down her spine, Supergirl leaned forward onto the desk. “Any idea why?” Kara couldn’t fathom it herself. Yes, she was powerful, but so were the Worldkillers. Darkseid, somehow, already had some Kryptonians underneath his control.

Somehow. Kara froze. Perhaps he’d genetically engineered them. If that was the case, for all of their gifts, they were still artificial. Maybe that was why he wanted Kara, to perfect the process. He’d had access to the citizens of Argo, but Kara was the only one who’d spent decades under a yellow sun.

He could study her. Dissect her. The alien conqueror could use her genes to augment his forces. Or even…even create an army of clones to do his bidding. Lena was right; they had no way of understanding the limits his technology.

By the look on Lena’s face, Kara could tell that the CEO was thinking of even worse possibilities. Clenching her fists, the villain placed her hands on her desk. “I won’t let him take you, Kara. I won’t let anyone take you.”

“I know,” Kara replied, believing it fully.

This was all wrong. Her mother was alive…and coming to help them! Together, Kara was sure they would be able to defend Earth and find Winn. They should have been celebrating. Seeking to defuse the tension in the room, and genuinely curious, Kara changed the subject.

“Did my mother and I have that entire conversation in Kryptonese?”

Lena rolled her eyes. “Yes.”

Kara’s eyes narrowed in confusion. She wouldn’t have missed that if she was thinking clearly. “You were taking part in that conversation, and you understood what my mother was saying?”

The villain crossed her arms. “I’ve found it useful to study alien languages. The language of your planet isn’t so different from some of the ones I’ve learned. Between that, phrases I’ve heard you use, and Lex’s notes, it wasn’t hard to put together.”

Her girlfriend being such a show-off would have been annoying if it weren’t so sexy. Since it was, Kara decided to indulge her. “Just how many languages do you know?”

“Human and alien?” Lena pretended to think about it. “Four hundred and eighty-seven. I’m literate in all of them, but my pronunciation isn’t so great in around half of them. Most of them I’ve learned from simple translation books. I only need to read each word once. The grammatical rules come naturally.”

Kara scoffed, but was unable to hide her smile. “You could try a little modesty now and then.”

“False modesty didn’t help me take over half of this planet,” Lena argued. “Or, more importantly, help win you over. I’ll stick with what’s provided me results so far.”

“Well, my mother’s going to be here in two days.” Supergirl moved behind the other woman, placing an arm over her shoulders. “If you’re going to win her over, we’re going to need to work on your pronunciation.”

Chuckling, Lena allowed Kara to lead her away. “I hope that’s all it takes. I’m the woman engaged to her long-lost daughter. I can imagine she’s going to have some high standards.”

\

Alura turned to her second in command. “I want the ship ready as soon as possible,” she ordered. After years…decades of waiting to see her daughter in the flesh, every additional second of delay was another moment of agony.

“I’ve already given the order to have it prepped. Don’t worry; she’s not going anywhere.” Selena stepped forward, placing a comforting hand on Alura’s forearm. “I must say I’m looking forward to seeing Earth for myself. She leaned in, placing a light kiss on the High Councilor’s lips. “I’ll go make sure everything else is in order before we leave.”

Alura smiled at her girlfriend as she walked out of the room. Her relationship with Selena was complicated, yet comfortable. With her husband dead and Kara on Earth, Alura had been desperate for solace. A mutual respect and attraction between the two women had made their coming together all but inevitable.

Were they in love? Alura wasn’t quite certain. But they shared a strong friendship and passion between them. Plus, Selena was someone who Alura had long since learned could be trusted unconditionally.

On the barren, decaying asteroid of Argo, that was more than enough.

\

“You can stop this.”

Winn stared down his tormenter. “So can you. All you have to do is let me go, beg my friends for forgiveness, and give up your evil ways.”

A hand roughly cupped his chin. “This false bravado will not save you.”

“I know that,” he replied, jerking his chin away. Two metal wires ran from the computer at the center of the room into two shallow incisions on his forehead. “I’m not going to pretend I’m not terrified. But humor is pretty much the only way I can amuse myself while-”

He broke off as a new round of pain erupted in his head. Winn desperately closed his eyes, though he long since learned that it would do nothing to abate his agony. By the time his tormenter finally deigned to deactivate his pain receptors, his fingers were jittering in anguish.

“This can all be over,” his torturer continued. “Tell us all you can about Kara Zor-El, and we will wipe this entire experience from your mind. We will let you go. It will be as if this never happened,” she promised.

Winn believed her. His arms and legs were restrained by metal bindings, but his skin was unblemished. There would be no record of this horrific experience. The techie even knew that his captors had employed a modicum of restraint to prevent his mind from fracturing. He could walk away from this.

He just didn’t care.

“Mistress Selena is on her way to Earth,” Ursa continued. “We are running out of time. If you don’t tell me Kara Zor-El’s weaknesses before she arrives on the planet, well, life might become more difficult.”

For you, maybe. “I don’t get it,” he said. “I’ve told you everything I know! What more could you want from me?”

She towered over him, hands on her hips. “I want to know Kara Zor-El. Her hopes, her passions, her fears. Everything that matters to her…how to reach her. You have told me nothing but lies. Do you think I do not know when a prisoner is telling the truth and when they are not?”

Winn couldn’t argue with that. He’d made up several lies in an attempt to get her to back off, but all of them had failed. Ursa had seen through them all effortlessly.

It was tempting to give in. There was no way of knowing how useful any information he had would be to his captors. Even though his body showed no sign of injury, the neural pain they had subjected him to had almost been unbearable.

Yet he knew who they worked for now. His safety meant nothing compared to what would happen if the enemy succeeded. Winn had to do everything in his power to lower their chance of success. Even at the cost of his sanity.

Ursa glared at him. Finally, she realized he wasn’t about to speak up. “Then we’ll move to Phase Two,” she continued. “I’ve been authorized to increase the dosage of pain. We would prefer not to risk snapping your mind, but you’ve forced our hand.”

Her fingers hovered over the switch. “Give me one piece of useful information, and this stops.”

No. No. NO! Winn’s headed exploded in pain. This was worse than before…this was indescribable. It felt like a volcano was erupting in his brain. Searing heat was crashing into his skull, melting it. His hands chafed against their restraints as he tried to bring them to his head, even though he knew it wouldn’t help.

Winn’s entire body began to spasm against the table, held in place only by his restraints. Let me die. Please, let me die.

“One minute on this setting will cause permanent mental damage. Two, and you’ll likely be reduced to a drooling imbecile,” Ursa’s voice sounded above him, somehow cutting through the pain.

He wasn’t sure how long he’d been screaming in agony. Yet he managed to get a few words out in between. “F-fine. Turn my mind…to mush…then. I’ll…never be able to…tell you…anything.”

BANG!  

A metallic crash sounded in the next room over. Even through his agony, Winn still managed to muster some shock as a small circular object all but carved through the wall. Moving in a blur of light, the metal circle came to rest on one of his outstretched fingers.

The pain was suddenly gone as a green glow consumed the room.
