Truth

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Kara, you are literally buzzing.”

The hero turned to look at herself. True enough, she was currently floating three inches above the ground and jittering back and forth so quickly it sounded like they were surrounded by a swarm of bees.

“Sorry Alex,” she replied, not really sorry at all. The grin stretching across her face was actually starting to make her cheeks ache, but Kara simply didn’t care. “My mother is landing here in five minutes. Aren’t you excited?!” She touched down on the ground, still vibrating with enthusiasm.

Her sister smiled at her. “Of course I am. I guess I can’t blame you. Go on,” she waved her hand. “Go on buzzing, little bee. Your queen will be here soon.”

“Okay!” Kara floated back above the ground.

Lena was standing in front of them, looking pensively at the horizon. “I thought I was your Queen?” she asked softly.

“I can’t have more than one?” Still buzzing, Kara glided over to her girlfriend and placed a kiss on her cheek. “I really do appreciate you keeping this private.”

There had been some debate among the higher echelons in L-Corp about how to greet the representatives from Argo. Some wanted a grand ceremony, with Alura’s ship touching down on top of the L-Corp building surrounded by welcoming banners and flashing cameras. It was, after all, the first meeting between the leader of one world and the most powerful figure of another.

Lena had decided against it. She’d argued that the proceedings should be kept away from the public eye until it was certain that things would work out. Announcing their alliance would also put Darkseid’s agents on alert, something that the CEO wanted to avoid.

Unofficially, L-Corp’s Senior Vice President also wanted a moment alone with her mother. 

So instead, it was just Lena, Kara, and Alex meeting with Alura’s ship at a predetermined point outside of the city and away from prying eyes. Everything was perfect.

Suddenly, Kara stopped buzzing.

The CEO noticed instantly. “What’s wrong?”

Supergirl’s head drooped at the same time her feet touched the ground. “I’m so happy, Lena. Everything feels like it’s perfect. And at the same time, Winn is probably being interrogated in a cell for Rao knows what! I shouldn’t even be smiling, much less-”

“Kara. We are doing everything we can to locate Winn, I promise,” Lena swore. “There’s nothing more you could do. Even if he’s suffering….he would want you to be happy today. You know it and I know it. This has been your dream for decades; take a day and enjoy it. Don’t feel guilty for things that aren’t your fault.”

The hero tilted her head, looking at her girlfriend meaningfully. ‘Like you’re one to talk,’ her eyes said.

Lena nodded, acknowledging the hypocrisy. “That doesn’t mean I’m wrong. Enjoy the day, dear. If I’m right about what’s coming, we should take the chance to be happy while we still have it.”

Two days ago, Kara would have agreed. But now, with her mother alive and an army of yellow sun-powered Kryptonians standing behind her, it felt like nothing could stop them.

“Why am I even here?” Alex cut in. “I can’t speak Kryptonese. I’ll just be staring at you all like a dupe, trying to figure out what the hell is going on.”

Supergirl zipped over to the other superhero, wrapping an arm around her sister. “You’re here because I want you to be here. I wouldn’t want you to miss this for the world.”

\

“Approaching the coordinates now. Atmospheric entry within one minute.”

Alura nodded absently, barely hearing Selena’s words. Her daughter was down there on this lush world. The very world Alura had sent her to…the greatest mistake of her entire life.

“You’re worried,” Selena said.

The High Councilor whirled on her. “Of course I am! I haven’t seen my daughter in decades! What if things don’t work out? With everything that’s happening…the fate of our world in the balance…I can’t lose her again. I refuse.”

“You won’t,” her lover promised. “A blind man could see how much you care for her. After everything you’ve done for her…how could she blame you?”

How could she not? “I sent her away,” Alura declared. “I-”

Selena rested her chin on the High Councilor’s shoulder. “You did what you had to do,” she assured her.

\

Kara could see her mother. See her. Her eyes followed the small, sleek ship as it descended through the clouds. The hero’s eyes penetrated through the shining silver hull, zooming in on the figure in the lead seat.

Supergirl could see the same nervousness and joy she was experiencing reflected in her mother’s eyes. It took every ounce of self-control Kara possessed…and Lena’s firm grip on her shoulder…to prevent her from flying up to meet the ship and breaking through the metal to embrace Alura that much sooner.

The dirt beneath her feet began to vibrate beneath her as she continued to buzz in the air ever faster. Then the ship was finally touching down, and the ramp was opening, and-

“Jeju!” Kara darted forward so fast a human observer would have believed her to be a teleporter. Her mother was standing in front of her, alive and healthy. In fact, her mother was in her arms. The hero hadn’t realized that she had taken Alura in a crushing embrace, tears flowing freely down her face.

It’s real. It’s real.

“Starlight.” Alura returned her embrace, running a hand soothingly through her hair. “You have no idea how much I’ve missed you.”

For the first time since she was thirteen years old, Kara felt complete.

\

Kara was resistant to pulling back from her mother, but Alex’s fingers tapping her on the shoulder eventually reminded the hero that she and Alura were not the only two people who existed in the universe.

“Mom, this is Alex Danvers. She’s my adopted sister. Unfortunately, she doesn’t speak Kryptonese yet. And you’ve obviously already met Lena Luthor, future ruler of this planet and my fiancé.”

Alura reached forward to shake both of their hands. Some gestures, it seemed, took root in multiple cultures. “It is a pleasure to meet you both. And where is Kal-El? Did he not wish to be here to see his Aunt?”

The words felt like a crushing blow. It took Kara several moments to regain the ability to speak, but Lena seemed content to let her explain. “Kal-El is gone,” the hero finally managed. For the first time since her mother’s arrival, Kara’s gaze turned away from Alura. “While serving as a hero for this world, he was killed in battle by…”

Oh.

“My brother.” Lena stepped forward, looking supremely uncomfortable. “He was a monster who despised aliens, especially one who was more beloved than himself. Lex attacked Clark on multiple occasions…he finally succeeded in a suicidal attack.”

Alura stared at her. “Your brother?” she repeated.

“Lena and her brother were both incredibly smart.” Kara stepped next to her girlfriend. “That is literally the only similarity they have. Lena has done so much good for this world, and she loves aliens…one in particular.” She gestured to herself. “I wouldn’t be alive if it weren’t for her.”

“Earth has made you far too trusting, Kara Zor-El.”

Kara looked up to see another woman walking out of the ship. She was looked around Alura’s age, with short black hair dropping down to slightly above her shoulders. “You would allow yourself to mate with the kin of your cousin’s murderer?”

She was staring at Kara with undisguised resentment. Her face growing red, the hero stepped towards the woman. “I would trust Lena with my life,” she replied furiously. “In fact, I have on several occasions, and she has never let me down. Who are you to accuse her?”

Alura raised a placating hand. “This is Selena, the other surviving member of our High Council and my current lover. You must forgive her. She can be a bit too…protective,” she said with a warning look at the other woman.

Lover?! It felt so sudden. Zor-El was long dead, but the last time Kara had seen Alura, she’d been in a loving relationship with her husband. To see with a woman Kara had never met, and had already insulted the hero’s own girlfriend…

She glanced over at Lena. The CEO’s face remained resolute, but Kara could see that odd mix of guilt and resentment in the villain’s eyes. As much as she disliked anyone bringing up her family’s crimes, Lena still couldn’t let go of her guilt.

Kara wasn’t quite as happy as she was five minutes ago.

\

“Come in. Make yourselves comfortable.”

Lena took her seat at the head of the boardroom, the picture of poise and smooth power. Kara, Alex, Alura, and Selena took the chairs closest to her. No one else was in the room. Even after relocating to L-Corp’s headquarters, it seemed Lena still wanted to keep this meeting private.

“I need to know everything you have about Darkseid. His attack on your world, his future plans…anything you can offer me.”

Selena didn’t look thrilled at the prospect of following the CEO’s lead, but Alura nodded solemnly. “He made his first move sixteen years ago. Our first contact was a scout ship that was picked up by Argo’s long-range sensors. It disappeared just as suddenly, using FTL.”

Faster than light. “You didn’t chase after it?” Kara asked.

“With what?” Selena questioned, making no attempt to hide her annoyance. “Argo has less than a dozen small craft capable of FTL. At the time, we perceived no threat. We’d already encountered countless alien craft on our journey through the stars.”

Alura tapped her fingers nervously against the table. “Interstellar civilization has been backsliding since the collapse of the Green Lantern Corps. Seeing a lone ship didn’t surprise us.”

“There was no warning. Three days later, the attack began. A fleet of FTL craft warped to our position. We saw them on our sensors and made overtures but were met with silence. In no time at all they had burrowed under Argo’s asteroid, and assaulted our defenses. Even with two thousand of us empowered by a yellow sun, the city was consumed by war,” Selena continued.

War. Hadn’t her people suffered enough? What heartless dictator could target a suffering civilization, one on its last legs, just to increase his own power? The very idea made the hero so angry her eyes threatened to glow with blue energy.

Kara would never understand evil.

She started slightly as Alura placed a comforting hand on her wrist. “We were fighting for days. Then Apokolips itself arrived…we were overwhelmed within hours. A force of two hundred of our people infiltrated the enemy planet and disabled its main reactor,” her mother explained. “Large landmasses like Argo or Apokilips can’t use FTL. They need a traditional power source to move through space. With their reactor crippled, Argo was able to escape and leave Darkseid stranded in space.”

“For now,” Selena grumbled. “We’ve expanded our sensor range since then. Apokolips has repaired its reactor and is following us. They’ve been gaining on us as our supply of Harun-el has run low. If they gain access to the rest of our population waiting in hypersleep, Darkseid will crush the entire universe under his fist.”

Lena was folding her fingers as she stared at the table in contemplation. “And you’ve said we only have months before Darkseid reaches us. Very well.” She looked directly at Alura. “Your people will be housed on Earth and incorporated into our defenses. The billions in hypersleep can be transferred to any location on Earth of your choosing and will be provided all possible security at our disposal. L-Corp and your Council will form a joint organization to oversee our efforts.”

The High Councilor looked at the CEO thoughtfully. “I would not be so quick to discount Argo itself, Lena Luthor. Our city is crippled, but much of its technology is still functional.”

“What do you have?” Lena asked simply.

Alura smiled thinly. “Perhaps you should see for yourself. Our craft can reach Argo within two days. That might give you a better opportunity to see what is at our disposal.”

“Let’s go!” Kara said excitedly. “We can both go see Argo!” The hero jolted her girlfriend’s arm. “If there is still any remnant of Krypton left, I need to see it.” Even if it was just one city, it was still a product of thousands of years of Kryptonian culture. Argo was proof that her planet, her people, still existed.

For decades, Supergirl had regarded her home planet as dust floating through space. To break out of that mindset, to truly hope again…she needed to see it for herself.

Lena took a deep breath. Nervously, Kara watched as the CEO made her decision. “Very well,” she agreed. “I cannot say if I can stay more than a week, but I would love the opportunity to see Kara’s home.”

“Then let there be no delay.” Alura stood up. “Selena and I will return to our ship and have it prepped to leave within the hour. That should give you and Kara plenty of time to prepare your traveling essentials and meet us there.”

The CEO nodded in agreement.

Beside them, Alex spoke up for the first time in the meeting. She still couldn’t understand the Kryptonian language, but her eyes and ears still worked fine.

“Kara, you’re buzzing again.”

\

“I’m going to miss you.”

Surprisingly, Alex wasn’t looking at her. The newly christened superhero was looking down at her phone, a curious look on her face. It was only when Kara unsuccessfully maneuvered her head to try and gaze at the screen that her sister looked up.

“It’s only for a week,” Alex said. Her mood seemed to match the drab conference room they were standing in. “I’m sorry I can’t see you off, but I have to go.”

Kara stared at her, slightly disappointed. Then again, Alex was going to be shouldering all of Supergirl’s responsibilities while the more experienced hero was on vacation. Even with all of the backup provided by L-Corp, she was going to be busy.

“I’ll be back before you know it!” Kara promised.

Alex nearly winced. “Kara…I know things are going to get complicated. Maybe more complicated than any of us could predict. But I want you to know that whatever happens, I’m with you. You understand?”

“Of course, but…complicated? My mother is back. What’s complicated about that?”

There was silence for a moment. Alex seemed to be thinking. At last, she said, “Well…what if she wants you to move to Argo? You have responsibilities to Earth, and L-Corp…and now you have a duty to your people. What if you can’t do it all?”

Move to Argo? “Alex, I can promise you I’m not leaving Earth.”

“You’d better not.” Lena’s voice suddenly sounded in the doorway. The CEO stepped into the room, giving Alex a knowing look. “I believe you’re needed, Sentinel.”

The new heroine nodded resolutely. “See you soon.” After a last hug with her sister, Alex supersped out into the hallway and vanished from sight.

Kara turned to her girlfriend. “I could never leave Earth. You, Alex, Eliza, Winn, James…I could never turn my back on this planet. This world is part of me now, just like Krypton. I wouldn’t be able to bear losing either one.”

Lena’s lip was actually trembling. “You have no idea how much I want you to be happy, Kara. If you chose…well, something else, I’d understand. But I can’t stand here and tell you I’d be able to lose you. You’re…I don’t have anything else.”

“You have-”

“Companies and planes and property and all of that, yes I know.” Lena interrupted her with a frustrated glare. “That isn’t enough to make me happy. Trust me, I spent years finding that out before you turned up.”

The hero crossed her arms. “I was going to say Jess, and Sam, and Ruby. Even Alex and…Winn,” she finished, a familiar pang of guilt hitting her. “They might not love you as much as I do, but you will never be alone.”

Lena’s whisper was so soft Kara barely even heard it. “They wouldn’t be enough.”

“What?”

“That’s not enough!” the CEO repeated. “I have plenty of people I care about Kara, but the thing you’ve never understood about me is that I am selfish. You were the first person on Earth, other than my real mother, to actually put me first. You have no idea how good it feels for me to be someone’s most important person. Not my money, or my power, but me. Jess has her son. Sam and Ruby have each other. They would all choose someone else over me and I don’t blame them.” The villain’s eyes were glistening. “You wouldn’t choose me over anyone, I’ve seen it plenty of times. And as guilty as it makes me…I’ve grown addicted to it.”

“Lena…” Kara couldn’t deny her words. Was there anyone on the planet more important to her than her fiancé? Alex, Eliza, and Alura…it was impossible to say. But deep down, maybe Lena was right. How painful would it be for her to never see the CEO again? Kara had survived her world’s destruction, but she wasn’t sure she would be able survive Lena’s.

Kara had never seen the CEO look so guilty.

“You have so many people who put you first,” Lena went on. “Alex, Eliza, me…Alura. And you deserve that. Me?” she laughed at herself. “I’m a manipulative villainous bitch. And I can’t even regret it, because that’s what it’s going to take to save the world. You…you know I’ve always been terrified you’re going to wake up and realize I’m not worth it. Now I have an entire planet…your planet, to compete with. If I…”

The supervillain stopped talking as Kara kissed her fiercely on the lips. For several moments they were glued together, all acknowledgement of the outside world forgotten. When Supergirl finally pulled back, she stared into Lena’s eyes with the same passion. “I don’t know why you’re feeling so unworthy-”

“Guilty,” Lena clarified.

“Feeling so guilty,” Kara amended. “You’re not going to lose me. Not now, not ever. Do you know how many people have wanted me? I chose you. I sided with you over my own sister and I’ve never regretted it. Even when we were on opposite sides I still chose you! That’s not going to change now.”

Seemingly slightly mollified, Lena leaned forward and draped herself over Kara in an all-encompassing embrace. “I really hope so.”

“I know so,” Kara countered. “That is the truth.” She smiled, gesturing to the door. “Now come on. I want to show you my world.”

\

They touched down right next to the ship, Kara carrying Lena bridal style. The villain had protested, being perfectly capable of flight herself, yet Supergirl had ignored her. After their last discussion, Kara thought that her girlfriend was due for a little pampering.

In the wide-open space outside National City, no one had yet chanced upon the Kryptonian craft. The only other two individuals within sight were Alura and Selena, both standing right next to the ship’s ramp. Kara’s heart did a familiar leap at the still shocking visage of her mother standing alive and healthy.

“Ready to go?” Alura asked as Lena dismounted from Kara’s arms.

The hero nodded eagerly. Lena, however, took out her cell phone. “I need to make a few last minute arrangements,” she said. “I’m leaving my planet for a week, after all.”

Selena scowled impatiently, but Alura shrugged. “Take all of the time you need,” she said.

“Hurry up, dear!” Kara said, bouncing on the balls of her feet. At the obvious sign of enthusiasm, Alura stepped closer and wrapped an arm around her daughter’s shoulders.

“Kara, I know you’re excited, but things might not be exactly as you expect,” the High Councilor warned.

The hero frowned. “What do you mean?”

Alura let loose a despondent sigh. “Argo is…well, it’s damaged. The war with Darkseid took its toll. Don’t expect to see a shining beacon of Kryptonian culture. Krypton is not gone, not while we still draw breath, but returning our people to their former glory isn’t going to be easy.”

Kara dipped her head in agreement. She knew this, of course. But with her peoples’ endurance and Lena’s brainpower, nothing was impossible.

Suddenly, Alura dropped her arm from Kara’s shoulder. “Do you hear something?” she questioned.

Kara cast out her superhearing. “No,” she replied. “Wait…yes! I hear something.” It sounded like it was coming from all sides…a familiar humming. It seemed to echo around them in a circle, growing ever closer. “Lena, are those your drones?”

The CEO looked up from her cellphone. “Did you know I designed Kara’s suit?” she asked the group conversationally. “The one she’s wearing right now? It shields her from ninety percent of the radiation emitted by Kryptonite.”

Supergirl narrowed her eyes. “Lena, what is-”

She broke off, her mouth gaping. Kara could see them now. Swarms of L-Corp drones coming over the horizon from every direction. And that wasn’t all. Supergirl could see glimpses of her fellow heroes amongst the horde….a red blur across the ground, the green trail of energy emitted by Starfire.

It took seconds for the horde to close in around them, stopping only a few hundred feet away. As Selena and Alura stared on uncertainly, Kara spotted Alex in her supersuit. Her sister was flying at the head of a group of drones, a glum frown on her lips.

Kara whipped her head around as a familiar hiss accompanied the arrival of Lena’s nanosuit. A second later, Vanity was flying into the air. She stopped to hover twenty feet above the Kryptonians, staring directly at-

“Alura Zor-El,” the villain’s voice intoned. “For sending the Worldkillers to Earth, ordering the death of Maggie Sawyer, and infecting your daughter with red kryptonite…you are under arrest.”

Conduit

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Lena, what the hell is all this?” Kara demanded. Her mind was whirling as even her enhanced vision struggled to take in the sea of drones and superheroes surrounding them. “You know my mother didn’t do any of that! It’s insane!”

“It’s absurd.” Alura stepped forward purposefully. “I have been on Argo since my world was destroyed. How could I have orchestrated any deaths on Earth?” she demanded. “And what, exactly, would I have to gain by antagonizing the planet I chose for my daughter?”

Vanity was still hovering above them. Even with her face covered, Kara could feel her girlfriend eyeing them coldly. Unable to take it any longer, Supergirl floated up to the supervillain and gently grabbed her arms.

“I don’t know what’s gotten into you, but my mother would never have done those things.”

Selena rose into the air. “What is the meaning of this? You invite us to your world, you propose an alliance, and then you seek to imprison us? How dare you!” she seethed. “Perhaps you plan to simply execute us. If you are the best humanity has to offer, then Argo is better without you.”

“No!” Kara exclaimed. She turned back to her girlfriend. As heartbroken as she was at the accusation…as much as it defied understanding…she knew Lena had her reasons.

Lena wasn’t evil. Lena was simply wrong. Kara could live with that. What she could not, would not ever accept was hearing that one of her loved ones was a murderer. Neither her fiancé nor her mother.

Vanity shook her head, staying close to Kara. “You sent the Worldkillers,” she said, her gaze fixed on Alura. “Darkseid isn’t following you; he never was. All he’s ever been is a smokescreen for your true intentions. A distraction from the beginning.”

“Darkseid nearly destroyed our world!” Alura retorted. She was floating now, but made no move to drift from her position. “Argo was all but crushed under his heel! If you had visited Argo yourself, you would have seen the devastation he left behind.”

“Devastation has more than one possible source.” Lena turned to Kara, her body language mournful yet firm. “For so long, I was wondering why Reign told us that she served Darkseid. The Worldkillers have proven cunning opponents, haven’t they? Why would they give the game away? It served no purpose. I’ve suspected it was a ruse for a long time. When Alura repeated it…that’s when I knew.”

Kara’s gaze shifted back to the horde surrounding them. Alex was still flying at the head of a drone squadron. Upon meeting her sister’s gaze, the new hero frowned regretfully. Yet the fact that Alex didn’t look away told Supergirl all she needed to know.

Lena told all of this to Alex beforehand. And Alex was convinced.  

“So Darkseid made a strange move,” Kara spoke to her fiancé. It was a struggle to keep her voice rational, rather than pleading. Pleading and emotion would work on Lena, her girlfriend. Only rationality would get through to the self-proclaimed overlord of the Earth. “That doesn’t prove my mom is evil!”

“A strange move?’ Lena demanded. “Darkseid is an alien conqueror who has crushed countless worlds. He wouldn’t show his hand without a purpose.” She turned to Alura. “What did you tell us…that Darkseid attacked you without warning? Odd that he was far more polite with Earth, isn’t it?” the villain demanded haughtily.

Kara watched as her mother’s fists clenched in exasperation. “Darkseid probably guessed we were coming here. He knew we would warn you.”

“Then why confirm to us that he had intentions for Earth?” Lena demanded without skipping a beat. “That would make us open up to you instantly, uniting two hostile forces who could pose a threat to his armies.”

Supergirl placed a hand on Vanity’s shoulder. “Okay, so it was a strange move we don’t understand. You don’t…that’s not enough to accuse my mother of being a killer.”

“No,” Lena agreed. “But the coincidences are piling up, aren’t they? We’ve known for a long time that the Worldkillers won’t harm you. They won’t even harm your loved ones…besides me. Reign could have killed Alex. Purity herself told Jess that she’d been added to, and I quote, the list.”

Ridiculous. “Darkseid wants me! Remember what we talked about! He could dissect me, or try to clone me, or…”

Wait a minute…  

“Why? He has all of Argo to choose from. What could he possibly need you for so badly?” Lena stated, giving voice to Kara’s thoughts. “And why would that entail sparing your friends? Don’t you see, Kara…it never made any sense! Not unless the real master of the Worldkillers loves you. And while you would never join a conqueror from Apokolips, perhaps you would side with your own people if those you loved were treated gently…”

Kara started to float down to her mother, to help Alura explain why she couldn’t possibly be behind any of this. Then a fierce grip took her by the arm, suspending her movement. “Kara, stay close to me.”

Alura stared up at them incredulously. “My daughter is in love with you!” she pointed out. “If the Worldkillers were trying to win her over to their side, why target you?”

“Because I’m too much of a threat,” Lena responded. “You knew that from the beginning. That’s why you did everything in your power to keep me and Kara apart. Yes, you wanted to prevent me from having Supergirl on my side…that would help me gain control of Earth and prepare for an invasion. But there was more to it, wasn’t there? Kara wouldn’t forgive you for killing one of her friends, and yet I needed to die. So you had Maggie Sawyer killed and pinned the blame on me, infected Kara with RedK to try and drive us apart.”

“My daughter is the most loving person I’ve ever met,” the High Councilor responded. “If you knew her half as well as I did, you would know she would never support an invasion of Earth.”

Kara didn’t miss Lena’s arm wrapping around her shoulder possessively. “I know that, but I don’t think you do. You thought that her attachments to her people and their legacy could win her over, especially if you could convince her it was ultimately in Earth’s best interests to be conquered.” The supervillain paused. “Outing her identity to the world and turning the human race against her would only improve your chances, wouldn’t it?”

A chill traveled down the hero’s spine. Kara Danvers was her connection to the human race. It had been her way of pretending to be human. Wouldn’t a hostile alien force try to take that away from her, if given the opportunity?

Not my mother.

“Lena, some of this makes sense, but it can’t be my mother!” Kara protested. “It must be someone else. Anyone else.” Her eyes roamed over to Selena.

Vanity took a deep breath. “It’s simple deduction. As soon as your mother told me Darkseid had attacked her, I knew. We know the mole in L-Corp leaked your identity to the world. They did it when we were most vulnerable, raiding the DEO and out of contact. And that mole is working with the Worldkillers, as Reign proved when she murdered that Martian right in front of us.”

“You could have more than one spy, you know!” Kara protested. Even as she spoke, her mind was whirling. If there was only one mole, that mole would also have been the one who covered up Maggie’s death. Which lined up with what Lena was saying…

“Lillian made the same point,” Lena replied. “Yet the pattern can’t be ignored. All of those leaks required the same level of security clearance, and they all fit the goal of driving you to side with Argo against me.”

Her vision flicked rapidly between Lena and her mother. There were dozens of eyes watching them, heroes and L-Corp agents from across the planet. Yet Kara, Alura, and Lena were the only three people in the world.

“The mole works with the Worldkillers. The Worldkillers lied to us about Darkseid; he doesn’t fit with their goals or their actions,” Lena intoned. “And your mother repeated that lie.”

Tears were dripping down the hero’s face now. “Lena, I understand what you’re saying, I do, but you’re wrong. My mother wouldn’t…she couldn’t. There has to be another explanation.” Kara was pleading now. “I know how smart you are, but don’t jump to conclusions again! Please, let her explain. Let’s sit down and talk about this!”

“We are talking about this,” her fiancé replied.

Selena growled. “Talking? You have done nothing but throw accusations at us…the very people who welcomed you to our last city with open arms.”

“Yes you did,” Lena agreed. “The exact thing you would do if I was right. Kara and I would be helpless at Argo; you would capture us effortlessly. I would be out of the way, and your daughter would be safe and isolated from the conquest to come,” she continued, turning back to Alura.

The High Councilor glared at her. “You are raving. Kara, come down here. Please.”

“Don’t!” Lena commanded. “Think, Kara. Winn goes missing right as Argo approaches! We can’t find him anywhere on Earth…why? Because he’s on Argo!”

“So are hundreds of people!” Kara protested.

Lena groaned in frustration. “Yet Alura is their High Councilor. You heard her say herself that Argo has sensors. She would have seen Winn being taken there! And why would he be captured in the first place? Only because of you! Alura wanted to know how to win you over, and so she took your most vulnerable friend to tell her how to do it!”

Kara’s mind flashed back to that terrible day. Jess had told the story in excruciating detail. Purity had been reluctant to harm either of them, and she’d outright admitted needing information. What information could Winn have possibly had worthwhile to a conqueror like Darkseid? The Worldkillers already had a mole within L-Corp.

“I would never betray you, Kara!” Alura swore. “I sent you to Earth because I loved you! I lead our people, yes, but my family is more important to me than anything!”

Kara wanted to believe it. She did believe it. All she wanted was for her mother to give her enough of a reason to convince her mind to do so.

A strange sense of satisfaction emanated from Lena. Supergirl drifted in midair, unsure of where to go, but the villain’s grip kept her firmly in place. “If that’s true, then answer one question,” Lena prompted.

The ground underneath the High Councilor’s feet cracked under the force of her rage. “My family is my life. You dare suggest otherwise, Lena Luthor? You who knows nothing of family? I gave up everything to save the House of El!”

Kara could feel her girlfriend smirk with victory. The sensation hit the hero like a blow to the stomach. “Then why didn’t you ask us about Kal-El?” the CEO demanded.

For the briefest moment, a flash of concern sprouted underneath Alura’s indignation. Then it was immediately replaced by bemused skepticism. “I did. This very morning, remember?”

“During our second conversation. Not our first. When we spoke for the first time, you said nothing about Kal-El to either Kara or me. Strange from a woman who claims to put family above anything,” Lena intoned viciously. “You sent Kara here with a mission to protect her cousin, didn’t you? It stands to reason you would ask one of us about him immediately. Unless, of course, you had agents on Earth who already confirmed he was dead.”

Alura stared up at the villain, her eyes unblinking. “I had just seen my daughter for the first time in decades. I’m sorry if she was the only thing on my mind.”

That made so much sense to Kara that relief sprouted within her chest. The brief sensation only made Lena’s next sentence sound that much harsher. “Yet you had enough time to talk all about Darkseid and our plans. Why didn’t you ask where your nephew fit into all of this?”

“You brought up Darkseid!” Alura pointed out.

Vanity nodded. “I did. I lured you into a trap to prove my suspicions. You see, I wanted to be wrong. Your appearance answered so many questions in my mind, but I knew what that would mean for Kara. I gave you a chance to deviate from what I expected, and you failed. You love your daughter, Alura. I know that…it’s what made all of the irregularities from the past year finally make sense. Yet you betrayed her and everything she stood for. Even now, you’re planning on using her love for you and her people to turn her against the world she now calls home.”

Even as Kara still knew that her mother would never do any such thing, a fierce and foreign anger erupted in her mind. Alura wasn’t guilty. So why was Kara so mad?

“You are despicable,” the High Councilor hissed.

“That’s how I felt.” Lena nodded. “So I gave you another chance to prove me wrong. You tried to make up for your mistake by asking us about Kal-El this morning, remember? In response, I told you that my brother killed Clark. Clark, not Kal-El. I didn’t tell you they were the same person. Kara didn’t tell you that either. You claim to have had no contact with Earth beyond your conversations with us. How did you know that they were one and the same, Alura?”

The question hit Kara like a tidal wave. Even as her brain desperately wracked for a solution, the hero realized that the answer didn’t exist. No. No! Lena can’t be right. My mom would never have done those things.  

Yet Kara had just been given irrefutable proof that Alura was, in fact, lying.

Silence hung in the air for several seconds. Despite the hundreds of drones surrounding them in a sea of battle, the only noise the hero could hear was the turmoil in her own mind. Why? How was this happening?! She stared at her mother, desperate for solace, but received none.

BZZT! Twin crimson beams erupted from Alura’s eyes. Kara could feel the heat emanating from them, yet this wasn’t heat vision. The two trails of energy sliced through the air at a thousand angles, moving impossibly fast. They separated, one slamming into Selena, the other hitting the ship. Both vanished instantly.

“Attack!” Vanity roared. But Alura had already fired again. Two more trails of energy split into the air…one heading directly for them! Lena reflexively teleported away, pushing Kara to safety as she did so. Yet the beam seemed locked onto Kara, even as the other was rounding on Alura herself…

The world went white.

\

She was lying in the snow. Rapidly blinking her eyes, Kara climbed to her feet just as Alura materialized into existence next to her. Selena and the Argonian ship were both waiting nearby, standing calmly in the middle of a seemingly endless expanse of snow.

Above them, the clear sky had given way to night. Countless stars shown from above, reflecting on the icy ground beneath them.

“Where the hell are we?” Kara demanded, backing away quickly.

Alura looked at her sadly. “I’ve brought us to the frozen landmass at the southern end of the Earth. It was the first place I could think of far enough away from Luthor’s forces that would give us a chance to talk.”

Her mother had just teleported them across the planet, yet there was only one thing on Kara’s mind. “Lena was right…about everything.” Her voice broke as Alura made no attempt to refute the claim. “How could you?”

“Our people are trapped on a desolate rock running dry of resources. Hundreds of us remain. Billions more are in hypersleep, unable to be woken until we find a world capable of housing us,” Alura stated. “There is a reason I sent you to Earth. It’s the perfect candidate."

Kara’s entire body was shaking. She glanced at the ground, hoping it would swallow her up and take her out of this nightmare. “You killed people!”

“And I would again,” Alura replied. “I take no joy in what I have to do, but our people need a home. It is my responsibility to care for them, no matter what the cost!”

Supergirl felt her knees shaking. “All of this. Why? Lena would have helped you! Whatever you’re planning to do…invade the Earth or whatever…you don’t need to!”

“There are billions of us, Kara. Humanity would never open their arms to us, and I wouldn’t expect them to. Do you really think, even with Luthor’s brilliance, this planet could support an additional three billion souls who each eat enough for ten humans? Do you think the human race would provide for and welcome a force of aliens with godlike abilities? One,” she nodded at Kara, “Is welcomed and celebrated. Three billion more would not receive the same treatment.”

Selena coughed. “Alura, Luthor can track her. We don’t have much time.”

“I know,” the High Councilor replied.”

Three billion in hypersleep? “No, it wouldn’t be easy,” Kara agreed. “It might take years or even decades to bring them all out safely. That doesn’t give you…you have no right to take away the home of an entire race.”

Alura sighed. “I know,” she said sadly. “But it is still what I must do. Humans have been waging wars of conquest for thousands of years. Why? Because they are loyal to their own nations and their own people. I’m the same, and I intend to be as merciful as possible. No one else needs to die.”

Kara gritted her teeth. “You say Earth won’t welcome you, and you somehow think you can take it over without hurting anyone? How?”

“You will see soon enough. Kara, I am genuinely, truly sorry for what I’ve done. The Worldkillers were engineered to feel no pity…I don’t have that luxury,” her mother said. “Lena Luthor doesn’t deserve death, and yet she must be taken down.”

Fresh rage flooded through the hero’s veins as she thought of the attempts on her lover’s life. All of them, this entire time. It was…?! “I’m never going to help you,” Kara hissed. “Surrender and negotiate with Lena. Please.”

“Our people need you, Kara. I need you,” Alura begged. “I don’t begrudge your love for Earth, but your first duty is to our people. They will die without this world. Earth is the only suitable planet within our range.”

“Lena can give you Harun-el!”

“It is not enough,” Alura answered. “We need to awaken our people and have an army powered by a yellow sun. Darkseid nearly destroyed us. Galactic civilization has collapsed, and soon it will only be the conquered and the conquerors. Can you imagine what a billion fully powered Kryptonians could do for this galaxy?” the High Councilor demanded. “We could defend ourselves and protect a thousand systems like Earth. If the loyalty to your people isn’t enough, think about the greater good! The universe needs us, and we need a planet.”

This was the woman who raised her. The woman who had kissed her forehead at night and made Kara believe that everything would be okay. Her mother who had swaddled her in a red blanket and waved goodbye as her pod was sent hurtling away from Krypton.

Kara’s eyes narrowed. “Darkseid was a lie.”

“Not entirely. Darkseid did attack Argo. It took nearly all of our strength, and the assistance of a remaining Green Lantern, to defeat him and his forces,” her mother claimed. “We won, Kara. Darkseid was the master of the Omega Effect, and it wrought havoc on our forces. Such a primal energy cannot be destroyed simply because its host perishes. When Darkseid’s neck was snapped, that energy found its way to the closest living being.”

“You!” That’s how Alura had transported them! “Just like Alex took Pestilence’s powers…you took Darkseid’s!” Supergirl’s mind flashed back to their confrontation with Purity months prior. ‘We have seen abilities transfer before,’ the Worldkiller had said. ‘Energy always outlives its conduit.’

Alura nodded. “I’m more powerful than I could have ever dreamed. Yet I cannot protect our people alone. We need a world…and I need you. Please.”

“There’s no time,” Selena said quickly. “They’re coming!”

The High Councilor frowned. “Then I don’t have a choice,” she said.

One moment, Alura was standing several feet away. A millisecond later, she was looming behind Kara and seizing her in a chokehold. How? Even Reign couldn’t…Supergirl struggled desperately, shoving her elbow into her mother’s stomach. The High Councilor gasped with pain, but her grip didn’t weaken.

Kara clawed at her mother’s arms, barely managing to budge them. Dark spots began to dance at the edges of her eyes, and part of the hero welcomed the oncoming relief from the waking nightmare that her day had become.

“I love you, Kara.”

Her vision went black.

\

Luthor’s fastest agents were approaching. They had less than a minute to be on their way back to Argo. Alura hurried up the ship’s ramp, holding Kara in her arms. She placed her daughter in one of the seats, tilting her head against the wall so that Kara wouldn’t strain her neck.

“Let us go.”

Selena nodded, dropping into the pilot’s ship. Her hands moved across the controls, eager to put the ship in the air and begin their journey back to Argo.

Nothing happened.

Luthor!  

“She had someone disable our engines when we are at L-Corp.” Alura’s mind moved faster than Selena’s fingers. She herself could leave, but Selena and Kara would never survive the journey to Argo. The Omega Effect sustained her lifeforce, but it would do nothing for her companions.

“Go,” Selena said simply.

Alura stared at her lover. “They’re closing in from all directions. You’ll never escape.”

Selena shrugged. “Then I’ll surrender. They won’t hurt me. You know how soft Luthor is.” She placed a hand on Alura’s cheek. “We both know this was a mission of convenience, not necessity. Once you’ve crushed her forces, you’ll have me back. Both of us.” She nodded at Kara.

And now this planet has even more time to poison her mine. Alura resisted the urge to swear. The only option was killing her daughter outright. Better for her to hate me than for her to die.

Her entire body glowing with crimson energy, the High Councilor shot up into the stars.

Chapter End Notes

Well that was fun. No chapter for ten days as I finish up the year of law school.

I'd encourage anyone curious to call up this entire story at once and Ctrl-F 'Alura'. Some things might be seen in a different light. :)

Silver Platter

Chapter Notes

I am back, with a law school diploma in hand! Now to study for the bar exam and finish this fic!

Lena stared at the bed. Kara was beginning to stir. The CEO’s feelings of relief immediately mixed with a wave of nausea. Physically, her girlfriend was fine. The light bruising around her neck had already faded. Her heartbeat was strong and stable; her other vitals exhibited no worrying signs.

Selena had surrendered without a fight, unable to escape and evidently forbidden from threatening Kara per Alura’s orders. She’d gleefully given Lena the details, knowing that the CEO would have them from Kara soon enough. And although the Kryptonian invader was now contained and being attended to, the situation was worse than Lena could have ever expected.

Defeating hundreds of Kryptonians in a straight fight was a hopeless endeavor. Lena had believed that capturing Alura might have been able to resolve the situation without bloodshed. With all of her forces arrayed to capture the invaders, Lena’s fears had been directed to the effect that her actions would have on Kara rather than the possibility that the plan could fail.

Then Alura had treated her to a firsthand demonstration of the power she now wielded…the power of Darkseid.

Lena swept her gaze around the infirmary, ignoring the slight trembling in her fingertips. All of her preparations, allies and technology…none of it had been able to stop the Omega Effect and its new wielder. The beams had teleported Alura away faster than L-Corp’s armies had been able to react.

Kara, I am so sorry. The pieces had clicked into place the very second that Lena had seen Alura on the telescreen. The CEO had known that her lover was facing emotional torment. Instead of preparing Kara for that pain, Lena had exploited her feelings to lure her opponent into a trap.

Lena Luthor, protector of the Earth and CEO of L-Corp, had done the right thing. Lena, fiancé of Kara Danvers, had committed an act so sickening that even thinking about it made the act of breathing painful.

“Was it a dream?” Kara’s voice echoed from the bed, small and hopeful.

Lena stared at the hero’s face, illuminated by the gentle light of the yellow sun lamps. “No,” she replied simply. It was woefully inadequate, but what else could she say?

There was a pause as countless emotions flashed across the hero’s eyes. Lena had been expecting tears, but it was words that emerged first. “How long did you know?”

“As soon as I saw Alura was alive,” Lena answered honestly, her eyes falling to the ground. “I lied to you so we could capture her. I…it was the right choice, and I would make it again. That doesn’t mean that I’m not…” she stopped herself. Losing Kara…hurting Kara, had been too high of a price to pay. Yet the CEO had been given no choice.

Lena nearly jumped out of her skin when Kara laid a comforting hand on her arm. “You had to. We could have stopped all of this by capturing her. It would have worked if it weren’t for-”

“The Omega Effect.” The CEO’s answer was toneless. This wasn’t right! She had known her girlfriend was about to experience incredible pain, and instead of preparing her for it Lena had chosen to exploit the situation. Kara couldn’t- shouldn’t – be forgiving her.

The RedK incident. Letting her be captured by Lillian. Lois’s death. Now this. Lena had hurt Kara so many times, and the hero welcomed her back with open arms each time Lena crawled forward and asked for forgiveness. Now she was doing it again, sending Lena’s relief and guilt into the stratosphere.

Don’t let her forgive you. You don’t deserve her. All you’ve ever done is cause her pain.

Lena couldn’t deny the words. Yet wouldn’t leaving Kara cause the hero even more pain? For whatever reason, Kara Zor-El had chosen to love her. Who was Lena to make Supergirl’s choices for her?

You’re rationalizing. You just want Kara. You’re selfish.

Fine, then Lena was selfish. For all of her strength, she was far too weak to push her lover away. If Kara decided to leave of her own accord, the supervillain wouldn’t stop her. Until that day came, Lena Luthor would bask in the light of Kara Zor-El.

“I don’t know what to do,” the CEO admitted. “I’m not sure if we can stop her.”

Supergirl smiled reassuringly. “Of course we can. We thought we were facing Darkseid, a galactic tyrant. This is my mother. All we have to do is convince her to back down and accept some kind of compromise.”

Oh Rao, she’s in denial. Lena bit her lip, struggling to think of a response. Someone had to tell the hero that Alura was, for all intents and purposes, just as dangerous as Darkseid. Logically, Lena knew that someone should be her. Yet the villain had already caused her girlfriend enough pain, and Lena found she didn’t have the strength to form the words.

Fortunately, that duty was claimed by someone else.

Alex slammed open the door to the infirmary. Not even acknowledging her sister’s recovery, the elder Danvers sister stormed to the side of the bed. “Alura is a killer,” Alex hissed. “She’s the one who ordered Maggie’s death, and she didn’t lose a second of sleep over it. We’re not going to talk her down…we’re going to bring her down.”

“I’m not defending it!” Kara protested. “She’s clearly willing to kill for what she thinks is right. Aren’t you? As I recall, you tried to kill Lena…and I forgave you for that.”

The logic was so faulty that Alex needed no help trying to rebut it. “I thought Lena was evil,” she said, slamming her fist down on the bedside table so hard that it burst into splinters. Kara flinched away, but her sister was unrelenting. “Maggie was clearly innocent, and your mom decided she should die. And what about that Martian? Remember him? He was literally in a coma when Reign vaporized him!”

Kara was shaking her head back and forth rapidly, as if slowly receding within herself. “Those were horrible things. I know that! Killing an innocent is never okay, no matter what the cost. But that doesn’t mean my mom is…”

“Isn’t what, Kara? Evil? That’s exactly what she is. If another villain had done those things, you wouldn’t be thinking they could be redeemed. You’re just willing to overlook murder because she’s your mother.” Alex crossed her arms, scowling down at the bed.

Passion flared in Kara’s eyes. “Yes, she’s my mother. That means I know her better than either of you! She’s done…unthinkable crimes. She’s desperate, but she’s not evil! On Krypton, jeju was always kind…to me and everyone else. Deep down, she’s a good person. I just have to remind her of that.”

Alex clenched her fists, but Lena held up a hand. Now she knew what to say- not that it made the words come any easier. “Lex was always good to me,” she spoke quietly. “He protected me from Lillian no matter the cost. Even when we were teenagers, he always put me first.”

Even now, Kara’s gaze shown with sympathy at the mention of Lena’s childhood. “What does that have to do with this?” the hero asked gently.

“Lex had good in him. I don’t think it ever fully died. It just wasn’t enough to stop him from becoming a monster. Alura does love you, Kara. That doesn’t mean she’s-”

Kara was shaking her head again. Lena recognized that pain all too well. When her beloved brother had murdered dozens of innocent people to bring down Superman, she’d refused to believe it. It had taken weeks and a national media trial for it to finally sink in. Giving up on him, even when he was dead, had been the hardest thing she’d ever done.

Would she have been able to, if he hadn’t died? Lena could imagine herself visiting him in prison, disgusted with his actions but unable to let him ago. How long would she have spent with him, trying to help him understand his mistakes and move towards redemption?

She leaned forward suddenly, taking her lover’s hands in her own. Lena would have given anything to remove Kara’s turmoil, but there was nothing she could do but sit down on the bed.

“Alura isn’t Lex. I’m sorry, Lena, but she isn’t.” Kara’s pleading gaze found her again. “She’s got billions of her people trapped in hypersleep and needs Earth to save them. We can make a deal. We have to.”

Alex was staring at her sister, a hint of betrayal on her features. Lena knew what she was thinking. When the inevitable conflict began, would Kara side with her mother and her own people?

No, never. Kara would never work with a murderer. She wouldn’t work with me until it was clear I would never cross that line. Her love for Alura might give her a massive blind spot, but it doesn’t mean she’ll turn on us.

Right?

 What if Alura convinced Kara that she was correct? The High Councilor could offer amnesty to all of Kara’s friends and family from whatever they had planned for the human race. Supergirl would never go along with any attempt to kill humans, but if Argo’s plans were more subtle in nature…

“Let me talk to her, Lena. Please. I can open negotiations.”

An idea suddenly sprouted in the CEO’s mind. It was brilliant, perfect, and thus could not be ignored. It also filled Lena with enough rage and despair to bring tears to her eyes.

I can’t use her again. Not now!

What choice did she have? They were outgunned by an invading alien army. Their enemy had one weakness, and she was currently lying in L-Corp’s infirmary. If Lena didn’t take every advantage at her disposal, the human race didn’t stand a chance.

“Lena?” Alex prompted.

The supervillain returned to herself. Without realizing it, she’d hopped off the bed and started pacing around the room. Her eyes rapidly flitted between the Danvers sister. The way forward was clear, but the risk…

She actually dropped her knees and started weeping. “I…I know what we have to do.”

Kara moved to get up off the bed, but Alex’s hand stopped the concerned superhero from rising. “What is it?” she demanded. Her entire body seemed to tense from the desire for revenge.

“We…need intelligence.” Lena climbed to her feet, wiping the moisture from her eyes. “Argo will detect any craft we send in. I need one of our ships to drop off an agent without Alura or any of the others realizing what we’re up to.”

Alex scoffed. “So you want to pretend we were just saying hi?”

“Yes.” Lena answered, suppressing a wince. “If…” she looked at her fiancé, trying to convey all of her pain. “If Kara goes in the ship and says she took it without permission, claiming that she wanted to talk to Alura and make peace, someone else might be able to slip in undetected and do some snooping.”

Kara brightened even as Alex’s nostril flared. “You want to use my little sister as bait?”

The CEO opened her mouth to respond before shutting it again. Yes. That was exactly what she was doing. Fortunately for Lena’s selfish side, Kara didn’t seem to see it that way.

“That works! I can talk my mother out of this. Or at least, I can begin the process. Meanwhile, someone else can slip around and see what’s going on with Argo. That could give us some leverage in negotiations,” Kara replied hopefully.

“Or in a war,” Alex muttered loud enough for all of them to hear. “Kara, if you don’t convince her, which you won’t, you’ll be captured. Alura might not be willing to hurt you, but she’ll definitely lock you up and keep you away from us.” The new superhero turned to Lena. “We just stopped Alura from taking her. Now you want to offer Kara up on a silver platter?”

National City’s skyline beckoned her gaze through the window, but Lena forced herself to stare at the sisters. “I can give Kara a short-range teleportation device that could help her get back to the ship. It’s not a guarantee, though. In fact, I estimate your chances of escape at less than fifty percent.” Now she was the one shaking her head. “No. I won’t do it. Earth can’t lose you. K-kara. I can’t-” she broke off, her lip trembling.

“I don’t like it either. I can’t lose you.” Kara was smiling at brightly, as if the CEO had just cured cancer and just planned their dream wedding. “But Winn is probably on Argo. Whoever you send with me might be able to save him. If there’s a chance for him, we have to take it.”

Her head felt like it was splitting open. Part of Lena cursed Winn for making it impossible for Kara to stay away from Argo. In fact, Supergirl would probably fight her way to the hanger and go alone if Lena refused. The other half of Lena could have kissed him in gratitude for forcing the issue and absolving the supervillain of her guilt.

Ha! As if she could ever be absolved. Lena looked again at her girlfriend, unsurprised to see that Kara’s face was still hopeful. It was the hero’s trusting nature that had opened the door to their relationship, even as they’d stood on opposite sides of the law. Lena would never forget the night that Supergirl had handed her a box of kryptonite, the hated substance seemingly designed to give Kara a painful death, just to prove her faith in the supervillain.

Would that same faith now cost her Kara forever?

\

Kara stared at the small ship in front of them. In hindsight, she should have known that her brilliant girlfriend would have such a craft at her disposal. If Lena hated anything, it was being unprepared.

That was why they were standing in the middle of a secret hanger underneath the Mojave Desert. Lena had been adamant that no one on Earth be informed of their mission; the risk was simply too great. Kara had been forbidden from even telling James about the effort to rescue her friend. As far as the rest of L-Corp was concerned, Supergirl was recovering steadily in a private facility as her sister watched over her. The story wouldn’t hold up longer than a week, but it didn’t need to.

“I should be going,” Lena was muttering as she finalized preparations on their craft.

Deep down, they all knew that she couldn’t. If Lena was captured, her efforts to prepare the Earth might crumble overnight. Worse, there was every indication that Alura simply wanted her dead. The notion made Kara feel physically ill.

No. She forced the thought away. Her mother had committed crimes that Kara might never forgive, crimes that the hero couldn’t even bear thinking about. That was why Kara had to go to Argo. Alura had to be talked down before she went too far. Even with all of the deception that had been whirling around her, Kara had seen that her mother loved her just as much as she did the day that their planet had exploded.

Alura could be reached…as long as it was Kara making the effort.

She glanced uneasily at her sister. Ever since Alura’s escape, Alex’s eyes had been hard and resolute. It was a look nearly identical to the one she had sported months prior, when she’d been convinced that Lena Luthor had murdered Maggie Sawyer and was targeting Supergirl. Now that Alex had found the real culprit, even Kara knew better than to try and calm her down.

It was hard to blame Alex for her anger. Kara didn’t begrudge her for wanting a reckoning with Alura. Even after she talked her mother down, it was a bridge that they would have to cross eventually. And Rao, she was not looking forward to it.

There were no easy answers.

Well, except for one. Alex had been an easy choice for the mission. Alura had already shown that she was unwilling to harm Kara’s sister, so the risk was capture rather than death. In addition to being fully trustworthy, Alex’s powers would enable her to escape pursuit even by regular Kryptonians herself. Alura was probably an exception, but it was Kara’s job to keep her distracted.

Alex’s hair color and style had been considerably altered in preparation. It was unlikely anyone on Argo besides Alura would recognize Alex Danvers on sight, but Lena was taking no chances. So instead of one blond entering the craft, there would be two.

Now finished with the ship, Lena was busy fussing over Kara’s suit. “Alura will let you approach,” the CEO said as she smoothed out her girlfriend’s sleeves. “Upon your approach to the city, agree on a spot to meet up with Alex. Then announce and surrender yourself while she slips away. Alex, you know what to do.”

“Find us a getaway craft, look for Winn, and seek out any intel that could help us.”

Lena nodded, clearly trying to hide her distress. “You shouldn’t have any trouble moving around; everyone awake on Argo should be a trusted agent. Review your cover identity on the way there.”

“Assuming no one on Argo realizes they’ve never seen me before,” the elder Danvers replied.

“It’s a risk,” the CEO agreed. “Keep your distance as much as possible. Don’t fight anyone unless you have absolutely no choice.” She paused, grimacing. “If you’re caught and facing insurmountable odds, surrender. Better caught than dead.”

Kara could see the pain on her lover’s face. There were too many unknowns with this mission. Far too many. Yet it was their only chance to get a real idea of what they were facing and try to find a weakness in their opponents. Unless Kara succeeded.

“I’ll convince my mother. I promise,” the hero swore.

As the ship’s engines began to fire up, Lena hesitantly bit her lip. “Try. But if it becomes clear you can’t, use your teleporter. It’s not as sophisticated or powerful as the one in my suit; it simply transfers you a short distance away. Alex has one too. They’re one-use only, but no one on Argo should be expecting it.”

“Got it.” Kara smiled.

Lena leaned forward, placing her hands on Supergirl’s face. “Do whatever you have to do to come back. I don’t care what it costs. You need to come back. To me.”

Kara closed her eyes, leaning forward and brushing her forehead against Lena’s own. “I will.” Her eyelids peeked open, revealing her girlfriend. Even when terrified and distraught, Lena was beautiful. Kara’s heart fluttered, redoubling her determination to return home.

Home. Krypton would always be her home. Now, Earth was as well. Kara would do anything to bring them together. She remembered her journey through Lena’s Black Mercy fantasy, how it had felt to see her two planets living in harmony.

Supergirl would make that a reality.

Suicide Mission

“Lena?! Lena help!”

The four-year-old ran to the water’s edge. Nothing was visible beneath the rippling surface of the lake. Somehow, Lena knew that her mother was beneath the water, drowning.

They were in a populated area. All Lena had to do was scream and help would arrive. There was still time! She opened her mouth to yell, but her body was frozen. The child struggled against the force restraining her limbs, visualizing her mother gasping for air. Her muscles wouldn’t budge.

You can’t help her. A sinister voice whispered in her mind. For the good of humanity, you have to let her go. You don’t want to be selfish, do you?

That didn’t make sense! Why would letting her mom drown help anyone? Then the struggling body briefly broke through the water’s surface. All Lena needed to see was the sheen of blond hair to realize the truth.

It wasn’t her mother who was drowning. It was Kara. Lena remembered now. She had pushed her wife into the water as a sacrifice, but it wasn’t too late to save her. All the CEO had to do was reach out her arm and the hero would be saved.

And Earth would die.

Kara’s lips rose above the water. She was treading water desperately, but it was clear it was a losing battle. “D-don’t let her take me!” the hero coughed loudly, water already seeping into her lungs. “Find another way!”

Now in control of her body, Lena leaned forward. Instantly, her mind was alight with visions. Vast sections of the Earth scorched by wildfires. Kryptonian hordes herding civilians into work camps. Sam and Ruby lying on the street, dismissed as useless and left for dead.

“I can’t!”

Kara sank beneath the water again. Her last conscious action was to stare at the CEO waiting on the shore. Even dimmed by her approaching suffocation, the superhero’s eyes blazed with betrayal…

NO!

\

Lena awoke with a start, swiftly raising her forehead from the edge of her desk. She’d been painstakingly updating her designs for the past two days, both to distract herself and out of sheer desperation for the threat they faced. Her groggy eyes stared at her computer screen, halfway through reading one of Pamela’s vital progress reports.

Unfortunately, Harun-el did not eliminate a person’s need to sleep. It had been inevitable that she would eventually find herself here. Caffeine could only do so much.

“Cruel,” she whispered to herself. It didn’t take a genius to figure out why that dream had appeared, although Lena had to hand it to her subconscious. Combining her remorse over her mother’s death with her guilt of sending Kara away had been a ruthlessly inventive touch.

And just like in the dream, Lena still had the chance to save her fiancé. Kara and Alex couldn’t be on Argo yet. All she would have to do is remotely activate the ship’s systems and redirect the craft back to Earth. Her eyes had constantly been drifting over to her bracelet, knowing it would take but a thought to bring Kara back to safety.

It was a mission that had to be done. Only Kara gave Alex a chance of infiltrating Argo. Of course, it was probable that both would be captured. Lena estimated they had only a 23.6 percent chance of both returning to Earth safely. They had every tool they needed to succeed…the villain had even provided them with a means of escape. Working off the ship left behind by Alura, Lena had designed a program that would give her remote control of any of Argo’s ships. All Alex had to do was install it in a cockpit, and the stolen vessel would be on its way to Earth.

There were just too many unknowns. Would one of Argo’s denizens realize that Alex wasn’t one of them, despite the forged uniform Lena had given her? Would she even be able to slip out of the ship successfully? Was it really possible for her to interrogate one of Argo’s citizens without being caught? Alura might even realize the trap at the outset.

It was necessary. Launching this mission was the only way to obscure Lena’s real plan for obtaining information to Argo. The cost was too high for Lena to pay, but it wass a fair trade for the safety of Earth. That was why her fiancé’s ship continued through space, into Alura’s awaiting clutches.

Her attempts to abate her guilt were pathetic rationalizations. Yes, Kara had agreed to the mission enthusiastically, but she was operating under false pretenses. This wasn’t Lena’s fault; nothing but Alura herself would be able to prove to Kara that her mother was irredeemable. It was very possible that Kara would have gone to Argo regardless, whether or not Lena had given her permission.

Of course, I could always have confined her here on Earth. It would have infuriated Kara to no end, but it would have at least kept the superhero out of the hands of the enemy.

The only upside to Kara’s potential capture was that the hero would be out of the way of the coming blitzkrieg headed to Earth. Supergirl was certainly one of L-Corp’s most powerful assets, but it was doubtful she alone could make a difference against hundreds of her people. Alura, at least, would keep her daughter safe and comfortable.

Lena’s gaze drifted to the skyline of National City, a metropolis that, for all intents and purposes, she owned. I have so much power. Possibly more than any human who has ever lived. And the only way I can keep the love of my life safe is to let her be captured by an alien invasion.

Her finger glided over the top of her bracelet, itching to recall the ship. Once again, Lena resisted the urge.

\

“Rao.”

Even through the pale shimmer emitted by its energy shield, it was clear that the city of Argo had been all but destroyed. Buildings that had once stretched hundreds of meters into the air now lay in pieces across the landscape. At its prime, the city had clearly stood tall and proud in an architectural style foreign to Alex’s mind. The ruins that remained, however, looked all too familiar.

The city was still powered by an electrical grid. Thin bolts of light ran through the structures that were still standing, casting a defiant glow on the rubble below. Yet even this displayed Argo’s inability to rebuild. Intermittent sparks flew from damaged power conductors scattered throughout the landscape, sending energy streaking across the domed sky.

She glanced at Kara’s horrified face.

“This is the enemy now,” Alex all but hissed. “Any weakness on their part is a good thing. The stronger they are, the more screwed the Earth is.”

Kara rose higher in her seat. “This is all that is left of my people! Most of them are innocent! Krypton didn’t deserve this. No one does!”

The elder sister resisted the urge to speak out. There was no sense in rehashing the same argument they’d been repeating for the last two days. Even though she acknowledged that Alura was a murderer, the hero was convinced that her mother could be talked down. All of the logic in the world had been unable to dissuade her.

It was a no-win situation for Alex. If, by some miracle, Kara convinced her mother to call off her plans, then Maggie’s killer would essentially be walking away scot-free. In the likely event that she failed, Earth would be facing an invasion.

Alex knew the landscape before her was a mirage. Much of Argo was in ruins, yes. But she could see dozens of dark shapes darting across the sky. The city was populated by fully powered Kryptonians, each as powerful as Supergirl herself. Could Earth stand against them, even with Lena Luthor at the helm?

Their desperate situation was one reason why Alex had agreed to this mission. It wasn’t suicidal, as Alura probably wouldn’t want to kill her, but it was almost doomed to failure nonetheless. Lena had another goal here; the look she’d shared with the CEO before their departure had all but confirmed as much. Alex couldn’t fathom what it was. Yet it was enough for Lena to sacrifice two of her best assets to capture, one of whom she was in love with.

Whatever it was, Alex hoped it was worth it.

Putting my faith in Lena Luthor. What has this world come to?

\

After they’d dropped out of FTL, it wasn’t long before they received a communication request from Argo. Alex slipped into the bathroom, out of sight, before Kara activated the comms.

Alura’s face instantly appeared on the video screen, filling the hero with equal amounts of warmth and regret. “Kara! I have to admit I was hoping you would be coming here.”

“Lena didn’t revoke my authorization in time. I stole a ship,” Kara replied. “Mom, I’m here to put an end to this. I don’t…I can’t even begin to understand some of the things you’ve done. But we can fix this! I’m not sure what you’re planning, but we can come to an agreement. Just hear me out.”

The words felt dirty. They were true enough, fueled by the genuine hope and despair that had cycled through Kara for the last two days. Yet to mask an underlying purpose using such authentic emotions felt…disgusting.

Then she remembered her mother’s crimes. Redeemable or otherwise, Alura had certainly forfeited any right to complete honestly. Not that it made the deception any more enjoyable.

The High Councilor sighed. “I would like nothing more, but it is simply impossible. The human race will survive, Kara, but Earth must be given to us. Come aboard Argo, see what’s become of our people, and you will understand.”

“And if I don’t, you’ll let me go?” Kara asked.

“I won’t lie to my daughter,” Alura swore. “It would be pointless anyway. We both know I cannot allow you to leave. You knew this even before you left Earth. I cannot let you fight in Luthor’s futile war against us.”

Supergirl nodded, appreciating the honesty. Yet the reminder of the attempts on her lover’s life brought a scowl to her face. “If you really care about me, you wouldn’t have tried to kill the woman I love.”

A pained look on her face, Alura bowed her head in acceptance. “I didn’t want to hurt you; Luthor is simply too much of a threat. Her survival could mean the deaths of dozens of our people. I didn’t know how close you had become with her…it happened so quickly.”

“That doesn’t matter!” Kara’s fists clenched. “Murder is never okay.”

“It’s not,” Alura agreed. “Sometimes it is simply the only option. Perhaps…with recent developments taken into account, Lena Luthor could be spared. I bear her no ill will. I’ve assumed she would fight against us to the end, but if you were able to convince her to work for the greater good…well, her intelligence would certainly prove useful.”

Greater good? “I will always be a Kryptonian, but I’m sworn to defend the innocent. There are billions of them on Earth,” Kara retorted.

“There are billions more on Argo, trapped in hypersleep,” Alura stated. “Please come and see for yourself. I promise, all of your questions will be answered.”

Kara stared into her mother’s face, still so warm and understanding despite all that had passed between them. It was with the thought of redeeming Alura in her mind that the hero nodded affirmatively, briefly forgetting about Alex’s presence in the back of the craft.

Alura smiled. “Then I’ll have the shields lowered. Come in.”

\

Stage one of the plan went surprisingly well. Alex slipped out of the back hatch of the ship as soon as Kara drove it through the shields. Then she was just a tiny dot in the sky, falling hundreds of feet before landing on the ground.

If she’d been unlucky, one of Argo’s closely would have been looking more closely. Most seemed to be consumed with their own tasks throughout the city. Those who were looking at the small ship in the distance were focused on the craft itself: their first visitor in years. Alex’s suit wasn’t as powerful as Lena’s, but the nanites did their job of cloaking her against the color of the sky.

The elder Danvers looked around. Argo was unlike any warzone she had ever seen. Humanity had been fortunate enough to avoid a major conflict since the Second World War, leaving mankind’s largest and most important cities free of devastation. Argo was that scenario realized. The crumbling streets looked like they’d been caught in the outskirts of an atomic blast. Fascinating alien architecture had been warped almost beyond all recognition, left to slowly corrode in the city’s artificial light.

Whatever. I’m not here to sightsee anyway.

\

The High Councilor’s Office was located in the tallest building still standing on Argo. The exterior was patched and decaying just like the rest of the city, but the interior had clearly seen repairs. She was even riding in a working elevator, no guards at her side.

What would have been the point? As far as Alura knew, there was no escape. The second Argo’s shield had closed behind her, Kara was a prisoner. She’d have been able to flee to anywhere in Argo she wanted, perhaps even hide for a few days, but returning to Earth was now all but a dream. Unless, of course, one happened to have a short range teleporter on their wrist. 

The doors opened.

“Kara!” Alura was sitting at her desk at the far end of the room. The wall behind her was nothing but a massive clear panel, giving the office’s occupants overwatch of the entire city. At one time, it would have been a magnificent view. Now they simply witnessed a landscape of rubble, punctuated with citizens flying across the city and the ever-intermittent sparks.

“Mother.” Supergirl walked in front of the desk, taking deep breaths. “You had Maggie Sawyer killed to turn me against Lena. Cadmus used red kryptonite on me because of you.” Any composure she’d planned to keep was rapidly falling away. “That Martian you killed…then you had my identity revealed to the world! Don’t deny it!”

Alura stood up, moving around the desk. “I won’t.”

Kara took a step back. “Why?”

“The High Councilor of Argo has one duty: to provide for her people. Alura Zor-El loves her daughter more than anything else,” the older woman said. “I refuse to give up on either one. All the pain you’re feeling right now…it’s all my fault. I sent you to Earth, and it turns out I didn’t have to! Lena Luthor had to die. The only way to avoid hurting you was to drive the two of you apart. I’m sorry about Maggie Sawyer’s death, but I don’t regret it. The same applies to the modified kryptonite.”

Supergirl felt like she needed to vomit. “It didn’t work. I love Lena.”

“I know,” Alura nodded sadly. “I’d forgotten just how kind of a person you were. I should have realized you would give her every chance. As for your identity, well, I knew that the people of Earth couldn’t hurt you. I wanted to show you they would turn against you, make you understand that you are a Kryptonian!”

“You sent me to Earth to protect it!”

Her mother frowned. “I did? When did I ever say that? I sent you and Kal to Earth because it was the best world for you. I told you that you could be whatever you wanted to be. I’m not surprised you became a hero and found people to love. If Krypton had been destroyed, it would have been the ideal outcome for you.” The High Councilor stared hard into her eyes. “Now we need you back. I need you back.”

“I want to come back!” Kara promised. “Finding out you were still alive, that Krypton was still alive, was the happiest day of my life! Why should I have to make a choice? Work together with Earth. Together, our worlds can make something new…better. Something we can all share.”

Alura placed a finger on her watch. Instantly, the view of the city disappeared. The wall-panel shifted to a view of a massive warehouse, lit by flickering bulbs as far as the eye could see. The room seemingly stretched into eternity, every centimeter aligned with…

“Pods,” Kara breathed.

“Three billion, twenty-seven million, four-hundred thousand, eight-hundred and fifty-one,” Alura supplied. “All of them have been asleep for over twenty years. We have to let them out!”

“Why Earth?” Kara demanded. “Why not somewhere else?”

The High Councilor sighed. “Do you think there’s a single planet in this universe capable of supporting us that hasn’t been claimed by advanced lifeforms already?” she demanded. “Earth is perfect for Kryptonians. That’s why I sent you there in the first place. It's located in a sector with yellow suns and complete with all of the resources and minerals we need to rebuild.”

“Then let them out! We can share the planet! All we have to do is play it carefully-”

“Look at us, Kara!” For the first time, there was audible frustration in her mother’s voice. “Argo is dying. Earth can’t hope to take on another three billion Kryptonians. Humanity would scorch the planet in their attempts to stop us from moving in, even if it was peaceful. Food, water, minerals…there simply aren’t enough for both of our people. Not unless all of humanity drastically cut back its resource consumption and gave us total control. No one, not even Lena Luthor, could ever make them do that willingly.”

Supergirl winced.

“I don’t blame them,” Alura continued. “Humanity serves its own interests. Krypton must do the same.” The image of the warehouse faded, bringing the ruins of Argo back into view.

“You can’t invade an entire planet!” Kara protested.

The hero watched in horror as her mother shook her head. “I can. I have to. My responsibility is to my people. Three billion of them are counting on me to find them a new world. I will. I’m not going to make them wait hundreds of years for the mere possibility that Earth might be able to support them all someday.”

“No,” the hero said rapidly. “No. We can find another way!”

“There is no other way. I’ve had twenty years to think about this. If there was another world to use, or a better way to make Earth cooperate, don’t you think I would have found it by now?”

“Jeju.” Kara stepped forward, taking her mother’s hands in her own. “I became a hero because I followed your example. You showed me how to do the right thing, to put others first always. I came here because I believed in you. I still do.”

There was not an ounce of hesitation in Alura’s voice as she replied. “I am doing the right thing. I’m alive today because thousands of years of Kryptonian civilization made it possible. It gave me a life, a family. I owe it my absolute loyalty, and so do you.”

No! “I protect the innocent, no matter where they’re from. I learned that on Krypton and Earth!”

The High Councilor laughed skeptically. “Earth? Kara, I know all about the planet’s history. For how many years have the nations and cultures of that planet been slaughtering one another? Ancient empires sacrificed armies simply for a few miles of land. Tribes slaughtered and enslaved one another for millennia. European nations used their technological advantage to dominate the planet.”

“Not anymore,” Kara retorted. “They’ve grown beyond that.”
