“Only because mutually assured destruction has made peace in their best interest. And that’s the key, Kara. I don’t blame them. It is natural to fight for one’s own people. Do you think a soldier in the Parthian Empire went to war against the Romans because he wanted to help foreign citizens?” Alura demanded. “Of course not! He had a duty to his nation, to make it as great as it could be. I am simply doing the same.”

A bright spark flashed across the sky, bringing more illumination to the High Councilor’s face. In it, Kara saw the gaze of a woman who would never be talked down.

“Mom, that doesn’t make it right!” Kara clutched the older woman in a pleading embrace. “We can be better! This…this is an entirely different scale. This is an entire world.” She was speaking quickly, throwing out any argument she can think of. “The cost is too high.”

Alura stepped backwards. “Leaving three billion of our people to rot in hypersleep is a cost too high.” Her face was both imploring and determined. “Do you think any nation on Earth would not invade their neighbor if it was the only way to save their own citizens? If it had the power to do it?”

“You can’t!” If morality didn’t work, maybe logic would. “You said it yourself, humanity would scorch the planet before giving up. Even if their missiles don’t work on you, they’ll irradiate the entire planet. Everyone loses!”

“That’s not an issue, Kara.”

The hero’s eyes narrowed. Was this really her mother? The warmth and affection wasn’t gone; it was all right there. But it was accompanied with the attitude of an unrepentant conqueror, unfamiliar and yet somehow not out of place.

This was almost worse than her mother dying. Did the Alura Zor-El Kara remembered, the paragon of virtue, ever exist at all? Or had Kara simply created her as a memory to sustain herself on a new planet?

Supergirl blinked away the years in her eyes. “Why not?” she demanded.

A brief glow shined in Alura’s eyes, and a flash of red sliced across the room. Kara’s bracelet, forged from enhanced nth metal, crumbled into ashes as it fell from her wrist.

Kara’s eyes widened as a pit of dread settled in her stomach. My teleporter. It’s gone.

“I’m sorry, Kara, but I can’t take the chance of any surprises popping up,” her mother stated simply. “Now that I know you’ll be remaining here, I can tell you everything you want to know.”

\

Phase two of the plan was also going surprisingly well. Clothed in a uniform modeled after what Alura and Selena had worn to Earth, she’d avoided detection by not flying too closely to any of Argo’s denizens. By the time she had approached one woman flying on her own, it had been on her terms.

With the element of surprise, her considerable training, and the powers of a Worldkiller at her command, it had been as quick as Alex could have hoped for. She’d caught her opponent in a sleeper hold, incapacitating her without suffering more than a few bruises to the rib cage. It had given her plenty of time to drag the Kryptonian to an abandoned building and activate her Sentinel suit.

“Let me go!” The Kryptonian thrashed underneath her grip, but Alex refused to budge. The gray streaks in her brown hair did nothing to reduce her captive’s vitality as she screamed. “Help! I’m being attacked!”

Alex shook her head. “No good. You see this blue shimmer around us?” Indeed, they were surrounded by a dome of thin energy on all sides. “It blocks out all sound. I know how well Kryptonians can hear.”

The Kryptonian tried to spit in her face, forcing Alex to lean to the side. “I don’t recognize you. What do you want?” she demanded.

Alex placed a hand over her enemy’s throat, pinning her closer to the ground. “I want you to tell me what Argo has planned for Earth. Or, at least, direct me to someone who knows. Do it and I’ll leave you here unconscious while I confirm. Lie, and I come back to break your neck. Or refuse to say anything, and I choke the life out of you here and now.”

It was a bluff…probably. Yet the rage and desperation fueling her words was all too real. Hopefully her captive would pick up on that.

“I see.” The woman was still struggling. “You’re the one who stole Pestilence’s powers. Well, I’d die rather than betray my people. Go ahead and kill me!” She paused, suddenly smiling. “Or I could just kill you!”

Ceasing her attempts to kick Alex off of her, the Kryptonian began to repeatedly slam her foot into the ground.

Fuck. The sound cage wouldn’t stop vibrations. She'd been unlucky enough to capture an enemy who could think under pressure. Alex fought to put increased pressure on her captive’s legs, but the Kryptonian simply began slamming her fists into the pavement. The building itself was shaking under her blows, and the infiltrator realized any chance of a successful interrogation had long since passed.

She delivered two swift punches to her enemy’s forehead, knocking her out instantly. Alex deactivated the sound cage, preparing to fly off and try again….

But it was too late. As sound rushed back in, Alex could hear the chatter of dozens of Argonians as they closed in on her position. Her blood chilled as she realized escape was impossible. The nanites in her suit couldn’t hide her from the determined gaze of a mass of searchers.

Well, Lena, I hope it was worth it.

Purge

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the delay! Writing this while studying for the bar exam. Once every two weeks is about the best I can do! If anyone takes a break from this story and catches up later, I totally get it!

Was this really the mother Kara had grown up with? This woman who had read her stories before bed, walked her through science projects, and raised her from birth was now planning a genocide? Even as Kara’s rational mind realized the truth, her heart refused to accept it.

Did I never really know her? Or have I just forgotten? Kara might have just been remembering the best parts of her mother. Was that because Alura had hidden her dark side from her daughter while growing up, or had Kara simply just chosen to ignore it?

No! I would have known! I would have. Yet Lena hadn’t known. The smartest human in history hadn’t realized her brother’s evil until it had been far too late. If the future CEO had failed to notice the genocidal murderer in the family member she’d loved, was it really any surprise that Kara had missed the same in her mother?

Perhaps for the first time, Kara truly understood the pain Lena must have gone through.

“There are three billion people waiting in those pods, Kara,” Alura continued. “There’s no guarantee we can keep them safe forever. If we don’t take Earth, you’re condemning them to death.”

The hero’s fists clenched. “And there are eight billion people on Earth!” she retorted. “How many of them are you going to have to kill to get what you want?”

“This is not about numbers,” Alura replied. Another spark cut through the atmosphere outside, illuminating her firm features. “This is about our people, the most advanced race in the galaxy, verses a lesser species. And as for how many of them I’m going to have to kill…very few.”

Just the slightest tinge of venom had entered her mother’s voice.

Kara’s knuckles were white. “Humanity won’t just sit back and let you take their entire planet.”

The High Councilor gave her a small smile. “Yes, daughter. That is exactly what they’re going to do.” The promise issued from her lips with such anticipation…such zeal…that it sent shivers trailing down Kara’s back.

\

Utterly surrounded within the wreckage of the abandoned building, Alex did the only thing she could do. Swallowing her distaste, she raised her arms in surrender.

“My name is Alex Danvers. Alex Danvers. Kara Zor-El’s sister!” she proclaimed loudly. “The High Councilor has forbidden you to kill me. Arrest me, and I’ll come quietly.” For now.

There were a dozen onlookers, all staring at her with a mixture of surprise and hostility. Several of their gazes dropped to the unconscious Kryptonian on the floor, and Alex knew a few were fighting the urge to charge forward.

An older Kryptonian stepped forward. “You come to our world, attack our people, and you expect leniency?” he demanded. “We accept your surrender, but there will be a reckoning. That, I promise you. Fyre, Tol-Ull,” he nodded at two of his companions. “Restrain our guest. Ginn-Vuth, find a pair  of-”

WHOOSH!  

Someone had just flown up to them…someone very fast. Before anyone could turn to look, a brilliant flash of green light burst through the air.

Pain! Alex rapidly stumbled back; the effect had been so strong that she’d been blinded. She rapidly blinked her eyes and tried to clear her vision, even as another body slammed into her own and tackled her out of the building.

Too stunned to resist, Alex allowed herself to be carried through the air at nearly supersonic speed. By the time her eyes had recovered, they were miles from the abandoned building and she was staring at one of the most shocking things she’d ever seen.

\

Kara’s horror was so great that she actually took several steps back. “You can’t! I won’t let you!”

Alura frowned. “I’m sorry, daughter, but that choice is beyond your power. I will spare those you love, but as the guardian of our people I have no choice. You should be pleased! This allows me to save Krypton and still show the humans mercy-”

“Mercy?!” Supergirl roared. “To spend the rest of their lives as…as what? That’s worse than slaughtering them!” Bile erupted in her throat, nearly overflowing into her mouth. She stared at her mother in disgust.

The High Councilor raised a placating hand, as if Kara was a child pleading for an extra hour before bedtime. “Eventually, we may be able to release some of them-”

“No. You won’t. They’d never forgive you. And neither will I!”

“Kara, I am sorry,” Alura apologized. “This is my fault. I sent you to that world. Anyone in your position would have forgotten who they are. How else would you have survived, surrounded by lesser beings and believing yourself the last of your kind? You adapted; I understand. In time, you will remember your true self.”

The hero was actually shaking in anger.

Her mother sighed. “I see you need time to process the news. Come. I’ll show you where you’ll be staying here. When you’re ready to talk, I’ll be-”

BZZT!

The twin blasts of heat vision caught Alura square on the forehead. Skidding back through the office, the High Councilor frowned. “Pointless. Do you know how many of our people it took to bring down Darkseid? Only an army could ever hope to stand against the Omega Effect!”

Dark red beams shot out of Alura’s eyes. Having expected the attack, Kara dived to the side to avoid them. As the beams curved around to strike her, Supergirl dug her hands into the ground and lifted a massive chunk of concrete.

Ow! The hero rolled to the side, propelled by the force of the impact. Her makeshift shield had exploded instantly, yet it had taken the brunt of the blast. She rocketed forward, preparing to strike her mother

Her mother.

Alura weaved around the blow. Kara attacked again with a sweeping kick, but the High Councilor’s reflexes were even greater than Pestilence’s had been. The hero avoided a retaliatory knee to the groin, but a palm strike to the torso sent Supergirl careening back. She fell to the floor in a heap.

Two continuous beams shot from Alura’s eyes, slamming into the stunned hero’s form. Resisting with all of her willpower, Kara tried to rise to her feet. It felt like she was lifting the sky. As the energy intensified, Supergirl climbed to one knee.

“Impressive, daughter. But you can’t-”

The window behind them shattered. Alex had appeared out of nowhere, slamming both of her fists into the back of Alura’s head. The High Councilor was launched across the room, slamming into the wall. The building shook under the impact.

“Get away from my sister!”

Alex! Kara tried to rise to her feet, but her sense of balance was gone. Dark spots danced at the edges of her vision, threatening to send her into unconsciousness.

“Not entirely unexpected.” Alura emerged from the crumpling wall, looking no worse for the wear. “Give up. I have no desire to hurt you, but I will do what I must.”

Alex’s eyes were glowing with green energy. “Go to hell, bitch!” They flew at each other, the force of the impact buffeting the entire room. Her vision blinking in and out of focus, Kara saw only flashes of the combat.

The two combatants exchanged a series of brutal yet sophisticated blows. Alura’s fists seemed to glow with a red energy as they rocketed across the room, demolishing any structure they came across. Alex fought back fiercely, countering many of her opponents strikes. The High Councilor launched several blasts from her eyes, but Alex had come across the same solution Kara had created. Unable to avoid the beams, she used objects to absorb the energy as best she could.

Then it was over. A punch caught Alex straight across the face. By the time she recovered, a continuous omega beam had seared into her chest. The new superhero fell to her knees, her lips contorted in agony.

“Do you see, Kara?” Alura prompted. “These humans may steal our powers and play at emulating our achievements, but they will never know how to use them correctly. Our people are blessed by the energy of a yellow sun, but we were forged through thousands of years of advancement. We didn’t need an executive with delusions of grandeur to save us from ourselves. Even the destruction of our very planet could not destroy our race! How could any human possibly compete with the best of us?”

Alex was now collapsed on the floor, her nose bleeding freely. Even Kara could tell something was wrong. Her sister wasn’t just in pain. This was worse. She was shaking uncontrollably, the color rapidly draining from her face.

Supergirl still struggled to rise. “What are you doing to her?!”

“Do not fear; she will live,” Alura replied soothingly, still maintaining the omega beams. “I am simply purging her of her sin. Once the Harun-el is burned from her body entirely, the Worldkiller powers she stole will seek a new host…a true Kryptonian.” She stepped forward, glaring at Alex. “You thought that with the power you looted, you would be able to protect my daughter?” the High Councilor demanded. “I will protect her. Be grateful for her love; it spares you greater punishment.”

Managing to climb to both of her knees, Kara shot a desperate look at her sister. Even when gasping with pain, Alex mouthed a single word. Run.

Never. Kara swiveled back to the High Councilor, finding enough strength to release another blast of heat vision. Not even looking away from Alex, Alura swiped out her arm and deflected the attack. Smoke was rising from her ungloved hand, but she paid it no mind.

VHOOSH!

Kara must have been hallucinating.

A missile soared through the open window, hitting Alura in the back with incredible concussive force. Rao. It wasn’t real, not exactly. The missile had been composed entirely of green light, yet the force of the impact was as tangible as any Supergirl had ever felt.

Alura went flying through the air, the omega beams gone, and fell out the other side of the building.

“Where the hell have you been?!” Alex hissed.

A figure was floating outside the window. The dark emerald suit he wore was unfamiliar, as were the glowing green eyes. Yet his face was recognizable at once.

“Winn!” Kara croaked.

He flew into the building, a light-green glow somehow radiating from him. “You fly faster than me.” His protest was directed to Alex, who attempted to rise. She managed to climb to her feet, only to wobble and lose her balance immediately.

“It’s gone!” Kara had never seen her sister so horrified. “I can’t…I feel…” Repressing her shock with visible effort, the elder Danvers sister turned to Winn. “You have to fly us out of here. Now.”

Her tone brokered no argument, and Winn obeyed. He snatched them both up, one in each arm, and flew them out the window. His muscles belied an inhuman strength, easily enough to hold them steady.

Kara’s shock and horror was battling her relief. “Winn!” They were rocketing through the air at near-Kryptonian speed, yet Supergirl’s attention was squarely on the young man in front of her. “You’re alive! You’re…green! What-?”

“I’ll tell you as soon as we’re off this rock!” he replied. The techie carried them into a nondescript building, blasting a hole through the wall. It was a hanger! Rows of small ships dotted the massive room, each identical to the one Alura and Selena had used to travel to Earth. All were open and completely inert.

He set them down on the ground. Shakily, Kara and Alex made their way into the nearest ship. Winn followed immediately. “I hope this device Lena made works, or we’re in for a short trip.”

How does he know about it? Yet Kara still replied. “Lena made it. It’ll work. Just hurry!”

Alex stumbled into the cockpit, pulled the small computer chip out of her pocket, and uploaded it into the slot in the dashboard that Lena had pointed out. The craft instantly roared to life, sealing its hatches and taking off into the air.

They flew through the hanger, out into the dark skyline above.

“The teleporter!” Kara called, but Alex had already pulled it out. It was their one chance to get past the shields. When activated, it would transport them several hundred feet forward. If it failed, they would splatter against the shield.

If that happened, Supergirl might not survive. Resisting the omega beams, even briefly, had drained Kara of most of her power. It would recover eventually, but sadly not within the next ten seconds. As for the others, well…Winn would probably be fine. His new alien glow-y powers would probably protect him. Alex, however…

They were already going too fast. There would be no reversing their course. Either the teleporter would work, or they would slam against the-

“…It’s dropping.” Winn murmured.

It was true! The section of the shield directly in front of them was splitting apart, providing them a clear way forward. Kara whirled around, staring out the back windows. Even with her powers drained, the hero’s eyesight was good enough to see Alura staring at their craft in resignation.

“She’s letting us go,” Supergirl breathed as they passed through the shield. She turned away, staring at her companions. Winn had been captured and held on Argo for weeks. Alex had been brutally drained. At that moment, Kara wasn’t sure whether she was relieved that Alura wouldn’t take a chance on her life…or wished that they had splattered against the shield after all.

\

“Argo had a Green Lantern helping them against Darkseid. Even after the Corps was decimated, a few were still around. The Lantern found them drifting through space and agreed to help them reach safety. She died in the battle with Apokolips and Argo kept her ring.”

The three of them were sitting in the cockpit. Kara and Winn were sitting in the chairs. Alex was on the floor, her back against the wall. “You gave me the basics earlier,” the elder Danvers replied. “But how on Earth do you know all of that?”

“Technically, we’re not on Earth,” Winn pointed out. At the look on Alex’s face, he continued. “The ring shows me flashes…memories…of what happened before. It’s attracted by willpower. When I was-” he hesitated, looking at Kara. “When I wouldn’t tell them anything, it flew to me. The guards didn’t expect it…how could they have? I blinded their vision and escaped. I’ve been hiding on Argo ever since. The ring has been telling, no, showing me how to use it.” There was no mistaking the enthusiasm in his words.

Kara blinked her eyes rapidly, trying to take all of this information in. “Why didn’t you use it to escape?”

“It couldn’t help me pilot one of their ships,” Winn explained. “And even if I could have made one of my own, where would I have gone? Space is big. Earth is small. I’d have starved to death long before finding anything. At least on Argo I could steal food if I was careful.”

Alex nodded. “Then he heard me yell when I was surrounded. He used that blinding trick again and we got away. He gave me the rundown.” Her voice was strangely dull.

“Are you okay?” Kara asked.

“I’m not hurt,” her sister replied quickly. “I’m weak. I don’t have Pestilence’s power anymore; I can’t feel it. The Harun-el is gone too. Somehow Alura burned it away. Maybe not all of it, Winn didn’t let her finish, but most of it.” Alex’s voice was still weak, but her eyes were brimming with anger.

“Lena can fix it,” Supergirl said quickly.

Her sister looked doubtful, and Kara understood why. None of them even understood how the Omega Effect worked. The idea that it could simply ‘burn away’ a human’s Harun-el infusion was terrifying. Yet if anyone in the universe could solve it, Kara knew who it would be.

“Why did they want you?” Alex asked, obviously trying to change the subject.

Winn threw an uneasy look her way. “They wanted info on Kara. Not just the basics…things only a friend would know. Who she cared about most, her principles, what she was afraid of. Alura wanted to know how to convince you to side with them.”

For the second time that day, Supergirl had to resist the urge to vomit. The question was primed on her lips. ‘What did they do to you?’ Yet she couldn’t bring herself to say it. Kara had seen the look in his eyes before. The ring hadn’t come to him simply for resisting a gentle interrogation. All she could do was take solace in the fact that he had come out of it seemingly okay and try not to think about what her mother had ordered.

I am a complete and utter coward.

Kara took a deep breath. “Did you find out anything else?”

Winn shook his head. “Other than the fact that Alura is in charge of them? No, they didn’t tell me much. I tried to spy on them as best I could, but I had to be careful. My hearing still isn’t nearly as good as a Kryptonian’s. I couldn’t get too close without being heard. Whatever they’ve got planned for Earth, though…it isn’t good.”

No. No it wasn’t. Kara knew she should tell them what she knew, but again her mouth refused to obey. The day had simply been too much. When they were back on Earth, after Kara had spent an hour in Lena’s arms and calmed herself by listening to her girlfriend’s steady heartbeat, she could tell them all. At least that way, she would only have to explain it once.

“There are hundreds of them,” Winn said. The excitement in his voice was gone now. “Probably around five hundred. And they have Alura and the Omega Effect. How are we supposed to stop that?”

Kara stared resolutely ahead. “We’ll find a way.” Part of her was longing for the days when the biggest problem in her life was an annoyingly beautiful CEO with a penchant for non-lethal villainy. Yet she was fully confident that that very same villain would find them a way out of this.

She had to.

\

It was an important meeting. The L-Shield was going into its final deployment stages. The project was Lena’s crowning achievement and possibly their only hope of saving the planet from an imminent invasion. It was critical that the CEO pay close attention.

Doing so was one of the hardest tasks in her life. She stared out at the faces arrayed around the table in front of her. Project leads, top scientists, and select board members were discussing the project’s integrity. Yet all Lena wanted to think about was her fiancé located lightyears away, probably already the prisoner of an alien invasion.

I’m going to hell. She tapped her toes rapidly against the floor. It was an unsatisfying outlet for her frustration, yet it was the only one available. I’m going to burn in the flames and I deserve it.

The out-of-key tapping was earning her a few curious looks, but no one made any mention of the potential distraction. Some, like Sam, knew exactly what was going through her mind and gave her a sympathetic glance. Others were hesitant to question the most powerful CEO on the planet during a public meeting.

Kara wouldn’t blame her for the decision to send her to Argo, especially if the hero was aware of the full context of the decision. Lena tried to use that thought to calm herself, but again it only made her feel worse.

BEEP!

Lena’s hand went to her pocket so quickly that it actually sliced through the table. The granite split apart, nearly upending the entire table. Papers went flying as the occupants scrambled away, yet the CEO paid no mind to the outbursts of shock around her. That had been a particular notification she’d programmed into her phone, designed to activate only if-

She looked at her phone. “YES!” Her override device had been activated. Alex had been given explicit instructions to destroy it upon capture. That meant they had seized a ship. They were on their way back.

Unless Alex had been forced to leave Kara behind. No. Lena couldn’t allow herself to believe that. She couldn’t simply see Alex choosing to leave and save her own skin, even if she knew that her sister wouldn’t be harmed on Argo. They were coming back. They had to be.

“Ms. Luthor…are you alright?” a particularly bold project head spoke.

Lena nodded brightly at him. “I’m fine, Thomas. I apologize; I’ve just received…some very good news.” She and Sam shared a knowing look. “I’ll have Jess call a repair crew for the table. In the meantime, why don’t we move this meeting to the auxiliary conference room?”

Puzzled but no longer startled, her loyal minions followed her out of the room. Working for a planet-dominating supervillain was certainly a strange job, but Lena knew they wouldn’t complain. L-Corp offered far better benefits and healthcare options than their contemporaries.

Oh, that’s right. We have no contemporaries. L-Corp has a virtual monopoly on the global economy. I won.

It seemed that her exultation and relief had put her in a particularly megalomaniacal mood, but that was all right. All she had to do now was sit through the rest of the meeting, pushing her daydreams of reuniting with, marrying, and ruling the world with Kara to the back of her mind.

For now.  

Sacrifice

Chapter Notes

I am back! Finished with bar exam! Won't know results until November, unfortunately.

The ship’s door had barely even opened before Lena had rushed forward, embracing her girlfriend in a hug that was immediately returned. The CEO had specifically mandated that the hanger be private for this return, mostly so that none of her employees would see their powerful, focused boss grinning like a schoolgirl while trying to hold back tears.

“I’m here,” Kara whispered softly, nuzzling against Lena’s cheek. Even as the words were said, the supervillain still felt like she was dreaming. Sending her fiancé to Argo had been a necessary sacrifice. It was an essential element in her schemes to save the world, and she knew that Supergirl would have agreed that being confined by her mother was worth the cost. Yet it would have meant Lena losing her pillar of strength during the hardest time of her life, and the notion still made her shudder.

Fortune had favored the ruthless. Lena had accomplished her goal without a sacrifice. From behind Kara’s shoulder, she could see Winn, seemingly normal but for the faintly glowing ring on his finger. The basics of what had happened on Argo had already been explained to Lena once the ship reached within Earth’s comm range, but she was eager to know more. 

In normal times, Lena would have spent hours…days…in her lab analyzing the fabled piece of technology that had fallen into their hands. The Green Lantern Rings were legendary, but few of the aliens L-Corp employed knew much about them. Creating constructs from pure willpower was beyond even Lena’s current grasp of technology. She needed to know how the ring worked…and how its powers could be applied and expanded.

Another glance over Kara’s shoulder dampened Lena’s good mood. Alex was standing alone. There was no joy or relief in her eyes from being back on Earth. All she managed was to give Lena a curt nod. The CEO knew that Alura’s Omega Beams had seemingly sapped most of Alex’s powers, but that appeared to be the least of the damage.

The woman standing in front of the ship, looking both sullen and uncertain, was not the same superhero who had left Earth a week previously. Through all of their experiences together, Lena had always respected Alex’s determination. That same determination had driven Alex to try and put a bullet in the villain’s forehead, willingly condemning herself to prison in order to protect her sister. Later, as they’d become allies, it had enabled Alex to offer herself as bait in order to save Kara from red kryptonite. More recently, during game nights, it had resulted in the dragging out of Monopoly games as Alex refused to concede defeat even as Lena’s deal-making and healthy manipulation of Kara’s heartstrings made her position unassailable.

There was none of that now. Lena knew that Alex had been hurting since her failed relationship with Sam- the details of which neither woman had been willing to disclose -but that couldn’t account for the empty gaze that had taken root in Alex’s eyes.

Winn was a lot happier. “Lena!” A flash of green briefly erupted in the room. Winn was now clad in an alien suit, his entire body radiating green energy. “Look what I picked up!”

Seemingly weightless, he began to fly around the room.

Still concerned about Alex, and somewhat bitter at being forced to end her close embrace with Kara, Lena’s tone was a bit dryer than she’d intended. “Yes, I can see that. Flying. Very impressive; I’ve never met anyone who could fly. Fascinating.”

Apparently determined to impress, Winn clenched his fist. Even knowing that it was possible, Lena could feel her jaw begin to drop as a fighter jet made of solid green light appeared in the middle of the room. It was…real. Heat was spraying from its engines, as their rumbling sent small vibrations cascading around the hanger.

I. Need. To. Study. This. Lena was just thinking about ways to kidnap Winn and hold him in her lab for a week when the jet finally vanished. The smirk on Winn’s face as his three superpowered friends stared at the empty space spoke more than words ever could.

“Lena,” Kara spoke, the euphoria of reunion beginning to dissipate. “Alura let us go. My mom…she could have kept up the shields. I…she still loves me.”

The hero’s eyes were all but pleading. Supergirl was begging her to find a way to stop this war before it began, and the knowledge that she couldn’t was a bitter pill of failure. Lena had devoted days to trying to think up a compromise, but based on what she knew of Argo and Alura…nothing worked. The information she’d learned made clear that their enemies would accept no result save total victory. They believed they had the resources to achieve it.

And they were probably right.

Sweet, noble Kara couldn’t understand it. Supergirl was not unfamiliar with evil, having faced and defeated some of the worst menaces the galaxy had to offer. Yet she couldn’t comprehend how a mother filled with love for her daughter could nonetheless sanction an atrocity upon an entire planet.

Moreover, Kara was a paragon of hope. It was both her greatest strength and her greatest weakness. In the near future, it would lead to complications for Lena’s plans if not adequately addressed. Supergirl would never give up on her mother or Earth as long as she still drew breath. She would never stop fighting for an ideal solution, even if any chance of a compromise had long since passed.

Lena’s fists clenched. Kara’s ability to hope- to believe in others- was what had brought them together in the first place. It had made it possible for an uptight superhero to forge a friendship with a villain bordering on megalomania. And now, it might ruin everything.

\

They were all there. L-Corp’s department heads, top agents, and lead scientists were all either cluttered around the conference table or attending remotely via Lena’s latest advances in holographic technology. Lena sat at the head of the table as Jess hovered behind her shoulder. The secretary looked ready to provide whatever assistance was necessary, even as she kept sneaking glances at Winn and the alien technology on his finger. 

He, Kara, and Alex were ready to report.

“Alura gave me the details.” Kara spoke confidently, but Lena could see through it. Every word was causing her pain. “Before Krypton was destroyed, the Science Guild tried to create a neural program to link every mind on the planet to try and stall the ecological devastation. It took them decades, but they couldn’t make it work. Not on Kryptonians, anyway.” The hero paused, wincing. “It’s called Myriad. A technological virus that can spread through any digital network into any neurons within range. It can’t work on Kryptonians, but it works on humans and most other aliens. Once a mind is infected, it falls under the complete control of Myriad’s operator. In effect, the infected become nothing more than…mindless drones.”

“That can’t be right,” Williams, one of L-Corp’s lead scientists, protested. “Controlling a single mind is incredibly difficult, and some can resist. You’re telling us that Argo can control billions at once?”

Seeing the skeptical looks around the room, Lena knew it was time to speak up. “It’s possible,” she said firmly. “I’ve done some research of my own into methods of mind control more refined than that of Poison Ivy’s. It would take years, even for me, but I’m confident I could develop a program that could spread from digital networks and seize control of a brain’s neurons. Krypton’s Science Guild had decades to work on such a project, and I have no doubt that they succeeded.”

The incredulity of the room lessened only slightly, but the tone of the CEO’s voice brokered no argument.

“That must be why the Worldkillers wanted to stop Pestilence,” Colville said. Her VP of finance was attending remotely, but his voice came through loud and clear. “They want to turn humanity into an army of drones and use us to rebuild their civilization. Digital networks are so widespread on Earth that virtually every human will be infected.”

Lena dipped her head in agreement.

“Why wait all this time?” another department head asked. “Why couldn’t they just send Myriad with one of the Worldkillers and have infected the entire planet already? And why bother trying to assassinate Ms. Luthor?”

Crunch. Lena’s enhanced hearing picked up the sound of the table edge crumbling under Kara’s grip. She shot her girlfriend an exasperated but grateful look. I’m glad you’re protective of me, but please try not to destroy the conference table. It was rather expensive.  

Kara took a brief break from her ominous but necessary exposition to shoot her a quick smirk back. Why? her smile said. You can afford it. Turning her attention back to the meeting, she continued. “Myriad needs a lot of power to work properly. It’s linked to Argo’s system core and can only be activated from there. As for why they wanted to kill Lena…” her voice dipped into a growl, “They knew she was smart enough to stop them.”

“How?” several people in the room demanded.

The supervillain took back over. “It’s my belief that anyone infused with Harun-el is immune to Myriad. My drones are as well. Given enough time, it’s theoretically possible that I could have assembled a force powerful enough to defeat them outright. Myriad will only work if Argo reaches Earth. As it stands, the L-Shield is now active and stands in its way. Its energy shield will stop the city in its tracks.”

“So?” Alex asked. “What’s our plan?”

The entire room turned to stare at Lena. The CEO could feel the weight of history bearing down on her shoulders. Her mind had run through every scenario, thought through dozens of contingencies, and the best she could come up with was nowhere near enough. The odds were simply too overwhelming.

Five more years. I could have solidified my control over Earth, made an indomitable horde of drones, and created enough Harun-el to form an army of soldiers. Every single day its creation becomes more refined. Even another year could have made a difference.  

Resisting the urge to sigh, Lena called up a hologram on the table. “For those few in the room who don’t know, this is the L-Shield’s central platform.” A hovering image of humanity’s largest station rotated above the table. “The entire system is controlled from here. If Alura’s forces take control of it, the entire system goes down and Earth will be defenseless.”

“Please tell me that the central platform is inside the energy shield,” Alex drawled. “And, assuming that it is, how will the Kryptonians reach it?”

Lena frowned. “The L-Shield isn’t complete,” she replied, making no attempt to hide her frustration. “At present, the energy barrier, when activated, can stop metal objects. Argo City itself and its ships won’t be able to penetrate it, but living tissue can. The Kryptonians themselves will be able to fly right on through.”

With a shift of her fingers, hundreds of dots appeared on the perimeter of the hologram and began swarming towards the central platform. “I’m confident Alura knows about the shield and its weakpoint. She’ll send all of her forces to bring the platform down. Once that happens, Argo will fly right into Earth’s atmosphere and activate Myriad. Human civilization will fall with a press of a button.”

Nearly the entire room went deathly silent. Yet one woman, the lead designer of L-Corp’s drone fleet, stood up. “Then we stop them. We know where they’re going, so we prepare.”

It was Sam who responded. “Unfortunately, nothing on Earth can stop a force of five hundred Kryptonians.” Her head shook glumly. “I’m not sure we can even slow them down.”

“We can,” Lena responded. “But not for long. As some of you know, L-Corp has increased its production of Kryptonite in recent weeks.” She sent an apologetic glance at Kara. “By next week, we can deploy as many as two thousand drones and arm them with Kryptonite.”

“Why not just make a bomb?” an executive asked.

Lena folded her hands. “Kryptonite loses potency as its dispersed. I have no doubt that Alura will equip her soldiers with radiation suits. Kryptonite will only grant us an edge; it won’t be a decisive factor. As it stands, my simulations project that our forces will be overrun within twenty minutes.”

Her matter-of-fact tone did little to allay the room’s shock. The thoughts of the attendees were palpable. L-Corp, the most advanced and powerful organization in human history, could only hold off the enemy force for mere minutes.

Voices around the room began to speak up. “What about our other forces?” a particularly loud scientist demanded.

“We have one hundred individuals infused with Harun-el,” Lena replied. “Each is roughly half as powerful as a full Kryptonian; they’ll serve as our last line of defense. As for our elite operatives…they’ll be the ones we’re depending on.” Another swipe of her fingers replaced the hologram of the L-Shield’s central platform with one of Argo. “Three teams will infiltrate the city once most of its forces have been deployed to the attack. I will lead one personally. Their goal will be the central core. If we can destroy Myriad, Argo’s invasion becomes hopeless.”

“Why? If they can defeat us, the rest of the planet’s militaries will have no chance at all.”

Lena turned to the questioning executive. “Because they know humanity won’t go quietly. Governments will fight back with both conventional and nuclear arms, with or without my approval. Earth will become a wasteland before Argo can conquer it. Alura’s best option will be to negotiate a settlement with Earth’s representative: me.”

Kara beamed at her, sending the CEO’s stomach into a guilty summersault.

“So our main force is essentially Aragorn while three teams of elite operatives attempt to infiltrate Mordor and try to destroy the One Ring?” Winn piped up.

The supervillain sent him a grim smile. “An accurate analogy. Unfortunately, I don’t think Alura is going to be stupid enough to leave Mount Doom unguarded. We don’t know the precise layout of the city or where the central core is. Our odds are…unfavorable.”

If only they knew.

“What about that one we captured?” a scientist asked. “Can’t we use her?”

Lena chose her words carefully. “No. Selena refuses to give us any useful information. Poison Ivy has tried to gain control of her mind, but her willpower is simply too strong. With time, we might be able to influence Selena enough to make her do jumping jacks, but she’s too loyal to give up information that could hurt Alura or Argo City.”

The panic was spreading around the room now. “We…we need to go public,” Colville argued. “Get the entire planet to-”

“No.” Lena shut him down immediately. “Earth’s militaries aren’t advanced enough to reach the central platform, let alone slow down a Kryptonian horde. Going public will only lead to riots around the world. If we win, we’ll be returning to a devastated planet. If we lose…well, there’s no sense in letting humanity’s last days be miserable.”

The rest of the room was silent. Lena stared down each section of the table in turn, glaring at any who wished to protest. “We have six days until Argo City reaches the L-Shield. Preparations for the assault will go on day and night. I advise everyone to use whatever free time they have to enjoy themselves. Spend time with friends and family.”

“Can we-?”

“You will not tell anyone.” The CEO cut off the questioning employee. “Anyone who breaks silence on this matter will be fired, blacklisted, and quarantined until the attack has passed…along with anyone they’ve told. L-Corp will be strictly monitoring both traditional and social media to ensure that no public disclosure is made. You have been warned.”

Well, that was certainly a grand motivational speech. Lena glanced briefly at Winn. Aragorn would be proud.

\

The second they were alone in Lena’s office, Kara could see her lover’s façade crumple.

“We’ll win this,” Supergirl promised. “We always do.” She glanced at the CEO and was shocked to see her hands actually trembling.

“A Kryptonian can be taken down in an ambush,” Lena said. “Metallo demonstrated that with you easily enough. But in a pitched battle, an army of them will be all but unstoppable. Alura’s going to know we’re coming. I’m sure she has a spy.”

Kara’s mouth gaped open. “Then why did you tell everyone our plan?” she demanded.

The supervillain offered her a sardonic smile. “Because I have another angle. I always do, don’t I? Notice what I didn’t mention at that meeting: that you told me that Alura is the only one who can activate Myriad.”

“So?”

“So while our army holds off the Kryptonian horde and our operatives go for Myriad, you, me, and Winn will be targeting your mother.”

What?! Kara was speechless.

“We’ll be using Kryptonite,” Lena explained. “While you were away, I finally perfected my vaccine to green Kryptonite, which I will be administering to you shortly. With the element of surprise, and her hesitance to attack her daughter, we might be able to-”

“Kill her?” Supergirl demanded. “She is my mother!”

Lena nodded. “And she’s leading a conquering force to Earth with the intention of turning all of humanity into mindless drones. As it stands, knocking her unconscious and taking her prisoner is the actual goal. With Alura captured, her forces may be more likely to stand down.”

Relief flowed through Kara, but her mind was still incredulous. “Lena, I saw how powerful she is. Winn might have caught her by surprise before, but even with the three of us…”

“I have nothing else, Kara!” The villain’s foot stomped into the ground, cracking the wood. “We’re outgunned about ten to one, facing an enemy who seems to know everything about us. You don’t need to tell me how fucked we are. I know humanity is probably done for. Our forces are going to be decimated, and I’m going to die alongside them!”

Kara placed two firm hands on Lena’s shoulders. “I will never let that happen.”

The villain laughed harshly. “What are you going to do? Offer yourself to your mother in exchange for sparing my life? Kneel at her feet and beg her to spare me?”

Supergirl frowned. If they did lose, and it came to that…

“We won’t lose,” Kara repeated herself. “There’s too much at stake. We’ve lost battles, but they’ve never been able to defeat us. Not when we’ve stood together.”

“A corny speech isn’t going to save us,” the CEO replied, even as the edges of her lips curved upwards. Then her frown reappeared. “If it comes to it, and I have no other choice…I will bring your mother down. Whatever the cost.”

No! “Lena, she’s my-”

“I know who she is!” the CEO retorted. “And hurting you in that way will be the hardest thing I’ve ever done. But I made my choice years ago, when I chose to become a supervillain and take over the Earth. This planet and everyone on it are my responsibility now, and I have to work for the greater good. Your happiness, and mine, are expendable in comparison. I’m sorry.”

Kara’s mouth simply gaped open. She wasn’t stupid. There was no logical argument she could make for insisting that Alura’s life be spared. Yet there was no way in hell she could simply sanction the murder of her own mother.

“You killed Pestilence,” Lena reminded her. “This is no different.”

Supergirl’s eyes began to glow. “Pestilence was pure evil! Alura is willing to commit an atrocity, but she’s trying to help her people. She’s not a sadistic monster!”

“Maybe not, but she plans on making eight billion people into mindless drones,” Lena argued.

Kara nearly swore with frustration.

“Hopefully, it won’t come to that,” the villain continued. “And if it does…I’ll be the one to do it. I wouldn’t ask that of you. If that means you’ll hate me, well, I don’t think I’d ever be happy again. That’s a sacrifice I have to be willing to make.”

Hating Lena? Kara couldn’t imagine ever doing that. But watching her fiancé strike down her mother was too painful an idea to even contemplate.

“I’m begging you to find another way,” the hero said. “You’re Lena Luthor!”

“I am.” Her girlfriend nodded sadly. “I’ve been willing to cross the line to do the greater good. I’ve crossed ethical boundaries you don’t even know about, some rather recently. That’s how I’ve gotten to where I am today, and it’s why Earth even has a chance of survival. I’m willing to burn in Hell if it means I have the satisfaction of knowing I did everything in my power to save the planet.”

Kara knew where Lena was coming from. She could understand her lover’s position, even sympathize with it. Yet she couldn’t agree. At the very least, there were some lines Supergirl would never be willing to cross. Joining Lena had forced to her to expand what she was willing to accept, but there would always be a moral line between the two of them.

Am I better for being strong enough to never take the easy way out? Kara thought. Or is she better for not being weak enough to do what’s necessary for the greater good.

Maybe it was both.

“I’ll help you fight my mother,” Kara promised. “If, by some miracle, we do win…you need to know. I won’t be able to watch you kill her.”

Lena dipped her head in acknowledgment. “I know. As you’re well aware, I never go into a battle unprepared.”

The words sent a chill down the hero’s spine.

“If you can make me a vaccine for green kryptonite, maybe you can make me stronger,” Kara offered desperately. “You told me once you never tested what Harun-el would do to a Kryptonian. Maybe if you used it on me-”

“Out of the question.”

Supergirl crossed her arms. “We’ve seen what it can do for regular humans. What if it had a similar effect on me; it could make me strong enough to stop Alura without killing her. You said yourself how bad our chances our. We need to try!”

“Your DNA is already Kryptonian. Infusing you with Harun-el could kill you; I highly doubt it would make you stronger. And, regardless, I would never test how Harun-el would affect a Kryptonian on you.”

The hero scowled. “You’re the one who just said we need to be prepared to make sacrifices!”

Lena shrugged. “Then I’m a hypocrite. I’m willing to sacrifice your short-term happiness and your freedom, but I’m not going to gamble with your life. If that’s not enough for you, then let me offer a completely pragmatic perspective: you need to be alive for when we face Alura.”

“Why?”

The supervillain offered her a small smile. “Because she and I share the same weakness.”

\

Alex sat in her apartment. Bored. Useless.

Being a hero had been amazing. It hadn’t quite compared to having a warm, humble, and witty girlfriend complete with a twelve-year-old child that Alex already adored, but it had helped soften the blow of Sam terminating their relationship.

For so long, Alex’s purpose had been simple: protect Kara. Emotionally, if not physically. When Kara had become adjusted to Earth and found love with a CEO, Alex had been left directionless. Being forced to quit her job after Kara’s identity had been revealed certainly hadn’t helped.

For a brief, dreamlike period, she had thought she’d found something with Sam. A sexy, caring CFO who possessed a temper that flared just often enough to make itself known. Sam had possessed all of Lena’s confidence, but none of the arrogance that Kara inexplicably seemed to find endearing. She was badass enough to facilitate a scheme for corporate domination yet loving enough to make her daughter the absolute center of her world. Alex, whatever she’d told anyone else, had been drawn in immediately.

That hope had, out of seemingly nowhere, been smashed to pieces. The universe had been eager to send Alex a message that personal happiness simply wasn’t in the cards for her, and Alex had heard it loud and clear. She should have heard it the first time, as she watched Maggie Sawyer die in her arms. Sam had made sure that it finally sunk in.

A new purpose had fallen into her lap almost overnight. Suddenly, Alex wasn’t simply infused with Harun-el…she was one of the most powerful beings on Earth. Her destiny had finally been clear. She could help protect her sister and share the burden of saving the world.

Then twin red beams fired from her sister’s birthmother had entered her body and ripped her life apart.

“Alex.”

Lena had just teleported into the middle of the living room. The ex-superhero considered reminding her that, owner of the building or not, it was still considered polite to knock on the door. But the words died on her lips. There was no point.

“What do you want?”

“I need to study you,” the supervillain replied immediately. “We need to see if I can restore your powers.”

A brief flare of hope rose within Alex, but she quickly quashed it. Even Lena Luthor wouldn’t be able to reverse the power of the Omega Effect within six days. “Forget it. Those beams felt like acid. I watched as they literally burnt the Harun-el out of my system. You can’t fix that.”

The CEO grimaced. “Maybe not. But either way, I need to check to make sure enough Harun-el remains in your system to keep you immune from Myriad.”

“Why bother?” Alex demanded. “Shouldn’t you be doing something more important right now?”

With a grim smile, Lena sat down on the sofa across from Alex. Pressing her fingers together, she stared intently at the former hero. “I believe that saving the entire planet from a fate worse than death qualifies as a worthy purpose.”

Final Battle: Part 1

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Keep it together, Lena. Because if you don’t, no one else will.

Argo would be arriving at the L-Shield in twelve hours. A vast array of deep space scanners made sure that there would be no surprise attacks. That gave Lena Luthor one last night to try and fall asleep while trying to figure out where it had all gone wrong.

Her victory had been inevitable. Lena’s technology had made her complete economic and political domination of Earth a certainty. She’d been looking forward to decades of ruling the planet, making it better for humans and aliens alike. Ruling as a lesbian power couple with Kara Zor-El had been her personal icing on the cake.

Now she was facing insurmountable odds from the most powerful force in the galaxy. Through no fault of her own, Earth was the target of hundreds of Kryptonians. With another five years of preparation, Lena’s drone armada and army of superpowered individuals might have been ready to defeat them in open battle.

I should have started sooner…before Lex died. I could have taken over even back then…

“Come to bed, love.”

Kara’s voice pulled her out of her thoughts. Even now, on the eve of battle, the hero was still full of hope. Whether it was simple naïveté or an inner strength that Lena could never hope to match, the CEO didn’t know.

Probably a bit of both.

Should I suggest we have sex? Lena knew that was something a lot of couples did before a war, but it didn’t feel right to her. How could she even begin to feel pleasure when billions of souls were resting on her shoulders? If it wasn’t for Kara’s presence, the villain was certain she would have broken down into tears hours ago.

I’m sorry. I’m so sorry.

“Kara, I want you to promise me something,” Lena began, sitting down on their bed as the hero shuffled closer. “You need to live. No matter what happens. Alura has definitely issued orders not to kill you, but battle is chaotic. If we lose…”

Supergirl all but growled. “We. Will. Not. Lose. You won’t let that happen.”

Guilt swirled in Lena’s stomach. “If we lose…you should surrender. Alura might listen to you…offer Earth a little better treatment.”

“Losing means all of my friends die,” Kara hissed. Even if she still remained hopeful her mother could be talked down, the hero clearly knew exactly what the stakes were. “I can’t accept that.”

Lena’s eyes trailed over to the stars shining outside their bedroom window. “The odds that we all live are…I don’t even want to guess. Alura might be willing to offer mercy to some if you stop fighting.”

“I was born on Krypton, but Earth is my home. This planet is still strange to me in a lot of ways, and not everyone here has welcomed me,” Kara admitted. “But it’s given me a new family…friends…and it’s full of people who deserve to live their lives. I’m ready to die for it.”

She placed a soft kiss on her fiance’s cheek. “I know. I wouldn’t expect anything less from the woman I love,” Lena admitted. “I just…you need to survive. For Earth…and for me. Do you understand?”

“You can’t make me promise that,” Kara replied grimly. “Just like I can’t make you promise me that you’ll live.”

The supervillain sighed. “I know.”

\

Winn stood in the hanger, staring at the array of destroyed targets. He’d been practicing for days, but the techie knew he had far from mastered the ring. Constructs formed from his very thoughts, but Winn could feel the energy at his fingertips. It was capable of more, he was sure of it.

But am I? The ring was fueled by willpower. Winn focused solely on his drive to save Earth and protect those he cared about, allowing all other emotions to fade away. The red of anger and the yellow of fear could not coexist with the Green Lantern Ring.

He looked down at the alien technology on his finger. I know what you want from me. I’m trying. I just hope it will be enough.

\

Jess placed a kiss on her son’s forehead, though she knew Luke was already asleep. By the time he woke up tomorrow morning, a family friend would have already arrived to watch him. Jess would be on the L-Shield, helping coordinate the last line of the shield’s defense.

Lena had offered to let her stay on Earth but the secretary had adamantly refused. She had chosen to take Harun-el that might have gone to someone else…with power came responsibility. Her boss had all but pleaded for Jess to remain behind, but the secretary had informed the CEO that that was one order she would refuse to follow. Faced with the choice of either wasting forces imprisoning her assistant or allowing her to travel to Argo, Lena had reluctantly backed down.

With another glance at her son, Jess stepped out into the kitchen. Soon, it would be time to take some of L-Corp’s patented sleeping pills and get some rest. For now, it was time for a last meal. She glumly set a steak on the stove.

“Fighting and dying in space,” she mused to herself. “Who knew it would end this way?”

“Change of plans,” a soft voice spoke behind her.

Harun-el enhanced Jess’s reflexes, but it did nothing to prevent her from being startled. By the time the secretary realized what was happening, her assailant had wrapped an arm around her neck and begun squeezing.

Instinct taking over, Jess thrashed furiously in her attacker’s grip. Each movement was countered easily, the assailant even preventing her from making noise. Whoever this was, they were far more skilled in combat than Jess and at least as strong.

“Earth falls tomorrow,” a familiar feminine voice whispered in her ear. “You’re not going to be there to see it.” The attacker squeezed harder and harder, her arms containing more than enough power to snap the secretary’s neck.

Luke…

Her body hit the ground second later.

\

Lucy Lane was actually looking forward to the next day. What did she have to lose? She’d lost her sister to Lena Luthor’s callous experiments, lost Clark to Luthor’s mad brother, and seen the rest of her friends abandon her.

Oh, they all still paid her lip service, but they’d all submitted to Luthor’s will. Even James. How any of them could look Lucy in the eye while still paying homage to the family that had destroyed her life, Lucy couldn’t fathom.

Lucy didn’t think that her sister’s death was intentional. Lena Luthor was just so focused on power that a casualty or two along the way was no great loss to her. When one volunteer died to an overexposure of Harun-el, others were still waiting in line to take their place.

It galled her that she would actually be helping Luthor the next day. But while she viewed maintaining any friendship with Lena Luthor as a massive betrayal of Clark and Lois’s legacy, refusing to help defend the Earth would be an even bigger affront to their memories. Argo was coming, and Lucy had agreed to be infused with Harun-el months prior.

Her hero was dead, her sister was dead, and her father was an unrepentant bigot. What did she have to lose?

\

“You could leave, you know. Find another planet. You don’t owe Earth anything.”

Starfire shook her head. “No, I don’t. But there are billions of good people here! I can’t just abandon them. And I made Ms. Luthor a promise.”

Barry sighed, looking around his friend’s room. Starfire was living in one of L-Corp’s luxury apartments, but Barry knew the standard of living meant next to nothing to Koriand’r. The former Princess wanted two things: to help people, and to enjoy time with friends.

He envied her way of thinking.

Some would call Starfire naïve. In many ways, she was. That didn’t mean she wasn’t afraid. Barry could see the fear in her eyes…it was the same fear that rested on his shoulders. So many people were counting on them. 

The Flash wasn’t a genius, but he was far from stupid. As a member of one of the three teams tasked with taking out Myriad, he knew he’d signed up for a suicide mission. It would not surprise him in the least if Luthor had a greater plan in mind, one that saw his mission as nothing more than a diversion.

He wouldn’t resent her for it. In fact, Barry hoped that was exactly was happening. A suicide mission was a senseless sacrifice. Serving as a diversion for a better strategy might actually make a difference.

Even if Barry didn’t live to see it.

\

James knew Alex was on the verge of cracking. After so many losses, and a brutal beatdown by her sister’s mother, it was inevitable. They were sharing drinks on potentially their last night alive, and it looked to be taking every amount of resolve she had to resist downing the entire bottle.

“Kara won’t give in. She’ll fight until her heart bursts. Alura wants to spare her, but some nameless Kryptonian soldier is going to snap her neck. I’m going to have to watch…and I can’t do anything,” the former hero moaned, taking another swig of wine.

James cast his eyes to the stars. “I know how that feels,” he replied quietly.

“Yeah, right.” Alex tossed her glass carelessly to the side, allowing it to shatter on the floor. “You’re an only child. I’m not…that drunk.”

The photographer watched as the vintage liquor rolled across the floor. “Clark was my brother. Not by blood…not even by name, but he was. Clark had a way of drawing people in…kind of like Kara. I watched my friend die, and I couldn’t do a damn thing except for spit on Lex’s grave.”

Alex winced slightly. She made no apology, but her dropping of the subject signaled her feelings well enough.

“When he died, I said this world didn’t deserve him.” James paused to take a shot of whiskey. “You know the worst part? Part of me is glad he’s dead. At least he didn’t have to see all of this…Lois dead, his people about to subjugate the planet he swore to defend. Maybe dying knowing he’d saved the world from Lex was a mercy.”

Alex pulled out another bottle. “Kara gets to die in combat with her own people, knowing she failed in the end. You know what…you’re probably right.”

\

The sun rose slowly over the Western Hemisphere. Hundreds of millions of people were preparing to rise for the day, or already preparing for school and work. On the other side of the planet, billions more finished their shifts, ate with their families, or continued to slumber peacefully.

Eight billion humans and aliens lived on Earth. Less than a few thousand realized it was probably their last day with free will. 

In the vast distance of space, the city of Argo grew ever closer.

\

Lena looked out at her forces.

Two thousand nth metal drones stood ready to defend the central platform, all of them armed with weapons of green kryptonite. Turrets laced with kryptonite bullets and missiles stood ready along every inch of the mile-long structure, prepared to supplement the defense.

Behind them, the single building on the platform stood strong and proud. It was a great silver tower rising defiantly towards the stars, forged entirely out of nth metal. Inside the building was her last line of defense. One-hundred of L-Corp’s best agents, chosen through a rigorous mental and physical screening program to be infused with Harun-el. A dozen other superpowered individuals, born from random scientific accidents or powerful aliens having descended to Earth: Firestorm, Blue Beetle, Hawkgirl, a few Tameranians…even a Czarnian whose allegiance had been bought with copious amount of cash.

And Lucy and James.

A sub-shield surrounded the central platform itself. It kept the space enclosed and prevented artificially produced air from spilling out into space, but it would be no barrier to any living being determined to make entry.

Three teams ready to infiltrate Argo and take out Myriad, each comprising six members.

One led by Lady Shiva, formerly an unrepentant assassin before being brought in line by a combination of threats and bribes. Shiva wasn’t the only former assassin on L-Corp’s payroll, but she was so high-profile that her presence was essential. She was renowned as Earth’s best martial artist, a claim that Lena wholly subscribed to. She was infused with Harun-el, just like the five L-Corp agents who accompanied her.

Another led by Barry Allen, infused with Harun-el and also the fastest individual Earth had ever seen. He was accompanied by Starfire and four other Tameranians who had followed their Princess to Earth. Incompatible with Harun-el, but so strong that they had no need of it.

The last led by Mr. Terrific, a rather unassuming man who also happened to be the third most intelligent human in history. His mind wasn’t the equal of Lena’s, or even Lex’s, but he’d managed to become a billionaire through his inventions even as L-Corp rose to dominate the world. So, naturally, Lena had quickly hired him and made him a department head. As a skilled blackbelt, he’d also been a natural choice for Harun-el infusion. Terrific had chosen his own team for the mission, consisting of four of L-Corp’s top agents and a superhero known as Cyborg. The latter was more than a genius in his own right, having been both infused with Harun-el and extensively modified with artificial components.

Including a big ass laser. Because why not?

The forces on the L-Shield’s central platform consisted of the most brilliant and powerful figures in the history of Earth. Each individual deserved to be protected and respected for the good that their abilities and intelligence could do for the Earth. And yet they were all being offered as a diversion for a three-person team.

Lena, Kara, and Winn. The three most powerful fighters in L-Corp’s army.

There were a hundred geniuses on the platform, and none of them could have held a candle to Lena’s intellect. Her technology and planning had all but taken over the Earth within the span of two years. And yet, now that it was time to give a speech, her mind failed her.

I can’t trust myself to speak. I can’t give the game away.

“Kara, you do it.”

The hero nodded, taking a deep breath before rising into the air. “I’m scared,” she began, her voice projecting across the platform. “I know you all are too. Everyone knows what’s at stake here today. If we win, we can make Earth into the most prosperous its ever been…a beacon of light for the entire universe. I know that’s worth fighting for.”

Supergirl paused, surveying the troops. “We’re outnumbered and outgunned. Argo knows this. They’re expecting to fly in here and crush us, but they don’t know who they’re fighting. I’ve learned a lot about humanity in my time here. Humans are capable of both great good and terrible evil. But above all, they’re damn stubborn. They know it’s better to die free than live as slaves; if they fall, it will be clutching at the throats of their invaders.”

Lena suppressed a small smile. Even as the cynics in the audience rolled their eyes, their attention remained fixed on the superhero floating overhead.

“To my fellow aliens, well, you’ve gotten a bad break. You’ve fled oppression on your own worlds only to have it follow you here,” Kara intoned. “But the fact that you’re standing here, right now, means that you know that this world is worth saving. We will win, and we will make Earth a sanctuary for refugees across the universe. I promise.”

The CEO forced herself to bury the guilt. It was business now, and her voice was back. “All three infiltration teams know their objectives,” she announced to the group. “Stick with your team leaders and stay alert; there’s a lot about Argo we don’t know. Everyone else, stay close to the shield generator. You’re the last line of defense. Let the drones handle the first wave and pick off any stragglers who get through. Once we have confirmation Myriad is destroyed, retreat to your assigned evacuation ships immediately.”

It was a point that had already been stressed to every member of the defending force. They couldn’t hope to hold the shield generator forever. But once Myriad was destroyed, the L-Shield would no longer be strictly necessary. With an easy conquest of Earth prevented, Argo would have to seek terms.

As for when the order to retreat would be given…

\

In a bunker hundreds of feet below the Earth’s surface, Alex watched the proceedings unfold on her monitors. It killed her not to be up there, but she knew her job was just as important. If not more so.

Her role wasn’t to coordinate strategy during the battle. That was left to L-Corp’s top tacticians, both stationed on the central platform or coordinating strategy in their own private bunkers. Alex wondered if they felt just as helpless as she did.

As Argo emerged onto the scanners, Alex’s scanners showed four stealth ships heading out to meet it. Each was reverse engineered with technology recovered from the ship Alura had used to visit Earth, which hopefully meant they would get through Argo’s shields and reach the city undetected.

That would be the easy part.

Her fingers absent-mindedly rubbed the syringe of Harun-el sitting in her pocket. It was the smallest amount that Lena judged could still be useful, but Alex was only to inject herself as an absolute last resort. According to the CEO, using it had a sixty percent chance of killing her outright.

It was still tempting.

\

James watched as Argo emerged from the blackness of space, terrifyingly large. The massive city hovered ominously just outside the range of the L-Shield, all but blocking out the sun. His heart crawled into his throat as he watched a swarm of flying objects emerge from Argo’s skyline and head straight for the L-Shield’s central platform.

There were hundreds of them. And all as strong as Supergirl. With his enhanced vision, he recognized Purity first and foremost among them. 

Where was Reign?

As living beings, the invaders slipped through the L-Shield easily. With his advanced sight, James could just make out the sleek space suits that each wore. He had no doubt that they were designed to defend against Kryptonite. Hopefully the two thousand drones serving as the first line of defense would be able to tear enough openings to leave a large portion of the attackers vulnerable to the deadly green material.

Kryptonite killed my best friend. It’s poisoned Kara multiple times. Now here I am, hoping that a Luthor manages to use it successfully against hundreds of aliens.

Suddenly, just as the edge of the Kryptonian swarm approached the central platform…

What?!

BANG! BANG! Hundreds of the L-Corp drones crashed to the ground. Half of their defending force had been deactivated in an incident. Cries of fear and confusion echoed throughout the building, sending shivers down the photographer’s spine.

“What the hell?!” Lucy demanded.

James didn’t know. He watched, open-mouthed, as the swarm of Kryptonians reached the central platform. They were immediately set upon by an array of green missiles and speeding bullets. The roughly thousand remaining drones stood ready.

As the first of the invaders buffeted their way through the barrage of missiles, the clash in the sky began.

\

Shiva moved rapidly through the deserted alleyways of Argo, her team moving right behind her. They’d penetrated the city’s outer defenses with no issue at all. Now all they needed was to reach the central core. According to Lena’s best estimates, it would be in the back half of the city.

The assassin knew a desperate mission when she saw one. It was a massive city. Even with three separate teams assigned to look in different sections of Argo, their odds of actually finding the central core were slim to none.

“Ma’am?” one of her operatives prompted. “I hear something.”

Shiva heard it too. It was at the edge of her hearing, but she knew exactly what it was. The rapid and concentrated swishing through the air could only be one thing. She looked up to see twenty Kryptonians flying right at their position.

Well, I’ve never been afraid of death.

\

“Barry!” Starfire screamed.

He heard it too. Roughly two dozen Kryptonians flying in on their position.

No! They’d been discovered. Their mission was over. They could only hope now that the other two teams were still hidden, but deep down he knew that probably wasn’t true. Clearly, Alura had kept some forces on Argo for a reason.

They knew we were coming.

There was no point in fighting. They were outnumbered four to one by individuals at least as powerful as they were. The Flash’s eyes took in the surrounding streets, looking for exits. Barry had only one option.

“Scatter!” he commanded.

\

Mr. Terrific was one of the smartest men in the history of the planet. He could recognize a hopeless situation when it appeared. His team was outnumbered four to one within enemy territory, and their opponents were faster and stronger than they were.

“Don’t do it, Holt!” Cyborg demanded.

I really hope Luthor has something else up her sleeve. There’s nothing more we can do for her, and I won’t let my team die for nothing.

“We offer our surrender!” Terrific yelled at the approaching Kryptonians.

A flash of lightning across Argo’s skyline illuminated the face of the enemy commander flying toward them in perfect detail. Through the visor in the alien’s protective suit, Terrific could see the Kryptonian’s lips set in a firm line.

Either the Kryptonians had been told not to accept surrenders, or this commander simply felt like pretending he’d heard nothing.

Even as the rest of the team backed up along the street, Cyborg stepped forward. His arm cannon had been heavily augmented with L-Corp technology, and it had been incredibly powerful already.

“Booyah!”

The street was consumed with blue light.

\

Lena, Kara, and Winn steadily moved down the streets. Unlike the other teams, they knew exactly where they were going: the High Councilor’s Office. There was no certainty Alura would be there, but it was by far their best chance.

The CEO was willing to bet that the other teams had already been discovered. Alura clearly had a mole within the upper echelons of L-Corp. The plan to send three teams to seek out and destroy Myriad had been given to the entire board and her top agents.

It was a diversionary tactic, plain and simple. Lena hoped that they would all survive, but she had to maximize Earth’s chances. The CEO would have gladly died in place of any of her subordinates, but that simply wasn’t an option.

She didn’t have the right to die. Not yet. Lena was the only one who could save the planet. She needed to see this mission through to the end.

“We’re almost there,” Kara said, clearly recalling her previous visit to Argo. Lena sent her an approving glance. The typical Kara Danvers nervousness had been replaced by Supergirl’s confidence. The superhero’s mouth was set in a firm line. Her eyes were emitting a soft blue glow.

She’s pissed.

The tension on Kara’s face exploded into anger as her eyes set upon the target building. Knowing that Supergirl had the best eyesight amongst the three of them, Lena turned to her fiancé.

“What do you see?” the villain asked.

Kara’s fists were clenched tightly. “My mother is standing in the lobby. And she’s waiting for us.”

\

Alex stared at the monitors, trying to fight off the encroaching dread. L-Corp’s drones were being swatted out of the sky, and the teams on Argo were…

“I did warn you.”

Alex turned around in shock. Sam was standing right behind her.

Chapter End Notes

Next chapter: Same time next week. Story is already finished, so one chapter each week until the end!

Final Battle: Part 2

“So nice of you to join us.”

Lena and Winn at her side, Kara stalked her way into the lobby. Alura was standing casually in the center of the building, entirely alone. Unlike the rest of the Kryptonians, there was no anti-Kryptonite suit protecting her. A small smile sat on her face.

The three defenders of Earth readied themselves.

“Mom, I am begging you,” Kara pleaded. Her voice was desperate, but the hero forced herself to remain controlled. “I know you’re better than this. I know! There are billions of lives at stake. Don’t make a new Krypton on a pile of corpses!”

Alura simply shrugged. “Most of the humans will live. I will simply be controlling their fate. Am I really any different than your…girlfriend?” she eyed Lena with visible distaste. The CEO evenly returned her glare.

“Fiance,” Supergirl retorted proudly. “And yes, you are. In Lena’s world, people will still be free to choose their own destiny. In yours, they won’t even be conscious! Just slaves following programming. How could you possibly be a part of that?”

A flash of lightning split the sky as Alura rolled her eyes. “I am tired of explaining this to you, Kara. My people are all that matter to me. I’ll teach you to remember your heritage soon enough.”

It was in that exact moment, staring into the blackness of her mother’s eyes, that Kara finally realized the truth. Her mother had no regrets…no doubts. There would be no convincing her to stand down.

I was so stupid not to realize it earlier. The hero glared at her mother. She would always love Alura, but now that love made her feel sick to her stomach. This is exactly how Lena must feel every time she remembers her brother.

The hope of peace withered inside her. All that arose in its place was rage.

“Save us all the trouble and surrender, Kara,” Alura beckoned. “Join me as Princess of the New Krypton. Simply because of my love for you…and my guilt for ever sending you to this planet…I will allow you to serve as an advocate for humanity. I can offer them a modicum of restraint…allowing a small minority to remain free of Myriad.”

Supergirl stared at the woman who raised her, who she still loved with all her heart, and spat on the ground. “Go to hell! I’ll accept nothing less than you leaving Earth…forever. And why would I want to be your Princess when I can be her Queen?” she nodded at her girlfriend.

“Empress, darling. Empress,” Lena replied with a thin smile, keeping her eyes fixed on Alura. Winn was doing the same, his ring emitting a bright green glow.

Alura frowned in annoyance, as if Kara was a child again and had spilled another drink on the living room rug. “So be it. Today is the day you all lose. Your friends looking for Myriad are being hunted down as we speak…I can hear the screams from here. The robot has just had his arm ripped off. Barry Allen’s team is running, but they won’t get far.”

Supergirl stared at her enemy. If this had to end with Alura stabbed through the heart with Kryptonite, so be it. “We’re not going to lose to you.”

The matriarch smirked.

Kara and Lena’s Kryptonian powers heightened their reflexes beyond human comprehension. That made them just fast enough to perceive Alura crossing the room in the blink of an eye. Winn, his reaction time far slower, didn’t react until the matriarch’s fist had slammed into his gut.

No! The techie’s body moved through the air in a blur, slamming right through the building’s reinforced walls and careening far out of sight. He’s alive. He has to be alive! The ring…

Alura rounded on Lena. “Now for you.”

\

This was impossible!

Alex stared at the CFO standing before her. There was no way Sam could be in this rom. Alex would have heard the elevator coming down from the surface…and it hadn’t even moved!

The woman’s mere appearance was bringing forth emotions Alex did not have time for that day.

“What are you doing here? How did you find me?” No one except Lena was supposed to know her location, not even executives.

“Simple tracking device on your jacket,” the CFO replied. “Now we find ourselves here. You made your choices. Serving Luthor cost you everything…your power is gone. There is no choice now. You must come with me to Argo, willingly or otherwise.”

The words were chilling. But it was the eerily familiar tone that truly filled Alex with dread. Sam’s voice had become deeper; she sounded just like…

Sam smirked. “Yes. I am Reign. The Worldkiller who ordered the death of your precious Maggie Sawyer and broke your heart a second time. The one whose actions have ensured that humanity falls today.”

No! No. Alex took a quick step back, her heart racing. This wasn’t possible. All this time it was Sam? How? Lena herself had told Alex the story of how Sam had saved her life after Lex’s trial! The Worldkillers had wanted nothing more than Lena’s death. It didn’t make sense.

“T-this has to be a trick.” Alex took a hurried step back. “Some Kryptonian technology. There’s no way.”
