“I’m afraid not,” Reign replied. “I must say, it was fun playing with your heartstrings. It was annoying keeping you alive, but Alura insisted for her precious daughter. I wasn’t allowed to hurt you physically, but I think I did my share of damage.”

If this was really happening, Alex was screwed. There was no way in hell she could overpower a Worldkiller, not with most of her powers gone. She blinked her eyes rapidly, trying to comprehend the nightmare standing in front of her. Sam had betrayed them all. Sam had ordered Maggie’s death.

It still didn’t make sense…

“Ruby…” Alex breathed. “You love her; I’ve seen you two together! Why would a Worldkiller ever love a human child?”

Sam took a menacing step forward. “A simple ploy. I needed to establish a good cover, after all. Once Myriad has been activated and Earth has fallen, Ruby will simply be another puppet for-” the Worldkiller trailed off, her eyes going glassy. Alex watched, still shocked and horrified, as Sam’s hands began to shake.

“Ruby…Alex…I-” the CFO looked like she was struggling to move forward. The triumphant sneer on her face had been replaced by a tortured grimace. “Find…Lois. Lois knew. Find her…Lois!”

The Worldkiller charged forward, but she clearly wasn’t at full strength. Even with her diminished powers, it was easy for Alex to grab her ex-girlfriend by the arm. Spinning around, she hurled Sam across the bunker with all of her strength.

\

Barry had given the order to scatter. As the fastest man alive, he’d managed to evade his pursuers so far. But when he heard Starfire screaming in pain several blocks away, the speedster haltered his course without hesitation.

The princess was bloodied and bruised on the ground before two Kryptonians. Another Tameranian was on the ground beside her, struggling to move. One of Kryptonians was already reaching for Starfire’s neck, clearly prepared to choke the life out of the beaten alien.

The Flash didn’t hesitate. He rocketed forward with all his speed, slamming into his friend’s attackers with a sonic boom. The force of the impact sent both Kryptonians flying into a nearby building, scattering shards of glass as they slammed through the window.

Barry reached down to pull his fellow hero to her feet. “Get out of here, Star. They’ll be back, and there were more following me. I’ll buy you some time.”

“No way!” Starfire snarled, spitting blood out of her mouth. “We’re in this together.”

There was no time to argue. Barry knew exactly where this was going, and it ended with the both of them lying dead in the street. He turned to the other Tameranian, who had now just made it to his feet.

“Take her. Find somewhere to hide. I’ll give you cover.”

Starfire rapidly shook her head. “No, I’m-” she broke off as twin bolts of green energy slammed into her back. Already weakened by the beating she had taken, the princess slumped to the ground unconscious.

“Sorry, Your Highness.” The Tameranian scooped Starfire into his arms, nodded at Barry, and flew off.

Their chances were slim. But they had a chance. If they could lie low in the aftermath of the battle, find a ship…maybe they could find a new world to settle on. One far from the ruins of...

The Flash looked up mournfully at the Earth. There was nothing he could do to save it. But if he could rescue two innocent refugees from this battle…then his life still had a purpose.

“You!”

Barry slid to the side at superspeed. One of his pursuers had caught up with him. A hurried glance over his shoulder confirmed that the two Kryptonians menacing Starfire had just recovered. In seconds, they would launch themselves after the Princess and her escort.

Unless the Flash intervened.

“Let’s go!” he screamed, mostly to himself. He tapped into every fiber of his being, reaching for his deepest reserves of speed. The Flash began to run in a circle in the center of the street, moving faster than even a Kryptonian could follow.

Within seconds, a tornado had formed.

The four Kryptonians were buffeted by heavy winds so great they couldn’t even fly. The beams launched from their eyes were simply sucked into the storm, fizzing out long before they could reach their target. All the invaders could do was brace themselves and stare at the ever-intensifying tornado. Dust, glass, and even bricks were sucked into the winds, forming a whirlwind of debris.

At its center was a red blur, moving as fast as he ever had.

Barry’s feet were hitting the ground so quickly that lightning was being generated from each step, all from the sheer friction that his feet created. The tendrils of electricity arced into the air, joining the massive tornado and all but blinding his Kryptonian opponents.

Another second. Another. One more. Again! Every moment the whirlwind endured bought more time for Starfire, her escort, and any other members of his team still in the vicinity. Giant chunks of concrete were joining the vortex now, but it wasn't enough. He. Had. To. Keep. Going.

And he did, for two more minutes. But his stamina was finite, and even his determination couldn’t keep it going forever. The Kryptonians still couldn’t fly. Gradually, however, their strength enabled them to push against the slackening storm. Barry, his heart about to burst, could do nothing more to stop their steady approach.

A hand reached into the tornado. Ignoring the electricity jolting across his body, the Kryptonian grabbed Barry by the neck. As the whirlwind stopped and the debris crashed to the ground, the Flash had just enough time to look up at his captor. She was breathing heavily, her eyes shining with murder.

Her arm darted forward, plunging into his chest.

Barry didn’t feel any pain. As his body collapsed onto the pavement, he didn’t notice his blood gushing out onto the street.

In fact, he never felt anything ever again.

\

Supergirl’s fists lashed out against her mother, staggering the matriarch and forcing her back. On the other side of the building, Lena rapidly teleported to avoid the Omega Beams. Each time she reappeared in a different position, the energy immediately locked onto her again.

“Kara!” Lena implored. The supervillain was teleporting in a pattern, one that the Omega Beams could not help but follow.

Got it!

Supergirl fired a blast of heat vision at Alura. Her mother dodged, darting forward with a punch that Kara just managed to avoid. Drawing upon all her combat training, she caught Alura’s feet with her own and redirected the matriarch’s momentum.

Alura stumbled forward…right into the path of the Omega Beams.

The impact sent her careening through the wall. She landed outside on the street, the force of her fall forming a crater. Lena sent Kara a brief smile before teleporting again, two Kryptonite blades forming out of her arms.

Supergirl felt a brief flare of irrational fear as Lena slashed at her mother, clearly going for the kill. The fear turned to disappointment as the green blades left only the slightest grazes on the matriarch’s skin, too shallow to even draw blood.

“Kryptonite? How quaint.” Alura rose to her feet. “The Omega Effect is far more powerful than that chemical concoction.” Her hand lashed out, grabbing one of the blades and immediately shattering it. “Despite all of your brilliance…you have nothing.”

Lena teleported to dodge Alura’s next punch, placing herself in a perfect position to land a scything kick to the back of the matriarch’s head. Alura merely stumbled forward, her eyes already releasing the next burst of Omega energy.

How can we hurt her? Kara was far beyond thinking of nonlethal solutions at this point. If a Kryptonite blade wouldn’t work, snapping Alura’s neck might be the only way. The Omega Effect didn’t make its bearers completely invincible; Darkseid’s death had proven that.

But he was killed by dozens. There’s only two of us.

As her fiancé teleported and dodged away from the beam, Kara shot forward again. Her mother failed to avoid a punch to the stomach, but Alura only grunted in response. The retaliatory backhand sent Supergirl careening into the pavement.

BOOM!

A defensive hard-light shield and the hardened nanites of Lena’s suit collided with the Omega Beams. Alura paused at the edge of the new crater to smirk at the rising cloud of dust, but that was a mistake. Vanity’s nanite whip emerged out of the smoke to lash around Kara’ mother, infused with thousands of volts of electricity.

Supergirl didn’t hesitate. The sight of her mother screaming in pain filled her with unease, but that didn’t stop Kara from unleashing a rapid series of punches to Alura’s sizzling flesh. Lena’s heavily damaged suit was hastily repairing itself, even as the supervillain continued to hold their enemy in place. Supergirl’s fists slammed against Alura’s face, sending the matriarch’s head reeling back.

WHOOSH!

 A blast of super-chilled air erupted from Alura’s lips, throwing Kara through the air once again. A second later, the matriarch lashed out with all her strength and broke the nanite whip into three pieces. Alura’s eyes glowed with the Omega Effect, and Supergirl knew her girlfriend was in no condition to take another blast.

She threw herself at the deadly beam of energy and was instantly filled with unimaginable pain. The blast only held her for a second, but it felt like an eternity of torment. Her bones were melting…her skin disintegrating…

An elongated tendril of nanites wrapped around her body, immediately teleporting her a dozen feet into the air. Breathing heavily, Kara fought off encroaching unconsciousness as dozens of smoke bombs erupted from Lena’s suit. They erupted at once, filling the air with so many diverse and thick gasses that even Supergirl’s x-ray vision couldn’t see though them.

Kara yelped as a pair of hands firmly wrapped around her waist. Still fighting off waves of pain, Supergirl barely noticed as Lena carried her hundreds of feet into the air. The cloud of gas gradually thinned as they rose higher, revealing the ruined skyline of Argo once again.

“What’s…the plan?” Supergirl managed. It was only a matter of seconds before Alura found them again, but she looked at her girlfriend hopefully. This was Lena. She always had a way out, even if it could be messy. This would be no different.

The supervillain coughed. “Remember what I said. Survive.”

Kara barely had time to react before twin beams of Omega energy erupted out of the smoke.

James coughed another glob of blood onto the ground.

Alura’s horde had torn through the remaining drones within minutes. Then they’d descended upon the generator building like a furious swarm, ignoring the few turrets and missile launchers that were still operational. The last line of defense had met them bravely, but that had done little to avail them.

They were outnumbered three to one, and the enemy was individually stronger than every one of them. The Kryptonians largely lacked advanced combat training, but that hardly mattered when their strength and speed tore through the defenders like paper.

Lucy was already gone. She’d charged forward to help a young L-Corp operative about to be ripped in half by two invaders. The remaining Lane sister had fought just furiously enough to give the operative time to scramble away from the melee before she received his intended fate.

That had filled James with a boiling anger. He’d charged forward, his next blow actually managing to knock multiple teeth out of a nearby Kryptonian. That had resulted in five of the invaders ganging up on him, and all the rage in the world hadn’t been able to save him.

A hand wrapped around his throat. “Purity gave orders to let you live, but accidents happen,” his assailant leered, blood pouring from his mouth. The sounds of scattered fighting continued throughout the building, but there was no one near enough to help him. All defenders in his vicinity were dead or unconscious.

The last thing he ever heard was a sickening explosion in the center of the building. In the back of his mind, James realized that meant that the L-Shield had just been taken offline.

The last thing he ever saw were his opponent’s eyes blazing blue with murderous energy.

\

Lois.

Lois had died due to an overdose of Harun-el. At least, that was what Sam had reported. Sam, who Lena had assigned to lead the investigation into Lois’s death. If there was something else at play, something Reign didn’t want her knowing, then Alex had to find out.

Fast.

Reign hadn’t emerged from where Alex had thrown her. The Worldkiller seemed to be struggling with herself, unable to rise to her feet. Alex had not the slightest idea what was going on, but it gave the former hero time to look through her files.

Was Sam actually not a traitor? Mind control, maybe…and now she’s fighting it? There were a lot of things that didn’t make sense about that theory, but nothing was making sense that day.

Lena Luthor was, if nothing else, paranoid. Emails that her employees sent or received through the company email server couldn’t be deleted, and all executive-level employees could view the accounts of any of their peers. It was a draconian system, especially since its creator had the only private email account in the company.

Right now, it was also Alex’s only hope.

Lois. Lois. Sam had been entrusted with handling all investigation of her death. Any emails pertaining to the matter would have been sent to the CFO. Alex’s fingers moved quickly across the keyboard, ignoring the sweat pooling on her forehead. Please let there be something.

It was a longshot, but there was no other option. Alex could not afford to lose this bunker. And whatever was going on, she had no doubt that Reign would come back to herself soon. There was no chance of escape, even if Alex turned the elevator on that very moment.

She reached Sam’s email account easily, searching her inbox for any mention of ‘Lois’. Most of what came up was irrelevant. There were plans for funeral arrangements, discussions about more rigorous testing of Harun-el, condolences for Lucy…

An old email from James. With the subject header Last Statements.

Alex clicked on the message.

Sam,

You’re in charge of the investigation into what happened to Lois, so I’m sending you this email. I was there when Lois died. Lucy was too. She thinks this is all Lena’s fault, but I’m not entirely sure. Lois was…saying some things right before she died. I know it’s probably nonsense, but I owe it to her to report everything. If there’s even a chance something else was at play, you need to know.

Lois kept saying “She’s her!” I have no idea what she was talking about, but she seemed to mention “Worldkiller” at one point. Lois mentioned Harun-el, saying it could…”split her. Fix her.” It doesn’t make sense to me either, and I know her brain was going through tremendous trauma at the moment. Part of me thinks Lois was trying to say something important. I’m grasping at straws, I know, but her last words deserved to be recorded. Even if they were just nonsense.

Best,

James

Alex was just starting to process the implications of the email before a vicious force slammed into her from behind.

Reign had her in a sleeper hold. Alex’s arms were free, but clawing at the Worldkiller’s arms didn’t even loosen her grip. It wouldn’t be long before Alex’s vision blackened, and she woke up in a cell on Argo next to her surviving friends.

Sam said to find Lois. Lois’s last words were that Harun-el could ‘split them’. How? And split who?

Supergirl raced through the air at top speed, very aware that the Omega Beam behind her was gaining with every second. Only years of training and experience with her flight enabled Kara to shift her momentum and turn at the sharpest angle possible, right in front of a building.

The Omega Beam slammed into the metal and concrete, disintegrating an entire floor of the skyscraper.

Kara turned around…only to watch in horror as Lena tried the same trick on her own pursuing beam. The supervillain was similarly trained and experienced with flight, but her suit simply didn’t give her the same mobility as a Kryptonian. The Omega Beam kept up with her turn. Seconds later, it met the CEO’s damaged suit full on.

“NO!”

Supergirl tore after the falling Luthor with all of her speed. Lena was dropping to the ground, unresponsive even as trails of black smoke arose from her form.

She caught her girlfriend just in time. Kara’s heart pounded with relief as she heard a slight groan come out from Lena’s lips, but there was no further response to the hero’s desperate prompting. Half of the nanites were gone from Lena’s mask, revealing some of the supervillain’s messy, scorched, and utterly beautiful face.

Wake up! WAKE UP! She dropped Lena gently on the ground. The CEO’s heart was beating slowly and steadily, but her eyes remained unmoving. Kara was alone.

“Kara!”

Another wave of relief swept through the superhero as Winn dropped down next to her, still brightly glowing green. “Lena! Is she…?”

“I think she’s okay,” Supergirl replied quickly. “But we have to get her out of here before-”

“Before what?”

Alura was hovering a hundred feet above them, looking down at the CEO with cold indifference.

“I’m sorry, Kara, but it’s time for her to die,” the matriarch stated, using the same apologetic yet firm tone she’d employed when denying a five-year-old Kara another piece of candy. “Everything she’s fought for is already lost. This is a mercy.”

Her mother gestured to the sky, and that’s when Kara saw it. Argo was now inside the L-Shield’s radius, which meant their defense had fallen. With a push of a button, Myraid would enslave the entire Earth.

 James. Lucy. If the L-Shield had fallen, what did that mean for the defenders?

Even if there were still standing orders to spare them, that didn’t mean those orders would be followed. Alura might be keen to win her daughter over with targeted acts of mercy, but the rest of Argo probably had no such concerns. James and Lucy were fighters, and they would not have gone down easily. They would have fought back brutally, even outmatched and outnumbered.

What if that brutality had been paid back in full?

Then there were the other teams that had been sent to Argo. Kara hadn’t known their members very well, but she could recognize true heroes when she saw them. The Flash, Cyborg, Starfire, Mr. Terrific…they wouldn’t go down easily either. Alura hadn’t given orders to spare any of them. What if they were already…

That’s when Kara felt it. A faint pulse emitting through the air, briefly sending static through her golden curls.

“Yes, daughter,” Alura intoned, still floating above them. She tapped the com-link in her ear. “Myriad has been activated. My brainwaves have been connected to the broadcast. Everyone on Earth now follows my will.”

No!

She glanced at Winn in despair. The techie hadn’t been affected by Myriad, likely due to the protection of the lantern ring, but the desperation on his face was plain. They’d failed. Earth had fallen.

Eliza. Ruby. Cat. Everyone she’d grown to know and love during her decades on Earth. Tears began to slip from her eyes.

“Don’t worry dear. Even if your adopted sister is under the control of Myriad, I’ll release her. I’ve already sent my best agent to retrieve her.” Alura smiled smugly, as if expecting Kara’s gratitude.

Supergirl’s foot smashed into the ground, sending cracks spreading throughout the pavement. James and Lucy were probably dead, all of Earth was enslaved, and even those who were spared now faced a lifetime of captivity.

She reacted too late as her mother released another blast of Omega Beams at the fallen Luthor. Kara’s heart skipped a beat as Winn stepped forward, his ring projecting an emerald shield. The Omega Beams slammed into the defensive construct, but Winn was undeterred. 

Alura simply sneered, maintaining the beams.

Now! Trembling with righteous fury, Supergirl launched herself at her mother. Alura dodged nonchalantly, still maintaining the Omega Beams, and lashed out at Kara’s chest.

WHAM! Even though Kara had braced herself from the blow, the force still sent her careening back to the ground. A sickening crunch near her stomach told her one of her ribs had been cracked. Wracked with pain, the hero climbed to her knees. Winn was still keeping up his shield, but cracks had begun to form under the tremendous pressure.

“Get her!” he yelled.

Supergirl’s next blast of heat vision was batted aside by a flick of Alura’s wrist. The hero leapt up into the air again, ignoring the agony flaring in her chest, only for her diminished reflexes to utterly fail her. Her mother’s kick landed straight on her shoulder with unholy force, all but shattering the bone. 

Supergirl crumpled back to the ground. Blackness seeped at the edges of her vision.

Kara could do little more than crawl to her knees. “It’s no use…we’ve lost,” she said, spitting up blood. Earth had fallen, her friends were dead, and Alura was undefeatable. Supergirl would never give up when there was still something to fight for…but was there anything left?

Beads of sweat were trailing down Winn’s face as he fought to maintain the shield. The instant it fell, he and Lena would be incinerated by the beams, and he clearly knew it. “Kara,” he managed through gritted teeth. “You don’t believe that. I know you don’t.”

The emerald shield seemed to glow brighter, but it was already starting to splinter under the relentless pressure of the Omega Beams.

She couldn’t fly. The pain was too great for her to even use her heat vision. All Kara could do was cry in impotent rage, sending a last glance at her unconscious lover. Even in the heat of battle, Lena still looked stunning. She was a fallen angel, having given everything to-

Survive.

Kara stared at Lena’s lips, then at Winn’s faltering shield, and knew exactly what she had to do.

“Mom! I surrender! Let them live, and I’ll join you!”

Winn, now on his knees and panting with effort, shook his head fiercely. “Kara, no!”

Alura frowned. “The Luthor is too dangerous to live. I already have you, daughter, and I’m not letting you go again. Your cooperation isn’t required.”

Supergirl spat up another glob of blood. “Yes, it is! You’ve already won…keep Lena prisoner and she’s no threat to you. Let Lena live, even imprisoned, and I’ll join you freely. We can…try to be a family again” She stared firmly into Alura’s eyes. “But if you kill her, I will never stop fighting you. I’ll spend the rest of my life in one of your cells, lashing out at the guards and refusing to speak with you. You’ll never have a daughter again.”

“Kara…she’s too dangerous.”

The hero kept her gaze locked on her mother. “She’s beaten! We’re beaten. Even after everything that’s happened, I thought you still loved me. If you really still see me as your daughter, then honor my request and have mercy. Please.”

Alura sighed. “You will always be my daughter.”

Her Omega Beams finally broke off. Winn collapsed a second afterward. It would take Alura only a thought to finish Lena off, but she simply turned to Kara. “She will be imprisoned for the rest of her life, and her legs and arms will be placed in permanent restraints. You may visit her, but your every interaction will be monitored. If I see a hint of resistance from either of you, she dies.”

Kara dipped her head sadly. “Okay. I won’t try to oppose you, and I’ll make sure she won’t either.” Supergirl averted her gaze, cowed and broken. “Will you let me at least advocate for some mercy for Earth…in ways that won’t hinder your plans?” she begged.

“You’ll have to accept my final decisions,” Alura replied, her gaze softening. “But yes, you may ask for a modicum of restraint.”

The hero bowed her head in acceptance.

Demise

Reign shrugged off the human’s pathetic attempts to drive an elbow into her stomach. Alex was even weaker than the last time they’d fought, Prestilence’s stolen power and most of her Harun-el baving been burned away. She kept up her grip as Alex began heaving for air.

The Worldkiller almost resented being sent on a mission such as this on their day of triumph. Yet it had been important for Alura that her daughter’s adopted sister be brought in alive, and Reign always followed orders. She consoled herself with the knowledge that she’d already done more than enough to contribute to their easy victory this day.

It had been her efforts that had enabled Argo to hack into half of L-Corp’s drone fleet. Her position within L-Corp that had enabled her to report the Luthor’s desperate gambit to destroy Myriad back to her Mistress. And most importantly, it had been Reign’s knowledge of Lena’s thought process that had led Alura to realize the Luthor probably had a backup assassination plan.

Alex was still struggling. Reign couldn’t fathom why. There was literally nothing the human could do-

Pain.

Reign looked down at the sudden agony in her leg. Alex had jabbed a syringe of enhanced nth-metal right through her skin. The pain stung fiercely, but the Worldkiller mentally shrugged it off. A pinprick couldn’t do much more than annoy her.

Unless Luthor gave her Harun-el to use in an emergency. Reign’s heart all but stopped. And-

Lena woke up slowly.

The first thing she noticed as her eyelids fluttered open was Kara sitting on her bedside. Lena instinctively tried to rise to her feet, desiring nothing more than to embrace her girlfriend. Yet her limbs would not obey her.

Her hands and feet were both locked together with large, bulky restraints. The CEO strained against them, but the chrome-like material refused to budge. Even in her disoriented state, Lena immediately grasped that she was now bound with enhanced nth metal.

Kara was dozing softly, bandages on her chest and a brace holding her right shoulder. She was no longer dressed in her normal suit, the costume that Lena had designed to incorporate both the House of El crest and L-Corp’s logo. Instead, the hero was now clad in one of the darker Argonian suits. Her family crest adorned the chest, but the L-Corp logo was nowhere to be seen.

Shit. Lena’s fears were confirmed as her returning vision brought more of the room into focus. There were no windows. A metal door adorned with several bolts blocked what appeared to be the only exit. Save for the comfortable bed Lena was sitting on, it looked exactly like a modern prison cell.

Her brain rapidly put the dots together. Kara surrendered and bargained for my life. Alura agreed to take me prisoner, locking me in these restraints to both keep me contained and to humiliate me. If Kara doesn’t do exactly what Alura wants, I die. Our every communication is now being monitored.

“Kara, tell me this isn’t what it fucking looks like!” she demanded.

The hero rapidly broke out of her dose. Her gasp of relief quickly shifted into a perfect guilty look. “What choice did I have? We’d lost! Myriad was activated. James and Lucy are dead. Barry too! I couldn’t lose anyone else, especially you!”

Lena’s heart dropped. Now she could see the tear lines streaking down Kara’s cheeks, and she knew that statement was no lie. Casualties had been inevitable, but Lena hadn’t been ready to accept them. It had been her duty to protect everyone on the planet, and she had failed.

Maybe it had been a hopeless goal from the beginning, but that didn’t make the guilt sting any less. Especially when Kara was staring at her with blood-red eyes, clearly having spent much of the last few hours sobbing.

“So now I get to spend the rest of my life in a cell?” she spat.

Her girlfriend bristled. “You get to live. Restrained, yes, but you’ll be comfortable. I even convinced my mom not to burn the Harun-el out of you. That’s the condition of my loyalty to Argo: you and the rest of my friends don’t get hurt. No more.”

Harun-el did her no good while restrained with enhanced nth metal. It was another humiliation for Alura to savor. So strong, yet entirely helpless.

“You betrayed the Earth. Betrayed me,” Lena hissed. “How do the rest of your friends feel about this?”

“Those that are left?” Kara growled. “They’ll get over it. Earth was doomed no matter what I did. This way, Earth might get a little better treatment. I made the intelligent, logical choice. You should be proud.”

The supervillain shook her head. “I would have been proud for you to die fighting with everyone else, just like I was prepared to do.”

Supergirl lifted her working arm in exasperation. “I know how smart you are. You always see the best way to move forward.” She paused. “You’ll be thanking me soon enough. Now if you’ll excuse me, I have a meeting to attend to. My mother is addressing the L-Shield’s surviving defenders…those who didn’t evacuate and save their own skins, anyway.” With a huff, she moved over to the metal door and banged on it.

The door slid open to let her through, then slammed closed again.

Despite all the lives she had lost and the planet she had failed to defend, Lena had to repress a smirk. Yes, she was proud. The CEO had known that Kara would surrender and bargain for Lena’s life…planting the idea in her head had just been a formality.

Lena shifted back against her pillow. She’d wanted to tell Kara the extent of her plans from the beginning, and it had taken every ounce of Lena’s self-control to resist the urge. Supergirl was too honest to keep secrets, even from the enemy. Her acting abilities simply weren’t up to the task. If Kara had known the full truth, Alura would’ve realized something was wrong in short order.

The supervillain had hinted just enough to Kara for the hero to grasp that there was some kind of backup plan, and that Kara’s role in that plan was to do her best to ensure Lena’s survival. That was why Supergirl had surrendered.

Kara had faith that Lena had something up her sleeve, even when everything looked hopeless. Lena was honored by that trust.

I hope I deserve it.

\

Sam had been sleeping.

She came to slowly, dragging her muscles over the hard surface below her. For months, she’d been forced to watch Reign use her body to commit atrocities and fool her friends, knowing that the slightest bit of resistance would mean Ruby’s death.

But Sam hadn’t given up. She’d made her play when the time was right, telling Alex to look into Lois’s death and buying her as much time as possible. It had been desperate; there was no guarantee that Alex had Harun-el on her person or would be able to reach some in time. Sam had taken the risk anyway.

It had taken all of her moral courage to do so, knowing Ruby’s life would be at risk. Ruby was her whole world. But Sam knew that her daughter would never forgive her for allowing the Earth to be enslaved, and would expect Sam to take any risk for the slightest chance of stopping it. And Ruby would never, ever have been happy in a world enslaved by Alura, even if she herself had been spared.

Reign had beaten her, in the end, and attacked Alex once again. That was the last thing Sam remembered.

“Sam? Sam?!”

Alex’s voice forced the CFO to open her eyes. She was kneeling on the bunker floor, staring at…herself? The crumpled form of Sam Arias was lying on the floor in front of her, also groaning and struggling to rise to her feet.

Reign.

Alex had done it! They were split! The Harun-el had separated them into two beings, removing the parasitic force that had been placed on Sam at the moment of her birth. She glanced at Alex, and their eyes met.

“It’s you,” the former hero said.

Sam nodded. Her body was still recovering, but her limbs were filled with unfathomable strength. The CFO had never had direct access to the powers of a Kryptonian before, but she’d grown intimately familiar with them throughout the waking nightmare as Reign possessed her body.

Now it was time to use those powers.

Reign’s eyes were just starting to blink open when Sam sprang at her. There were no fancy moves or theatrics. The CFO simply clawed her hands around the Worldkiller’s throat and pinned her to the ground. She dug her fingers into Reign’s flesh. Bruises sprouted almost instantly. The Worldkiller coughed and sputtered, but Sam had already used her knees to pin her enemy’s arms. Alex launched herself forward, adding her comparatively meager strength to Sam’s own and helping to pin the Worldkiller’s legs.

A bright red glow appeared in Reign’s pupils.

Sam slammed her forehead into Reign’s own, relishing in the pain. Maggie Sawyer. Lois Lane. SLAM! The bitch was going to rot in hell for the lives she’d taken, and the agony she’d caused all of Alex’s loved ones. Reign’s nose crumpled under the impact, unleashing a steady torrent of blood. The red glow in the Worldkiller’s eyes faded.

Reign was still struggling desperately. Yet they were of equal strength, and Sam had the advantage of leverage and Alex’s help. Cracks sprouted on the ground, but the CFO refused to be thrown off. Reign used a headbutt of her own, slamming her forehead into Sam’s chin and busting her lip open. Sam simply grinned viciously, spitting a glob of blood into the Worldkiller’s eyes.

That’s for breaking Alex’s heart.

The Worldkiller was clawing at Sam’s arms, heaving for breath. The CFO launched a long blast of heat vision, scorching Reign’s face and driving her head further into the ground. The pressure on Sam’s arms slackened.

And that’s for making my daughter think, even for a second, that I didn’t care about her.

With a final heaving gasp, Reign’s eyes rolled into the back of her head. Sam kept up the pressure, hearing the Worldkiller’s heart continue to beat.

“Sam?” Alex’s voice was soft. She lifted herself off of Reign’s legs. The CFO glanced at the other woman, almost expecting a plea for mercy.

Alex’s tone remained gentle. “Snap the bitch’s neck,” she commanded.

The CFO complied.

When the deed was gone, Sam tossed Reign’s body aside and climbed to her feet. Killing the monster who had tormented her for months was certainly cathartic, but that feeling paled in sensation to her concern for her daughter.

“Where’s Ruby?” she demanded.

“She’s safe,” Alex assured her. Her tone was so certain that Sam believed her instantly. The CFO would require details in the near future, but for the moment she could turn to other concerns.

“Reign disabled half of L-Corp’s drone fleet. The L-Shield-”

“The L-Shield is already down,” Alex interrupted. “While you and Reign were unconscious, I gave the order for our remaining forces to evacuate.” She gestured to the bunker terminal.

Sam stared at her. “How long were we unconscious?”

“About five minutes. I would have killed Reign myself, but I had no way of knowing who was who,” Alex replied. She had clearly figured out the basics of Reign’s possession of Sam, though she undoubtedly had many questions. Sam found herself impressed at the former hero’s quick grasp of the situation, even as her lips formed a scolding frown.

“You should have killed us both. You had no way of knowing who would wake up first.”

Alex smiled grimly. “And incur Ruby’s wrath? Your daughter is scarier than you are.” The former hero’s expression sobered. “Besides, I think we’re going to need you.”

“Need me?” Sam demanded. The full reality of the situation was sinking in now. “If the L-Shield is down, then…” Her heart was beating so quickly that it was painful. Lena was probably dead, along with all of their forces.

If I’d somehow stopped Reign sooner, or realized what was going on…

Alex sighed. “Myriad has been activated. We lost. But you should know your boss well enough to realize that she always has a backup plan.”

“Backup plan?” Sam sputtered. “Everyone on Earth is now just a meat puppet for Alura. Lena…god, she’s probably dead. How can we possibly come back from this?”

“Lena might be dead…Kara could be dead.” Alex’s lip trembled. “Lena knew we would probably fail today. The key was making Alura think we lost completely. Lena realized that for that to work, she would have to send a lot of our forces into a nearly hopeless battle. Including herself. She…she was ready to die.”

Alex was clearly barely holding it together. Sam couldn’t even be bothered to try. “You’re telling me that Lena meant to lose today, knowing it would get most of our forces…our friends…killed? And herself?”

“No. She wanted to win. The forces she held back wouldn’t have made the difference today. She just knew we needed to be prepared for the worst.”

Sam stomped a foot into the metal floor, forgetting her own strength. “And just who did she hold back?”

“You’ll see later. Right now, you need to fly me out of here.”

Kara didn’t have to fake her despair.

She gazed at the rows of prisoners. About a third of the defenders remained to be taken prisoner. Another third had been killed, with the remainder having retreated to their assigned evacuation ships when it became clear further resistance was pointless. Alura had already appointed some of her agents to hunt them down.

“I lost thirty-five of my soldiers in that battle, with another hundred injured. Your girlfriend is lucky I’m merciful. A lot of my lieutenants are clamoring for her execution,” Alura intoned, turning her head to Kara.

Supergirl simply nodded. Hate was almost a foreign concept to her. The enemies she’d fought, aliens and humans alike, frequently disgusted her. Lillian Luthor inspired something that could be called contempt. But this was the first time she’d ever felt hate. It was the first time she fantasized about reaching out her hands and choking the life from an enemy.

Her own mother. Kara still felt love for Alura, but that was for the mother she remembered from her childhood. There was none of that for the woman standing next to her now. Only the desire to snap her neck and end her torrent of gloating and thinly veiled threats.

Eight billion individuals on Earth were now under the control of Myriad. Alura had them on autopilot for now, commanding them to go about their jobs and continue to eat and sleep. From the footage of the cities Kara had seen, things looked almost normal. That is, until the watcher realized that everyone was walking around with blank stares and saying nothing to one another.

They were just robots performing their tasks. Kara had convinced her mother to ensure that infants and invalids continued to receive their regular care, arguing that there was no sense in allowing potentially useful tools to die off. The language had disgusted her, but it had gotten the job done.

In the coming weeks, Alura would delegate control of sections of the planet to her hundreds of agents. They would coordinate Earth’s inhabitants more closely, ordering them to prepare the planet for the arrival of billions of Kryptonians.

“Why not just do it yourself?” Kara demanded, curious in spite of herself.

Alura frowned. “The most I can do on my own is give them a general order to continue their regular routines. Each of my agents will be assigned control of less than twenty million. Then they’ll be able to exercise a bit more fine control…to order large groups of humans to stockpile specific resources and begin to remake the planet in our image. No single mind can exercise detailed over billions of individuals, even your girlfriend.”

I beg to differ, Kara thought. But she said nothing. It would do her no good to remind Alura that her prisoner’s brain was more powerful than a supercomputer.

What is Lena not telling me? She knew her girlfriend had something up her sleeve. Kara had realized it just before the battle had ended. Lena had meant for Kara to survive, just like she’d intended for Kara to beg for the CEO’s own life.

Why the subterfuge? Why not just tell me the real plan?

Deep down, Kara knew the answer. Supergirl would never have accepted the possibility of losing the battle for Earth, as Lena clearly had. More importantly, Alura had needed to see her despair. Only after witnessing her daughter beaten and broken would the matriarch of Argo have let her guard down.

Evidently, Lena had judged Kara’s acting abilities to not be up to the task. So much so that she had taken the risk of Supergirl failing to recognize her hints and act as intended.

No. She was just confident she could manipulate me. It wouldn’t be the first time the CEO maneuvered Kara into doing exactly what she wanted to bring a villain down. That was exactly how Lillian had finally been captured and neutralized. Lena had controlled her like a puppet on a string, allowing her to vaguely realize there was another plan in store too late to give the game away, but just in time to save their lives.

Does Lena know what I’m thinking right now? Did she guess that my distaste for the situation would show at just the right time for Alura to take it for resigned bitterness at our loss? The back of her neck tingled, as if a far away string was gently tugging at her skin.

For now, all Kara could do was play her part.

“This is close enough. Let me down.”

Sam did so. They were in the middle of the Nebraska plains. Nothing was around for miles save for a sea of wheat stalks. “How close are we?”

Alex climbed out of Sam’s arms. “About a hundred miles. Enough for me to be able to run there in a few minutes, even with only a little Harun-el left in my DNA.”

Sam stared at her…girlfriend? Ex-girlfriend? Did Reign’s breakup with Alex even count? It was a pressing concern, but the for the moment the CFO needed to focus on more pressing matters. “What are you talking about? I’m flying us there.”

“You’re not going. Reign is going back to Argo, to tell Alura that she failed to find Alex Danvers. Then you’re going to bide your time and wait. You told me you have been watching Reign’s actions for the last few months. Now you’ll have to copy her.”

“No!” Yet even as she protested, Sam knew it made perfect sense. One didn’t become Lena Luthor’s CFO without having a high IQ. If Reign didn’t return to Argo, Alura would know something was wrong. For Lena’s plan to work, the matriarch needed to have her guard down.

Sam sighed heavily. “Okay, I get it. And you’re not bringing me to the bunker on the off chance at Alura realizes I’m not Reign and tries to torture the information out of me.”

Alex nodded grimly.

“At least tell me-”

“Ruby is down there,” Alex confirmed with a small smile. “Safe, and far enough below ground to be out of the range of Myriad. I’ll let her know…” she paused. “I’ll let her know that you love her, that the last few months haven’t been your fault, and that she was the only thing that kept you going.”

Sam smiled. “Couldn’t have said it better myself.”

“Go on,” Alex demanded. “If you don’t get back soon, Alura’s going to realize something is wrong.”

The CFO simply continued to smile. Earth had just lost a war, most of their friends were missing in action, and Kara was likely in the hands of the enemy. And yet Alex Danvers still stood strong, her face barely even cracking. She had the same look of determination as she always did, as if ready to jump to Argo with nothing but her own two feet and kick the crap out of every invader by herself.

Hot.

Sam mentally scolded herself, but she couldn’t stop the words from coming out of her mouth. “Alex…you know that me breaking up with you…it was Reign. Not me. I know this is hardly the time, but if the worst happens-”

Alex hesitated for only a fraction of a second before stepping forward and claiming Sam in a searing kiss. “I know,” the former hero said briefly, leaning her forehead softly against Sam’s own. “You need to come back to me…so don’t fuck up.”

She descended into the darkness alone. Lena had built this bunker, along with three others just like it, over a mile beneath the Earth’s surface. They’d been built years before, as a last refuge in case the worst ever happened to Lena’s plans. The bunkers were so far underground to be completely undetectable.

To ensure that no electrical signals were in range of the surface, no elevator waited to carry her down. Only an endless circle of descended stairs, accessed through an undescript hatch in the middle of the Great Plains. Lena’s sources informed her, in a rare instance of fortune, that Myriad’s signals couldn’t penetrate that far underground.

Hundreds of people would be there, most having only been informed of its existence mere hours beforehand. It had been hoped that the mole would reveal themselves before knowledge of the bunkers was released to L-Corp’s higherups, a calculation which had proven correct. If not, well, that was why there were four bunkers. They shared communications with one another, but no individual knew where any but their own was located.

Except me.

Her lips still tingled from the kiss. Despite her outward bravado, Alex was terrified. Every time she'd let her guard down and opened her heart to someone, disaster had struck. Maggie. Logically, Alex knew that Sam's possession hadn't been her own fault. Yet her instincts were screaming at her that, soon enough, everything would go wrong again. 

The instinct to kiss Sam had just been a bit stronger. 

Finally reaching her destination, Alex reached into her pocket and pulled out her bunker pass. She pressed it into the slot on the blast doors, wondering who would be the first to greet her. Would it be one of the survivors of the battle in the stars who’d received her order to evacuate, and subsequently were given directions to this facility?

No. No it would not.

“Hi Jess.”

The secretary stood on the other side of the blast doors, scowling with her arms crossed.

Subterfuge

Ow! Damn, my neck is sore.

Jess woke up to see a very familiar woman standing over her. It looked like they were inside a typical bedroom, but the slightly artificial quality of the air informed the secretary that she had been placed far below ground.

“You! Why did you bring me here?!” Jess demanded. I thought you were about to snap my neck.

Selina Kyle shrugged. “Boss’s orders.” The thief was clad in her typical catsuit, a whip infused with strands of nth metal resting in her hand. “Ms. Luthor told me to bring you down here, so I did. Sorry about the chokehold, but…well, I’m a consummate professional. Especially when my boss pays me a fortune.”

Fuck! “I need to get up to the L-Shield. So do you! Argo is-”

“Already here,” Catwoman finished. “And the L-Shield is already down. We’ve already had a few evacuees from the battle join us down here. Myriad was activated.”

No. No, this wasn’t happening. Jess jumped up from the bed like a cannon. “Where’s Ms. Luthor?”

“Unfortunately, I don’t know,” Selina answered. “Look, I get that you’re confused. The short version is: Ms. Luthor expected us to lose. This bunker, and a few others, was her backup plan. She ordered me to bring you here.”

“I-” The secretary’s mind was reeling. Myriad was activated? They’d been expected to lose? “Why didn’t she tell me?! It doesn’t make sense!” Jess growled. “And I still can’t fathom why you were told to ambush me!”

Selina actually looked sympathetic. “Ms. Luthor knew someone she trusted, someone whose clearance level was way above mine, was a mole. No one in her inner circle knew anything about these bunkers until two hours ago. And even if you had known, would you really have been content with waiting down here while our forces stood against five hundred Kryptonians?”

“No!” Jess replied. Her eyes widened in comprehension. “She had me brought down here to save me? I’m no more valuable than any of our other Harun-el infused operatives! How…how could she just…”

“Make that choice for you?” Selina asked, idly wrapping her whip around her wrist. “Weren’t you one of the first ones to join her plan for world domination? You wanted her to make the decisions, and so she did.”

Jess wasn’t sure she was touched that she’d been singled out for safety or enraged that her boss had stolen that choice from her. “What about everyone else up there? Kara’s friends? What gave Lena the right to pick me over…everyone…”

“It was probably in your contract somewhere,” Selina replied. “Personally, I don’t blame her. After all she’s done for the planet, can we really fault her for being just selfish enough to spare one of her friends from danger?”

Jess was barely listening. Another issue had come into her frazzled mind, one far more important. “Luke? Where is he?!” Her hands were shaking with emotion. “Tell me!”

Selina held up a placating hand. “He’s fine. Holly is looking after him; they’re in another room down the hall.” She smiled reassuringly. “My adopted daughter might share my affinity for stealing anything that isn’t tired down, but she’s great with kids.”

Alex Danvers was surprised, and not especially thrilled, to see Jess Huang awaiting her. Having not yet seen much of the bunker, she accompanied the former superhero throughout a tour of the complex.

Even knowing what to have expected, it was still impressive. L-Corp’s drones had done the tunneling and construction work to remain secrecy, but the facilities underground could have supported a large population of individuals for an indefinite amount of time. Food and water were in high supply, there were more than enough comfortable furnishings, and even plenty of entertainment options had been provided.

No sense in letting us all slowly go insane underground. Always makes sense to keep the army’s morale up.

There were hundreds of people in the bunker, though only a minority were infused with Harun-el. Most were support personnel or the immediate family members of the remaining soldiers, in order to keep them from getting distracted.

The unfairness rankled her.

“How long did you know?” she asked Jess as they walked through a chamber lit by artificial sunlight. Alex was unable to keep the accusation out of her voice.

The secretary bristled. “Not until I woke up here. Ms. Luthor asked Selina Kyle to knock me out and bring me to safety. I planned to fight. I…” she paused. “I can’t say I’m not relieved to be down here, alive and with my son,” Jess admitted with a guilty frown.

Alex’s foot scrapped along the floor. The admission had eliminated her anger at Jess, but it had certainly transferred some of that fury to Lena. She’d known that Lena had been forced to make impossible decisions. It had been entirely up to her who was chosen to take part in the war for Earth’s freedom.

The CEO had been playing a careful balancing act, trying to conserve as many of their forces as possible while fooling Alura into thinking she’d committed everything. Alex had understood that. It was why high-profile targets like James, Lucy, the Flash, and Lady Shiva had been deployed in the battle. Jess, as a secretary and one of Kara’s more distant friends, would reasonably escape Alura’s notice.

What bothered Alex was that she knew the choice to keep Jess behind had been a purely selfish one. While Alex’s friends fought on the L-Shield, on Argo, Lena had kept her favorite minion safely back on Earth. Alex hadn’t been given the chance to ask for James and Lucy to be given the same treatment. Now, for all she knew, they could be dead.

No. I can’t believe that. They’re resourceful. Alura had them on the list; they were probably captured. Right?  

They continued through the bunker complex, sharing stories. Alex knew she couldn’t hold in the bombshell for much longer, and duly let it fly.

“Sam was Reign?” Jess’s face was stricken with shock.

Sam tore through the metal walls of the safehouse, tearing through the reinforced structures like paper. Serving as an impromptu mole within Alura’s forces meant doing the matriarch’s dirty work, and right now that required the release of a certain prisoner.

Even if that prisoner had been in charge of the operation that had turned you into a Worldkiller as a newborn. 

She ripped the cell door open, trying to contain her burning anger. Selena of Argo smiled as she stood up from her bed, observing Reign in all her glory. "Well," she said with a smile, "You certainly were my finest creation."

Lena was staring at the ceiling.

How long had she been left alone in this room? There was no clock keeping time, or even a window that would have let her see the rise and fall of Earth’s sun. Unfortunately, Lena’s mind was forcing her to keep count of every second.

So far, she had been confined for three days, two hours, eight minutes, and three seconds. Kara hadn’t come to see her again. No one had, save for a surly guard who brought her food. It was little more than refined paste inhaled through a straw, though anything else would have been difficult to eat with her hands locked together with restraints.

All this time alone had left her very little to do other than ponder her situation. Her plans had already been set in motion, and there was no point in adjusting them until she had more information. In truth, she was living on extra time at this point. Lena had been confident Kara would grasp the implicit instruction to surrender and beg for the CEO’s life, but there had been no guarantee Alura would agree to it. The supervillain's backup plans hadn’t required her personal survival.

She had to be careful. Lena had designed events so that no one captured during the battle would know of her enclaves still on Earth. If Alura had even the slightest inkling that the war was not yet won, all of the CEO's plans would be ruined. Kara had been given just enough hints to ensure that the hero would be willing to surrender, but nothing solid to pin her hopes on. The depression she felt would not have to be faked.

Lena shuffled her head against her pillow. She knew everything. Alura could not be allowed to see any hope or anticipation in her movements or expressions. Fortunately, decades spent with the Luthor family had more than prepared her for concealing her emotions.

The consequence of not having planned to live for this long was that Lena found herself with her first long stretch of free time in years. To distract herself from her guilt and her fears, she turned her mind to the project of finally solving chess. For days, the CEO did little but eat and stare up at the ceiling, analyzing every possible combination of moves.

It was a project that, before L-Corp’s rise to power, was estimated to take decades more even with the world’s most advanced supercomputers set to the task. For Lena, it simply took fifty-five hours of no distractions. Chess was a game of no human emotions or unknown variables. Easy.

Huh. With perfect play on both sides, black can force a win in two hundred moves.

The CEO was just pondering what game to solve next when her door opened to admit her guard. “Alura demands your presence,” he said simply.

\

It took all of her effort not to vomit on the floor.

Kara was constantly being monitored, but she wasn’t imprisoned. The hero had been forced to accompany her mother on a tour of the Earth, viewing “their new domain”. Humanity continued to perform their usual routines, shambling through their lives with empty expressions.

Can they perceive what is happening? Or are they just unconscious? Kara hoped with all of her heart that it was the latter.

“Myriad has been synched precisely with my brainwaves. It will take a few more weeks to disperse control to the other Kryptonians,” Alura was saying. “Once that happens, we can exercise some more fine control of the human race finally begin to rebuild our world.”

Supergirl nodded, not trusting herself to speak.

The matriarch placed a hand on Kara’s shoulder. “I know this is hard for you. I don’t blame you for forming attachments to a planet that was your home for decades.” She shot Kara an indulgent smile. “With time, the pain will fade. For now, I think you’ve earned a reward.”

The hero lifted an eyebrow.

“Let’s invite your girlfriend to dinner.”

\

Kara watched as her fiancé was escorted into the room.

Lena was all but hobbling through the doorway thanks to her restraints. The metal cuffs entirely covered her hands, binding them closely together. The shackles on her legs were smaller, not covering her feet, but the CEO’s ankles were still bound so tightly that she had to hop to her seat.

Alura had had one of the antechambers of her office converted into a private dining room. In contrast to the decaying metal and concrete that comprised most of Argo, this room was well-furnished and adorned with stark-white paint.

Alura waved away Lena’s guard. “You may sit,” she said, gesturing to the chair beside Kara.

Lena kept her face utterly emotionless as she moved to her seat, save for a twinge of displeasure as her gaze passed over Kara. It was so believable that the hero actually felt her stomach turning. Was I wrong? Did Lena not want me to save her life…is she disgusted with me? 

Supergirl felt another tug on her invisible string. That’s how she wants me to feel. She wants Alura to see my guilt.

“I understand this is awkward, but you must know, Lena dear, that none of our conflict was ever personal. You defended your world to the best of your ability, and I fought for my people. There was a winner…and a loser.” She nodded at Lena. “

The Luthor scoffed. “The assassination attempts felt rather personal.”

Alura stroked the arm of her chair. “It might have been personal for Reign. I’ll admit that. She was forged to be a weapon, after all. And after having spent so much time in close proximity with you, she obviously grew a bit frustrated.”

Lena’s eyes widened slightly, but it was Kara who spoke. “Close proximity?” she demanded.

“Reign was Sam Arias,” Alura replied casually, as if answering a question about the weather. “She was a Kryptonian I sent to Earth shortly after Argo survived Krypton’s explosion. We imprinted a pre-determined personality within her, but it took years to manifest and take control. A human personality developed in the meantime, one with no knowledge of her origins or access to her power. Reign emerged some years ago, unlocking her body’s Kryptonian DNA and gradually assuming control.”

Neither Kara nor Lena could hide their looks of incredulity. Sam?! No one spoke for several seconds, Alura calmly reclining in her chair as her guests tried to process the revelation.

“Sam saved my life once,” Lena finally whispered. “Where is she?”

Alura shrugged. “I’m afraid that the human personality was suppressed. She’s gone. Reign is currently supervising matters on Earth, at my direction. She still hasn’t located Alex Danvers, though I suppose that’s not too surprising. Earth is a large planet, after all. It’s part of the reason why we chose it.”

Whether Lena would have been able to control her emotions, Kara would never know. Supergirl perceived the shock, rage, and sorrow on her lover’s face. It was the sight of unadulterated grief in Lena’s expression, more than anything, that pushed Kara over the edge.

She launched herself out of her seat, her eyes brimming with heat.

“Need I remind you what is at stake?” Alura asked, her voice now an icy calm. Her gaze landed on Lena.

No! I can’t lose anyone else. Especially not her! Never her… Kara collapsed back into her chair, the heat vision in her pupils fading away. It was only through drawing upon her sheer anger that the hero was able to keep the tears at bay. You better have a plan, Lena. You better! 

“Good. Let us eat!” Alura clapped her hands twice. Five Kryptonians entered the room on her signal, bringing with them a large selection of Earth delicacies. To Lena, who probably hadn’t eaten real food in days, the aroma alone must have been irresistible.

The matriarch motioned to the white tablecloth, upon which sat three sets of gleaming utensils.

Kara glared at her mother. “Take off her restraints.”

Alura shook her head, as if slightly regretful. “I can’t take chances. Besides, they were made with some enhanced nth metal produced by L-Corp. Utterly unbreakable once molded. I couldn’t remove them if I wanted to. I’m afraid Lena must simply adjust.”

Supergirl’s chest panged. Alura simply began eating, paying the Luthor no further mind. Lena looked away from her food, staring straight at the opposite wall.

The matriarch looked up from her steak. “Your manners are appreciated, but I can look past a lack of elegance on this occasion. I’m sure Kara could likewise forgive a few spills.”

Kara didn’t hesitate. Ignoring her own food, she grabbed her utensils and began to cut her fiance’s meat into tiny pieces. Lena simply sat, stone-faced, but there was no way the hero was going to let her go hungry or force her to eat like an animal.

She placed a piece of meat on her fork, holding it up for Lena. A single tense moment passed before the CEO leaned forward, taking the bite and chewing gracefully. Alura was looking at them gravely, her lips tinged with disappointment, but Kara paid her no mind before repeating the process several times. The hero then lifted her girlfriend’s glass, allowing her to take a long sip.

Lena shot her the briefest, smallest smile.

“You should know that Reign released Selena two days ago,” Alura spoke up. “I imagine you might have been hoping that she would perish once her captors were subsumed by Myriad and left her alone.”

The CEO gave an impassive shrug. “I didn’t really care one way or the other. She was no of use to me.” The supervillain took another sip from the goblet in Kara’s hands.

“Yes. I know you dabbled in mind control, but I suppose the will of a Kryptonian was too difficult to break,” Alura replied with a smile. “Still, I must remember to give Selena a commendation. If you had broken her, imagine all she could have told you. Selena was responsible for the Worldbuilder program, you know.”

Supergirl’s hands began to shake, nearly sending liquid splashing over her girlfriend. As far as Alura knew, Lena was completely beaten. There was no point in taunting her. This was simply her mother’s idea of a fun evening.

Bile rose in Kara’s throat. Or maybe this is my punishment for begging for her life?

Winn sat in his cell, unable to keep his fists from clenching in frustration. This was his second time he was imprisoned in Argo, and while this stay was free of torture, it was made far worse by the knowledge of what was happening on the outside world.

James and Lucy were gone. No more game nights or Thanksgiving dinners for them. There was no chance of James ever winning his coveted Pulitzer, or Lucy moving out of her father’s shadow and avenging her sister.

Nothing for me either. The last time he’d escaped, the ring had come to him. There had been no such luck for him this time. He’d woken up after the battle with the ring gone, and Kara had admitted during her visits that she didn’t know where it was. Alura was probably keeping it contained somehow, forever out of his reach.

He’d spent hours exerting his willpower, trying to summon the ring. I need your help. Let my will charge your energy. Come to me.

Maybe Kara could get it for him, one day. Winn couldn’t believe that she’d surrendered, even if he understood her reasons. Giving up in order to save Lena and earn some better treatment for the Earth made sense for most people, but not Supergirl. There had to be something else at play, something she couldn’t tell him about.

Or maybe he was just lying to himself.

“Princess Koriand’r and her escort have reached our bunker.”

Alex nodded. “Good,” she replied, cutting off communication with their Siberian base. Starfire probably wasn’t pleased to learn that Lena had been keeping her in the dark. There was a lot of that going around. Between the many L-Corp executives who’d been informed at the last minute to the evacuees of the battle above who’d received sudden bunker coordinates, there was a lot of resentment of Lena Luthor floating around.

She felt it too. But there was no denying that the CEO’s plan was brilliant in its scope and simplicity. Now that their secret weapon was deployed, all they needed to do was wait. Their underground bunkers continued to create Harun-el as fast as possible, and there were more than enough operatives standing by who’d already been pre-tested for the substances. Their drone facilities similarly continued to work apace. Within six months, they would have more than enough soldiers ready.

Alura’s army had been unbeatable in a pitched battle. They’d been more than prepared with protective suits that limited the effectiveness of Kryptonite. But when they were scattered around the Earth coordinating Myriad, they would be unprepared and vulnerable.

She’d always been afraid that Kara would be ambushed with Kryptonite, unable to fight back or call for help. That fear had almost been realized when Metallo had attacked Supergirl in her apartment. As powerful as the hero was, a sudden attack with her weakness was incredibly dangerous.

Lena, it seemed, had learned that lesson well.

Soon, they would have enough soldiers armed with Kryptonite to take down every Kryptonian stationed on Earth. That would immediately put the numbers in their favor. After that, all they would need to do is swarm Argo and take Alura and her remaining defenders down. The matriarch was incredibly powerful, but she’d be outnumbered ten to one.
