It was a few hours after her lovely dinner with Alura that Lena’s cell door opened again. In stepped Sam Arias, clad in Reign’s uniform save for her distinctive mask. The Worldkiller sauntered into the room, folding her arms and smirking.

How did I not know? Lena’s brain might be more powerful than a supercomputer, but it was far more prone to glitches. A computer would have analyzed the facial similarities, tonal inflections, and other clues to have found the truth. Lena had been so blinded by respect for her friend that she’d never even considered the possibility of her betrayal.

“Here to gloat?” she demanded bitterly.

Reign scoffed. “Didn’t I tell you that Earth had no chance? You could have simply died months ago and saved everyone so much suffering. Now all you’ve gained is a lifetime as Alura’s plaything, at least until Kara grows tired of you. When that happens, I’ll execute you myself.”

Lena narrowed her eyes.

“Sam was a true friend of yours, you know,” Reign continued. “But the other personality inside her proved far stronger. It took years, but eventually the right personality won out. The true one.”

Yes!

Lena knew that every moment in her cell was being closely monitored, but the slight inflection in her visitor’s tone gave her hope. The CEO raised her eyebrows slightly, wordlessly asking the question. Sam’s chin dipped a fraction of an inch in response.

She kept the bitterness in her tone. “You lied to me for years. How do I know that anything you say is true?” ‘How do I know you’re really Sam?’

“I guess you don’t,” Sam replied easily. “After all, even Ruby didn’t realize when her mother’s personality was subsumed by a Worldkiller. Ruby meant more to Sam than anything, even L-Corp.” Sam unfolded her arms, quietly tracing a hand along the left side of her chest.

Her heart. Sam always said that Ruby was her heart. Reign might have heard her say that, but she wouldn’t have cared enough to remember. This is Sam. Lena dipped her head slightly in return, acknowledging the truth.

“I suppose I’m here to see how the brilliant and powerful Lena Luthor has fallen. But I’m afraid I must go. Now that your world has fallen, there are so many tasks that require my attention,” she preened. “Alex Danvers, for one. I couldn’t find her the day of the invasion, but she’ll show herself eventually.”

Lena didn’t miss how two of Sam’s fingers narrowly crossed during that sentence. Reign did find Alex. Somehow, Alex must have set Sam free. That means that Alex told her about my backup plan.  

“Whatever.” Lena waved a hand. “Keeping serving as Alura’a lapdog, if that’s what really makes you happy.” ‘Keep acting as a mole until the time is right.’

“Serving my mistress is my only desire,” Sam replied. “Enjoy your time in this cell. How long do you think you’ll be here…before Alura decides to execute you?” ‘How long is your plan going to take?’

The supervillain shrugged. “Maybe not too long, but we’ll see how it goes.” ‘Not too long, but it’s out of my hands right now.’

With a final smirk, Sam turned and turned through the door.

“You’re a monster, you know,” Lena said. “I’m only sorry I didn’t see it sooner.” ‘I’m so sorry I couldn’t help you.’

The Worldkiller looked over her shoulder. “Don’t blame yourself, Luthor. There was nothing you could have done to stop me.” ‘It’s not your fault. You couldn’t have known.’

Lena sat back on her bed as the door slammed shut. There was fierce exultation in her veins, but she fought to keep it down. Focusing on her guilt made it far easier.

No. Because I chose not to.

Culling

“You wanted to see me?”

Alex nodded as Ruby walked into her room. It wasn’t much of a space, having been carved out of the Earth, but some simple furnishings and the thick blanket made it surprisingly comfortable. The constant din of drone production in the background had initially been distracting, but after two weeks underground it barely registered in her thoughts.

She smiled at the girl as she sat on the small bed. “Ruby, I noticed you’ve been…well, a bit out of it.” In their time underground, Alex had observed Sam’s daughter generally walking around aimlessly, rarely interacting with the other children. Perhaps unsurprising, but not something Alex was able to ignore. 

Ruby shot her a questioning smirk. “Well, yeah. You do know that we’re in hiding a mile underground from a force that has invaded Earth, right? And that I haven’t seen my mother…my real mother, for months. Oh!” her eyes lit up. “There’s also the fact that I found out I’ve been living with a Worldkiller who was wearing my mom's skin!”

“Point taken,” Alex agreed. “But if there’s anything else…you know you can talk to me, right?” The former hero wasn’t sure why exactly Ruby’s happiness was such a priority for her, but there was no doubt that it was. Maybe it was her natural affinity for children despite having had so little opportunity to spend time with them. Or it could have been that she felt she owed it to Sam to look after her daughter while the CFO couldn’t.

And, in the back of her mind, maybe she’d once briefly entertained the idea that Ruby would be her daughter one day…before everything had gone to hell.

When Ruby didn’t say anything, Alex continued. “You know your mom wanted to see you more than anything, right? I wouldn’t let her come here. She saw the logic in that, but the pain in her eyes…” the older woman sighed. “I don’t think she would have gone back to Argo if she thought you couldn’t handle it. You’re her whole world, you know. She knew you would be strong enough without her, no matter how much it hurt. I’m sorry.”

“It’s not that.” Ruby stood up from the bed, crossing her arms. “I don’t blame my mom for anything. She’s always done the right thing, no matter what. She’s still the same person she was when I was three years old and we were dirt poor. Whenever it came for sacrifices, she would put me first, others second, and herself last. That didn’t change after she became a CFO.”

Alex raised an eyebrow. Was that…guilt she heard in Ruby’s voice?

“Ruby, you can’t blame yourself for any of this.”

The girl stomped her foot on the floor. “I knew my mom better than anyone! We always promised to protect each other, no matter what. She lived up to that promise. I couldn’t protect her when I was a kid, and I understand that. When you’re practically homeless and barely have enough to eat, there’s only so much a five-year-old can do.” She paused, staring at the floor. “But I could have realized something was wrong. How could I…why didn’t I realize a monster was possession my mom? I should have!”

Wow. A horribly selfish feeling rose up in Alex. Sam really was the luckiest woman in the world. To have a daughter like that…not even a teenager yet so conscientious. Alex couldn’t help the feelings of longing that erupted.

If I ever become a mother, I could never hope for a daughter as good as you.

“Denial is a powerful thing,” she replied. “Who would ever want to believe their mother had been possessed? Hell, we didn’t even know such a thing was possible. And you did notice something was wrong, even if you didn’t realize what was actually going on,” Alex told her. “I’ll never forget you yelling at Lena Luthor to stop overworking your mom.” She smiled fondly at the memory.

Ruby bit her lip, sitting on the floor and leaning her back against the bedframe. “It didn’t exactly do my mom any good in the end.”

“Ruby, you saved her.” This immediately earned her a skeptical look from the girl, but Alex went on. “When Sam broke free of Reign…she told me it was the hardest thing she’d ever done. It was her love for you that gave her that strength. If it wasn’t for you, Reign would still be alive and I’d be a prisoner on Argo.”

A gasp erupted from Ruby. There was the briefest look of gratitude on her face before she spun around, wrapping her arms around Alex’s legs and burying her face into the former hero’s knees. “I just want my mom back.”

Alex lifted Ruby off the floor, sitting the girl back on the bed and wiping a stray tear from her eye. “Of course you do. What, you think it makes you weak if you cry?” she asked, noticing Ruby’s renewed guilty frown. “It means that you care. I’ve cried for Kara. More than once.”

“Ha!” The sadness disappeared from Ruby’s eyes. “You were good for my mom, you know. I hope you don’t let what happened stop you from trying again.”

The older woman smiled once again. “You really want her to be happy, don’t you kiddo?”

“Yeah,” Ruby agreed, before frowning in indignation. “And don’t call me a kid. I’m thirteen, you know!”

“Still a kid.” Alex’s fingers slipped under Ruby’s arm, tickling her and playfully shoving the girl sideways onto the blanket. “When you’re bragging about how old you are, you’re still a kid. You’re not an adult until birthdays scare the hell out of you.”

Ruby was silent for several moments. The slight twinging in her fingers implied that the girl was pondering a counterpoint, but memories of her mother’s birthdays was probably proving Alex’s point.

“Touché,” the girl agreed with a slight grin. Her eyes looked toward the bedroom door briefly before she turned her gaze back to Alex, a hopeful look in her eyes.  

“You mind if I stay here tonight?” Ruby asked.

Alex smiled. “Sure thing, kid.”

\

“You wanted to see me?”

Alura nodded. “Walk with me.” She turned around, setting a brisk pace down the corridor and beckoning Kara to follow. They moved through the hallways silently, their feet carrying them through some of the more well-maintained sections of Argo’s central building.

The silence was uncomfortable, but Kara couldn’t bring herself to say anything to the monster while next to her. Alura didn’t seem intent on speaking either, so the hero instead turned to look out the windows. Argo had been brought within Earth’s atmosphere, allowing the city to drop its protective shield for the first time in over a decade. This both conserved power and gave its residents a welcome respite from staring into the endless depths of space.

“Here.” Alura stopped outside a door flanked by two guardsmen. The matriarch nodded to them as she walked up to the security system. Only after inputting a long password at superspeed, placing her fingers on the scanner, and allowing her retina to be verified did the heavily fortified door open.

Supergirl’s eyes narrowed. Even that security system wouldn’t prevent a Kryptonian from simply blasting their way through the walls. All it did was prevent someone from sneaking in undetected. But if the guards were busy elsewhere…

It was a simple elevator that awaited them. Kara stepped inside next to mother, nearly shivering with revulsion at the close contact. The compartment dropped down far underground, opening to reveal…

Pods.

It was the largest room Kara had ever seen. Row after row of tightly packed pods stretched for an impossibly long distance, illuminated only by dimly flickering lights overhead. Even with her incredible eyesight, Supergirl couldn’t hope to see them all.

There were thousands, no, millions. More? The room was deathly silent, filled with nothing but the pods and steadily gathering dust.

“This is what remains of our people, Kara. Three billion Kryptonians. They’ve been asleep for fifteen years, and I refuse to let them wait any longer.”

The darkness of the Phantom Zone stretched out endlessly. Sinister voices whispered at the edges of her consciousness, seeking their way in. Even as she slept, they slipped into her dreams…

Supergirl blinked her eyes rapidly, pulling herself out of the memory.

“Why…why bring me here?”

Alura sighed. “I wanted to remind you what was at stake. I know how you’re going to react to what comes next, but it simply has to be done. All of these souls are now in my hands, and their future is my responsibility. I will not let our people wait one second longer than absolutely necessary.”

“Control over Myriad is being transferred to four hundred Kryptonians next week,” Kara reminded her. Saying the words disgusted her…pretending that she was okay with what was happening on any level was sickening. But information was key. “Our estimates say that it will take four years after that for Earth to be ready for colonization. Even with fine control over the human race dispersed among our operatives, remaking a planet is a difficult task.”

The matriarch placed a hand on one of the pods. Her finger trailed lightly over the surface, moving aside a layer of dust. “Yes, and I can’t take that chance. Every day we wait risks a power failure, or another attack by an alien force. I’m moving up the timetable. Release protocols will begin in exactly one year. Bringing them all out of hypersleep safely will require an additional two days.”

“Food distribution channels won’t be ready!” Kara protested. “They’ll starve!” Her concern was genuine but was laced with another fear. If the pods were woken up, three billion new Kryptonians would crush whatever Lena was planning.

“Unless we change our plans,” Alura replied. “A culling will be required.”

Kara stared at her. “A culling?”

Her mother nodded, as if confirming an unwelcome change in the weather. “Roughly one billion of the humans will be allowed to starve. Those too old, injured, or otherwise incapable of working or bearing children. With the resources saved by letting them die, we can release our people within a year.”

One. Billion. Supergirl wouldn’t have thought it possible, but her hatred of Alura had just increased. “No. NO! You promised me you would listen-”

“I have listened,” Alura cut her off. “I never promised I would do as you suggested.”

Kara’s feet were vibrating so quickly that they began to burn through the floor. “You…genocidal bitch! I won’t let this happen. I will fight you, over and over again, until I break your neck or die from exhaustion. And if I win, I will spit on your grave!”

“You will comply with my wishes, daughter, or I will execute your friends one by one. Do not mistake my mercy for forgiveness. Defy me in any way, and they will pay for your actions,” the matriarch promised. “Look around you, Kara. Remember what’s important! And fall in line…or I will make you.”

Supergirl’s eyes began to glow with blue energy. How satisfying it would be to fire the beams directly at Alura's skull...

“Careful, daughter,” Alura reproached her. “I will execute your friends if you defy me.”

I hate you. “You’re a monster,” Kara hissed. It was an immature, simple thought, but it was all her brain could conjure after learning that her mother was planning to commit the biggest mass murder in known history.

“I am not. If you do force me to execute your friends, most will be disposed of humanely. We still have a large stock of the Black Mercy, you know. I will use them on our prisoners, allowing them to die while living their happiest fantasies.”

A plant that drains the life of its victims while feeding them their heart’s desires. That was Alura’s idea of mercy?

The matriarch sighed. “Of course, Ms. Luthor has already been infected by a Black Mercy and so has developed an immunity to the plant. I suppose poison would be an efficient way of killing her quickly, but there are other options. Should I consider them necessary.”

If it was truly a choice between resistance and surrender, Kara would have chosen the former. Supergirl would have challenged Alura despite the impossible odds, knowing that none of her friends would have ever wanted to live in the world the matriarch was building. If she had less than a one-in-a-million chance of defeating her mother, the hero would have taken those odds.

Only she didn’t. Kara still had faith in her girlfriend.

\

Sam had returned to ‘gloat’ once again.

“Culling?” Lena demanded.

The Worldkiller nodded. “One billion humans. It will begin as soon as control of Myriad is transferred to our operatives across the planet, four days from now. Oh, I’m sure Alura would be more than happy to do it herself at this very moment, but even her brilliant mind couldn’t exercise that much fine control. We might lose valuable slaves while killing the weak!”

All of Lena’s plans were shattered. She’d directed her forces into hiding to buy time. Six months would have given her a force of drones and Harun-el infused soldiers to ensure her victory. Alura might have captured the Queen, but she’d already been in checkmate.

Lena had two options. She could direct her forces to attack early, risking utter destruction and ending Earth’s last hope…or wait, and sacrifice a portion of the planet’s population so the rest could live.

She wasn’t afraid to make sacrifices. The CEO had sent Kara and Alex to Argo simply to confuse Alura, accepted that many of her agents would die in the first battle against Argo, and given into the inevitability of Earth’s population being controlled by Myriad for a period of time. Lena felt the guilt of each and every one of those sacrifices, and she’d moved forward because there was no other way.

But this is too much. It has to be.

For all her brainpower, Lena didn’t know whether taking the chance and striking early was the moral decision or the weak one. Compassion was both a strength and a vulnerability, but in this situation…?

Killing innocents, or allowing them to die, was never something to be done lightly. Anyone who could write off the death of an innocent as an acceptable loss was a sociopath at best. Yet when the lives of seven billion people and their countless descendants were at stake, was sacrificing one-eighth of Earth’s population really the wrong move?

Maybe a perfect leader would make that choice…and agonize over it for the rest of their lives. Lena couldn’t help but suspect that she was making a foolish decision. An understandable one, yes, and it was driven by the compassion that had made her such a force for good in the world. But foolish nonetheless. 

If I strike early and succeed, I’ll be hailed as a supremely moral leader who made a brave choice and saved a billion lives. If I strike early and fail, any denizens of Earth who happen to survive will remember me as the fool whose idealism doomed everyone on the planet.

Even though she was a supervillain, Lena considered herself very moral in one sense. When the right decision was obvious, she could make it easily and without hesitation whatever the personal cost. But she wasn’t always so great at determining which choice was the moral one.

Lena Luthor generally considered herself a utilitarian, who prioritized the lives and happiness of the innocent. That moral philosophy now demanded that she allow one billion to perish so seven billion could live. Kara would disagree with such a decision, but as much as Lena loved her hero…Supergirl wasn’t always right.

But in the end, I’m only human.

Lillian and Lex, the two individuals Lena despised above all others, would have made the sacrifice of a billion willingly and without hesitation. Kara, the person Lena loved most in the world, would have never even considered it. And yet the more Lena thought about it, the more she believed that the right thing to do was to heed the needs of the many and let the few die.

I really am a Luthor.

Except, she couldn’t do it. Lena couldn’t stand back and watch a billion die, even knowing what was at stake. The same human emotions that disrupted her otherwise-supreme intelligence wouldn’t let her go through with it.

“I’ll leave you to reflect on the price of your failure,” Sam said. ‘I’ll give you some time to think of a plan.’ “How long before you simply give into despair, I wonder?” ‘How long do you need to think of a plan?’

Not long. The optimal course of action sprouted in her mind almost immediately, though it would require some fine tuning. Unlike her previous strategy, it was far from an obvious victory.

“You and Alura. The two of you can burn in fucking hell!” Two hours. Of course, a plan would be pointless if Lena didn’t have a way to escape, and that meant she had to play her best card. Sam needed to know the truth, and there was no way to reveal that without speaking to her directly.

The CEO lunged forward, lashing out with her restrained hands and clubbing her fists into Sam’s stomach. For a brief moment they were entangled in a melee, and Lena seized her one chance to speak the words. All three of them, hissed softly through clenched teeth.

Sam was so stunned she barely realized it was time for her to shove Lena back. Her eyes were widened in wonder, amazement, confusion, and horror. There were clearly a thousand questions burning in the CFO’s mind, but Lena knew one would stand out above the rest.

She shook her head ever so slightly. ‘No, I didn’t know you were Reign. You’ll get the full story later.’

Sam nodded a fraction of an inch before turning and marching out of the room. Her lips were issuing the venomous taunts that Alura would expect to hear, but Lena’s ears barely registered them. Every neuron of her brain was focused on her plan. Contingencies. Misdirections. Sacrifices.

\

Why didn’t you ask her, Lena? Why?

Sam now understood why Kara and Alex had been sent to Argo, but so many questions continued to plague her. The CFO forced herself to calm, calling up memories of Ruby in her mind. The thoughts steadied her, if only slightly.

I will see you soon, my love.

Kara couldn’t be brought into the loop yet, not with the listening devices Alura had doubtlessly placed on her suit. Soon enough, Lena’s secret weapon would have them disabled. Fortunately, as a trusted agent of Argo, Sam wasn’t being bugged.

Neither was her contact.

It took some close analysis of the scheduling, but Sam was eventually able to speak with her target privately. Once the CFO revealed her status as a mole, her words were accepted without any complaint. With the target's high clearance level- higher than Reign’s-, it would be arranged so that the footage and audio of Lena’s cell would be played on a loop for several hours. 

After giving the contact time to do her work, Sam returned to Lena. She wanted to scream at the other woman, demand how she hadn’t known her CFO was a Worldkiller, but current events stayed her hand. There was too much at stake to waste time satisfying her burning curiosity.

Lena placed her hands on the table, the heavy restraints sending a thump echoing throughout the small room. “Well,” she began. “Let’s pray I’m as smart as I think I am, or we’re all fucked.”

\

Even as the door opened to admit their guest, Alex couldn’t believe her eyes.

“How did you find us?!” she demanded as Sam stepped into the bunker. Had she been taken over by Reign again, somehow, and sent by Alura to wipe them out? Had Alex helped kill the wrong one by mistake? Why…?

“Lena told me where you were. There’s been a change of plans.”

What? “That can’t be right. We don’t have nearly enough drones and soldiers yet. A horde of Kryptonite is useless if we don’t have enough units to deploy it. We’re not ready.”

Sam nodded. “I know, but it doesn’t matter. Alura’s soldiers are going to be stationed throughout Earth in three days. As soon as they’re given control of Myriad and can give detailed orders to the human population, they’re going to kill anyone not of use to them. At least a billion deaths…possibly more.”

Alex reeled back as if struck. It wasn’t easy to rattle her, but that news certainly did the trick.

She breathed deeply for several seconds, forcing herself to remain in control. At the very least, Lena was still alive and had formed an adaptation to her plan. “Kara,” she said suddenly. “Winn, James, Lucy. Are they…”

The CFO’s face fell. “Kara and Winn are prisoners. James and Lucy didn’t make it. I’m so sorry.” She started to move forward, as if to embrace Alex in a hug, but seemed to think better of it.

Her knees were wobbling. After hearing Lena’s plans, Alex had accepted that their initial force would take casualties. Yet she had refused to believe that her friends would be part of that sacrifice. It wasn’t right. It wasn’t fair.

And how many others have lost people in this war? What gives me the right to keep everyone I care about?

And yet Lena had saved Jess. A very human decision, but one that hit hard all the same. Alex grunted, all but forcing her river of anger along a different course. Lena had been selfish, and there would be a reckoning for that, but it was Alura who was really responsible. She was the one who had taken all of these lives, and was preparing to kill far more. James and Lucy’s deaths were on her hands, and a lack of Harun-el wouldn’t stop Alex from avenging them.

Alex was so engrossed in her memories of her friends…victories won and celebrated…holidays shared…game nights fought to the bitter end…that she barely registered the change of expression on Sam’s face.

“Mommy!”

Ruby had clearly just awoken in bed, but that didn’t stop her from running across the bunker and jumping into her mother’s arms. Sam reciprocated the hug instantly, wrapping her arms around her daughter and whispering sweet nothings through her tears. The CFO maneuvered Ruby’s hand over her beating heart, and Alex knew exactly what was being said even as she was unable to hear.

The right thing to do in Sam’s position would have been to dismiss Ruby immediately. Every second that Sam delayed relaying Lena’s instructions to Alex and returning to Argo increased the possibility that Alura would learn something was amiss. One girl’s happiness could not compare to the fate of an entire planet.

And yet Sam hugged her daughter even tighter. She was human too.

\

The next few days passed quickly. Lena simply sat in her cell, going over the details in her mind. Any refinements to her plan were passed on to Sam, who had come to her cell to ‘gloat’ each day. She hadn’t been permitted to see Kara. No doubt the hero was being subtly punished for helping Lena avoid humiliation at Alura’s dinner table.

It was probably a good thing. Lena was afraid, and she wanted nothing more than to crawl into her hero’s arms and be assured that everything would be alright. The CEO wasn’t certain she would be able to resist the next time Kara visited, which would obviously reveal to Alura that Lena still had hope.

Then the day came. Lena had no way of knowing at precisely which time she would be released; it would be up to her agents to time the moment perfectly. Too soon, and Alura would discover her plans before they could be implemented. Too late, and countless millions would perish.

Swish.

Lena looked up, her heart pounding. It wasn’t Sam who stood on the other side of the opening door. It was Argo’s second-in-command, Alura’s confidant, and the immediate superior of the Worldkillers.

“Selena.”

Taking Control

Kara was going to do it. What choice did she have? There was no more time for waiting. Alura would be transferring control of Myriad to her subordinates scattered throughout the Earth in ten minutes, and the slaughter would begin.

Even Supergirl couldn’t hope to do it alone. Clenching her fists, Kara silently made her way through the halls of Argo. Most of the Kryptonian force was now on Earth, and the few she passed by gave her little more than a passing glance. That was going to change very soon, the instant she broke down the door to Lena’s cell.

Alura was now in her office, about to coordinate with Argo’s technicians to begin the transfer. She’d all but demanded that Kara join her, but the hero had sulked off. It had been a challenge to hide her rage, so Kara had adapted. Anger and despair were rather similar, and it had been all too easy to pass off the former as the latter.

Two sets of footsteps, echoed down the corridor. One was very familiar.

Lena!  

Supergirl raced down the hallway, stealth and subterfuge forgotten. The instant her eyes saw Lena being escorted down the hallway by Selena, the hero didn’t hesitate.

She darted forward at maximum speed, slamming Selena into the wall and all but breaking it apart. Suffer. After weeks of helplessness, forced to watch her friends and fiancé held prisoner by a monster, it was the height of catharsis to finally cut loose. Two punches immediately broke her enemy’s nose, creating a quick splatter of blood.

It wasn’t enough. Kara’s eyes blazed bright blue…

“Stop!” Lena dived forward, placing herself between Kara and Selena. “We need her! She belongs to me. Pamela took control of her mind a month ago!”

She turned around, helping Selena to her feet as Kara stared. Impossible. If Alura’s most trusted woman had been under Lena’s control the entire time, how had they lost the war so badly? Why hadn’t Lena known who Reign was? It didn’t make any sense.

The supervillain turned around, locking gazes with Kara. Trust me.

Kara released a nervous, exasperated sigh. “Lead the way. Let’s go,” she said simply. Lena nodded in reply, quickly tearing off down the hallway with Kara and Selena right on her heels.

Where were they going? Supergirl had absolutely no idea, but it didn’t matter. Alura was minutes away from starting a genocide, and there was no time to explain. The only question was whether she trusted Lena’s judgment, and the answer was clear.

Is it? How many are dead already because of her so-called ‘plans’? James! Lucy! Either Lena let them die as acceptable losses or couldn’t find a way to save them. Either way, how can you possibly trust her?

Kara’s nails bit into her skin. Because I love her, and I have faith she’ll always find the best way forward. Even Lena can’t protect everyone. 

Are you saying that because you believe it, or because you simply have no other option? Your plan was to bust into Lena’s cell and pray she had a solution. What are you, Supergirl, besides a glorified attack dog for your fiancé? Of course you’ll follow her orders! You couldn’t even begin to think of a way to stop Alura yourself.  

Lena held out a hand for Kara to stop and quiet her movements. Selena continued onward, walking forward briskly to what Kara realized was the command center.

“We can’t let them hear our footsteps. Carry me and fly us forward,” Lena whispered.

Supergirl scooped the supervillain into her arms, stunned. Clearly, Selena was going ahead to order anyone in the command center to clear out. What was not clear was how Lena had planned to sneak forward before Kara had shown up. It wasn’t like the CEO had known…

Oh. She did. Lena must have accurately predicted Kara would desperately come to free her at the moment of truth. Such foresight boded well for Supergirl’s decision to place her faith in the CEO, but the thought sent another twinge through the imaginary string sticking out the back of Kara’s neck.

“You three. The High Councilor wants a word in person before control is transferred.” Selena’s words up ahead carried to Kara’s superhearing. “No, not even over secure channels. She wants to see you face to face. Get going!”

It was ludicrous, but Kara could hear the technicians obey. Why wouldn’t they? Selena was Alura’s second-in-command, the creator of the Worldkillers and the most trusted operative on Argo. Even her imprisonment by Lena hadn’t dented that trust…

Because Lena gave Alura every reason to believe Selena hadn’t broken! She sent me and Alex to Argo to find out knowledge Selena had already known…just so Alura would think Lena had no other source of information. And Lena never asked Selena who the mole in L-Corp was to not give the game away.  

There was a lot to process there, but Kara simply didn’t have the time.

“What are we doing?” Supergirl demanded as they made their way into the command center, empty except for a patiently waiting Selena.

Lena hurried over to the central console, typing furiously. “Transferring control of Myriad to me.”

“Why? If we have it, just destroy it!”

“I’d like nothing more, but that’s not an option,” her fiancé replied. “Myriad is a program. Alura’s locked it deep within Argo’s systems, and only her private access codes can take control of it. The only reason I’m about to be able to gain control over Myriad is because Alura’s going to release the surface-level locks. She thinks the technicians here are going to transfer control to her flunkies on Earth.”

Lena’s hands ceased their typing. “Done. Myriad is now coded to my brainwaves.” She sat down on a chair. “As soon as Alura releases control, I’ll have dominion over every human on Earth.”

“So what? As soon as she realizes something’s wrong, Alura is going to fly right here; it will take her less than a minute!” Supergirl pointed out. And that wasn’t her biggest worry. There was no telling what trying to take fine control of billions of minds at once was going to do to Lena’s brain.

The CEO simply smiled. She wordlessly beckoned Kara to take her hand, which the hero instantly did. “There’s no time to explain. Just trust me, okay? Once it’s done, we’re going to get out of here.”

Kara swallowed. “Okay. I trust you.” And it’s a good thing I do, because I have no other choice.

\

Ab-Kar of Krypton was waiting patiently. He’d been ordered to take position in the very center of New Delhi, one of the largest cities on the planet. As soon as the matriarch transferred control of Myriad, all twenty-five million minds in the city would answer to him.

They were little more than sheep…the humans and alien immigrants. For now they continued to walk throughout the city, still following the High Councilor’s general order to maintain their routines. Each and every one of them walked forward with determination, but with no words or attention spent on one another.

With his enhanced vision, Ab-Kar could see a group of humans continuing their task of building a skyscraper. Even as they cooperated to lift and maneuver massive steel beams, they failed to so much as look at their fellows. It was an impressive building too, despite having been commissioned by a human. Perhaps he should order it completed, with some pertinent changes. Ab-Kar would need a headquarters, after all.

The humans were so oblivious that they even passed by him without so much as a glance. At times, they were inches away. It was admittedly unnerving behavior, but that would soon change. The instant the High Councilor transferred control, none of them would ignore him ever again.

Ab-Kar looked at his watch. Any moment now. The anticipation was getting to him, it seemed. He felt off balance…almost as if ill. He couldn’t imagine why. There was nothing to be nervous about…

Pain!

A sharp blade of agony stabbed through his heart. One of the humans, not so docile now, had procured what looked like a dagger of green glass and thrust it into his chest. It shouldn’t have even broken the skin, but that didn’t stop his blood from beginning to flow out in torrents.

Ab-Kar fell to his knees. His body had mercifully gone into shock, so much that he barely the second and third blades pierce his skin. Kryptonite, his mind supplied. How had the humans gotten it? What the hell was going on? 

He collapsed to the ground, his questions going unanswered.

An L-Corp drone flew overhead, ready to join a battle, but its task was already complete.

\

Across six continents, hundreds of Kryptonians suddenly found themselves assailed by those they would have used as puppets. Each and every single resident of Argo was beyond powerful, but even they were not immune to being taken completely by surprise with their greatest weakness.

Alura hadn’t believed it possible for a single mind to closely coordinate Myriad over the entire planet, yet Lena handled it easily. Her intellect was split amongst four hundred separate locations, but that was little challenge for her. It was just another simultaneous round of chess, and this time all of the pieces were in her favor.

L-Corp drones and Harun-el soldiers distributed Kryptonite weapons at the location of each and every Kryptonian on Earth. Thanks to Selena, of course, all of those locations had been known well in advance and supplied to Alex Danvers. The second Lena took control of Myriad, thousands of ordinary humans took those weapons and struck.

The CEO was commanding a group of humans as they slit the throat of a Kryptonian in Australia, another collective as they stabbed through the head of a Kryptonian in Warsaw, and a third as they assailed a Kryptonian in Cairo. This invader reacted faster than the rest, nearly managing to get away, only to be grabbed and held down by one of L-Corp’s Harun-el infused operatives. With her strength already depleted by the deadly green rock, the Kryptonian was unable to resist as the humans converged on her location…

Lena had always known that a Kryptonian army couldn’t be beaten in direct battle, not when they were prepared and equipped with anti-Kryptonite gear. But when suddenly ambushed with kryptonite, they were simply out of their depth. It was a lesson Kara had learned when Metallo attacked the hero in her apartment, and one that Lena had never forgotten.

There was no room for mercy here. Only death.

\

“We have confirmation, Ms. Danvers. The ambush is in progress.”

Alex nodded to herself, watching the computer screen with bated breath. “Good. Deploy all aircraft to assault Argo immediately. Alpha and Bravo teams to release the prisoners. Now!”

“Yes ma’am.”

Jet aircraft were slower than L-Corp’s drones. More importantly, without anti-Kryptonian weaponry, they would be almost useless in battle against the invading force. All they would be was a distraction, but Earth needed every advantage it could get at the moment.

L-Corp’s military software had been purchased by every advanced country on Earth. Many had understandably been wary of buying from a supervillain who clearly had designs on world domination, but a combination of infiltration, subversion, and simply being the best products on the market by a mile had gotten the product sold.

The software did as promised, upgrading the targeting systems of each aircraft and tripling energy efficiency. It also gave L-Corp’s operators the ability to assume automated control of each and every plane whenever they wished. That time was now.

They wouldn’t be as effective without actual pilots, but L-Corp’s employees were well-trained. They assumed control of humanity’s advanced air fleets from their positions in the bunkers, ordering them to assault Argo.

All thirty thousand of them.

\

Kara watched in awe as Lena continued to sit serenely in her chair.

“It’s going well,” the CEO assured her.

How someone could control every mind on Earth while also holding a conversation was something Kara could never understand. But what troubled her at the moment was that her girlfriend was doubtlessly ordering hundreds of deaths at that very moment. Supergirl bit her lip at the thought, but she made no move to stop the supervillain.

They are enemy combatants, and this is war. What choice do we have? the hero thought bitterly.

Lena winced. “A few have escaped their ambushes and, yes, it looks like they’re speaking into their communicators. I estimate it takes Alura ten seconds to process this information before she realizes what’s going on and flies right here. Selena, you stay behind and cover our escape. Kara, fly us out of here now.”

Kara didn’t stop to think. She simply lunged forward, grabbing her girlfriend and flying through the window.

“We need to save the prisoners!” the hero cried over the wind. “Alura will execute them all!”

Lena looked up from where she was cooped in the hero’s arms, her restraints forcing her to huddle awkwardly. “It’s already being taken care of! We need to regroup!”

Supergirl could see countless aircraft heading toward’s Argo’s position in the atmosphere. It was a swarm of black dots stretching across the entire horizon. If this was going to be their last roll of the dice, Kara needed to be part of it.

“No, Kara. Take me to your sister’s bunker. I’ll guide you. This is only the first move, and if we stay and fight we’ll be slaughtered!” Lena ordered. “I still don’t have a way to beat the Omega Effect. It’s going to take all of us at once, and we can’t coordinate from here. Let’s go!”

Supergirl obeyed, but her doubts only grew. Could anything beat the Omega Effect? Alura still had a force of over a hundred Kryptonians on her side. If Lena couldn’t think of a way to beat her, who could?

But…even the best player doesn’t always see every move.

\

No sooner had the panicked cries started ringing in her earpiece then an endless swarm of aircraft emerged over the horizon. Before Alura could even process what was happening, the barrage of missiles already began to slam into Argo’s buildings.

“Just escaped a mob of humans. They have kryptonite!”

“Something’s wrong…Myriad…I don’t have control!” 

“Help…I need immediate-”

There were dozens of desperate cries for help, and the abrupt ending of many informed the High Councilor that casualties were beginning to mount. The people of Earth were revolting…impossible! Alura had relinquished control of Myriad, but it should immediately have been transferred to her subordinates. And how could the humans have obtained Kryptonite so quickly?!

A missile fired from ten miles out exploded just outside her office. The impact sent her desk careening across the room, even as a sortie of bombers crossed the perimeter of the city and started dropping their payloads. Alura lashed out with her Omega Beams, destroying a dozen planes almost instantly, but far more were on their way.

Luthor. The realization slowly gripped her mind, coiling through her thoughts like a mass of writhing tentacles. Only Lena Luthor had the resources to direct this coordinated attack, though Alura had no idea just how she’d managed to do so.

The answer came when she arrived at the command center seconds later. Selena was standing in the center of the room, looking utterly serene.

Selena greeted her casually, without any emotion in her voice. “Hello Alura. As you might have guessed, control of Myriad was not transferred to your agents on Earth. It was instead given to Ms. Luthor, who used her brainpower to execute a simultaneous attack on all of your agents.”

Bitch. “So, Luthor got to you after all?”

Selena nodded. “Ms. Luthor gained control over my mind very quickly. Pamela Isley’s techniques combined with the targeted administration of pain were very effective.”

Alura nodded, not trusting herself to speak. How her daughter could ever love someone so vicious, the matriarch didn’t know. There would be a reckoning for that, and soon. Right now, confusion was still preeminent in her thoughts. “So, Luthor knew about Samantha Arias the entire time?”

“No. She would not allow me to tell her the identity of the mole within L-Corp. Ms. Luthor was unwilling to risk her deception being uncovered. That is why she sent your daughter and Alex Danvers to Argo…to uncover answers she already knew,” Selena explained.

And now she’s using you to distract me.

A pair of Omega Beams erupted from her eyes, slamming into Selena at point blank range. The Kryptonian took the hit directly, falling unconscious immediately as her body slammed into the far wall. Hopefully, in time, the damage Luthor had done to her most trusted servant could be reversed. For the moment, there were larger concerns.

Alura rushed over to the command console, transferring full control of Myriad back to herself. A simple command to Earth’s residents to resume their normal routines stopped the attacks immediately, but the damage might have already been done.

She brought up her commlink. “Awaken every relative of each agent sent down to Earth,” she commanded her lead scientist. “Bring them out of hypersleep as fast as possible.”

Dax-Ur coughed in shock. “High Councilor, skipping all safety procedures is ill-advised. Over thirty percent of those awoken will die!”

A tear slipped down Alura’s cheek, but sacrifices had to be made. “I’m sorry, but it needs to be done. How long will it take?”

“Thirty-six hours, but-”

“Begin immediately,” she commanded, shutting off the transmission.

Alura had intended to wait to awaken any of her people until Earth was ready for full colonization. There had been no reason to do so. More importantly, the more Kryptonians on Argo, the greater the possibility that some of them would decide that enslaving Earth’s people was morally unacceptable. Argo could ill avoid sabotage, let alone open rebellion.

Now, it had to be done. In thirty-six hours, thousands of Kryptonians would awaken from their slumber. As relatives of those who had been attacked- and murdered- on Earth, they would be unlikely to harbor sympathies for the human race. It would be enough to overwhelm whatever Luthor was planning.

Her eyes fell on Selena’s unconscious form. There was no doubt that Luthor would have predicted this move, and Selena would have told her how long it would take to bring more Kryptonians out of hibernation. That meant her endgame would be coming very soon.

Alura opened another transmission. “Mala, execute the prisoners immediately.”

The warden’s reply was only slightly hesitant. “All of them, High Councilor?”

The matriarch considered it. “All but the one being held in the basement. Keep her contained. The rest are to be killed immediately and efficiently.”

Luthor isn’t the only one with backup plans.

\

Explosions echoed in the distance, sending vibrations that pierced through his cell. Winn knew exactly what it meant: this was Lena’s last play. He needed to escape, to fight, but the ring was still out of his reach. All of his attempts to call to it had failed.

Let my will fuel your power. Please. We need to end this.

Then his cell door was being ripped open! The metal gave away instantly, under the soft but strong hands of a wonderfully familiar face.

“Princess Koriand’r?” Winn breathed.

The flying alien shot him a small smile. “You can call me Starfire, but right now we need to leave.” She seized his arm, dragging him out into the cell block. An assortment of L-Corp forces were arrayed in the hallway, freeing other prisoners from their cells. Winn saw some, Lady Shiva and Mr. Terrific among them, reacting quickly. Yet other prisoners seemed to be in a state of shock.

Explosions still sounded from outside, even louder now that they were no longer muffled by the cell door. Dust was raining from the ceiling, falling faster under each new impact. Chunks of mortar started to crash to the ground.

“It’s time to go!” a voice shouted over the confusion. “The ships are outside! Alura’s execution orders have already been given!” It was an L-Corp operative, one Winn didn’t recognize, but the air of authority was clear.

Starfire tugged Winn along. “Agent Anderson isn’t kidding. Our forces defeated the guards here, but more are on their way. Maybe Alura herself!”

Throngs of people were now running outside, but Winn hesitated. “The ring! I need-”

Starfire scooped him up in her arms and started flying. “Don’t be silly!” she said, flicking him lightly on the forehead. “You need to live.”

The alien princess gently but firmly brought him to an evacuation ship and strapped him in. Dozens of prisoners and their liberators did the same. “Isn’t it smart?” Starfire asked, sitting down beside him. “Argo is under attack from hundreds of human aircraft. They won’t even notice us as we fly away!”

Winn sighed, staring at his empty finger.

Willpower

Sam stepped forward, looking up at the containment field. It was a simple piece of technology, but it had kept the green lantern ring floating in stasis and off of Winn’s finger. Now, all she had to do was disable it and Earth’s first Green Lantern would return.

No one else was in the area thanks to the chaos now unfolding on Argo. All Sam had to do was disable the containment field, pass it off as a system malfunction, and Winn would have his powers back with Sam’s cover preserved.

Lena had specifically ordered her to wait until the time was right. Sam would have liked nothing more than to walk up behind an unsuspecting Alura and snap her beck, but the Omega Effect made her so damn powerful that even a Worldkiller didn’t have the necessary strength to finish her off alone.

Speaking of Alura…

Sam raised a hand to her commlink. “Yes, High Councilor?”

“What year is it on the Kryptonian calendar?”  

Fuck. The blood drained from her face. Sam didn’t have the slightest idea. Reign had never mentioned it while possessing her body, and Sam hadn’t spent much time looking in the city’s databases. There was no point in guessing.

Sam shut off the comm. Fuck. Fuck. She knows. How the fuck does she know?! 

The CFO lunged forward, smashing the containment field generator. No sooner had the ring zoomed off to join its owner than Sam had flown after it. Her body broke through the ceiling effortlessly, revealing the city of Argo in all its crumbling glory. There was no point in remaining now. She had to make sure she wasn’t being followed and get to the-

BZZT!

A sickeningly powerful force slammed into her side, radiating such powerful heat that it burned even the skin of a Worldkiller. Unable to resist the impact, Sam went careening into the ground and skidded along the pavement of a deserted street.

Scrambling to her feet, Sam felt her heart drop as she saw Alura flying right in her direction. A second blast of Omega Beams followed, streaking across the sky and ionizing the air itself. Fuck. Sam crossed her arms in front of her body and braced herself, but even the durability of a Worldkiller couldn’t stand up to the Omega Effect.

The impact sent her rocketing off into the sky. Battling against the pain enveloping her body, Sam fought to reverse her momentum. She was turning end over end, blood from her broken nose trailing through the air.

BZZT! Another blast of the Omega Beams collided with her body. Sam screamed in agony as her skin began to burn, smoke streaming from her hair. The pain was too great for her to think. She could barely breathe; her breath coming through instinctive gasps.

She was still careening through the air. Sam had to stop herself. She had to-

WHAM! A punch of horrifying power collided with her stomach. A fresh wave of agony erupted in her core as multiple ribs cracked under the pressure. Through the pain, Sam’s vision was just clear enough to see Alura’s snarling face.

Another blow slammed into her shoulder, breaking the bone. Sam barely felt the impact as Alura followed up with another punch to her face, knocking out multiple teeth. The CFO found herself curling up into fetal position as the mid-air onslaught continued, desperately trying to shield herself.

Someone…help. Please!

\

Alex was watching the scene from a drone feed, clenching her fingers in horror. Her hand slammed into the console, instantly putting her in direct communication with each and every one of L-Corp’s remote pilots.

“All craft in range are to focus on Alpha Target immediately!”

I can’t lose anyone else. Especially you. I refuse.

\

It had been a hunch, really, that had allowed Alura to ferret out another spy. Someone must have been relaying instructions to Luthor’s forces on Earth. It couldn’t have been Selena, given just how much time she spent in close proximity to Alura.

The High Councilor knew that Harun-el could split a Worldkiller in two. If that had occurred to Reign, it would explain why the mission to capture Alex Danvers had ended in failure. It was just a suspicion, but Alura was glad she had acted on it.

Now another pathetic agent of Luthor was reeling before her, drifting out of consciousness as Alura readied her next blow.

SLAM! A missile collided with Alura’s torso. The explosion was harmless, but it was startling. The High Councilor glanced around to see that every vehicle in range was zeroing in on her. There were hundreds, perhaps more.

“Fine,” she muttered under her breath. Samantha Arias was horribly wounded, perhaps fatally. Even if she survived, the healing powers of a Worldkiller wouldn’t return her to fighting shape for weeks. The CFO was out of the fight.

Alura used her remaining second to fire a final blast of Omega Beams at the helpless Worldkiller. Completely unresisting, Sam’s body caught the impact full on and was blasted miles away, falling outside the perimeter of Argo and down to the earth below.

Still, the High Councilor mused as she began to tear through the scrap arrayed against her. Killing her might hurt Luthor’s morale. I’m needed here, but…

She reached for her commlink.

\

One second, Winn was breathing heavily as their craft descended to Earth.

The next, a green blur was slicing through the hull and onto his finger. A wonderfully familiar feeling of weightlessness took him as a green glow filled the interior.

“You got it back! See!” Starfire winked at him, as he stared at his finger in shock. “Ms. Luthor said it would be taken care of. Now we just need to get back to base and…”

Winn’s exultation was shattered as a voice broke out over the intercom. “All units. Ms. Arias is down. Repeat, Ms. Arias is down! Alpha Target has blasted her off of Argo. She needs assistance immediately!”

“Give me your commlink!” he said quickly to Starfire, who hastily obeyed. “This is Green Lantern. Ready to assist.”

Starfire smoothly plucked the commlink from his grasp. “This is Starfire. Also ready to assist, of course! Tell us where she is.”

\

The bunker was bigger than Kara had been expecting. L-Corp employees were running around the complex in a flurry of activity, coordinating the battle above Argo and preparing their forces for tomorrow’s final attack. The hero casted her eyes around for Alex and Eliza, but there was no sign of her family.

“This was their assigned bunker,” Lena told her quickly, guessing exactly what was on her mind. “They’re both here somewhere. Go find them while I get prepped for surgery.”

Kara whirled around, facing her girlfriend. “Surgery?” she demanded.

The villain nodded, raising her restrained hands. “These cuffs are made of enhanced nth metal,” she replied matter-of-factly. “There’s no removing them. I need to be able to fight tomorrow, and that means-”

“No! Lena, no!” Getting off the restraints would require cutting off both of Lena’s forearms, as well as cutting off her legs at the knees. It was monstrous. There had to be another way! “You can’t-”

The CEO smiled sadly. “I have to. Others have already given their lives…sacrificing my limbs is nothing in comparison. I’ve already had one replaced, remember?” she nodded to her leg.

“I remember,” the hero swallowed. Oh yes, how Kara remembered.

Lena winced. “Sorry. I didn’t mean to bring that up. But what I’m trying to say is that I can handle it. I’ll be unconscious the whole time as the surgery is done and the replacements are fitted. Soon enough, I won’t even notice the difference.”

“I…I…” Alura was going to pay. And pay dearly.

The CEO leaned forward, meeting Kara in a brief kiss. “I can’t spend the rest of my life in these shackles. I…” she looked at the hero, her eyes desperate. “I want more than anything else to hug you right now, and I can’t. Alura won’t take you from me.”

Supergirl wrapped her arms around her fiancé. “You’ll always have me, even if you were shackled,” she replied, hugging Lena fiercely. It was true. There were several issues they had to talk about, and multiple arguments in their future, but Kara knew they would end in forgiveness. It was selfish of her, perhaps, but the hero was past the point of caring.

After having lost so much already, Kara refused to surrender anyone else. Lena was manipulative, calculating, and willing to sacrifice, but her actions were ultimately driven by compassion. She’d done more for the people of Earth than anyone Kara had ever met.

“I love you,” Kara whispered, placing her chin on the CEO’s shoulder. “When this is over, I’m going to berate you for using me like a puppet. Then we’re going to get married and live happily ever after. That’s a promise.”

Lena’s eyes were shining with that same combination of bemusement and affection that Kara found so endearing. “You always were too forgiving…and too trusting.”

Stragglers around the bunker were staring at them now, but Kara paid them no mind. “I will never, ever regret trusting the kind, brilliant, self-sacrificing supervillain who swept me off my feet.” Her eyes fell to the restraints on her girlfriend’s limbs, and Kara’s brief flare of happiness faded as she was reminded of what Lena was about to go through.

“Don’t watch,” Lena ordered. “I don’t want you to see it. I know it will hurt you. Go find Alex and Eliza. Prepare to give me a situation report. Once my surgery is done, we’ll need to move fast.”

How the CEO could be so calm, Kara didn’t know. “Are you ever afraid?” she asked.

Lena’s lips set into a hard line. “I am terrified, Kara. Not about the surgery. We’re going into battle tomorrow and I have no idea how it will end. I’m…I’m afraid of dying,” she admitted. “And for entirely selfish reasons. You gave me a reason to hope for myself, Kara. I want to live! I want to spend the rest of my life with you, ruling the world side by side and finally convincing you to eat kale.”

Despite herself, Kara laughed. “That is one thing I might never forgive you for.”

The CEO sent her a smoldering look that made Kara’s heart flutter. “I can be very persuasive. Now go find your sister while I take an anesthesia-assisted nap.”

Kara nodded, unable to stop herself from taking a last look at her girlfriend’s limbs. She didn’t care that her fiancé would have limbs of metal…Lena could have been a literal cyborg and Kara still would have loved her. All that mattered to her was the pain and mental agony the CEO would have to endure. It wasn’t fair.

War is never fair.

\

They found Sam easily enough, but Winn almost wished they hadn’t. The collection of burns, bruises, and dried blood made the CFO almost unrecognizable. If it hadn’t been for the slight rise and fall of her chest, the Lantern would have doubted that she still lived.

Sam had fallen in a grassy field in a Russian wheat field, miles from where Argo was currently hovering. The suit she was wearing marked her as a Worldkiller, a fact that still made Winn’s mind spin. Starfire had filled him in on the basics on their short flight here, but the fact that Reign had been possessing one of his friends for months would horrify Winn for years.

Starfire took Sam’s prone form gingerly into her arms. “How cruel,” the alien princess murmured sadly, having never been one to hide her thoughts. She raised a hand to her commlink. “We found her. She is still alive.”

Winn heard Alex’s voice gasp with relief before speaking back. “Understood. Return to your base immediately.” He looked up as the transmission ended, still trying to process recent events, only to receive a very unwelcome surprise.

“Look out!”

Winn created a green dome just in time, deflecting the blast of purple energy. Purity was floating down towards them, a calm frown on her face. There were no other hostile forces in the vicinity, but the Lantern knew it was only a matter of time.

“Give her up and you may live,” the Worldkiller stated.

Starfire’s eyes blazed with green energy. “We would die before doing so!” she declared.

Purity countered the princess’s eye beams with another blast of her own, but was caught off guard by Winn’s construct. A giant green fist lashed out from the ring, ensnaring the Worldkiller in a punishing grip. Winn poured his willpower into the ring, imploring it to hold the alien invader even as she thrashed against it.

“More are coming!” Winn yelled to Starfire. “I’m dragging this fight somewhere else. You get Sam to safety!”

“I will not abandon you!”

Winn was straining with effort. “You have to, or Sam dies! Get her to safety and send help as soon as you can!” He glanced one last time at the reluctant princess before engulfing both himself and the Worldkiller in a dome of green energy.

A deafening pain took him as Purity unleashed a sonic scream, but Winn fought through it. Gritting his teeth, he launched their dome into the sky. Rocket energy constructs materialized at the side of the energy cage, soon carrying them miles away.

\

“Alex!”

“Kara!” Her sister was staring at her commlink intently, but she turned around at the sound of her voice. “I’ve been worried sick. I’m sorry I didn’t tell you what was really going on, but we couldn’t take any chances. I’m…I’m so glad you’re back.”

Then she broke off, returning to the monitor. Alex’s every movement was tinged with nervous energy, clearly overshadowing whatever relief she felt at Kara’s return.

Supergirl leaned forward with trepidation. “Alex, what’s going on?”

“Sam. Alura somehow found out she was pretending to be Reign and ambushed her. It’s…it’s bad. Winn and Starfire are on their way to find her, but I saw the attack through our drone feed.” Alex’s face was calm, but her sister was actually shaking.

Sam was pretending to be Reign? Kara felt like she was standing in a hurricane of confusion. It seemed that a new revelation passed through her every second.

Alex seemed to perceive her confusion. “Harun-el separated them, and we killed Reign,” she explained weakly.

Kara’s mind was reeling, and it was only her sympathy for her sister that kept the hero’s thoughts somewhat grounded. So Alex had lost Maggie and found Sam, only for her new girlfriend to be possessed by an evil force? And now, on the cusp of their reunion, Kara’s mother had brutally attacked…

Oh, Rao. Ruby.

Kara needed comfort, and there was only one option available. Lena was in surgery, and Alex had her own problems to deal with. “Where’s Eliza?” the hero asked eagerly. “Lena told me she was here.”

Her sister tensed.

A female voice spoke through Alex’s commlink, interrupting the moment. “We found her. She is still alive.”

Alex breathed a shaky sigh of relief. “Understood. Return to base immediately.” Then she shut off her commlink, turning around once again to stare at Kara. “You don’t know where she is?” Alex demanded.

No! “She has to be here!” Kara protested. “Lena told me she was here!”

Her sister growled. “She was supposed to be, but Alura got to her first. No one slated to go into the bunkers was given advance knowledge…except me. During the Battle of Argo, one of our agents went to go find mom, but she was already gone.” Alex looked close to shattering at this point. “I assumed Alura took her as a hostage to use against you!"

Supergirl shook her head fiercely. “I never saw her. Alura didn’t even mention anything about Eliza while I was on Argo! Why would she need her, anyway? She already had Lena!”

Slam! Alex’s fist smashed into her chair’s armrest, denting it. “She must have been a backup if Lena was executed. Her last trump card. Mom…” she took another deep, unsteady breath. “I’m going to kill Alura. I don’t give a damn what you say about it. If we take her alive, I’ll execute her myself.”

Kill Alura. Kara didn’t know if she would ever be capable of killing in cold blood. Sure, there had been Pestilence, but Supergirl had only managed to carry through with the act because millions of lives had been hanging in the balance.

And there was still some small part of Kara, a part of her that she resented and did her best to silence, that still loved her mother. Was it wrong for her to hope that the good woman who had raised her was still in there somewhere, even after all the damage that Alura had caused? Almost certainly, but Kara couldn’t help it.

“I won’t stop you,” the hero replied, having no time or energy for a pointless argument. “I’m sorry. If it hadn’t been for me…” Eliza would still be here. But it was more than that, wasn’t it? How much had Alex lost because Kara had come barreling into her life?

Supergirl startled as Alex leaned her head against the hero’s neck. “You’re my sister, whatever happens. We’re going to get our mom back or die trying. Agreed?”

Kara returned her hug emphatically. “Agreed.” And when it’s time for Alura to die, I won’t stop you.

\

Purity rolled over in midair as Winn smacked her with a claymore construct. The Worldkiller quickly righted herself, her skin showing no bruises or blood.

“Is that it?” she demanded, firing off a blast of heat vision that Winn barely managed to dodge. “The real Lantern we took that ring from was far more impressive.”

Winn knew she was trying to demoralize him, but that didn’t mean the alien was wrong. He had an instinctive grasp on the ring’s capabilities, but no formal training. The green energy that flowed through his body enhanced his strength, speed, and reflexes, but it wasn’t nearly enough.

Purity charged forward at superhuman speed, launching a midair kick at his forehead. Winn tried to dodge…too late, her boot clipped the side of his face. Pain thundered within him as he fell hundreds of feet through the air, halfway down to the waters of the Caspian Sea waiting patiently below.

Damn it. He righted himself, spitting blood from his mouth. Trying to coax every bit of power from the ring, Winn materialized a jet fighter and launching it at his enemy. The construct impacted Purity head on, sending the Worldkiller flying backwards but doing no noticeable damage.

Winn glanced at the ring in desperation. There was no escape; Purity was faster than he was and Winn had no idea where he was even supposed to go. Hopefully Starfire would be able to send him help, but the battle had already drifted hundreds of miles from its starting point.

Purity had flown after him eagerly. She was in no mood to allow him to flee.

\

Starfire desperately tapped her commlink, but it was no use. Purity’s sonic scream seemed to have damaged the device. She was almost to her assigned bunker in Siberia, a still-breathing Samantha Arias in her arms.

The alien princess willed herself to fly faster. Two lives depended on it.

\

Night was falling now, and still Purity pursued him in a running battle through the skies.

“This is the power that policed the universe for centuries? Pathetic.”

Her next sonic scream pierced through his ears, barely leaving him conscious enough to raise a green dome around himself. The Worldkiller’s fists smashed into his shield, not breaking through but leaving several cracks in the barrier. 

The ring had to be capable of more. He had to be capable of more. Winn’s willpower fueled the ring, which in turn enhanced his physical abilities and strengthened his constructs. The techie tried everything to focus his will. He used his love for his friends, his hope for the future…nothing. Purity’s next attack nearly broke through his defenses.

Winn willed the shield to explode outward, throwing his opponent back and giving himself valuable breathing room. He turned to his anger next…his fury at what had happened to his friends. Lucy and James had died at the hands of these invaders, and they deserved to pay.

No construct formed.

Anger is fueled by fear. Fear is not willpower.

A blast of heat vision struck him in the torso, burning through his green aura and blistering his skin. Okay, no fear. Fear didn’t work. Pure willpower.

Winn struck back with a giant baseball bat, too wide for Purity to avoid. She raised her arms to block, and the construct shattered against her. The alien floated backwards through the air and grunted in pain, but her skin remained unblemished.

Her next blast of heat vision was deflected by a hastily raised shield. “NO!” Purity cried in another sonic scream, blasting the barrier to pieces.

Winn flew off desperately through the air, his opponent in hot pursuit. The techie’s next construct, a series of delayed explosives released behind him, did little to slow the Worldkiller down. He glanced at the ring in frustration.

Why pick me if my willpower was too weak?

Unless it wasn’t. Winn swerved through the air, barely avoiding a pursing blast of purple beams. Perhaps the problem was that he was thinking about this all wrong. The ring wasn’t a piece of technology, not like any he’d ever seen. It was nothing on its own.

The ring doesn’t have any energy. It isn’t fueled by my willpower. It just converts it into energy!

He’d been looking at the ring like a gift, as if it was a blessing that let him be useful to his friends. Winn had considered himself a tool to release the ring’s power. But he’d had it backwards. The ring released his energy.

The Lantern stopped in the air, turning to his enemy. As Purity observed him warily, Winn focused all of his willpower not into the ring, but through it. His green aura swelled around him, sharpening his senses.

Her next blast shot through the air, but to Winn it seemed a hair slower than before. He shot a quick blast of energy to his right, allowing the recoil to move him out of the way. It was close: the heat from Purity’s beams seared his shoulder, but he avoided the worst of the attack.

My will commands the ring. My will-

“DIE!” Purity’s sonic screech hit him directly, sending him tumbling back.

My will. Mine.

Her next blast slammed into a shield of green energy. Purity flew forward, lashing out with two kicks so fast that they blurred through his vision. The first smashed through his shield. He leaned back to avoid the second, but the Worldkiller’s boot still slammed into his face. Warm blood flowed into his mouth as he reeled back.

He ignored the pain. The pain was nothing. My will, to protect and avenge my friends, is everything.

Purity’s next punch sailed over his shoulder. Winn’s fist lashed out, coated with pure energy.

“GRRRGH,” Purity groaned as the air was knocked out of her lungs. As she reeled back, Winn followed up with his next construct. A missile launcher materialized next to him, launching a barrage of rockets at his foe.

Their impact was palpable, battering her throughout the air. Winn lunged forward, a massive two-handed sword in his hands. He yelled, slamming it down across his foe. Purity raised her arms to block just in time.

The sword shattered against her arms, but the blade left a thin cut in her suit. A trickle of blood seeped out, even as she retaliated with a blast to Winn’s midsection.

Both combatants reeled back, still floating in midair. Assessing one another.

“You can’t win,” Purity said calmly. “Your quick mastery of the ring is impressive, but even a trained Lantern can’t stand against a Worldkiller.”

Winn spat out a glob of blood. “I’d like to test that theory.”  

Silk and Steel
