See the end of the chapter for notes

“Why are you here?” the prisoner questioned, her voice hostile and cautious.

Alura ignored the question. “I have no particular enmity for the humans; they are just obstacles standing in my way…and now tools to be used. You, however, are the exception. My daughter would be a proud Kryptonian, standing by my side, were it not for your influence.”

“I’m afraid you’re wrong. Kara was a good person without my help,” Eliza replied, smiling thinly.

The nerve of this woman! “I would thank you for providing my daughter with accommodations, but your corruption of her spirit is unforgivable. You raised her to believe she was no different from the teeming masses of humanity, fit only to work a life of drudgery.”

Eliza rolled her eyes. “You are raving.”

“Am I?” Alura questioned. “Did you not encourage Kara to hide her abilities as a child, suppressing her gifts for the sake of normality? You didn’t even permit her to save humans, did you? And when she finally decided to emerge as a hero, you were horrified, were you not?”

A blast from a nearby exploding missile vibrated through the room, but Alura paid it no notice.

“I wanted Kara to wait until she was ready. I gave her as normal a childhood as possible, without being hunted down by supervillains or taken to a government black ops site,” the older woman explained.

Alura smirked. “Is that really all of it? Or is the truth that you just weren’t ready to parent an alien child? You were willing to love Kara, but not sacrifice your life for her. And so you let her rot in mediocrity rather than use her gifts, knowing it would destroy your comfortable suburban life.”

The human’s eyes flared, and Alura knew she had hit her mark.

“I never wanted Kara to hide from who she is; I only wanted her to be safe.”

The matriarch looked at her curiously. Eliza was fidgeting in her chair, and it was wonderful to see. “Really? You always wanted a second daughter, didn’t you? A human daughter. When Kara came into your life, did you ever try to help her connect to her heritage? Did you make an effort to learn her language, or ask her what traditions she enjoyed during holidays? Or did you just close your eyes and pretend she was human?”

“I love her,” Eliza said slowly. “More than you ever will. I repeat my question. Your city is under attack. Why are you here?”

Alura waved a hand dismissively. “The fleets of humanity are nothing more than a nuisance. Despite the losses, I have one-hundred and fifty Kryptonians ready to defend my city. Luthor won’t be attacking for several more hours.” She smiled in satisfaction, knowing that her enemy would right now be cutting off her own limbs to remove the restraints. “My daughter will be with her.”

“So I’m your hostage. Threatening me won’t stop Kara.”

You wish. “Maybe not. That’s why I’m just going to kill you, right in front of her. She is Luthor’s most powerful weapon, and I need to break her spirit.”

Eliza’s eyes widened in alarm, though the human did her best to hide it. “You do that, and she will never return to you.”

“I think she will, once humanity is a distant memory. And…that is a risk I am prepared to take,” Alura admitted, hesitating for the first time during this conversation. “Kara has allowed Luthor to massacre hundreds of my agents…my people. I have a duty to prevent her from doing any more harm. If the cost of victory is her love…” the matriarch swallowed. “So be it.”

Alura refused to shed a tear.

“I wasn’t a perfect mother to Kara,” Eliza admitted. “But I never took pleasure in punishing her.”

The High Councilor slammed a foot into the ground, jolting the entire room. “You think I enjoy this?” she demanded. “I gave Kara every chance to live in peace with her friends spared, and she repaid me with the ultimate betrayal. My daughter must answer for the deaths she let happen.”

“No. She has to answer for defying you,” Eliza scoffed. “You might care for your people, and you might even love Kara, but what you want above all else is control. Kara defied you, ruined your victory, and now you want revenge. For all your technology…and your posturing…you’re just the latest in a long line of conquerors. Dangerous, but ruled by your basic instincts.”

Alura took a deep breath, calming herself. “You do not understand. I seek control only to save my people. They would have already died on Krypton if not for me! Am I really any different from Luthor, who used murder, blackmail, and theft to dominate your planet?”

“Lena never killed innocents.”

The High Councilor laughed. She had to commend the Luthor: her manipulations were impressive. Which, of course, was why she had to die. “Luthor never killed innocents because she never needed to, and because she knew that doing so would alienate people like Kara. Do you think that if Luthor had Myriad, she wouldn’t have used it?” Alura asked. “I bet she already plans for its use if she defeats me.” She smirked. “Why else do you think she didn’t even try to destroy Myriad while she had control over it?”

Eliza didn’t answer.

\

My will controls the ring. My will.

Purity unleashed a barrage of blasts, punches, and kicks. Winn dodged them all. His senses were sharper than they’d ever been, fueled by the power of the ring. He had unlocked its full power…he could feel it. The power flowed through him as he counterattacked, firing at Purity with a beam of concentrated emerald energy.

The Worldkiller dodged. The blast steaked past her, lighting up the darkness of the night. Purity recoiled, the flash so brilliant that her eyes needed to adjust. As the beam dissipated over the distant horizon, Winn materialized a massive green fist and seized the Worldkiller.

Clutched in his grip, Purity struggled as he crushed ever tighter.

“NO!” With a wild scream, the Worldkiller spread her arms and shattered his construct. Winn was sent flailing backwards but instantly materialized a new construct. A large katana appeared in his hands. He focused all of his energy on making the edge as sharp as possible, even as Purity flew at him again.

The wind was picking up around them.

She dodged his first strike, replying with a right hook that clipped his forehead. The Lantern reeled back, cursing in pain, but again brought his weapon to bear. Caught off guard by the maneuver, Purity hissed as his blade streaked across her chest.

Then she sent him flying with another sonic scream.

“Fool.” Purity swept her finger across the new cut in her suit, revealing a very thin stream of red. “A shallow cut. You wield that ring with skill, but it doesn’t have the power to kill me. Nothing you create is strong enough to crush me, or sharp enough to truly wound me.” Her eyes blazed with power. “All you can do is delay the inevitable.”

The wind was stronger now, whipping across his face.

As if to prove her point, the Worldkiller took his next construct head on. The giant fist he materialized sent her reeling but failed to even bruise her skin. She retaliated with a blast of purple energy, one that he barely deflected with a shield.

WHOOSH!

Winn’s eyes flicked to the sea far below, and he couldn’t believe what he saw. A massive waterspout was forming, millions of gallons of water circling into an all-consuming funnel. The liquid tornado was rapidly growing bigger, stretching ever taller as it increased in speed. Even thousands of feet in the air, the Lantern could feel himself swaying as the wind became a hurricane in intensity.

What the hell? It was an awe-inspiring sight. Terrifying. Yet the waterspout was rising in Purity’s direction, and the Worldkiller seemed just as surprised at the turn of events.

Winn launched himself backwards to a safer distance, simultaneously materializing another giant hand and clutching Purity in its fingers. The Worldkiller fought against his grip desperately. Cracks immediately formed in the construct, but it was too late.

SLAM! Countless tons of water smacked into the Worldkiller. Winn released his construct as Purity was sucked into the vortex. The wind was moving so fast now that it threatened him even at a distance; only a hastily-constructed dome of green energy stopped him from being swept in after the alien invader.

Then another force, straight and focused, slammed into his dome and carried him a mile away.

“Hey Winn! I saw your light show. Nice work!”

The Lantern released a breath he hadn’t realized he’d been holding. “Kara!” he exclaimed, dropping his shield. The Kryptonian was dripping wet, and panting with the effort it had required to create a tornado, but she was here.

There was no time to ask questions. “We need to end her. Now,” Winn said.

The hero shook her head.

“Kara, this is our chance to take out a Worldkiller. We can do it!”

Supergirl smiled. “Oh, I know. I’m not saying we should run. It’s time to kick her ass. What I’m saying is that we can’t kill her. There’s an innocent person in there, just like with Sam.”

Winn blinked in confusion.

“I can’t explain right now. Just help me knock her unconscious and do not kill her.”

The waterspout was starting to slow down. “Sure,” he said. “But you owe me an explanation later. Ready?”

“Let’s do this.”

\

Alex stared at the monitor. As soon as they had gotten the call from their Siberian base, Kara had launched herself out of the bunker. From the now-static position of Supergirl’s in-suit tracker over the Black Sea, it seemed that she had found their Lantern.

There were other forces en-route, but it was doubtful they would make it in time. Alex took a deep breath. She had faith in Kara. Always.

Go get her, sis.

\

The green glow extended from Winn’s ring and surrounded Kara. The hero didn’t resist its hold, allowing her friend to fill her with energy and seize her in its grip. He raised his fist into the air, lifting Supergirl well above the battlefield.

“Now!” she screamed.

Winn flung her cage of energy down like a slingshot. Instead of fighting the motion, Kara added all of her speed to it. She was a green streak of energy shooting through the air, aimed straight at the Worldkiller still struggling in the center of her liquid tornado.

WHAM! She collided with Purity at supersonic speed. A wave of force exploded from their point of contact, radiating outward to shatter the massive encircling wall of water. Kara wrapped her hands around Purity’s neck as her momentum carried them miles through the air, still a green bullet shooting over the Black Sea.

Worldkillers were stronger than regular Kryptonians and exceptionally durable. But, still stunned by the effects of the whirlpool and reeling from Kara’s recent blow, Purity’s counterattack amounted to two weak blows aimed at her hero’s stomach. Supergirl pressed on until they slammed into a Turkish beach. The force of their impact drove them through the sand like a piledriver as the beach exploded around them.

They were now perched in a massive crater of rock and mud, Supergirl’s hands still around Purity’s neck as the hero continued to bear down on the Worldkiller. She pressed down hard with all of her strength, forcing Purity’s back into the harsh rock beneath them.

The green energy was fading from Kara now, but Purity remained dazed as Supergirl slammed her head back into the rock. As the stalagmite crumbled under the impact, a vast network of giant green chains erupted from the ground and latched themselves onto the Worldkiller’s limbs.

With her hands now free, Supergirl got to work beating the crap out of her opponent. Her blows were emotional yet methodical, wielded with the knowledge and experience she’d acquired after dozens of battles and countless hours of training.

Purity tried to retaliate. But as her eyes filled with purple energy, a green visor materialized around her face. The heat vision dissipated against the barrier, scorching the Worldkiller’s cheeks as it vanished. Kara continued her assault the entire time.

There would be no killing today. Not again. The hero kept up her onslaught just long enough to knock Purity unconscious. Blood poured out of her broken noses and seeped out of a dozen gashes in her body, but her breathing was still steady and even.

“Let’s get her back to base.”

\

Lena ran her chin along one of her hands. One of her new hands. L-Corp’s prosthetics were so advanced that they looked identical to flesh, and were just as easy to control as her original limbs. But they weren’t her limbs. The small scars and marks accumulated by decades of life were gone. Standing on two artificial legs and staring at two artificial hands…it almost felt like she was in someone else’s body.

Buck it up, Luthor. People have died in this war. Your suffering is nothing in comparison.

At least she could move freely again. After weeks of being trapped in restraints for Alura’s sick amusement, having the ability to simply scratch her nose again felt like a liberation. It was almost enough to distract her from the coming battle, her final chance to save the Earth.

What really made Lena want to puke was the knowledge that one of her best- and only- friends had been ambushed and nearly killed by Alura. Sam was in stable condition, but even the healing of a Worldkiller hadn’t yet been enough to wake her from unconsciousness. Lena hadn’t seen her yet- the CFO was currently being transferred to their bunker -but the reports had made her dire situation clear.

Hasn’t she suffered enough? Oh…Ruby. That girl is going to kill me, and I can’t blame her.

At least she’d gotten some good news.

She hugged Kara as soon as the hero entered the medical bay. “You did it,” she whispered. Her lover had taken down Purity, their second-greatest threat. There was opportunity from this victory, but for the moment all she cared about was that Kara was alive and safe.

“We did it,” Supergirl corrected her. “Winn has really gotten the hand of that ring. I…” her fingers stroked Lena’s hand tenderly. “You didn’t deserve this. It feels…different.” The hero’s face blanched as she realized she’d been musing out loud. “Not that I care! I mean, of course I care, but it doesn’t change anything between us.”

The supervillain chuckled, placing a kiss to Kara’s forehead. “I know that. And it feels so good to hold you again. I…” Lena hesitated, but couldn’t stop the words from issuing forth. “I know you’re mad at me, and you have every right to be angry.”

Kara frowned. “This isn’t the time to talk about this…”

“They’re still getting ready for our strategy meeting. We have time. More importantly, in ten hours we’re going to war.” Lena took Kara’s hands into her own. “I have plans and tricks up my sleeve like always, but I can’t be sure we’re going to win. Alura might be impossible to take down. She isn’t going to spare me again. If I do die tomorrow, I don’t want anything left unsaid between us.”

There was a pregnant pause. Then, Supergirl nodded slowly. “I am mad. I’m not actually sure if I have any right to be. You manipulated me in order to trick Alura, again, and didn’t trust me with the truth. I know…I know the fate of the world is at stake, and it’s stupid to take any chances…but it still stings.”

Lena wasn’t surprised. “Kara, I am sorry. But I won’t lie to you and say I wished I’d done anything different. I wish it hadn’t been necessary, but I did what I had to do.”

“Yeah,” the hero replied bitterly. “Because you’re Lena Luthor, so smart that us mere mortals can’t even try and understand what you’re up to. You always know best, and I should just be happy to hold the honor of being your favorite attack dog. Isn’t that right?”

The CEO didn’t know what to say.

“You use me to defeat your enemies, telling me only what I need to know. You’ve been controlling me like a puppet on a string for months. It doesn’t make me love you any less…” Kara sighed. “But a relationship is supposed to be about trust, about being completely open with someone and taking comfort that you know all of each other. How do I know when I’m just talking with my girlfriend and when I’m being carefully influenced by Lena Luthor, CEO and supervillain extraordinaire?”

“I…don’t know,” Lena admitted. Even when she was at her weakest and most vulnerable, her mind could always see all angles of a given situation. Lena knew how people would react to her statements and actions. And since she knew Kara as well as she did, that went double for her girlfriend. “Does that mean…?”

Her heart began to race in desperation. Don’t leave me. I won’t survive it. Lena would respect whatever Kara chose, but that didn’t stop her urge to plead for her fiancé to stay with her.

The hero smiled slightly. “No. You’re stuck with me. Just…if we don’t die tomorrow and get to spend the rest of our lives together…it’s something you need to keep in mind.”

“Noted.” Asking Lena to try and stop thinking, even for a moment, was like asking her to stop breathing. But if it would make her future wife happy, Lena was willing to try and live without air. “And about you feeling like my attack dog…”

Kara crossed her arms and turned to the side. “Forget about it. You’re miles better at planning than me. Why shouldn’t you call the shots?”

“If you want me to be open and honest…” Lena forced herself to try. The smart thing to do was to raise Supergirl’s self-esteem for the fight ahead, and the best way to do that was to deny the allegation. The urge to do so was palpable, but she forced it back down. “Supergirl is a valuable resource for me, and I view her as such. She is blessed with unimaginable power, but I know how to employ it better than she does. Not that she can’t use her power effectively, but I’m better at it. I tell her how to save lives more efficiently, use her to prop up my public image, and employ her as a weapon if need be. That’s the truth.”

The hero said nothing.

“Kara Zor-El is a different story,” Lena continued. “Rao, Kara…you don’t even see it. I might manipulate you at times, but you change me without even realizing it. I’m not my brother. I am not and would never be a monster. But I can get so focused on the bigger picture that I can make the wrong decisions.” The CEO stared at the floor. “If it hadn’t been for you, I might have waited and let Alura go through with her culling to guarantee that everyone else would survive. I’m still not sure that I’ve made the right decision by striking early, but I did so because of you. So if you think this relationship is a one-way street…it’s not.”

Kara smiled sardonically. “Well, good. Because you’ve definitely made me way more ruthless than I used to be. So at least we’re both a bad influence on the other.”

“We balance each other out,” Lena replied as she placed her hand in Kara’s own. “You’re the silk to my steel…which I know is ironic considering you’re the Girl of Steel. It’s why we’ll make such an excellent pair if we do win and end up ruling the world.”

“That actually sounds kind of nice,” Supergirl admitted. “You’re forgetting that you don’t rule the world yet, even if we beat Alura.”

Lena shrugged. “Close enough. And as I’m sure you’ve guessed, I’ve got my plans for how to proceed afterwards. We’re going to capitalize on this victory for all its worth.” And Alura just might have handed me the tool I needed.

“Did you know?” the hero asked suddenly, any warmth in her tone suddenly gone. “That James and Lucy would be killed?”

Her heart was pounding with guilt. “No,” she answered honestly. “I knew there was a chance…that’s all. I would have bet that they would have been spared, but I suppose some of Alura’s forces are vengeful. They needed to be there, or Alura would have realized something was going on.”

“Not Jess?” Kara asked pointedly.

There it is. “Alura didn’t have a firm way of knowing if Jess even had been infused with Harun-el, and she wasn’t nearly as close to you as James and Lucy were. But…I won’t deny that I kept her back for the wrong reasons.” She shook her head in disgust. “Maybe I’m not as cold and logical as I thought. I…she has a son, Kara. She’s done so much for me. That’s all I can say.”

Jess had been with her since the beginning, offering her quiet and constant support. She’d turned down far higher paying positions to stay where she felt she’d be most useful to Lena, even after multiple offers. They hadn’t been close…perhaps not until recently, anyway, but there had been a longstanding mutual respect.

“I’m not going to blame you for being human, Lena. And the only ones at fault for James and Lucy are the ones who attacked us. I want revenge,” Supergirl said firmly. “I guess I’m human too.”

\

As soon as she walked into the conference room, the inevitable meeting Lena had been both looking forward to and dreading made itself apparent. Jess walked up to her, the secretary’s hands on her hips, and looked her up and down with the judgmental glare she usually reserved for Lena’s business rivals.

“Ms. Luthor!” The secretary lunged forward, consuming her boss in a fierce embrace that a startled Lena quickly returned. “I’m so glad you’re okay. I was so worried.” Then she stepped back.

SLAP!  

Lena raised a hand to her stinging cheek. By the time she’d opened her mouth to respond, Jess had already taken her seat at the table and crossed her arms. Half of the room was staring at her, but the secretary paid them no mind. After a few seconds, most shrugged and took their own seats.

I suspect most of the room wants to give me a hug and punch me. They were probably just glad to have someone else do it for them.

The CEO sat down at the head of the table, Kara and Alex taking their places on either side of her. The seat on Alex’s other side was empty, but no one dared sit in Sam Arias’s unoccupied seat. Her remaining board members and advisors took their usual places.

“No time for preambles,” Lena said. “First things first. Have we successfully separated the Worldkiller Purity from her host?”

Her Chief Medical Officer rose from his seat. “No, Ms. Luthor. We have injected her with Harun-el, just as Ms. Danvers did to Reign,” he replied with a nod at Alex. “The injection was incredibly painful for Purity, but no split occurred. She claims that the weaker soul within her has been extinguished.”

Lena paused for a brief moment, giving respect to the innocent life snuffed out by Alura’s machinations. If by some miracle they won, she would reach out to the loved ones of Purity’s human identity and pay for all funeral arrangements.

“That is both a problem and an opportunity,” she finally said. “I assume Purity is properly contained?” There were nods around the room. “Good. And what is the status of Ms. Arias?” Lena questioned, trying to keep her voice neutral. It was an admirable effort, though likely no one in the room was fooled.

Alex leaned forward in her chair, nearly vibrating with worry.

“Stable, but barely improving,” the medical officer replied.

From the other end of the table, the recently released Mr. Terrific cut in. “Isn’t she a Worldkiller?” he asked. “Shouldn’t her rate of healing be beyond superhuman?”

“It appears to be, but the damage she took was extensive,” came the reply. “The Omega Effect is…brutal. It’s a miracle she even survived. At best, she’ll regain consciousness in three days.”

A chill seemed to take the room as they were reminded of the power they were facing. Alex tried and failed to suppress an audible gasp, her face pale. Kara reached across the table to grasp her arm in comfort, but the elder Danvers seemed stuck in her own world.

Time to move on. “Mr. Colville, give me your report.”

A hologram emerged in the center of the table, showing Argo under assault by the massed air forces of humanity. “We’ve sent one hundred of our drones armed with Kryptonite to join the attack,” he said. “With the planes serving as a distraction, they’ve brought down another ten invaders. We estimate that Alura has one-hundred and fifty Kryptonians remaining in fighting condition. Obviously, they have consolidated around Argo to wait until their reinforcements wake from stasis. They know our final assault will come tomorrow.”

“We have an additional five hundred drones ready for deployment, as well as eighty Harun-el infused operatives,” L-Corp’s Chief of Defense offered. “Plus yourself, Supergirl, and fifty other superpowered agents.”

Bad odds. Very bad odds considering Alura’s forces would be prepared for Kryptonite. Even with her hidden strategies, Lena wasn’t playing chess any longer. There was no clear path to victory. The CEO was rolling dice and praying to a higher power she didn’t believe in.

Lena would do anything to win. Even draw upon her greatest fear.

Hesitation

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the break. Weekly updates are now resumed! We've got the (real) finale starting up!

It was the last meeting of the Superfriends. Kara, Lena, Winn, and Alex. Plans were shared and comforts were given, but Supergirl had never felt so empty. Even as they caught up on their adventures of the past month and paid tribute to their fallen friends, there was no escaping the existential dread that bore down on them.

“We launch in nine and a half hours. Time to get some sleep.”

It was a fitting end to their depressing circle. Alex and Winn stood up, bid their goodnights, and walked out of the room. Kara’s eyes were drawn to the empty chairs that might have been filled. James. Lucy. Lois. Clark. Even in their absence, Kara could feel their gazes upon her. They demanded she follow in their example…make all of their suffering worth something in the end.

There was a final missing member of what had once been the Superfriends. Sam, who was currently lying in a coma. And how many others might have joined their circle of friends if not for her mother? Barry. Cyborg. Alura had hurt so many people, and she was prepared to replicate her crimes on a grand scale.

Supergirl couldn’t let that happen.

Kara moved to the side, leaning into Lena and nuzzling her cheek into the CEO’s shoulder. Once, the hero had believed that there was no more heroic a sacrifice than giving up one’s own life to save others. It was what Clark had done, and Superman’s legacy still cast a shadow over the world. So many people had done the same in this war, willingly or otherwise.

For many people, perhaps such a sacrifice was the greatest price she could pay. But Kara had realized she was different. That wasn’t to say the hero wasn’t determined to hang onto her life, live out her days with Lena, and serve as Earth’s guardian for decades to come. Yet if it came to giving up her own survival to save the planet, Kara knew she would be able to do it.

“I need a favor,” she said softly.

Lena leaned back, raising an eyebrow. “Why do I get the feeling this isn’t going to be an easy request? You’re not asking for extra donuts in the breakroom, are you?”

“Nope,” the hero replied.

Lena’s fingers drummed on the table. “If you’re going to ask me if there’s anything I’m keeping from you…please don’t. I need you to trust me one more time. But there is one thing you need to know, otherwise you’ll probably be confused as to why A-”

“No!” Kara held up her palms. “Don’t tell me anything! With what I’m about to ask, it’s better that I don’t know any sensitive information.”

Her eyes blinking in confusion, the supervillain motioned for Kara to proceed.

Hands shaking, Kara forced herself to take a deep breath. “It’s war, tomorrow. We’re still outgunned. We need everyone fighting at their best, and that goes double for Supergirl. Alura’s forces might be Kryptonians, but they don’t have my experience or immunity to kryptonite. I can take them down, if…”

She couldn’t force the words out. Committing the act in the heat of battle, with millions of lives on the line, had been heart-wrenching. To go in with a pre-meditated plan to…it was almost impossible. Kara felt wrong just thinking about it.

That’s exactly why I’m asking now. Because I can’t hesitate tomorrow.

“You kill?” Lena finished for her. The CEO’s gaze remained calm, but Kara could see Lena’s fingers twitching. She was nervous. Kara could see it all in her eyes. The supervillain knew that Kara was right, but she didn’t feel comfortable trying to force the hero into violating her moral code.  

The hero nodded, forcing her gaze to remain on her fiancé. Sounds of preparation and last-minute drone production still echoed throughout the bunker, but for the moment the world was empty but for the two of them. A supervillain trying to save the world, and a superhero trying to force herself to take life.

“You’ve made me immune to both red and green kryptonite. I want you to make me vulnerable to Red K again.”

With a will of their own, Lena’s eyes moved to her first cybernetic limb. “What?”

“I can’t fight with inhibitions tomorrow,” the hero said. “I need to strike quickly…without mercy. But that’s not who I am. I will hesitate, I know it! Unless…”

The pain in Lena’s eyes made Kara feel even more guilty, but she had no choice. Only Lena Luthor had the scientific acumen to make a Kryptonian immune to kryptonite. Even Alura’s best scientists had been unable to replicate the feat. Which also meant that the CEO was the only one who could remove that immunity.

“I need Supergirl by my side,” Lena said firmly. “Not a killing machine.”

“A killing machine is exactly what you need tomorrow.” The words made Supergirl feel physically sick, but she forced herself to continue. “I know you still have Red K stashed away for study. Give me a small enough dose, and I won’t become a megalomaniac. At least, not immediately. I’ll still be on your side…cutting down invaders without hesitation.”

The CEO stood up so quickly that the floor cracked. “No. Kara, no.”

Kara stood up right with her. “You tell me that it’s not the right move. Go ahead. You, with your big bursting brain, tell me that it won’t improve our odds.” Her gaze bored into Lena’s eyes. “Tell me this isn’t necessary and I’ll drop it.”

A moment passed.

“Kara…” the villain’s tone was pleading now. “This is-”

“Necessary! The thought of killing people makes me sick, but imaging us losing because I hesitated is even worse. I don’t know how much of a difference it will make…maybe we all lose and die anyway!” the hero hissed. “But if it saves even one of our soldier’s lives, it’s worth it. You know it has to be done. You can cure me after we win. Even if I wake up in a river of blood…I won’t blame you.”

“I’m calling your sister,” the villain replied. “Maybe she can talk some sense into you.”

Nice try. “Go ahead. I already told her. It took some convincing, but she agreed. She doesn’t want me hesitating against Alura any more than I do.”

Lena was blinked rapidly, as if the computer in her brain was short-circuiting. “That’s not what I’m worried about. You’ll blame yourself. For the rest of your life, you’ll be tortured with the knowledge you went on a killing spree, and it will be all my fault! I-” she broke off briefly, the desperation in her voice seeming to diminish as a logical counterattack occurred to her. “If our positions were reversed, would you do the same to me?”

Unfortunately for her, Kara was- for once- one step ahead. “No. Never. I could also never have freed prisoners, blackmailed governments, or mind-controlled hundreds of people. You did. You’ve always said you were the right person to rule the world, not only because you’re the smartest but also because you could make the hard choices,” the hero reminded her supervillain girlfriend. “You want to be Empress of Earth? Earn that title by protecting the planet now.”

The battle currently raging in the skies around Argo was probably nothing compared to the war being waged inside Lena’s mind. The CEO didn’t move a muscle for a solid ten seconds as her mind desperately searched for a way out…some way to argue logically that poisoning her fiancé with Red K was not the right move. Kara knew that and loved her for it.

But there could only be one ending.

\

“Let me in!”

The guard to the infirmary frowned at her sympathetically. “Ms. Arias, I apologize, but no visitors are permitted. I promise you that your mother’s condition remains stable. Please return to your quarters.”

Ruby usually prided herself on being intelligent and rational. They were traits she sought to emulate from her two biggest role models: her mother and Lena. At this moment, however, her mother was in danger. All bets were off.

The thirteen-year-old charged forward, trying to slip past the guard or barrel through him if necessary. Unfortunately, he was more than twice her age. Even more unfortunately, he was enhanced with Harun-el and Ruby was not. He held her back gently with a single hand.

Ruby didn’t give up. She screamed, ineffectually lashing out with her fists. If it meant seeing her mother, she would claw out his eyes.

Another arm suddenly wrapped around her midsection, pulling her back. Ruby wheeled around, more than ready to assault her new target, but it was-

“I’m sorry kid, but you can’t go in,” Alex said, kneeling down to Ruby’s level.

Ruby fought through her surprisingly weak grip. “That’s my mom. You can’t imagine how I’m feeling. I don’t care what Lena says…or what you say. I’m going in!”

Alex’s eyes hardened just a fraction. “I do know how you feel. My mom is being held prisoner by a genocidal maniac at this very moment. You think every fiber of my being doesn’t want to go charging off to Argo immediately, reason be damned?”

Ouch. Ruby gave off a guilty wince, but she was no less determined. “If you went to Argo, you would die. There’s nothing dangerous in that room!” she gestured sharply to the infirmary.

“Lives depend on things in there going smoothly. Ruby, I promise you, Sam will be fine. You need to be strong. Please.”

The love and determination in Alex’s eyes made her hesitate slightly. Ruby knew the older woman wouldn’t lie to her, but still. “That’s my mom. I need to see her.” She choked back a soft sob. “When she was brought in…people were talking as if she was dying. I can’t…I can’t-”

Alex brought her into a fierce embrace. Ruby didn’t have the strength to resist any longer. She brought her arms over the older woman’s shoulders as her tears flowed freely. The nearby guards and other passerby glanced at them awkwardly, but Ruby paid them no mind. All she wanted was to hug her mom…

“Come with me,” Alex finally said. She wiped away Ruby’s tears. “Let’s talk.”

“You hit your boss.”

Jess nodded. “Yeah. I suppose I’m getting fired.”

Winn snorted. “Oh, please. Lena’s more likely to give you a raise just for standing up to her. I…suppose you’re not going to let her make you stay behind again.”

The secretary shook her head firmly. “No way in hell. I’ve been looking over my shoulder to make sure I don’t get ambushed by a cat enthusiast again.”

They were sitting in the mess hall, both having had the idea of getting a last snack before trying to fall asleep. A few other people were milling about, having had the same thought, but no one was paying them any mind. Everyone was off in their own worlds, doing their best to cope with their anxiety.

This was their second chance. Everyone knew there would not be a third.

He wanted to tell Jess to stay behind. She had too much to live for…a son depending on her. Even though Jess was empowered by Harun-el, she still wasn’t a match for a true Kryptonian. The odds that her presence alone would make a difference were remote.

But Winn knew that was pointless. If he were in her position, he wouldn’t remain on Earth. There was a reason that Lena had taken her out of the previous fight via ambush.

“Lena Luthor is the best boss ever,” Jess said. “And if we somehow win tomorrow, I’m putting cinnamon in her coffee every day for the next year.”

The techie sat back in his chair. “And how is that a punishment?”

Jess grinned slightly. “Lena’s allergic to cinnamon. Nothing dangerous, but it makes her lips get all puffy. She doesn’t tell anyone because it would conflict with her ‘invincible supergenius I’m-taking-over-the-world-to-save-it’ persona.”

Despite being on the literal eve of the most important war in human history, Winn couldn’t help but laugh.

“So…I heard you took down Purity,” the secretary said with a forced casual tone. “That must have been…interesting.”

Winn’s face went red. “Kara did most of the work, I just held her down,” he replied. Superheroes were supposed to be humble, weren’t they? In his fight against Purity, Winn couldn’t have cared less about personal glory; his only aim had been to stop the Worldkiller and save lives.

Still, after sitting on the sidelines for so long, it felt good to have actually contributed for once. And if it won him the praise of a pretty girl, well....

“Come on, Lena. Fuck me.”

The villain had never hated herself more than in this moment. Giving Kara another dose of RedK had been the hardest thing she had ever done. The hero had been right; it was the logical option. If Earth’s defenders were going to win, Supergirl would need to be willing to do whatever was necessary.

That wasn’t the real reason why Lena had eventually agreed. In the end, it had come down to her personal selfishness. After having been thwarted and humiliated, Alura and her minions would not be in a merciful mood the next day. Even Kara might not be spared.

Lena couldn’t let her die. Hesitation is defeat. Defeat means death. A Kara willing to kill was a Kara far more likely to survive.

“Lena.” The hero was kissing her neck, lovingly running her hands over Lena’s chest.

It was undeniably hot, but it didn’t feel right. Kara wasn’t in her right mind. Yes, they had had sex many times previously and were already engaged, but still. It felt like taking advantage of her heroine in the worst way possible.

“Your inhibitions are already weakening,” Lena argued. “I don’t-”

Kara laughed. “Oh, please. You think that after we win and I’m cured of RedK, I’m going to regret sleeping with the woman I plan to marry? Who, may I remind you, I’ve fucked dozens of times already?” She leaned forward, her breath hot in Lena’s ear. “Do couples never have sex while one of them is a little drunk?”

Lena resisted the urge to melt into Kara’s touch. “You’re on RedK. Not alcohol.”

“Psssh. Same thing. Less inhibitions, but I’m still fully conscious of what I’m doing.” She paused her speech to nibble at the CEO’s earlobe. “It’s been a month, Lena. We’re going to war tomorrow, and I am not going to die horny just because you’re being self-righteous.”

That’s it.

Lena whirled around, grabbing her girlfriend’s arms and pinning them to the bed. “Fine,” the supervillain said, heat blossoming in her chest. “You want to fuck me? I’ve been in a cell for weeks, Kara. Do you know how many times I’ve dreamed about this? So you better not disappoint me.”

“I love it when you give the orders.” Kara could have easily overpowered Lena’s grip, but instead she leaned forward and began to undo the CEO’s blouse with her teeth. “My rich, powerful, sexy-ass girlfriend who’s going to rule the world. Fuck,” the hero whispered as she stared up at Lena’s form. “You’re such a goddess.”

This could be Lena Luthor’s last night on Earth. If fucking her girlfriend was wrong, then Lena simply didn’t have the strength to be right. For the next hour, she was going to enjoy herself. Kara was right…dying horny would suck.

She smiled down at her hero, her gaze predatory. “I am, aren’t I? Beat the World Chess Champion in an online game when I was five, won the nobel prize in four different fields. I dominated this planet with nothing but my intellect.”

Kara had called her a megalomaniac the first time they’d met in her office. That wasn’t really true. But Lena could admit that, in her most private moments, acting like one was enjoyable in certain situations.

Like when she was straddling her super-hot, submissive girlfriend.

Supergirl was finished unbuttoning Lena’s blouse now. The CEO released her grip on Kara’s arms, allowing her girlfriend to raise the blouse off her body. Her hands came back down to lovingly stroke Lena’s temple. “I better there’s more brainpower here than on the rest of the planet combined.”

“There is,” Lena replied with a smirk. According to all of her estimates, anyway.

Another quick flourish of Supergirl’s hands removed Lena’s bra. Kara simply stared at her for several seconds, breathing heavily despite not being the slightest bit exhausted. As the pause went on, Lena raised an eyebrow. “Why do you hesitate?”

Kara’s eyes were twinkling, her pupils dilated with arousal. “I wouldn’t presume to touch such a brilliant and powerful goddess without her permission.”

They were going full out into their fantasy, and Lena absolutely loved it. “Worship your Empress,” she commanded.

And Kara did. Lena was quick to reward her afterwards. Neither of them lasted very long- the product of long confinement and forced separation -but that was remedied by a second round. And a third. Until at last they fell asleep in mutual contentment, wrapped tightly in one another’s arms.

“I love you,” Kara whispered. “RedK or not.”

“I know,” Lena replied. “You are my world, Kara.” She kissed her fiance’s forehead, closing her eyes as they still basked in their afterglow.

We will not die tomorrow. I refuse to let it happen.

Alex was terrified. There was no shame in admitting that. They were going into war outgunned. She herself would be on the front lines, powerless and vulnerable. Her mother was in the hands of a genocidal dictator and could be killed at any moment.

Dwelling on her fear served no purpose, so the agent simply accepted it and moved on. She managed to coax herself to sleep that night by focusing on Ruby’s body as it snuggled into her motherly embrace, lulled into unconsciousness by fantasies of a family that might never be.

The morning came all too soon as her alarm blared. Can’t believe I might never hear that again…one benefit of the end of the world, I suppose. She made her way into the briefing room with the rest of the bunker’s inhabitants, taking her seat near the front.

There were fifty of them. Harun-el operatives, superpowered individuals, and powerful aliens. Even knowing that there were other forces in the other three bunkers, it seemed far too small for any army about to fight the most important battle in Earth’s history.

Lena addressed their assembled forces, her voice transmitted to the other bunkers. It was all information that Alex already knew. They had roughly one-hundred and thirty fighters on their side, along with a force of five hundred drones. Alura had one-hundred and fifty Kryptonians, all now equipped with protection against Kryptonite.

And then there was Alura herself, worth dozens of fighters on her own. In the end, it all came down to Alura. She was the only one who had control over both Myriad and the pods of Kryptonians. If they killed her, L-Corp’s forces could use her body to turn off Myriad and avert the activation of Argo’s reinforcements.

Alex glanced at Lena. How much was the CEO not telling them? There were secrets Alex was privy to that were not being shared to the rest of their forces, but that didn’t mean the agent knew everything. Hopefully, the CEO had an ace up her sleeve, because Alex still didn’t like their odds.

The plan, as it was presented to their wider forces, was relatively simple. Argo was currently in chaos, still under constant attack from automated jet planes. It would be relatively easy to deploy several teams of L-Corp’s troops throughout the city. From there, they would target and eliminate any of Argo’s agents.

Their drone support and the element of surprise might even the odds a little against the Kryptonians, but it would still be an uphill battle. Unless Alura was taken down quickly, the best they could hope to achieve would be a bloody stalemate.

What if she just runs away and waits for the soldiers in those pods to wake up? It was a distinct possibility. Alura wouldn’t run unless her forces were losing, itself a dubious proposition. L-Corp’s operatives would be tracking her every movement via satellite in anticipation of just that scenario, but there was no guarantee any of their forces would be able to catch her in time.

They would use her pride against her, hoping the matriarch wouldn’t think to retreat until it was too late. Until then, they would just have to survive against her ludicrous strength and speed as well as the one-hit-kill known as the Omega Beams.

Alura. It all comes down to Alura.

Alex would relish a chance at revenge. The urge for vengeance had been a dreadful thirst inside of her ever since Maggie’s death, and it had only grown with each new casualty. But now that she had a target for her wrath, her dream was farther away than ever. Yes, Alex would be going to Argo, but she was now no stronger than a regular human.

Her gaze switched in Kara’s direction. A brief flash of red in her sister’s eyes confirmed that the hero had roped Lena into her plan. The very thought made Alex uneasy, but thinking about Kara dying on Argo was worse. If RedK increased Supergirl’s odds of survival even a fraction, Alex would condone it.

Why isn’t she asking me to stay behind? Either Lena had told Kara the full story, or the hero assumed that Alex still had some power. Or the RedK is already affecting her thought processes.

A quick shudder passed through the agent.

“You have your assignments,” Lena was saying. “Stick with your team leaders and follow their instructions. There is no room for mercy today. No retreat, no surrender. This is it. Go to your transports. We roll out in ten minutes.”

Alex’s walk to the hanger paused as a small body slammed into her side. “Please don’t go!”

She smiled down at Ruby, keeping the sadness out of her eyes. “You know I have to, kiddo, and you know why.”

Ruby nodded, hugging Alex tighter. The agent could tell that despite her young age, Ruby understood perfectly. She didn’t make Alex promise to come back…lies were of no use to any of them. Ruby’s embrace grew tighter, not out of an attempt to hold Alex back on Earth but out of a desire to show her affection.

“Careful,” Alex said. “I think you’re stronger than me.”

What will happen to her, if we lose? Even with her forces out for blood, Alura would end up with many prisoners after the battle if Argo was victorious. Then they would be tortured, both with physical pain and the knowledge that they had utterly failed. Soon enough, they would tell their captives where to find the bunkers, and then…

Alex refused to think of it.

Lena watched as her small army made their way into the transports. She forced herself to memorize each and every face, knowing exactly what she was asking of them. This was going to be a bloodbath even in the best case scenario.

She was joined by her team in their own transport. Kara, Winn, Alex, Jess, Selina, and four other Harun-el infused operatives. True, Supergirl and herself could have flown to Argo unaided, but it made more sense to stick with their team.

“Look at who we’re with.” Jacobs, one of the agents, spoke up. “The head honcho herself and her inner circle. I guess that makes us the red shirts.”

Nervous laughter echoed throughout the transport as the vehicle took off. Even Lena couldn’t hide her anxiety as her gaze turned to the window. The ground above the hanger opened, hundreds of feet of rock and dirt sliding apart revealing the stark blue sky. The only one who didn’t seem to be fidgeting with nerves was Kara, which was not a comforting thought.

It’s time to end this.

The Burning World

Argo City burned.

Starfire should have been happy to see the enemy’s stronghold crumbling. She could see hundreds of jet aircraft outside the transport window, watching as they continued to bomb the floating city and its inhabitants. To her, it all felt like such a waste. Argo was a marvelous piece of technology, an ark that had preserved billions of lives from a dead planet and given an entire society a second chance.

Now it was a weapon of war and needed to be crushed. That didn’t mean the princess was happy about it.

The damage to the buildings and structure of the city was catastrophic, but ultimately superficial. Conventional bombs and missiles could do little against a prepared Kryptonian defense. It was up to L-Corps’ soldiers and drones to do the real work.

“Target their suits,” her squad leader was saying. “If their protective equipment is damaged, they will be vulnerable to kryptonite from our drones. Strike hard, fast, and without mercy,” he reminded them.

Starfire glanced down sadly at the two kryptonite knives in her hands. Then her eyes hardened, and she nodded to herself as the transport opened.

“Go.”

\

Over a dozen separate teams were landing on Argo. Each had their own objective, though their chances of achieving them were uncertain at best. One was to attack the command center, another was aiming for the city’s power generator, and a third was going after the pods of sleeping Kryptonians.

In a word, they were decoys. With the support of L-Corp’s drone armada, their primary purpose was to whittle down the enemy’s forces and divide their defenses. It was a transparent strategy, but Lena knew it would be effective. If the command center fell, communications would be disrupted. The destruction of the power generator would send Argo plummeting to the Earth, killing countless Kryptonians still sleeping in their pods.

Alura could ignore all of these threats. Only killing the High Councilor would enable Earth’s defenders to stop Myriad and save their planet. Even if Argo crashed to the ground, Myriad would still remain active. Enough Kryptonians would survive to overwhelm their defenses.

But the CEO knew she would not. Letting L-Corp’s forces knock Argo out of the sky or capturing some of their pods would not be acceptable to the matriarch. Knowing one’s enemy was key, and Lena had studied her opponent thoroughly. Alura was proud, and she had staked her ego on protecting the lives of all her people. Some would call her selfless, but Lena wasn’t fooled for a second.

You may tell yourself you have a responsibility to the Kryptonian race, but your pride comes before all else. It was a mindset Lena had long since grown to recognize, having spent years living with Lex Luthor.

Was she herself so different? Lena would have liked to think so. She would gladly go down in history as a villain, or simply be forgotten, if it meant saving her planet. The CEO would get on her knees and beg if it meant assuring Earth’s survival and prosperity.

But begging won’t help here. This victory can only be won through blood.

Lena’s transport landed last, after the other teams had already engaged. They landed in what was once a park, having purposely selected a wide-open space. Alura would have to be lured to them, and that meant they needed to allow themselves to be found. Only then would it be time for…

“Fliers!”

Four Kryptonians were converging on their position. Lena felt a brief shiver of fear and quickly suppressed it. “Kara, with me! Winn, stay close to the rest of the squad.”

Supergirl immediately rocketed into the air, colliding with her opponent with such force that some of the decaying trees splintered under the shockwave. Lena followed her into the sky, teleporting next to another Kryptonian before he could react. Her blade of nanites slashed through the air, nicking his protective suit.

The last two soldiers targeted the rest of the squad. Lena glanced down briefly to see Winn raise a shield of green energy, but the others would have to fend for themselves. Her own combat required all of her focus.

A smoke bomb dropped from her suit, blanketing the air with a thick fog. Lena’s suit could see perfectly, but the smoke had been specifically calibrated to block typical x ray vision. As her opponent flailed through the sky searching for her, the supervillain teleported to her fiancé.

Supergirl was grappling with her own opponent, evenly matched in strength.

“Kara, down!”

The hero disengaged, falling out of range as Vanity’s suit formed a massive nanite tendril. The appendage caught Kara’s opponent completely off guard, wrapping around his torso before he could react.

Enjoy my upgrades.

Countless volts of electricity emanated from the appendage, frying the Kryptonian’s skin. Even as he writhed in pain, Lena mentally commanded the tendril’s nanites to superheat themselves.

SWISH!

The villain’s original opponent through off the smoke and rocketed towards her. NO! Lena’s free arm materialized a hard light shield, cracking under his punch but not breaking. Then Supergirl was flying at him, tackling the invader hundreds of feet through the air.

“Stop!” the Kryptonian in her grasp begged as his protective suit began to literally melt away under the heat. Lena wasted no time in transforming her left arm into a blaster and firing a concentrated beam of kryptonite.

His eyes began to blaze with blue energy.

BZZT!

Supergirl, having kicked her own opponent to the ground, intervened with her own blast of heat vision. The energy struck Lena’s prisoner right between the eyes, stunning him even as Vanity’s kryptonite blaster continued to fire. His desperate writhing began to subside.

Now! Lena retracted her tendril, formed her arm into a kryptonite blade, and stabbed him through the hole in his suit.

“One down!” Kara called. Her own opponent was flying back up off the ground, staring at them with murderous intent. Supergirl responded with a massive gust of freeze breath, slowing his speed and briefly blinding him.

It only lasted a second, but it was just enough for Lena to engage her thrusters and tackle the invader into the ground, instantly forming a crater. Kara followed her at top speed. Her kick lashed out at the Kryptonian's neck by the time the dust settled.

Snap!

“So much for him.” Supergirl shoved the body aside with her foot. “Let’s get back to the others.”

She stared at Kara. I did this. I…

 Ignoring her torrent of emotions, Lena nodded.

\

Kara felt great. Two enemies were taken down, another step closer to their goal. Logically, she knew her reaction was the result of the RedK, but did it really matter at this point?

This time, she didn’t feel the urge to conqueror the world as a goddess. Lena must have given her a small dose, and it hadn’t been inside her for very long. She still loved her friends, her sister, and…of course…her fiancé. Now, however, that love was accompanied by hatred of the invaders who had dared disturb her life.

Everything would have been perfect if not for you. Which is why you have to die.

By the time they’d made it back to the rest of their squad, Winn and the others had already taken down the other two Kryptonians. They’d been joined by five L-Corp drones, each fully armed with kryptonite.

That’s four down.

“Think Alura knows we’re here?” Jess asked.

Lena’s gaze was raised to the sky as the CEO scanned the air carefully. “Most of her forces are engaged with our soldiers, but she’s coming. I’m certain of it.”

“Are we winning?” Alex asked.

The supervillain didn’t answer.

Alex looked to be about to repeat her question when a scream erupted into the air, so close and so loud that even human hearing could perceive it. The voice was horrifyingly familiar. A bruised and bloody figure emerged from the wreckage of a fallen skyscraper, limping her way into the outskirts of the devastated park.

“Mom!”

Alex charged forward, covering the short distance between herself and the wounded Eliza easily. Kara ran right up beside them, taking in her adopted mother’s injuries. Her skin was blackened in several places and multiple cuts were visible through her tattered clothes, but Eliza’s breathing was still steady.

Relief and anger burned through Supergirl in equal measure. Alura would pay for this, and the punishment would be her life.

As their squad surrounded her, Eliza coughed loudly. “She’s here. Alura is-”

Distracted by Eliza’s condition, Kara was too slow to react as a blast of Omega Beams burst through the air. Not Winn. He shoved himself forward, materializing a massive green sword and deflecting the attack with a single swipe.

“Impressive,” a familiar voice intoned. Alura was floating down to the ground several meters in front of them, seemingly not perturbed in the least. “But how long can you keep up such heroics, I wonder?”

Supergirl wondered too. Winn was still standing tall, but Kara could hear the wobbling in his knees. He wouldn’t last long against the Omega Effect. None of them would.

We have to kill her quickly. But can we?

“After all your scheming, all your efforts…where did they bring you? Right back to me. There will be no mercy this time, Kara. Today is the day you watch your friends die. Starting with that pathetic specimen you thought could replace me.” Alura frowned, pointing at Eliza. “And after it’s done and Earth is culled, you will finally realize where you truly belong.”

Supergirl stepped out in front of Alex and Eliza, her arms tensed in a protective stance. Alura’s tactics were simple and cruel. She had released Eliza to them only to make Kara watch as the matriarch killed her immediately. It would demoralize the squad, proving that none of them could hope to stop her.

And it will punish me.

Kara’s eyes were blazing with blue energy. She could see other Kryptonians hovering nearby, but Alura’s backup wasn’t her concern. The hero stared at her birth mother, refusing to give into fear. “We’re not going to lose to you. Not again.”

Alura smirked.

No! The matriarch became a blur of motion as she charged forward, aiming directly for Eliza. Even Kara, the fastest member of the squad, had barely any time to react. In the microsecond that it took for Alura to close the distance, Supergirl desperately tried to move to stop her charge. She knew it was too late. Alura was going to reach Alex and Eliza, and-

WHOOSH!

Another blur of motion came out of nowhere from behind Kara, meeting Alura with equal speed. A cloud of dust erupted from the point of impact as the matriarch found her charge stopped cold, locked in a contest of strength with her new opponent.

Even as she grappled with her enemy, the matriarch’s eyes were widened in shock. “How are you-?!” she grunted as she was pushed back, barely maintaining her ground.

“Got you, bitch.”

The new arrival threw her arms forward, shoving Alura back through the air. The High Councilor’s feet hit the ground several meters away, skidding across the ground.

Jess’s voice matched Kara’s own shock. “Sam?”

“Impossible!”

Sam stepped forward, her eyes brimming with energy. “How I’ve waited for this moment.” Reign had been the one to possess her, and Selena had been responsible for giving the Worldkiller her direct orders. But in the end, they had both been pawns of Alura.

It all comes back to you. You’re the reason I had to watch as the monster controlling my body alienated my daughter for sixth months. You broke Alex’s heart twice, first by killing Maggie Sawyer, then by allowing Reign to take me. Yesterday, you nearly killed me. You’ve caused so much pain to so many people…it’s time for some suffering of your own.

Alura hissed, settling into a ready stance. A blast of Omega Beams erupted from eyes. They were fast, but not fast enough to stop Sam from jumping to the side at the perfect moment. The energy hit the ground where the CFO had just been standing, dissipating inside the melting concrete.

Her body bursting with power, Sam charged forward at top speed.

She slammed into Alura with such force that the two women were launched into the air, well above the ruined skyscrapers of Argo. Lena’s squad were small dots on the ground by the time the matriarch broke the grapple, sending Sam floating backwards with a punch to the gut.

Sam growled, then flew forward once again. Alura did the same, meeting her with such speed that a wave of force exploded from the point of impact. Both combatants unleashed a furious barrage of punches and kicks, neither scoring a decisive blow. Green claws extended from the CFO’s hands, furiously seeking out Alura’s flesh.

A blow to the forehead sent Sam stumbling back. As the CFO recovered, the matriarch’s gaze burned with Omega energy. In the split second before the beams could be fired, Sam unleashed a sonic scream at her opponent.

Alura winced in pain as the attack connected. The force of the scream sent her moving back, disrupting her concentration. The Omega Beams sprouting from her eyes dissipated into nothing. Through the haze of battle, Sam could see the High Councilor’s eyes still widened in shock.

What Alura didn’t know was that Sam was now more than a mere Worldkiller. Lena had removed the last traces of Harun-el from Alex as she stood at Sam’s bedside, removing the agent’s last link to Pestilence’s powers. Those powers had fled to the closest available conduit. Then the captive Purity, her human soul having been extinguished, had been quickly executed in Sam’s hospital room.

The end result, as Lena had intended, was that Sam now wielded the power of all three Worldkillers. Her enhanced powers completed the healing of her body within hours, bringing her back to consciousness just in time for the war to begin.

Her ears continued to pick up the distant sounds of battle from where she had left Lena’s squad. No reinforcements yet.

What frightened Sam was that Alex was with them. The agent was now completely human. She had volunteered herself to come to Argo in order to preserve the element of surprise, so that Alura wouldn’t suspect the Worldkiller powers had been transferred. If she’d realized, she might not have revealed herself.

I just need to kill you. Sam stared intently at her prey. I kill you, and they’ll all be safe.

Silena’s whip lashed out, wrapping around the neck of her target. The Kryptonian, having pinned Jess to the ground and been poised to beat the secretary to death, was caught completely off guard. She clawed desperately at her neck, but Catwoman’s whip was no ordinary rope. The tendril was infused with strands of nth metal, and even a Krytponian could not break it easily.

Jess climbed wearily to her feet. The secretary was a walking target, made even more vulnerable by the fact that the rest of their squad had already been scattered. Their fights had carried them out of sight, as the flyers struggled to break through the horde to join Sam’s battle against Alura.

Her opponent’s eyes were glowing as she grabbed at the whip. It wasn’t pure nth metal, and it would break eventually. Silena used all of her superhuman strength as she spun her weapon around, whipping the Kryptonian through the air and releasing her at the moment of maximum velocity.

The invader went flying through the air, smashing through a thirtieth-floor window of a nearby skyscraper.

“Go!” Jess demanded. “I’ll be fine.”

The thief wasn’t so sure. Save for two L-Corp drones, there was no support in sight. But it was in Jess’s best interest that Silena keep her fight as far away as possible.

Without any more words, Catwoman nodded and leapt through the air. Even months after having been infused with Harun-el, the strength at her disposal still felt exhilarating. The wind rushed across her face as she soared through the sky.

Silena landed right where she had thrown the Kryptonian, the broken glass of the window marking her location clearly. Amidst the remains of what had once been an office floor, her opponent was already climbing to her feet.

Swish! Catwoman threw a bola- also infused with nth metal- at the Kryptonian’s legs. It was kicked aside contemptuously, slamming into the rotting wreckage of an old desk.

“You really think you can take me?”

Silena grinned. “You’re new to Earth. Cats have nine lives, didn’t you know?” Nth metal claws extended from her fingers, gleaming wickedly in the weak sunlight.

Her opponent stepped forward. “Then I’ll be glad to take them all.”
