“Mom, come on!” Alex tugged her mother through the street, dragging them into the cover of a nearby building. Eliza’s breathing was pained, hitching with each step they took. It didn’t matter. Neither of them would last a second against a Kryptonian, and their only hope was to hide.

“Alex…”

The agent groaned, practically carrying her parent. “Not now!” She dragged her mother through a splintered set of doors, placing them in a side room without windows. They huddled together behind a still-intact counter, both gasping heavily.

“Was that woman who saved you…was she…?”

“My girlfriend? I think so.” Alex smiled despite the situation. If Sam hadn’t intercepted that punch, both the agent and her mother would be paste on the street. She was terrified for Sam, of course, but also proud. Even with her enhanced powers, it took serious strength of will to climb out of a hospital bed that fast.

Go get her. Make her pay!  

Eliza placed a hand on Alex’s shoulder. “I’m so proud of you, dear. Kara too. There are millions of daughters on this planet, and I was lucky enough to get the two best girls a parent could ask for.”

“We were the lucky ones, mom.” She hugged her mother tightly.

Eliza patted her on the back reassuringly. “No. I did my best, but I…I have a lot to be sorry for. I shouldn’t have put so much pressure on you after we adopted Kara. I practically demanded you give up your childhood for her…I blamed you whenever she had an incident at school. It wasn’t fair. You never asked for any of it.”

Her mother was voicing thoughts that had slithered inside Alex’s head for years, but she no longer cared about any of it. “Maybe you made some mistakes, but I will never blame you for giving me a sister. It was the best thing you’ve ever done, and I’m just sorry it took me so long to realize it.”

“Your sister…” Eliza pulled back to look into Alex’s eyes. “Tell her I’m sorry too. I shouldn’t have made her hide herself. When she came to us, I never tried to keep up with her traditions. I made her change to fit my life. It should have been the opposite. Tell her…”

Alex shook her head fiercely. “You’ll tell her. We’re going to win today.”

“You will. I know that! But…” Eliza winced. “Did you think Alura would let me go if there was even a chance I could survive? She was too angry, dear. Even if she planned to kill me herself, Alura made doubly sure…”

The agent’s entire body froze. Eliza’s words made complete sense, but they couldn’t be true. They couldn’t be true, because if they were then Alex’s world had ended.

“What did she do?!”

Eliza’s breathing was more labored now. “The poison is designed to slow my heart rate. I...I’ll stop breathing in about two minutes.”

Alex jumped to her feet. “Let’s go!” she yelled, not caring if any Kryptonians heard her. “There has to be an antidote. We can search her office, or find Lena-”

“Why do you…” Eliza wheezed. “Why do you think Alura didn’t choose a more painful poison? She picked one for which there was no anti…antidote. I’m sure Lena could make one…but no time.” Seemingly exhausted from speaking the words, Eliza laid down on the ground. Her chest was barely moving.

The agent wasn’t upset. Her mind simply refused to process the words she was hearing. Eliza had been a pillar of love and support since she was a child…even through her adult years. Dressing me up for school. Cheering as I graduated college. Comforting me after my first break up. It was simply ludicrous…impossible to accept that it could ever end.

“We need to get help. Get up!” she tugged at her mom’s arm. “Move, damn it!”

Eliza shook her head weakly. “Stay…with…me…” Her eyes closed.

“Mom? Mom?!”

\

Starfire blocked the blow with her left arm, but nothing she could do would completely stop the power of a Kryptonian. Her opponent grinned as he heard her bones crack. He immediately followed up with a scything kick to her already dislocated elbow.

Pain! The alien’s left arm became a rod of white-hot agony. Her eyes flared bright green. The powers of a Tameranian were fueled by emotion, but her culture had always considered it taboo to draw upon their darker impulses for strength.

She was in too much pain to care. Not like that custom did my people much good any way.

The glow of her starbolt flooded through the alley. The princess’s anger, pain, and desperation fueled the blast, throwing her opponent off his feet and briefly blinding him. A nearby L-Corp drone seized on the opportunity, diving after the invader and slashing at his throat with a kryptonite blade.

Any life lost was a terrible waste. That was what she had always been taught. But at the moment, all Starfire could think was that it was another step closer to her goal. Each fewer Kryptonian meant that the Earth was a little closer to saving.

This planet has accepted me. I will not let it down!  

Another Kryptonian was zeroing on her position. She was pinned down on the west outskirts of Argo like most of her team. The command center they’d been targeting was miles away, well and truly out of their reach.

But they could still fight. For now.

\

“Our squad is falling back,” Mr. Terrific spoke into the comm. “We can’t stop them.”

Ms. Luthor’s voice was strained, but it carried through clearly. “Just keep them occupied as long as you can. There’s already too many-” the CEO broke off briefly as a blast sounded through his earpiece. “Too many here. We can’t reach Alura!”

The hero looked at the dead Kryptonian at his feet. They’d been engaged by Argo’s forces well before they could reach the power generator on the east side of the city. Half of his team was out of action, either dead or lying unconscious in the rubble of the ruined city. The Krytponians had suffered casualties as well, but nearly as many.

And not nearly enough.

\

“I don’t know how much longer we can hold. Some of them might already be heading to your position.”

Lena shut off the comlink. There were simply too many enemies opposing them. Flashes of light and concussive blasts still echoed from far above the city, which meant that Sam was still taking on Alura. But how long could the CFO hold out alone?

Where is Shiva? It’s time to act.

\

The L-Corp drone fighting beside her was smashed to pieces. That didn’t stop Supergirl from picking up a piece of its shattered kryptonite blade, pinning her weakened opponent to the floor, and stabbing him through the stomach.

She burst through the roof of the building she’d been fighting in, scanning for threats. Other Kryptonians were fighting and flying nearby, but it seemed as if Kara was unnoticed for the moment.

This is my chance! I have to help Sam!

Supergirl’s telescopic vision could see the CFO a mile in the air, still trading punches furiously with Alura. She winced as Sam took a blast of Omega Beams straight to the chest, but even then the Worldkiller refused to fall.

“You!”

Kara fell onto her back as she was tackled at superspeed by yet another Kryptonian. She kneeled him hard and fast twice in the stomach, weakening his grip on her throat. Yet he was still pinning her down, leaning to the side as he dodged her blast of heat vision.

Another figure burst into the air! A suit of black nanites launched itself from a nearby building, heading straight for the battle in the sky. Lena! Kara headbutted her opponent, desperate to join her fiancé.

As Kara watched, another blast of Omega Beams sent Sam reeling. A kick from the High Councilor sent her spinning hundreds of feet through the air. By the time the CFO righted herself, Alura had already sighted the rapidly approaching Lena Luthor.

NO!

The next blast of Omega Beams slammed into the supervillain’s suit. The heat was so intense that steam rose from the impact, obscuring Lena’s falling body from view. Even Kara's x-ray vision couldn't adjust fast enough to pierce the fog. By the time the smoke cleared, the CEO was already in the middle of a smoking crater on the ground.

A member of Kara’s squad appeared out of nowhere. The operative lunged forward, stabbing at her opponent with a kryptonite blade. The Kryptonian disengaged from his grapple with Supergirl as he dodged, but the attack still grazed his side.

Supergirl kicked him away, leaving the operative to continue that fight. Lena’s prone form was still in the crater. Vanity’s suit prevented Kara from hearing whether her heart continued to beat, but the hero refused to accept the possibility that her fiancé was-

She took off into the air, rocketing at Alura.

Together

Chapter Notes

Sorry for the delay. It's hard for me to get the action right, so I did some rewriting!

Four waves of planes approached Argo from all directions. Unlike the multiple of jet fighters that continued to harass the city’s defenders, these had been produced directly by L-Corp and built for a single purpose. Their payload was valuable…too valuable to send in as a first wave and risk destruction. But now, with the invaders fully occupied, the time was right.

\

“Princess.”

Starfire ducked another blast of heat vision. “I’m here!” she replied back into her handless commlink. Each of L-Corp’s fighters had a direct link to a handler back in their bunkers, ready to help coordinate their forces. The handlers were supervised by company’s head tacticians, who now coordinated overall strategy with Ms. Luthor occupied.

What advice they could give at the moment, other than ‘survive’, the Princess couldn’t imagine.

“We have an incoming bombing run. All forces are to use the opportunity to disengage and regroup at a single position. It’s several klicks from your current location, so I’ll need to guide you.”

She was raining down starbolts at her opponent, keeping him at bay. The Kryptonian struggled against her blasts, but Starfire couldn’t keep this up forever. Already, she was breathing heavily. “Just tell me where,” the Princess said quickly into her comm. “I’ll be able to see it.” 

“No one is going to see much of anything in a few seconds. Prepare for bombing run in three…two…”

\

Argo was engulfed in a massive series of explosions as the planes dropped their ordinance. Clouds of green smoke erupted from the points of impact, quickly spreading out to engulf the entire city in a poisonous fog. The gas rapidly overtook the streets, expanding rapidly from thousands of initial detonations. 

Jess coughed heavily as the haze overtook the entire park. The air was so thick with green smog that her enemies slipped out of view. The x-ray vision provided by the Harun-el did nothing to pierce the darkness; it was as if the substance had been designed to block her sight.

Which, of course, it was.

The gas did nothing to block her hearing. Jess’s coughing quickly subsided, but from the sound of it her opponent was desperately gasping for air. All of Argo’s defenders were wearing protective suits, but this particular soldier had been slashed by Selina’s claws. The secretary remembered having seen blood trickle out of the rupture in the suit.

Harun-el allowed L-Corp’s agents to emulate Kryptonian abilities, but it did not give them a weakness to Kryptonite. Supergirl had been rendered immune from the substance thanks to Lena’s vaccine. Argo’s inhabitants weren’t so lucky.

Jess resisted the urge to wince as the Kryptonian woman gagged violently as the poison began to take effect. This was war, and their enemies had forfeited their right to live.

How many of them will die from this smoke? A dozen? More? Their suits will protect them at first, but if our agents can expose them just a bit…

The secretary stumbled away, stepping quickly across the rotting grass of the park. Ms. Luthor. The last she had seen of her boss, the CEO had been struck out of the air by one of Alura’s Omega Beams. Jess refused to accept even the possibility that Lena was gone, but the supervillain clearly needed help.

Green fog still blocked her vision, but Jess the Secretary had a memory for detail. She remembered where her boss had fallen. It would take only minutes to find her.

\

“Look around you, Kara! Is this what you wanted!?”  

Alura performed a wide sweep of her arm, gesturing to the city far below. Thick clouds of green smoke were suffocating all of Argo, and Supergirl had no doubt as to what it was. She smirked as thin whisps of the substance stretched up towards her. Kryptonite had long been her greatest fear; its mere presence had cut deep into her soul. Now, her lover had made her immune. Better.

“To see the people invading my home die?” Kara retorted. “Yes, this is exactly what I wanted.”

The High Councilor narrowed her eyes at Kara in suspicion but had no time to voice her next thought. A crimson beam of energy erupted from Sam’s eyes, one which the matriarch barely dodged.

BZZT! Alura retaliated with her Omega Beams. Sam moved to dodge, but the effort proved unnecessary as a bright green shield materialized between the two women. As the barrier absorbed the blast, Supergirl rocketed forward and punched her mother right between the eyes.

“Oof,” the matriarch grunted pathetically. But Supergirl had no time to celebrate. Even as she fell backwards through the air, Alura retaliated with a kick at Kara’s head. WHAM! The blow barely clipped her face, yet the impact still sent her reeling. Stars danced in her vision.

She righted herself, shaking her head. How dare Alura strike her?! “I am going to kill you!”

A sonic scream sprouted from Sam’s mouth. The High Councilor scowled and slammed her hands together, releasing a wave of force so great that it diverted the soundwaves. Winn was struck directly, and the Lantern clasped his ears and convulsed in pain.

Another torrent of Omega Beams blasted from Alura’s eyes. Only Sam was fast enough to react, moving in front of Winn just in time to take the attack. Even with all the powers of the Worldkillers at her disposal, the CFO screamed in agony.

Kara breathed deeply, gathering air in her lungs before expelling a cloud of freeze breath from her lips. Alura broke off her attack on Sam to expel an even larger just of air, deflecting Supergirl’s attack to the side.

The CFO recovered and darted forward, extended her green claws engaging Alura with a barrage of blows. As the High Councilor retaliated, the impacts of their punches and kicks struck with such force that even Kara was buffeted through the air.

A blast of heat vision erupted from a combatant below. Supergirl shifted to the side to dodge, even as her new assailant was suddenly engaged by two of L-Corp’s drones. It seemed that most of L-Corp’s remaining drones and agents had regrouped on their position. They continued to hold Argo’s defenders at bay, preventing them from coming to their leader’s aid.

But for how long? More Kryptonians were rising above the fog and joining the furious battle in the skies. At a distance, the dozens of darting combatants looked like a swarm of angry bees trying to devour itself. Yet no matter how small they looked, each of them was capable of leveling a city.

So much power in one place.

Sam and Alura continued to exchange attacks. Neither woman made any attempt to block the other’s blows. Each simply wanted to damage the other as quickly as possible…as brutally as possible.

Supergirl fired off a burst of heat vision…just in time. The blast scorched Alura’s forehead just as the High Councilor was about to launch another assault of Omega Beams. A bright green visor materialized on the matriarch before she could recover, obscuring her vision.

As Kara watched, tendrils of barbed wire erupted out of Winn’s ring. The emerald bindings latched themselves onto Alura’s limbs, wrapping around her arms and trying to hold them in place. Alura shrugged them off, continuing her melee with Sam, but more wire continued to pour from Winn’s ring. With each strand that the High Councilor snapped, another immediately took its place.

A few of the barbs even managed to graze her skin, but the shallow cuts seemed to heal immediately. Kara had never seen a wound recover so quickly.

It’s time! Supergirl flew behind her mother at maximum speed, reaching out for Alura’s neck.

WHAM! The matriarch’s head slammed backwards, smashing into Kara’s nose. Supergirl staggered back through the air as she heard her cartilage snap, pain radiating across her face.

Two swift kicks to Sam’s midsection sent the CFO backing away. A third sychted through the air and slammed into Sam’s her right hand, shattering four of her green claws. Howling with pain, Sam kicked off the High Councilor to gain precious distance.

Ignoring the tendrils of wire trying to dig into her skin, Alura reached up and clawed the visor off of her face. The next blast of Omega Beams slammed into a shield Winn barely raised in time.

The explosion sent him plummeting towards the ground, nearly slamming him into the pavement.

Alura was glaring at Supergirl, the High Councilor’s eyes blazing with energy yet again. Knowing that the Omega Beams were too fast to outrun- and nothing available in the wide-open skies above Argo to absorb the energy- Kara unleashed her own blast of heat vision.

The two streams of energy collided in midair. Supergirl’s heat vision disintegrated before its opposition, and the Omega Beams continued to rush forward.

“NO!” Kara screamed in agony as the blast took her full in the chest. She had been hit with her mother’s power before, but not like this. Even as her skin flared in agony, it seemed like her blood was burning away.

No. Not her blood. Something else. Something…

The Omega Beams ended. Kara wobbled in midair, struggling to maintain consciousness. A green platform extended from far below her, providing a solid surface for her feet and helping Supergirl remain upright.

It wasn’t the pain that was the problem. Something had changed. Everything. It felt like her emotions were rushing back into her mind; a river of guilt was carving itself into her soul. Faces she had seen over the last hour -terrified and desperate- burned through her brain.

How many have I killed?

“The Omega Effect has cleansed you of the Luthor’s poison, daughter.”

Kara’s hands were shaking wildly. She had killed repeatedly, and she had enjoyed it. This horror had been an inevitability, but now? The thought of what she had done was enough to make her vomit, and there was still far more to do.

“I asked her to do it,” Supergirl replied. “You were the one that poisoned me with RedK against my will.” She narrowed her eyes at Alura, trying to use anger to block out her horror. RedK or not, she needs to die. I know that! She will kill billions unless I stop her.

The High Councilor frowned. “I did what needed to be done. Deep down you know that. Now I ask you…can you really kill your own mother?”

Alura reading her bedtime stories…her parents telling her about the Science Guild…her mom kissing her forehead before placing her in the pod…no! Kara’s feelings didn’t matter. Alura deserved to die.

A recovering Sam was returning to the fight, though perhaps flying slower than she had once been.

Kara’s heart yearned to reach out to her mother, to beg her to surrender. Yet she knew Lena was right. The matriarch was beyond saving.

“I have to,” she replied. “May Rao have mercy on your soul.”

Alura’s eyes were burning with energy. “Save Rao’s prayers for your little friends. They are wasted on a goddess.”

Battle resumed.

\

“Ms. Luthor!”

The kryptonite fog was beginning to thin. It was bad news for L-Corp’s forces, but it was enough for Jess to find her boss’s body. The secretary leaped onto the building, knowing this was the roof where Lena had fallen.

No! The CEO was still lying prone on the roof. Smoke continued to rise from her suit. Her body seemed almost peaceful as it laid on the smooth, unbroken pavement.

Jess frowned. What? There were no marks from the impact. No crater. And even as the villain’s suit appeared to sizzle, no sound emerged from the CEO’s form. The secretary sprinted forward, placing her hands on Lena’s-

They fell through the transparent visage, hitting the pavement. All Jess’s fingers found was a tiny disc of nanites, its job finally completed.

The hologram vanished.

\

Lady Shiva’s sword slashed through the air at blinding speed. Her Kryptonian target was even faster, darting to the side and avoiding the blade. Shiva merely reversed her grip, sliding the hilt of her sword easily between her fingers, and cut out again with all the speed granted by the Harun-el.

The Kryptonian was unprepared for the warrior’s skill. She avoided the worst of the blow, but the nth metal blade still cut across her chest. Even as it was thinning, Kryptonite fog flowed through the rupture and into the wound.

Game over.

“Impressive,” Lena intoned emotionlessly as she dropped to the ground nearby. The CEO was not a fan of Shiva. She was an incredibly skilled warrior, respected across the world for her mastery of martial arts. But for Lena, one’s abilities were far less important than how one chose to use them. Shiva was not without honor, but she was more than willing to kill for selfish reasons. Altruism was not in her DNA.

Fortunately for Lady Shiva, she was useful. So much so that in the beginnings of her villainous career, Lena had sought her out for a face-to-face meeting rather than luring her into a trap and imprisoning the assassin. Shiva had agreed to work for L-Corp provided that Lena defeat her in a fair fight after the assassin was infused with Harun-el.

Lena’s suit had handed her the victory, but that hadn’t stopped the CEO from receiving martial arts training from the assassin. Shiva was far from her favorite tool, but she was valuable.

“Were you followed?” Shiva asked.

“No. Alura thinks I’m unconscious or dead,” Lena replied. As the High Councilor’s top target, the villain would never have slipped away from the fight without trickery. A lifetime ago, Lena had won her second victory over Supergirl by tricking her with a solid-slate hologram. Now Alura had fallen for the same ploy.

The assassin nodded. “The last guard I killed was very helpful before he died. I found what you’re looking for.” She gestured down the deserted street. “I hope you know what you’re doing. Alura didn’t seem to make guarding this sector a priority.”

“It was an oversight. She’s too focused on the obvious targets.” Lena turned to the small facility in front of them. There was no time to waste. The CEO wasn’t certain how well Sam and the others could occupy Alura, but it certainly wasn’t going to last much longer.

She stepped forward, moving towards the one thing that could defeat her enemy.

\

The Kryptonian’s hands were on her throat, digging deep into her skin. Selina grasped at his hands desperately. Her claws had been broken, and her opponent had the advantage of both strength and leverage. Black spots were darkening her vision.

Holly…

SLAM! A blast of green energy arced through the air, hitting her enemy directly in the face. He rolled off the weakened burglar, who took the time to intake a precious breath of oxygen. The Tameranian -not the Princess- who’d fired the starbolt flew forward to continue the fight.

The building she’d been fighting in had collapsed into rubble. Argo’s skyline was visible to her in its full, horrifying glory. The green smoke had all but disappeared. L-Corp’s forces had clearly seized their chance to regroup in the area. Dozens of individual fights on the ground and in the air formed a rough circular perimeter, keeping Argo’s forces outside a small section of the city.

L-Corp’s human and alien agents fought ferociously, knowing the alternative was a quick and painful death. Only those unconscious or too wounded to stand were out of the fight, having been brought together in the middle of the dilapidated park by their allies. How many were there? 

Too many. And countless more soldiers doubtlessly littered the streets throughout Argo, having fallen in earlier battles. Still, the pile of wounded- and dead- in the park continued to grow. The soldiers who still stood retreated from the frontlines only to bring the severely injured to relative safety before diving back into the fray.

The hurricane of fighters and energy blasts was joined with L-Corp’s remaining drones. They fought without fear or hesitation, stopping only when Argo’s forces stripped them limb from limb or crushed them into dust. Formations of jet fighters whizzed through the sky, disorienting the Kryptonians with targeted explosions.

Not enough.

Argo’s defenders had been thinned by combat and kryptonite, but it wasn’t enough. The frontline was pushed and pulled as soldiers of impossible speed engaged in the chaos of war, but the perimeter was steadily constricting inward. It wouldn’t be long before a number of Kryptonians slipped past the melee to join Alura in the sky, and with that their last hope would be gone.

Selina had nothing but her fists and her whip. She charged back into the fight.

\

Green energy surrounded Kara. Winn was slinging her through the air like a slingshot, aimed straight at Alura. The hero was contributing with all of her own power, flying at the High Councilor with incalculable force.

Alura couldn’t run. She was grappling with Sam, each woman trying to choke the other. The High Councilor’s eyes glowed with Omega energy, but a sonic scream at point blank range disrupted her concentration.  

Supergirl was flying at the enemy, all of her power unleashed.

The disaster seemed to unfold in slow motion. Alura slammed her head forward, breaking Sam’s nose. The CFO’s strength had been drained by combat, while the Omega Effect kept Alura in peak condition. Finally overpowered, Sam failed to resist as a hand wrapped around her throat.

It all took place in less than a second. Supergirl was still flying forward, half of her power and momentum provided by the Green Lantern. Winn lacked the reflexes to respond in time, leaving Kara unable to even reduce her velocity as she rocketed forward in the same direction.

In the instant before the collision, Supergirl saw a smirk on her mother’s face.

Alura moved a few inches to the left, leaving Sam in her place. The physical pain was nothing compared to the horror Supergirl felt as she slammed into her friend in an explosion of emerald energy. A flash of white streaked through the air- one of Sam’s teeth.

The green glow dissipated. Kara was stunned. Sam was nearly unconscious. That was all Alura needed to unleash a torrent of Omega Beams at the CFO. Sam’s scream of agony faded in Supergirl’s ears as the blast carried her a mile into the ground.

“Sam!”

Winn’s movement toward the falling CFO was halted as the next blast of Omega Beams locked onto the Lantern. Alura’s grin widened as she batted aside Supergirl’s burst of heat vision, watching as the beams exploded against Winn’s hastily-constructed shield.

The explosion rippled through the air. One second latter, Winn’s form was trailing smoke and falling through the sky.

Kara caught him in time, rushing to the ground as quickly as possible. Winn was unconscious, but still breathing. Supergirl sighed with relief as she heard Sam’s rattled breath as well. With one friend in her arms, she flew down after the CFO.

Sam had landed in a crater a few blocks from the main battle, having fallen so fast that none of the other combatants paid her any notice. Kara knelt down next to her, placing Winn on the ground beside the CFO.

“Do you realize how hopeless your position is?”

Alura was floating down from above, her arms folded. The High Councilor sported no visible injuries. She didn’t even look winded. “It is time for a lesson, Kara. I am going to kill your friends, and you can do nothing but watch.”

Supergirl defiantly took a step forward. She was standing alone in the rubble, with no help visible over the horizon. Her only company were the thin remaining wisps of kryptonite smoke…useless against Alura. Yet she stood her ground.

“You’ll have to kill me first.” The hero was careful to stand directly above her fallen friends, making it impossible for Alura to hit them with an Omega Beam. “Go ahead. I would expect nothing less from a monster like you.”

A moment of silence passed between them, as the sounds of distant battle still echoed throughout the city. No help was coming.”

“Daughter, you will always be my greatest disappointment.”

Kara placed a hand on her suit’s crest. Stronger together. She was prepared to die by those words, even as Alura had forgotten them. “Coming from you, I’ll take that as a compliment.”

She braced herself, holding out her arms as her enemy’s eyes glowed with energy.

The Omega Beam slammed into her form. PAIN! All she could think about was pain as the agony spread through her body. Yet she refused to move. Supergirl screamed in agony, but she maintained her position against the stream of energy. Smoke was rising from her skin…her hair was on fire. The disgusting smell of burning flesh filled her nostrils. She closed her eyes to avoid watching her skin dissolve.

Must not move. Must not.

The hero fell to her knees. They dug harshly into the gravel as she moved back an inch. It was with pure instinct that Supergirl was still straining against the blast. Alura wasn’t stopping. Kara had expected nothing less.

“You deserve this, Kara. I was wrong. I let myself feel guilty for sending you to this planet, but it is time for me to let go of that burden. You were weak for letting Earth corrupt you. Let it be known to all that Kara Danvers is unworthy of being my daughter.” Alura smiled. “She is unworthy of a quick death.”

\

Alex could hear her sister’s screams. She ran through the streets, having no defense save for a shattered blade of kryptonite. The agent was powerless, but Alex didn’t fear death. Her mother was dead. Sam was probably dead. Kara was about to die.

She moved forward. There was no hope of saving her sister, but Alex could die with her.

\

Lena could hear the screams too. Kara’s cries of agony only increased her speed. Shiva had been long left behind, unable to keep up with the speed of Vanity’s suit. The assassin had achieved her purpose, and Lena was now equipped with her weapon.

The weapon she had been angling for all along. Sam and the others had been trusted to keep Alura occupied, but the CEO had known they would fall eventually. The Omega Effect was simply too powerful.

Her blood boiled as she came upon the sight of Kara on her knees, still taking a torrent of Omega Beams for Sam and Winn. Supergirl’s skin was beginning to evaporate, but Alura seemed to have no qualms about torturing her child. In fact, she seemed to be relishing the moment.

It gave Lena the chance to cloak herself, fly silently behind her enemy, and use her weapon.

Alura barely had time to gasp as she was taken by the parasite. The thorns of the Black Mercy were even sharper than nth metal, and they penetrated the matriarch’s skin instantly. The Omega Beams vanished. Alura toppled over, falling to the ground as the plant’s tentacles embraced her.

“Kara!” Lena charged forward.

Freed from her burden, the hero crumpled on her side. Her skin was burned severely, but Supergirl would live. Lena clung to that thought as she embraced her fiancé, trying to stop her hands from trembling.

“L-lena…”

“Hush.” She materialized a blaster from her suit, spraying a coating of ice over Kara’s hands. “Don’t talk. It’s over.”

Kara’s eyes were unfocused, but they were wide. The hero could barely move, but she seemed determined to speak. “…Lena-”

A blast of horrifying intensity slammed into the villain’s back, ripping through her suit’s nanites like tinfoil and throwing her several meters away. She crumpled on the ground, barely able to turn herself over.

Her vision was hazy with pain. She saw Alura rise to her feet, tossing away the Black Mercy contemptuously. The plant was still writhing and pulsing, but it could do nothing without a host. The High Councilor was stepping forward, moving past her daughter without a glance. She slowly approached Lena, smiling in victory.

“An interesting gambit. But the Omega Effect protects more than my body. It shields my mind from any form of control. The Black Mercy might have been able to project my fantasy, but it could trick me for less than a second.”

I’ve lost. For the first time in her life, Lena had nothing left. No schemes. No back-up plans. Her strategy had been well-calculated and inventive, and it had failed utterly thanks to an immunity the CEO had had no way of knowing about.

It wasn’t fair.

“I should thank you.” Another blast of Omega Beams issued forth, slamming into Lena’s chest. White hot agony filled her lungs as she danced at the edge of unconsciousness. She was desperate for air but breathing itself was excruciating. “My fantasy gave me some wonderful ideas. Your planet burning…your people suffering. My servants torturing your soldiers who survive the slaughter today. I can make it all a reality…”

Lena had failed her planet, her friends, and her love. She wanted Alura to blast her again…death would be a mercy. Kara might still be alive, but she would soon wish that she wasn’t. Let us die together. Please.

There was movement out of the corner of her eye. Kara was crawling. Alura either didn’t notice or didn’t care. The hero was crawling in the wrong direction, away from Alura…not that it mattered. There was no other way to…

No. Kara, no.

Alura placed a boot lightly on Lena’s chest. It took all of the villain’s willpower to remain focused on her enemy. She wanted to scream out, to stop all of this…but there was no choice. The CEO was so weak she wasn’t sure she could have made a sound even if she’d wanted. The only thing she could move was her eyes, and she kept them firmly on Alura’s smirking visage.

She needed to remain conscious. If this was going to work…but Lena didn’t think she could stay awake. Alura was pressing down slowly with her foot, beginning to crush her ribcage…

A flurry of movement! Lena’s eyes were drawn to the struggling morass of blue and brown erupting behind the High Councilor. Alura turned too…just in time for Kara to slam into her. The hero released her grip on the plant as they fell, allowing the central thorn to plunge into her chest. With her last free movement, she hugged her mother fiercely.

Ensuring the thorns would penetrate.

The two women collapsed in a heap. Kara was on top, already deep in the thrall of the Black Mercy. Thorns from the plant jutted out into Alura’s form below, bringing the matriarch into the illusion. Alura might be immune from the plant’s direct attack, but she could still be brought into another’s fantasy.

Lena willed herself to rise, trying to take advantage of her fiance’s brilliant move. If she snapped Alura’s neck now, this would all be over.

But do I have the strength to?  

Or she could snap Kara’s neck. If the hero died in the thrall of the Black Mercy, everyone connected to the fantasy would perish. Kill Kara. I have to kill Kara. I can’t kill Kara.

The mental struggled raged in her mind, and it was too much. Lena’s last visage of willpower collapsed, and the villain fell into the depths of unconsciousness.

\

Kara moved through the party. Lena had gone to get refreshments, leaving the hero to chat with her friends and family. Everyone was happy, especially Alura. Kara’s birth mother was sitting on the couch, smiling broadly.

“It seems that your wife couldn’t do it,” she said.

What? A twinge of unease swept through Kara. “Do what?”

“Never mind,” Alura said. “Just enjoy yourself.” She was moving oddly, as if struggling to free herself of an invisible wire. Kara moved forward instinctively to help, then paused. Alura. Alura is…

Her mother waved her off. “I’m fine, dear. I’ll be free in just a moment. Please, just enjoy this wonderful dream.”

Yes, everything was wonderful, wasn’t it? Everyone was happy and alive. Sam and Alex were adopting another child, Clark and Lois had just won another joint Pulitzer, and Eliza was in the kitchen baking cookies. Perfect.

Kara smiled.

A New World

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

Alura clenched her teeth as she continued to extract herself from the thorns. In the real world, Kara’s body was lying on top of her own and pinning it to the ground. Multiple thorns from the Black Mercy were cutting deep into her skin. As she continued to sit in the illusion, her mind was only barely aware of her position in reality. She was free to walk and fly around this fantasy, but moving even an inch in the real world required tremendous concentration.

But she would be free. And Kara would be left to die.

The matriarch looked around the room. Kara’s family and friends were smiling and talking jovially. Multiple romances seemed to be taking place, which no doubt accounted for the unknown children running around. Kara herself was staring at the door, clearly anticipating the imminent return of one Lena Luthor to the party.

A beautiful wish, daughter. But there will be no future. Not for you.

She had loved her child, but Kara had made her own choices. One could only betray their own people -their family -before forgiveness was no longer an option. Hundreds of Kryptonians were lying dead on Earth and on Argo thanks to Kara. More would no doubt follow. Supergirl had given Alura no choice but to eliminate her as an enemy.

Her responsibility to her people came first. She was their High Councilor, and it was her destiny to lead them into a new age of prosperity. Alura would guide their civilization into a new apex, a beacon which the entire universe would eventually come to follow. Kara had simply been too weak to see it, unable to let go of her attachments to the human race.

Kara had always been weak. Alura could see it now. Her daughter would never be able to let go of any of the people she cared for. The fact that Alura was in this fantasy, despite the war that raged between them, proved it. Kara still loved her.

I will be stronger than that. I will let you go, daughter, for the sake of our people. You will die in this fantasy. May Rao have mercy on your soul.

Alex Danvers was walking towards her now. Alura simply ignored her, continuing to make progress extracting herself from the thorns. What point was there in interacting with an illusion when her life was at stake? If she was still in this fantasy when the Black Mercy killed Supergirl, Alura’s real body would die as well. Kara was already weakened by intense combat and severe wounds. It wouldn’t take the plant long to drain her dry.

She was almost free of the thorns. Alura could feel it. A few more seconds-

WHAM!

Alex’s fist suddenly lashed out, slamming into Alura’s cheek with near-Kryptonian strength. As the matriarch reeled, the human’s hands moved to grab her neck. Gasps erupted from the illusionary party guests, but Alura paid them no mind as she reflexively dodged Alex’s attempt to choke her.

The human was unperturbed, following up with a kick that caught the still-stunned Alura right in the stomach. The High Councilor was barely processing what was happening as her body smashed through the glass windows of the apartment.

Shaking off the shock, the matriarch righted herself in midair. Alex was standing next to the shattered window. Alura readied herself to blast the human with her Omega Beams…nothing came.

I have my Kryptonian powers in this reality, but not the Omega Effect. Until I get free, I’m playing by Kara’s rules.

\

Alex had never seen a more horrifying scene. Winn, Sam, and Lena were all unconscious. Kara was trapped by a Black Mercy, with Alura seemingly also forced into the fantasy.

She had no idea what had happened, and no time to figure it out. All Alex knew was that her sister was being drained of life…and their greatest enemy was suddenly vulnerable. If Kara or Alura died, the High Councilor would perish.

Kill Kara. Whether Alex would have been able to bring herself to do so, she would never know. It didn’t matter anyway. Her human body lacked the strength to harm either of the women. She could try calling for help, but it was far more likely than not that an enemy would respond first.

The color was already draining from her sister’s cheeks. She wouldn’t last long, and there was no way the hero would make it out alone. The Black Mercy grew upon its host’s brainpower to maintain the illusion. Supergirl didn’t have the superhuman intelligence that had made freeing Lena a near-impossibility, but she was still smart enough to give the plant plenty to work with.

I have to go in there.

Alex’s body collapsed the instant the first thorn pricked her skin. Consciousness immediately returned, but the ruined world of Argo had disappeared. In its place was a luxurious apartment, the sound of children scampering across the floor, and Sam on the couch next to her. The CFO smiled, placing a chaste kiss on her lips.

“Alright, darling?”

She was, actually. All of Alex’s aches and pains had disappeared. Her body was brimming with energy. She didn’t feel as strong as she had after absorbing Pestilence’s powers, but her Harun-el infused abilities had clearly returned to her.

I need to find Alura. Kill her. Then free Kara. I can move fast, but can’t fly. Alura has to be near here somewhere. Where-

Bile rose in her throat as she saw the High Councilor sitting nearby. After all of the horror Alura had unleashed, she was placed in the middle of Kara’s fantasy. Really, Kara? Really?

 There was no doubt that Alura’s consciousness had taken hold in her illusionary body. Alex could already see her moving awkwardly, no doubt trying to free herself of the thorns in the real world. The agent wasn’t sure how strong her enemy was in this world, but there was only one way to find out.

WHAM! Her fist smashed against Alura’s jaw. The matriarch reeled but managed to dodge Alex’s attempt to grab her neck. Even as she processed her dread at the lost opportunity, her foot lashed out and caught Alura in the stomach.

The impact sent the Kryptonian out the window, but Alura immediately righted herself. Alex’s blow had struck hard, meaning her enemy didn’t have the Omega Effect. But she did have her Kryptonian powers, which were greater than Alex’s own.

Fuck.

It took half a second for Alura to realize that all she needed to do was fly away and escape Alex’s range. The agent used that time to leap out of the shattered window, slamming into her enemy and tackling her into the street below.

\

Kara stared out the window in shock. Alex had suddenly attacked her mother, without warning or provocation. The hero knew she needed to go help…diffuse whatever situation had led to this…but something felt wrong.

Or, rather, something felt right. Alex fighting Alura didn’t seem surprising. It felt natural, which didn’t make sense. Why would two of her family members be fighting? The world seemed to shake at her confusion, even as the sky grew a shade darker.

The rest of her family had barely seemed to notice the situation. They were still going through their routines. Sam was finishing a glass of wine as Ruby playfully wrestled with two of the younger kids on the couch. Even Lena, who had just walked in carrying two bags of snacks, didn’t even look at the broken window.

Lena.

“Kara!” the CEO greeted with a smile. “I brought potstickers!”

No. That wasn’t right. Kara wasn’t supposed to eat potstickers yet…not until they were married. But aren’t we already married? The ring on her finger seemed to agree, even if the hero couldn’t even remember receiving it.

The world shook again.

“Lena, why aren’t you reacting to this?!” she gestured wildly to the wall. “Why can’t I remember anything?!”

Her lover shrugged. “Sometimes we don’t remember the things that are most painful. It’s probably best left forgotten. Everything’s fine here. Alex and your mother are just sparring dear. Come on, aren’t you hungry?”

Yes, Kara was hungry. But…painful memories? What was she suppressing? There was something there, an undercurrent of fear and uncertainty flowing through her body. Why couldn’t Kara put her finger on it? What the hell was going on?

I can’t remember. I can’t bring myself to remember, because if I do then… I have to…

She looked at Lena’s face as the world shook again. Sam’s empty wine glass fell from the table and shattered on the floor, but no one paid it any notice. Memories flashed through her mind…staring at names on a page. People dead of plague. People dead because of her hesitation.

Not again. 

The world shook as Kara struggled to move. The bags of potstickers fell from Lena’s hands, spilling open on the floor. An alluring aroma filled the living room. Wouldn’t it be better just to sit down with her friends and have a snack. Everything was fine. Lena had said so.

And when has Lena ever said anything like that?

\

Alex had her enemy pinned to the ground, but Alura hardly looked concerned. It was taking all of the agent’s strength to pin her opponent to the gravel of the road. The matriarch was struggling against her, slowly slipping free with her superior strength. Once she broke free and flew away, it wouldn’t take her long to escape the illusion.

The High Councilor smiled. “You can’t possibly win.”

Alex glanced at the sky. The light in the fantasy was fading rapidly. It looked as if the sun itself was vanishing out of existence. Kara was losing strength quickly.

I could never live with myself if I let Kara die.

But, then again, she wouldn’t have to. Kara, Alex, and Alura would all die together. The Omega Effect would go to the closest survivor…probably Lena. Alura’s DNA could be used to deactivate Myriad, and Earth would be saved.

Kara wouldn’t blame her. Supergirl would tell her that she was making the right choice. But knowing what she had to do still made Alex’s heart split open.

“I don’t have to win,” Alex hissed down at her enemy. “I just have to make sure that you lose.”

Alura’s own eyes looked toward the darkening sky, widening as they saw the danger. The matrarich’s head reared forward, but Alex avoided the blow. The movement jolted her, allowing Alura to slip her left fist out of Alex’s grasp.

“Ugh!” the agent grunted as Alura’s punch slammed into her stomach. The High Councilor threw her off, climbing to her feet.

No! Alex jumped forward desperately, wrapping her arms around Alura’s midsection and tackling her to the ground once again. She held on with all her strength, locking her fingers together over the matriarch’s chest.

The High Councilor fought furiously. Her elbow slammed into Alex’s ribcage, cracking bone. Alex had barely registered that pain by the time the back of Alura’s head smashed into her nose. It was agony, but the agent embraced it. She allowed it to fuel her, refusing to loosen her grip on her hated enemy.

Maggie. Lois. Sam. You killed my mother, you fucking bitch!

The bitch was trying to rise into the air. The agent clenched Alura even tighter, pulling her back to the ground. With a sudden yell, the High Councilor reversed her momentum and smashed Alex back into the ground. The wind left her stomach.

Alex’s strength was spent. It was pure adrenaline keeping her going now. Hatred of the woman who had ruined her life and fear of what would happen if she got free. Sweat was pooling from her fingers, making her grip ever more slippery. Her teeth were clenched, but she didn’t even have the energy to scream with exertion. Alura was too strong…she was slipping free…

A shadow appeared out of nowhere, ripping Alura from Alex’s grasp!

Within two seconds, the new arrival had wrestled Alura into a headlock. An arm covered by a blue suit was wrapped around the High Councilor’s neck. Alura’s own hands clawed at the limb restraining her, but it didn’t budge.

“This is my fantasy,” Kara said. “You have no more power here. You’re human, now”

Alex climbed to her knees as Alura took a shuddering breath. “Daughter, don’t do this!” the matriarch begged. “You don’t want to do this! This isn’t you!”

“No.” Supergirl sighed heavily. “But for the world to live, you need to die.”

Alura actually sobbed. “You’re not a killer! Not your own mother!”

The hero’s gaze was tormented, but resolute. “I’m what the world needs me to be. If saving Earth means sacrificing part of myself…I can do it. My fiancé taught me that.”

Twin beams of blue light appeared in the hero’s eyes. Alex watched as the heat vision slammed into the back of Alura’s head, melting through the matriarch’s now-human skin like paper. The blue energy ripped through the other side in an instant, slicing through Alura’s forehead before dissipating into the distance.

Then it was over.

Alura’s body toppled over to the side, spasming pathetically one final time before falling still. Kara fell to her knees. The hero was staring at her trembling hands, her mouth slightly open. “A-Alex. Alex, I-”

The sky was still darkening. “Kara, we need to get out of here!”

“…Yeah.”

\

Lena swam in and out of consciousness. The villain was still trying to climb to her feet…except she didn’t have feet. Alura’s Omega Beams had blasted one of her robotic limbs clean off. She needed to get up. Needed to…rise just a few inches…

Through her hazy vision, she was Kara, Alura, and Alex all caught in the Black Mercy’s embrace? Alex? When had Alex gotten there? Lena couldn’t remember, and the mental effort sent her collapsing back to the ground.

“H…ahhh.” The CEO looked up as a soft breath passed Alura’s lips. Then the matriarch seemed to deflate, her body almost melting into the ground. Lena’s enhanced hearing could no longer hear her heartbeat.

Is she…dead?!

Red energy issued from her body, seeking out its next host. There were two suitable candidates equally close by, and the Omega Effect appeared conflicted. The red energy separated. Half disappeared into Kara, the other half into Alex.

The Black Mercy shriveled seconds later, falling off to the side. The Danvers sisters both rose to their feet quickly, their wounds seemingly fading.

“Lena!” Kara raced over to the villain’s side, helping her rise off the ground. The movement made her body ache, but Lena barely noticed the pain.

Kara, Kara, Kara.

She placed a hand on her fiancé’s chest. “You have the Omega Effect. You and Alex. Half of it, each. Do you feel any different?”

The hero frowned. “I feel strong, like I could fly to the next galaxy and back. But no urge to conquer or anything. Just me. I guess…it looks like Alura was never under any influence at all.”

“Kara, the energy healed you. Maybe you can use the Omega Effect to-” Lena broke off as a set of Omega Beams fired from Supergirl’s eyes. The villain reflexively winced, but the energy passed into her body painlessly. She felt wonderfully warm as the cuts on her skin mended, her exhaustion faded away, and even her ribs seemed to knit back together.

She smiled at Kara breathlessly. “Well…that was a risk.”

Supergirl shrugged. “It feels natural…like I’m using a third arm. No risk. Now we need to go. This war isn’t over.”

Out of the corner of her eye, Lena saw Alex using her own Omega Beams on Sam and Winn. As they climbed to her feet, the CEO hardly dared to believe it. Alura was dead. Victory was within her grasp, and all she had to do was seize it.

All she wanted to do was to melt in Kara’s arms, but Lena forced herself into business-mode.

“I have a plan,” the villain said.

\

The final battle for Argo and Earth ended with a whimper, not a bang. Winn flew into the center of the raging battle, carrying Alura’s body on a green contraption and holding it up for all to see. Many of the remaining defenders surrender en-masse, and those who didn’t were quickly knocked unconscious by the combined power of Sam, Alex, and Kara.

Most of L-Corp’s forces had survived, and those who were badly wounded were quickly healed by the Omega Effect. Jess ran up to Lena the instant she saw her, shoving aside the agent who had been supporting her weight and proudly taking up that duty for herself. The CEO caught glimpses of Selina, Starfire, and Mr. Terrific in the commotion as Alura’s forces were either carried or pushed into L-Corp’s prison transports. With the vehicles all equipped with heavy-duty red sun lamps, the odds of escape were remote.

Lena didn’t feel like celebrating.

After the work was done, Kara found her way to the villain’s side. No words needed to be said. From the look on her lover’s face and her knowledge of Alura’s tactics, there was no doubt that Eliza Danvers was dead.

Kara was in shock as she leaned on Lena’s shoulder, the two of them sitting on a ruined sidewalk. There were no tears. They would come later, when there was time to mourn and process the calamity. Given how Alex was walking towards them with a determined look on her face, the agent felt the same way.

Though Lena doubted that Alex would be half as composed if Sam weren’t standing at her side, looking for all the world like she was ready to follow the agent into hell if need be.

\

Turning off the reactivation of the pods came first. Lena had assured her that all of the Kryptonians would be awakened eventually, once the logistics were in place, but Kara couldn’t bring herself to worry. She knew she should, but there were other priorities at the moment.

Surprisingly, guilt wasn’t one of them. Kara had killed several Kryptonians under the influence of Red-K and executed her mother after the substance had been removed. At another time, that probably would have sent her into a tailspin. Not now. And it wasn’t because the Omega Effect was affecting her personality, or the fact that Pestilence had been her first kill months ago.

It was the pain. Eliza’s death had put things into perspective. Why mourn invaders who’d needed to die when the woman who had raised her had been murdered?

Eliza. I should have called her ‘mom’. I wish I had.

Then it was time to deactivate Myriad. They went alone to the command center, leaving Sam and Alex behind in the city just in case any of the Kryptonians decided to try a breakout.

“You’re not okay,” Lena said softly as they landed in the command center, Kara now supporting her weight.

“No. But I will be…because that’s what E-…what mom would have wanted. I just…I miss her already, and I haven’t even really processed…”

Lena smiled sadly. “I’m not a therapist, Kara. But despite how busy I’m going to be these next few months, I’m here for you. You know that.”

The hero leaned into her lover’s shoulder. “I do. And that means more than you’ll ever know. Though some professional counseling might not be a bad idea after all of this.” She sighed. “Ready to free the world?”

“Almost.” Lena paused in front of the central console, holding up her collected sample of Alura’s DNA. There was a strange gleam in her eye. “I’m going to unlock the program, but I can’t destroy it. If I just let everyone free immediately…can you imagine the panic?”

Kara could imagine. “So what’s the plan?”

“I’ll take control of Myriad and speak to everyone on Earth. From the last time I used it, I know that I have enough brainpower to divide my consciousness between each being on Earth. I can give each one an individual message,” Lena explained.

The hero’s fingers froze on the control console. Now she understood the gleam in the villain’s eye. “This isn’t just to calm things down. You’re going to use this to take over the world, aren’t you?”

Lena shot her a small smirk. “Of course I am. But I’m not giving them anything but the truth. I’ll show them how our world was helpless before an alien invasion, and that the only reason we’re still standing is because my plans went as far as they did.” The CEO smiled. “I’ll let them see a glimpse of my mind, so that they realize I’m both smart enough to lead this planet and that I have the best of intentions.”

“But…Myriad is…”

“Evil?” Lena answered. “Any tool can be used for good or evil. I’m not trying to seize control of anyone’s thoughts…or even distorting their memories.” She looked at Kara, her gaze imploring. “I’m letting them see the truth of my mind…what I’ve done to get to this point and how I plan to move forward. How they choose to use that knowledge will be up to them.”

Supergirl was skeptical. “You’re going to tell them everything?”

Lena didn’t even look fazed. In fact, it seemed like she had rehearsed this conversation a thousands times…which she probably had. The villain had planned this from the beginning.

“Not everything,” Lena answered. “Enough that they’ll see I really do want what’s best for everyone…and how intelligent I really am.”

“Lena…”

The CEO held up a hand before continuing. “They’ll learn how a force of humans and aliens worked together to save our world from a hostile force…how Supergirl fought against her own people to save us all. We’ll minimize the backlash against aliens and the general panic that will ensue.”

“And have everyone ready to follow you,” Kara pointed out.

“Not everyone,” Lena clarified. “But once they see the truth of how I coordinated the effort to save this planet, and how I plan to keep it safe and prosperous, most of Earth’s population will be willing to follow me.

Kara hesitated.

The supervillain kept speaking. “We have three choices. One: deactivate Myriad immediately, which will lead to mass panic. Not an option. Two: Give everyone the basic facts before we deactivate the program. Fear and uncertainty spread across the planet, humanity becomes more xenophobic than ever, and it takes me years more to build our defenses. Earth remains vulnerable. Or three: My plan, which gives everyone enough of the truth to provide a vision of hope for the future, and increases trust in L-Corp.”

“In you, you mean,” Supergirl pointed out.

Lena smiled thinly. “It’s not my choice. It’s yours. You and Alex both have half of the Omega Effect. You each could take me down whenever you want.”

“That’s not what I want.”

“I know, Kara. But I think it’s good that I’m not invincible. There are two moral people out there who could stop me in my tracks,” Lena said. “Look how we got here.” The CEO spread out her arms. “You learned to let go of some of your principles. I made the choice to attack early…against every instinct telling me otherwise.”

The words were truer than Lena even knew. The CEO hadn’t yet been told how Alura had died. That was a conversation for later, sitting in their penthouse next to two large cups of tea.

Lena held out her hand. “This is what I’ve wanted from the beginning. You and me, ruling the world together. Not through fear or force, but by showing everyone that we can be trusted. We can set that path in stone, right now, and all we have to do is tell them the truth.”

Supergirl crossed her arms. “So this is usually the part in the story where the villain makes the hero a final temptation of power, isn’t it? Don’t you know how that usually ends?”

“I didn’t think that was this kind of story,” the CEO answered.

Kara shook her head. “No, it’s not.”

She stepped back from the console and took Lena’s hand. “Do what you have to do. If it weren’t for you, everyone on Earth would be Alura’s puppet from birth until death. We need someone to lead us into the future with hope, help, and compassion for all. I’ll be at your side every step of the way.”

Lena bit her lip. “But…”

“But if you cross the line, I will overthrow you,” Supergirl promised.

“I can handle that.” The villain laughed lightly, relief evident on her features. “As long as you promise not to leave me.”

Kara used her superspeed to wrap her fiancé in a hug. “Never. And you better marry me soon, because I really miss potstickers. So, go ahead. Send your message.” She motioned to Myriad.

Lena smiled. “Yes, ma’am.”

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

“Kara, you don’t have to pretend,” Alex said.

The hero frowned. “Pretend about what?” she replied, sitting down in one of the conference room chairs. Kara stared out one of the windows at the bright sunny day, taking care not to wrinkle her dress.

“I know this isn’t how you imagined it,” her sister answer. Alex hopped onto the table and crossed her legs, avoiding messing up her own dress through enviable grace. “You wanted something small, a peaceful gathering of the people you care about. Not a media circus.”

“No, but I’ve got no right to complain.” After the chaos of the last year, Kara was alive. She had the woman she loved, a bright future ahead of her, and more power and wealth than she’d ever wanted or needed. “This is what has to be done.”

Alex moved a lock of hair away from her eye. “Yeah, it is, but that doesn’t mean you have to be happy about it.”

Kara was getting married. To Lena. The thought still made her heart skip with excitement, which was only slightly diminished by the thought that her upcoming nuptials would be more of a publicity stunt than a wedding. She and Lena had both wanted a private ceremony, but L-Corp’s PR department had strenuously objected.

'You’re the two most popular people on Earth, a symbol of human-alien coexistence and a beacon of stability. People need to see you get married. It will show everyone that the chaos is over and things are finally stable. We can’t miss this opportunity!”  

Lena could have simply overruled them, but that wouldn’t have changed the fact that they were right. Both women had reluctantly agreed. They’d sought and received special permission from the National City authorities to hold the event on the wide street in front of L-Corp. Most world leaders would be in attendance. The nearby blocks would be flooded with citizens, and the networks were projecting a television audience of over three billion.

“We could have a second, private ceremony whenever you want,” Alex offered.

Supergirl shook her head. “Lena said the same thing. No. It wouldn’t be real. This is our wedding. It might not be the ceremony of my dreams, but if it helps make things better…then I’m happy with it.”

The unspoken truth hung in the air between them. Kara would never have the wedding of her dreams. Clark, Lois, James, Lucy, Maggie, and Eliza would always be absent. Even thinking about them seemed to knock the air out of her stomach. Kara welcomed the peace that Earth had experienced the last six months, but the calm had given her mind far too much time to remember…

“Ruby is still far too excited,” Alex said, changing the subject.

Kara smiled at that. The thirteen-year-old might be a little older than normal for a typical ring-bearer, but there really had been no other choice. Besides, this wasn’t a wedding entirely based on Earth customs. Bracelets would be exchanged, not rings.

“Hopefully she’ll still be young enough for your wedding,” the hero replied.

“Oh, I-I don’t know.” Alex blushed, her cheeks glowing bright red.

Supergirl simply smirked. Alex’s relationship had blossomed in the last few months, the baggage stemming from Sam’s possession having seemingly melted away in the face of mutual affection and Ruby-driven encouragement. Any resentment the two women still had was directed at the dead Worldkiller, and Kara suspected that their relationship had moved farther than either woman had omitted.

Ever the dutiful big sister, Alex was doing her best not to steal any of Kara’s spotlight.

\

Lena looked out the window, drawing comfort from the familiar logo. Her wedding preparations were taking place in a conference room across from the main L-Corp building.

The CEO had had no desire to emulate her brother’s desperate ego-stroking and make her headquarters higher and higher, but expansion had been a necessity. L-Corp had long since bought out the surrounding blocks, using each building to house its various departments. The complex was growing so large that it was almost a mini-city onto itself, but every square inch was necessary when the company was running most of the world.

Well, that requirement wasn’t quite accurate. Much of the space was devoted to restaurants and (most importantly) coffee shops. Lena had finished her acquisitions of all of the major coffee chains months ago, though she kept them separate to encourage competition. All of their products were now sold at cost, Lena considering it ethically morbid to make a profit from the lifeblood of humanity when she had so many other sources of income available.

The original L-Corp building had changed little by itself, with the exception of its logo. L-Corp remained L-Corp, but its headquarters was now adorned by a new symbol. The L-Corp logo had been fused with Supergirl’s crest, creating a symbol to both reflect the company’s identity and honor National City’s greatest hero.

And now, it would symbolize her marriage.

I’m marrying Kara!

“I hope you got her something good,” Sam said. The CFO was wearing a suit, like Lena. Alex had wanted to wear one as well, but the marrying couple had wanted to keep the wedding party symmetrical. “You’re marrying way out of your league, you know.”

Lena smiled and nodded. “Don’t I know it. At the reception, I’m unveiling our new water distribution program.” It wasn’t the most exciting project, but it was extremely critical. L-Corp’s infrastructure would soon be moving vast quantities of water around the world, taking moisture from the clouds themselves. Areas oversaturated with rain would see some relief, while drier areas would see their droughts end permanently. Much of the water would be purified and given to communities directly, ensuring that nearly the entire planet’s population had access to clean drinking water.

“It’s impressive,” Sam agreed, obviously knowing all of the details as the company’s CFO. “But you would have done that anyway, and Kara knows it. Please tell me you got something special for her.”

“Oh, I did. It won’t be ready for some time, but I think she’ll appreciate it.”

\

Lena personally didn’t hold much in the superstition that one shouldn’t see the bride the night before the wedding, but Kara absolutely refused to step within a mile of the villain before their wedding began. Which meant that while the rest of the Superfriends were enjoying a small celebration in Alex’s apartment, Lena was on her own.

Alex had offered to organize a separate party for Lena after Kara’s finished, but the CEO had turned her down. The wedding reception would be more than enough for her, and this free night gave her the chance to conclude some unfinished business.

For that reason, she conducted her monthly visit to L-Corp’s prison a few days earlier than scheduled. She received regular updates on her prisoners, more than willing to release those who had paid for their crimes and demonstrated that they were no further danger to society. Tonight, however, she was adding another stop.

To a prisoner who would never be released.

“Ah, the prodigal daughter returns,” Lillian intoned as Lena stepped in front of her cell. “I see that you’re flush with victory, but it won’t last.”

The CEO raised an eyebrow. “And how did you come to that conclusion?”

“Because your velvet glove approach will never work in the long run. Lex learned that lesson early. Fear and superior firepower are the only way to ensure domination. Oh, you may consider yourself ‘ruthless’, but you would never risk the life of a so-called ‘innocent’, would you?” Lillian asked rhetorically. “Nor will you ever take action to purge this planet of the alien filth that infests it. They’ll turn on you sooner or later, and take everything you have.”

Lena sat down on the bench, crossing her legs. “I didn’t come here to listen to your deranged xenophobic ravings. Although, for the record, I’ve won.” She smiled smugly. “L-Corp is dominant in every notable industry on the planet. Those who opposed me have, for the most part, accepted the inevitable. After I broadcasted my thoughts and intentions through Myriad, no elected official is able to oppose me without being voted out of office.”

It was true. There had been a prolonged period of morning after the invasion had ended. Millions had died during the occupation due to natural causes, and the rest of the planet had had a month stolen from them. The fact that an invading enemy had managed to subjugate Earth so seamlessly had terrified the human race and the planet’s alien immigrants, and there was still a palpable sense of ease among the citizenry.

Fortunately, that fear led hearts and minds right to the only organization that had shown itself capable of defending the planet: L-Corp. By and large, the people of Earth had placed their trust in Lena, and she wasn’t going to let them down.

“Why are you really here, Lena? Gloating is beneath you.”

“Where you are concerned, Lillian, gloating is most definitely not beneath me. I’m only human, after all,” Lena smirked. “L-Corp is only going to grow stronger in the coming years. Governments will enter into partnerships with me, gradually handing over their responsibilities and authorities until they become nothing but rubber stamps. I will turn this world into a utopia. But the most important thing for you to know is that my mere existence will erase the memory of your precious baby boy. Lex will become nothing but a footnote in history, and the Luthor name will be washed of his stain forever.”

Lillian’s fingers clenched on the bar of her metal chair, but she kept her face neutral. “I’d like to see you try.”

“Oh, you will. I’ll make sure you’re kept updated. The real reason I’m here, though, is to let you know that you failed.” The CEO took a breath, no longer trying to keep the venom out of her voice. “You and Lex tried to break me…to make me into one of you. For all my intellect, I was a scared little girl desperate for comfort when I walked into the Luthor manor. You pushed me down, to make me weaker than my brother. Lex was there to pick up the pieces, whispering sweet words of reassurance in order to bring me to his side.”

Lillian shook her head. “Lex loved you.”

“Lex saw me as a useful minion, nothing more. I’ll admit, you did have some influence on me. I’ve been more ruthless than I should have been. I was even willing to sacrifice a billion lives for a sure chance at victory. That’s your upbringing, and it’ll never fully go away,” Lena admitted. “Fortunately, I’ve found someone who will keep me in the light. I’m marrying her tomorrow.”

Finally, Lillian scowled. “She’s an alien. It’s disgusting. Kara Zor-el might not have green skin or seven fingers, but she’ll never be one of us.”

“And yet that doesn’t stop me from having hot interspecies sex with her every night,” Lena replied, smiling as her adoptive mother grimaced in revulsion. “And, by the way-” the CEO rose to her feet and turned to leave. “She’s taking my name. Kara Zor-el Luthor-Danvers.”

Her grin widened as she stepped through the door, hearing Lillian’s hands slam into the bars with fury.

\

“I thought I’d find you here.”

Kara had excused herself from the party a few minutes early, claiming that she’d wanted some privacy. Apparently, Alex hadn’t been so easily fooled. The hero sighed as she felt Alex sit down next to her in the grass.

They both stared forward silently. The simple mound of stone in Midvale Cemetary was illuminated only by a patch of moonlight, but Kara knew the words by heart. Eliza Danvers. Devoted wife and mother. A true hero to all who knew her.

Supergirl finally forced herself to speak. “If I hadn’t come to Earth-”

“Then mom would still be alive?” Alex finished for her. “Yeah, you’re probably right. But she would have considered that well worth the trade. She loved you so much, Kara.”

“I should have told her,” Kara managed, her voice carrying over the crickets chirping in the night. “I should have called her…”

Alex wrapped an arm around her little sister’s shoulders. “She knew. You were her daughter, Kara, and nothing could have convinced her otherwise. I…wish she was going to be there tomorrow. I won’t be right without her, not really. But she died happy. Mom knew we were going to win. She knew we both had bright futures ahead of us. That’s all that mattered to her.”

Supergirl found herself chuckling softly. “Mom would never have forgiven us if we didn’t make the most of it, would she?”

“Never,” Alex agreed.

\

Kara was on her knees, pleading freely as she struggled to shift away from the glowing green rock. “No, not today…” she groaned.

The thieves’ ringleader shrugged, holding the kryptonite out forward. “It didn’t have to be this way,” the woman replied. “You weren’t supposed to be here. Why do you think we picked today?”

Supergirl shot her a menacing glare. Kara knew exactly why they had picked today. She had just changed into her wedding dress, Alex at her side, when an alert had come through L-Corp’s network. A team of sophisticated thieves had broken into the U.S. mint in Denver, supported by some hired alien muscle that had all but smashed into the vaults.

“Did you think I wouldn’t come?” Supergirl asked, gritting her teeth. L-Corp’s drones handled a lot of hero work these days; they were just as capable as Kara of holding up crumbling construction equipment or carrying civilians to safety. But today, hostages were involved. A huddle of federal employees were huddled in the corner, staring down an AR-15 and a grinning Czarnian.

Alex had offered to take over the rescue or assign another hero to the job, but Kara had turned her down. Alex was skilled in fighting powerful opponents, but she didn’t yet have the practice with her powers to use them as precisely as Supergirl did. If Alex took the mission, the hostages were in slightly higher danger. And the other heroes simply couldn’t match her abilities.

If it improved the hostages’ odds of safe recovery by one percent, then Kara had to go herself. And so she did.

“I did not,” the leader admitted. “I’m glad you did, though. How much will Luthor pay for her fiancé’s safe return? Ten billion? A hundred?”

Kara gasped as the kryptonite inched closer. “You really think getting on Lena Luthor’s bad side…is a good idea?”

“I’m a gambler,” her enemy replied. “I’ll keep a couple of hostages with me long-term; Luthor won’t risk civilians. It’ll be easy to afford some new guards with the money Luthor will-”

Supergirl dashed forward at maximum speed. The leader didn’t even have time to widen her eyes before Kara lightly thrust her arm forward, calmly placing a finger against the leader’s forehead. It was a carefully calculated use of force, and it did its job perfectly. Her opponent flew backwards and onto the ground, unconscious but alive.

By the time her body hit the floor, Supergirl had already flown across the room in a blur. Two more light taps to the pair of human accomplices and a quick punch to the Czarnian had every thief unconscious in less than a second.

The hostages shouted and recoiled, having gone from ‘mortal peril’ to ‘rescued’ in between heartbeats.

Now that the danger had passed, Kara made another show of stumbling away from the kryptonite. The chunk of green rock was now on the floor, near the feet of the unconscious leader. “That…still hurts,” the hero moaned as she looked toward the hostages.

“T-thank you…”

Supergirl smiled back. “You’re welcome. Time for me to go.”

She took off through the building and was in the clouds within seconds. Kara had, of course, been inoculated against kryptonite prior to the invasion, and her Omega powers only increased her immunity. Lena had ordered that this information be kept secret. If resourceful criminals knew that Supergirl’s weakness was gone, they might employ other measures to foil her heroism…measures that put innocents in more danger.

Kara’s pride in her acting abilities – it took some effort, after all, to pretend to be nearly helpless – vanished immediately as she remembered exactly what she was missing. By the time she floated down in front of L-Corp headquarters as best she could, her face was bright red.

Lena was already standing at the altar, looking as immaculate in her suit as always. She was the very essence of a confident executive. The image brought to mind activities the two women had shared on Lena’s conference room table, which only made her face burn brighter.

The crowd clapped gratefully as she landed, letting forth some good-natured teasing. By now, the audience both in the streets and watching at home knew she’d been delayed by an emergency. Somehow, that didn’t diminish her embarrassment at being late to her own wedding.

“I thought we were going to walk down the aisle together?” the hero whispered.

Lena shot her a bemused smile. “The crowd was growing restless, darling. Someone had to explain your absence.”

“You’re not mad?”

The supervillain shook her head. “The woman I fell in love with would never let anything get in the way of her saving others, even if it was the most important day of her life.” Lena glanced over Kara’s shoulder. “Alex, though, is probably going to be giving you grief over this for years.”

Kara looked behind her. The sparkling of her sister’s dress didn’t quite match the fire dancing in Alex’s eyes. The agent had just been handed a decades’ worth of sister-teasing on a silver platter, and she clearly planned to take it.

“If we may begin…”

The rest of the ceremony passed in a blur. Kara was well aware that billions of pairs of eyes were watching her, but all she could do was stare at her fiancé. This compassionate, powerful, brilliant woman wanted to marry her, and it was happening. It was happening!

She was only jolted out of her reverie when Lena’s fingers gently enclosed around her wrist, bracelet in hand. “I, Lena Luthor-Danvers, take you to be my wife and partner. By all the customs of Earth and Krypton, I declare us as one.”

Kara took her own bracelet from a grinning Ruby with trembling hands. “And I, Kara Zor-El Luthor-Danvers, take you to be my wife and partner. Under Rao’s light, and standing before the people of Earth, I declare us to be one.”

They kissed.
