One more chapter to go, and then we're gone! Big time skip coming up!

Epilogue

Chapter Notes

See the end of the chapter for notes

She hadn’t intended on making a big entrance. Kara had touched down calmly, well out of sight of any cameras, and slowly walked towards the stage. The hero approached carefully, weaving between the crowd and trying to appear as non-threatening as possible.

“Supergirl. It’s Supergirl!”

That lasted until a member of the crowd finally recognized her. Kara wasn’t wearing her uniform, but neither had she bothered with a civilian disguise. There had been no point of that for over a decade. Even without her cape and tights, she still had one of the most recognizable faces on the planet.

There was hurried shuffling around her as the crowd backed away. Supergirl had been incredibly careful to avoid instilling fear over the years, but these people had just been echoing derogatory chants about her wife. Even if Kara didn’t often show it, they knew she was physically the most powerful individual on the planet.

The speaker on stage, however, showed no fear.

“Well, if it isn’t Supergirl. Here to put us back in our place?” the woman asked, her eyes glinting with venom.

Kara shook her head, trying to appear conciliatory without displaying weakness. “I’m only here to listen, and to try and work out a solution to this problem.”

Tiffany Warner laughed scornfully, gesturing for Kara to join her on the stage. “And how are you going to do that? While we all appreciate your swooping in to stop crime and save the day, this seems to be above your paygrade.”

The hero repressed a wince. Lena had sent her because she was L-Corp’s most popular and recognizable asset, not because Kara had a firm handle on the issue. Supergirl was there to start a dialogue on the issue, not fix it herself.

“By inviting you and your associates to a meeting with L-Corp’s Board,” Kara replied, keeping her voice firm and loud for the cameras to hear. “Lena acknowledges that you have some fair points, and while she still thinks her Free Trade Program is a good idea on the whole-”

“I don’t care how much money your wife has; she can’t buy us out,” Ms. Warner interrupted. “We’re not here for a handout. We just want our jobs, plain and simple! Isn’t that right everyone?”

The chanting resumed. “JOBS! JOBS JOBS!” was the main through line, but Kara’s hearing also caught several exclamations of ‘fuck you!’ and ‘Loser-Corp!’

Supergirl hated seeing protests like this. The others were a lot easier to ignore. So many protests against L-Corp and Lena were based on little more than pure bigotry- unsurprisingly, a lot of people had an issue with a pro-alien and pro-immigrant lesbian running the world in all but name.

These protestors here, however, had a genuine point. Lena had recently implemented a free trade agreement with a large coalition of developing nations. She’d waited for years, until L-Corp gained enough influence in those regions and used its resources to put them on a semi-equal playing field with the west. Companies would now be able to fully move into those countries, offering jobs and economic growth but unable to offer substandard wages.

The time had come where allowing Amercian companies to once again spread to new horizons was a net positive for the world. It did, however, lead some people in a worse position. There were always trade offs in governance. Many American workers would lose their jobs in the short term.

She glanced out at the crowd, seeing the righteous anger on their faces. And Kara knew there would be no compromises that day.

\

“You shouldn’t feel guilty, sweetheart. You weren’t the one who signed that trade agreement,” Lena consoled her wife.

Kara shot her a small smile. “Technically, neither did you.”

The CEO simply shrugged back. “Semantics.”

Yes, the current President had signed that agreement. And yes, he had been put into office in a free and fair election.

Of course, few got elected these days without L-Corp’s official endorsement. In its early days, bribery, blackmail, and outright thefts by Vanity had given the company a headstart. But now, it had grown so large that it could afford to play fair. Lena was generous with this success, and that ensured L-Corp’s continued popularity.

Lena’s stunt with Myriad and role in ending the Kryptonian invasion also played a large role, of course.

Everyone knew that Lena was Vanity, and no one even bothered issuing denials at this point. However, executives and governments around the world had given L-Corp blanket pardons for ‘Any and all past actions taken to defend Earth and its people.’ It was a previously unthinkable step, but alien invasions had a way of changing the status quo.

Yes, their approval ratings around the world were high. However, popularity was never universal, and the decisions Lena had to make did sometimes have negative side effects. It was part and parcel of governing.

Kara sighed. “I’m sorry I couldn’t pressure them into talking with you.”

Lena waved the concern away. “I didn’t really expect them to come to the table. Warner is nothing if not stubborn. All we needed was to show everyone else that we’re open to dialogue, and-”

“Moooom!”

Kara immediately glanced at their bedroom door, an exasperated smile on her face. “Looks like we’re being summoned.”

“Excuse me?” The CEO raised an eyebrow. “I believe I heard my name called, not yours.”

“Jeju!”

Lena ignored her wife’s victorious smirk and followed her across their penthouse. Together, they entered their daughter’s bedroom. Or, more accurately, her galaxy. Everything in the room was space-themed, from the stars painted on the walls by Kara to the custom holographic displays of planets crafted by Lena.

She moved over to the spaceship-bed. “Hey Cassie. You have fun today at the park?”

Cassandra nodded vigorously. Although she was a mix of both their genes, it was obvious which parent she took after. Her hair, eyes, and lips were all the spitting image of Lena’s. As the CEO said, Cassandra had inherited three things from Kara: “Your heart, your powers, and your appetite.”

“Ruby took us on all the slides! Except the big ones, since I’m not tall enough yet.”

“Well,” Kara replied, “You’re only five. Still a little too small for Captain Spacemaker.”

Their daughter shook her head. “I ran the calculations. Assuming I maintain the optimal position in the raft, the risk of me falling out is only 4.86 percent. The gravitational force of the drop would counter the centrifugal force assuming that our velocity remained above sixty miles an hour. With Ruby’s weight along with mine-”

“And 4.86 percent is still far too much of a risk for our little genius,” Kara interrupted. “Even .000486 percent would be too high.”

Cassandra rolled her eyes. “I’m half-Kryptonian. The odds of me being hurt by a fall like that are astronomical.”

Lena ruffled her daughter’s hair. “Yes, but everyone at the park would panic and your day would be ruined. Plus, even if your calculations are correct-” (they were, Lena had just mentally done them herself) – “The ride attendant doesn’t know all that. They’d have to change the rules just for you.”

“L-Corp owns the park through a subsidiary. I’m sure you could have called ahead,” Cassandra pouted playfully. “But seriously, I know. Most kids don’t get to travel to Europe for a day with their cousins. I’ve got no right to complain.” She paused, smiling teasingly. “But I still might.”

She pressed a kiss to Cassandra’s forehead. In truth, Lena had been terrified of being a mother. Lillian hadn’t exactly set a good example. And there was the real danger that any child of Lena’s would be corrupted by privilege. Of the three people in their household, only Kara knew the value of a dollar. To Lena and Cassandra, money was an abstract concept rather than a matter of concern.

They’d done their best as parents to emphasize how fortunate Cassandra was. It was a delicate balance between ensuring that their daughter did not become entitled and allowing her to take pride in her accomplishments…of which there were many. Cassandra had inherited Lena’s remarkable IQ, which only added another dimension to her parenting.

“Can I have a story, please?”

Of course, she was still a five-year-old child. Kara and Lena were determined to provide her with as normal a life as possible without diminishing her intelligence. Unlike Lena during her early years, Cassandra was allowed to watch cartoons, eat sugary snacks, and sleep with a stuffed teddy bear. She wasn’t enrolled in school, however. There was little point. While technically homeschooled, most of her education was self-taught.

Like her mother, she possessed an insatiable appetite for knowledge.

Lena raised an eyebrow. “Oh? And which one of us gets to read it?” she asked.

Cassandra frowned thoughtfully. “Both! No, how about one from each? Since I didn’t see you until tonight. Jeju can read one in Kryptonse and mom can read one in English.”

She’d also inherited Lena’s penchant for firm negotiating.

\

“You’re still nervous,” Kara said.

After all these years, the hero could recognize when Lena was agitated. It wasn’t much…a tightening of her ring finger was the best indicator. But when it was there, Kara could see it.

Lena uncharacteristically flopped down onto their bed. “We have to stop her from feeling entitled without making her feel like she isn’t special. Make her confident but not arrogant. Encourage her intellect without ruining her childhood.” She sighed. “In some ways, ruling the world is easier than being a parent.”

“No. It’s just more personal stakes,” Kara replied, sitting down next to her wife. “Look at her. She’s happy…she has friends. She goes out of her way to help people, even little things like just picking up Ruby’s cell phone after she dropped it. I couldn’t be prouder of her.”

“That’s the thing though, isn’t it?” Lena sat up, hunching over her knees. “Are we placing too much expectations on her?”

It was one of the most difficult issues of their marriage. Kara wanted a child to help continue the legacy of Krypton and the House of El, to redeem it from Alura’s actions. Lena wanted an heir with her intelligence capable of running L-Corp and managing the world once she eventually grew older. It wasn’t fair to place those burdens on a child, but there was no one else. Only someone born of both of their genes had a chance to meet those goals.

“Probably,” Kara admitted. It wasn’t the first time they’d had this discussion and it wouldn’t be the last. When they were completely honest, both women could admit that they had selfish reasons for wanting a child that went well beyond the norm. It had led to a handful of bitter fights between them, both accusing the other of prioritizing their need for legacy over Cassandra’s happiness.

Kara’s hearing stretched out, allowing the CEO to hear her daughter’s soft breathing two rooms over as she settled into sleep.

“She has my brains. It won’t be long before we need to have this talk with her. She’ll accuse us of wanting an heir more than a child, and she won’t be wrong.” Lena breathed deeply. “Cass will tell me she’s nothing, but a product of a test tube meant to run my company.

Kara shook her head. “That’s not true. We both have hopes for her future, but we’ve always put her first. It’s something we both have to struggle with. But we’d love her even if she wasn’t smart and didn’t have powers. The fact that she was born in a lab instead of one of our stomachs doesn’t change that.”

“I do love her, Kara. I love her so much it hurts. I’m just afraid she might doubt that.”

“Like you said, she has your brains.” The hero stroked her wife’s hair. “How long did it take for you to realize Lillian didn’t love you and probably never would. Five minutes? She might struggle with our expectations for her, and we’ll need to be honest and admit our own failings. But she will never believe that we don’t love her more than anything, even if she was a C student who didn’t have an ounce of Kryptonian DNA.”

Lena nodded once before getting up and walking over to the door. “Cassandra?” she called softly.

There was a blur of speed as their daughter instantly appeared in the doorway, her own super-hearing having picked up the sound of her name. “Yes, mom?” she asked, holding her teddy bear in her arms.

“I’m feeling nervous about my meeting tomorrow. I think I need some extra protection tonight. Can you sleep with me and jeju?”

Cassandra smiled. “If you wanted a hug mommy, you just had to say so.” Still holding onto her bear, she jumped forward and tackled Lena onto the bed, embracing her warmly.

Kara allowed herself a second to watch the happy smile on Lena’s face. The hero knew her wife would have given anything to grow up with a maternal figure who woke her up in the middle of the night just for another hug.

Then she joined her family on the bed, and within minutes they were fast asleep.

\

“Do you miss it?”

Kara turned away from the television screen silently relaying images of a reporter covering L-Corp’s response to a recent hurricane in the South Pacific. “How can I? I never really got to start, remember?” she replied to her sister.

The response was phrased as a joke, but Alex must have picked up at the bitterness in her voice.

“It’s okay to be upset.” Alex plopped herself on the sofa’s armrest, looking fondly out the window. Sam was flying with Ruby alongside the boat as the others watched.

It was hard to complain. “Is it though? Look at me. Full-time superhero, beloved by millions. And I’m rich,” Kara added as an afterthought, gesturing to the interior of the yacht around them. It had taken years for Lena to warm up to the purchase, only able to justify it with the promise of family outings and trips to make the kids happy.

“Your wife is rich. You’re technically still skint broke.”

Kara sighed, focusing on the waves rushing by and keeping her gaze off the television screen. Lena had meant her promise to get Kara reinstated at Catco, but they’d both come to the realization that it wouldn’t work out. Supergirl was too busy to commit herself to the job, and her fame would make reporting very difficult.

The one area L-Corp stayed out of was the media. The company hadn’t touched either traditional media or social platforms. Lena believed the discussion of her company needed to be as unbiased as possible. It was the one remaining check on her power. If the public couldn’t honestly say that it supported her actions by this point, then Lena’s mission had failed.

Having Lena’s wife serve as a reporter really wouldn’t fit with that idea.

And so Kara had turned her back on the idea of a normal job. Her only piece of normalcy came from her family, and that had been enough. As extraordinary as their lives were, they could still sit down at the dinner table like anyone else.

The air in the room briefly shifted as the door slid open. Jess slipped inside, smoothing her windswept hair. “Luke wants to try fishing. Winn’s helping him set up.”

Kara frowned. “I thought the captain said there were almost no fish in this area?”

Jess rolled her eyes. “Yes, but Luke was insistent on giving it a try. Winn is handling it, which gives me the opportunity for a break.” She sprawled out onto a couch. “Even on a staffed boat in the middle of a vacation, raising a tween is exhausting.”

“Don’t remind us,” Kara and Alex said together. Cassandra was still several years away from her early teenage years, but it was an inevitability. Connor, Sam and Alex’s son, was now eight years old. The happy boy currently sitting with his cousin on the top of the boat would be reaching that age before his parents knew it.

All three couples had staff, of course, but refused to let hired help take the lead role in raising their children. Sam had been kicked out as a teenager, Jess’s parents were as distant as they came, Winn’s father had been in prison for decades, and Lillian and Alura were best forgotten. Alex, as the only one who’d been raised by a stable family since childhood, often found herself sought out for advice.

Together, they’d all made it work.

“Kara, there’s an earthquake in Dubai they need your help with,” Jess said suddenly, looking at her phone.

The hero was halfway out of her seat and groaning in determination when the secretary raised a placating hand. “Calm down, I’m just teasing. That look on your face was priceless.”

“Well, that still counts as my save of the day. Alex can take the next one.” Alex, Kara, and Sam all served as superheroes and the spearheads of the Justice League. L-Corp and the League had many other heroes and resources at their disposal, of course, but the three women were the big guns on call to respond to any major catastrophe. Even when on vacation, they were still on call.

Jess smiled. “I was tempted to let you fly halfway to the Middle East before calling you back. That would have made headlines. Do they even have earthquakes in the UAE?”

Kara crossed her arms, doing her best to appear angry. “And I would have had you fired.”

“Oh, that’s not up to you. I’ve known Ms. Luthor for longer than you have. You might be the light of her life, but I run her schedule. This isn’t a battle you can win.”

And the hero had to admit Jess was probably right.

\

“I hate to ask, and I know you’ll tell me, but…any progress?” Kara finally asked.

It was the middle of the night. She was sitting with Kara on top of the boat as the craft continued its smooth journey to the Bahamas. Most of the guests and off-duty crew were already asleep, planning to get up early the next day to explore the new resort.

Lena’s gaze rose fup to the stars. It was her most ambitious project yet, the terraforming of an entire planet. Even after ten years of planning, it was still a long way off. But she was confident that it would be successful in the not-too-distant future, allowing humanity to spread throughout the solar system.

And giving the Kryptonians still asleep on Argo a world of their own.

“Still five to ten years away. But I promise that the Kryptonians will be settled on the first transformed world. Probably Mars. Humanity doesn’t need another home quite yet, with the advances we’ve made on Earth.”

They sat in comfortable silence for the next several minutes. The couple had a room downstairs, of course, but not the master suite. Ruby had claimed it as her own, declaring ‘dibs on the master bedroom!’ as soon as this trip had been planned.

When Lena had protested that she owned the yacht, Ruby had reminded her that concepts of ownership hadn’t stopped the CEO’s wife from devouring Ruby’s snack cabinet the last time she’d hosted game night. And so Ruby had gotten the master suit all to herself, except for the nights that the younger kids came in to watch television and all fell asleep.

“How is Cass?” Lena finally asked.

The hero smiled dreamily. “Sitting on her bed in her space pajamas. One hand around her teddy bear, and the other on her laptop as she runs circles around grandmasters in an online tournament.”

Lena grinned. “That’s my girl.”

Kara glanced at her quizzically. “How long before she’s able to beat you?”

Even the rustling of the waves below seemed to still as Lena gasped, scandalized. “I haven’t loss a chess match once in my life, and I solved the game while imprisoned on Argo. There’s no beating me.” Cassandra had been learning that the hard way, having challenged Lena to over four hundred games of chess in the last year alone.

The younger Luthor hadn’t yet managed a draw against her mother, even as she anonymously dominated the professional circuit online.

Kara wasn’t deterred. “I suppose that once she solves the game herself, you’ll be even in direct matches.” She grinned wryly. “But if she solves the game at a younger age than you did, doesn’t beating your record mean she takes your title as the most impressive chess player ever?”

Lena’s skin went white. She’d believed her position as the conqueror of chess was secure until the end of time, but she hadn’t thought of someone matching her record at a younger age. “No, that wouldn’t be fair,” Lena protested. “I was a lot busier than she will be. Remember, taking over the world and all? It’s not a fair comparison!”

“Are you being competitive with our own daughter? And what will you do if she beats you?”

The CEO frowned. She’d always assumed that her offspring would equal her own intelligence. If Cassandra proved to be smarter…it wasn’t a possibility she’d considered before. No one was smarter than Lena.

Cassandra knows two more languages at her age than I did. And I didn’t master quantum physics until I was six. Oh god, what if it’s true?

 Lena glanced at her wife. “Then I will throw a weeklong tantrum, during which you’ll have to bring me ice cream from every country in the world as I mope on the couch.” She paused, finally smiling widely. “And I’ll be the proudest mother in the world. Not because she’s smart, but because I’ll know she’ll use her brains to change the world.”

Kara grinned back, leaning into Lena’s shoulder. “I thought you already changed the world?”

The CEO nodded, glancing up at the crescent moon. “Yes, we did. But the world always needs changing.”
